title: docs: tombstone; superseded by the Statecraft family

Updates `regex` from 1.12.4 to 1.13.1
Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

Updates `libc` from 0.2.186 to 0.2.189
Release notes

Sourced from libc's releases.

0.2.189

Added

  • Emscripten: Add pthread_sigmask, sigwait, sigwaitinfo, sigtimedwait, faccessat, and pthread_kill (#5270)
  • Linux SPARC: Enable the clone3 syscall (#4980)
  • Solarish: Add CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID and CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID (#5274)

Deprecated

  • Deprecate CLONE_INTO_CGROUP and CLONE_CLEAR_SIGHAND. These overflow their types and will be changed to a larger size in the future. (8c6e6710458d)

Fixed

  • Musl riscv32: Rename padding fields to avoid a conflict and fix the build (2499ff0ad993)
  • NuttX: Fix wchar_t definition under Arm (#5245)
  • Windows: Add back link names for time-related symbols (#5300)

0.2.188

Changed

  • Restore Send and Sync for DIR (35b062263401)

These were removed in 0.2.187 because libc does not actually make Send and Sync guarantees about DIR (or other extern types), but this caused some crates to break. The traits are added back for now to allow time to migrate, but will be removed again in the future; please make sure your crates are not relying on libc::DIR: Send or libc::DIR: Sync.

0.2.187

This release contains a number of improvements related to 64-bit time_t configuration. Of note the existing RUST_LIBC_UNSTABLE_* environment variables have been replaced with configuration options. The new way to use these is:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_musl_v1_2_3' cargo ...
RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_gnu_time_bits="64"' cargo ...

Being able to set this via RUSTFLAGS makes it easier to only apply configuration to specific targets (and notably, not the host if build scripts are used).

There are two other notable changes:

  • The 32-bit windows-gnu targets now respect libc_unstable_gnu_time_bits

  • uClibc now supports a similar configuration option:

    RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_uclibc_time64'

Updates `regex` from 1.12.4 to 1.13.1
Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

  • Integers just outside the i64/u64 range incorrectly compared against numeric bounds through lossy f64 rounding (e.g. {"minimum": -9223372036854775808} accepted -9223372036854775809).

[0.48.0] - 2026-07-16

Added

  • iter_errors for #[jsonschema::validator]-generated validators.

Fixed

  • Per-branch context on generated anyOf and oneOf validation errors, matching runtime validators.
  • $recursiveRef in generated validators incorrectly resolved to the innermost $recursiveAnchor (it should resolve to the outermost one).
  • Integer instances just outside the i64/u64 range incorrectly compared against numeric bounds through lossy f64 rounding under arbitrary-precision (e.g. {"minimum": -9223372036854775808} accepted -9223372036854775809).

Performance

  • Faster multipleOf validation for integer instances with integer divisors, via integer arithmetic instead of floating-point modulo.

[0.47.0] - 2026-07-08

Added

  • #[jsonschema::validator] attribute macro (behind the macros feature) that compiles a JSON Schema into is_valid and validate implementations at build time.
  • Keyword::iter_errors for reporting multiple validation errors from a single custom keyword. #1071

Changed

Performance

Fixed

  • type under items asserted with the Validation vocabulary disabled.

Updates `regex` from 1.12.4 to 1.13.1
Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

Markdown: Cap ordered list mark at 999,999,999 (#19351 by @​tats-u)

CommonMark parsers only support ordered list item numbers up to 999,999,999.

With this change, Prettier now caps the ordered list item number at 999,999,999 to ensure that the output is correctly parsed as an ordered list by CommonMark parsers. Numbers larger than 999,999,999 are not parsed as list item numbers and are left unchanged in the output:

<!-- Input -->

1000000001. text


1234567890123456789012) text


<!-- Prettier 3.9.5 -->
999999998. text
999999999. text
999999999. text
999999999. text


1234567890123456789012) text

Do not remove <> from an inline link or image with an empty URL and a title, as this removal would change its interpretation.

Updates the requirements on [lz4_flex](https://github.com/pseitz/lz4_flex) to permit the latest version.
Changelog

Sourced from lz4_flex's changelog.

0.14.0 (2026-07-14)

Features

  • Add alloc feature to allow no_std operation without an allocator. The std feature now implies alloc. Without alloc only the _into variants of the block API are available, e.g. compress_into; the compression hash table is placed on the stack or can be provided via compress_into_with_table.
Note: Users with `default-features = false` need to additionally enable the `alloc`
feature to keep the APIs returning `Vec`, e.g. `compress` and `decompress`.

0.13.1 (2026-05-09)

Fixes

  • Fix compression with short dictionaries (less than 4 bytes), avoiding a panic/out-of-bounds read #222
Compression with dictionaries shorter than the minimum match length of 4 now falls
back to compression without a dictionary instead of panicking or reading past
the dictionary. 

This is a security fix for unsafe compression with untrusted dictionaries.

Users on 0.13.0 should upgrade to 0.13.1.

  • Fix panic in From<io::Error> implementation for frame::Error #221 (thanks @​phoerious)

0.13.0 (2026-03-15)

Features

  • Add option to reuse compression dict #207 (thanks @​matthewfollegot)

Fixes

  • Fix handling of invalid match offsets during decompression #055502e (thanks @​Marcono1234)
Invalid match offsets (offset == 0) during decompression were not properly
handled, which could lead to invalid memory reads. This is a security fix
that was also backported to 0.12.1 and 0.11.6.
  • Fix get_maximum_output_size overflow on 32-bit targets #205 (thanks @​dglittle)
Cast input_len to u64 before multiplying by 110, avoiding overflow on
32-bit targets (e.g. wasm32) where input_len * 110 overflows usize
when input_len > ~39MB.

0.12.2 (2026-05-09)

Fixes

  • Fix compression with short dictionaries (less than 4 bytes), avoiding a panic/out-of-bounds read #222
Compression with dictionaries shorter than the minimum match length of 4 now falls
back to compression without a dictionary instead of panicking or reading past
the dictionary.

title: feat(231): policy-kernel re-consumes the four extracted Apache-2.0 primitives
body:
## What

`policy-kernel` becomes consumer-zero of four domain-neutral primitives that
were extracted from it into standalone Apache-2.0 crates and published to
crates.io. This is the direct analog of OAP already consuming the external
`spec-spine` CLI rather than a vendored compiler.

| Crate | crates.io | Delegated internal |
|---|---|---|
| [`canonical-keysort-json`](https://crates.io/crates/canonical-keysort-json) | 0.1.0 | `canonical_json_sorted` |
| [`attest-ledger-core`](https://crates.io/crates/attest-ledger-core) | 0.1.0 | `link_record_hash`, `sha256_hex` |
| [`trust-window`](https://crates.io/crates/trust-window) | 0.1.0 | `CoherenceScheduler` internals |
| [`action-gate-core`](https://crates.io/crates/action-gate-core) | 0.1.0 | `evaluate()` gate machinery |

## The invariant: keep the shapes, swap the internals

Every public type and function the seven consumers and two verifier binaries
touch is preserved byte-identically. Only internals delegate:

- **Hashing.** OAP keeps `ProofRecord` (flat fields) and its anchor signing.
  `canonical-keysort-json` produces byte-identical canonical JSON to the previous
  in-tree sorter, pinned by a new parity test across scalars, nesting, arrays,
  unicode, and a real `ProofRecord`, so every proof-chain and audit-chain hash is
  unchanged. The `audit.rs` file writer + rotation are OAP persistence and are
  **not** extracted.
- **Trust scoring.** `CoherenceScheduler` / `PrivilegeLevel` keep their API; the
  scheduler now wraps a `trust-window` `WindowScorer` (`DegradeOnly`). A boolean
  action is a `Sample::aligned`, so the scoring math is identical.
- **Decision gate.** `evaluate`, `ToolCallContext`, `PolicyBundle`,
  `PolicyDecision`, `PolicyOutcome` are unchanged. `evaluate()` now runs an
  `action-gate` `Gate` whose six checks are OAP's six domain checks in the
  original order; the code-governance context maps to a domain-neutral
  `ActionContext` (typed extras in `attributes`), and the generic `Decision` maps
  back to `PolicyDecision` (bundle-derived rule ids ride in `check_ids`). Reason
  codes, rule ids, degrade-vs-deny, and first-match order are preserved.

## Verification

- The crate's own proof-chain, audit-chain, coherence, and all fifteen
  `evaluate` tests pass unchanged (73 total).
- Spec-code coupling gate: OK, 5 paths, no drift. Codebase index: fresh.
  clippy: 0 warnings. rustfmt: clean.
- The five real consumers (provider-registry, tool-registry, factory-engine,
  policy-compiler, and the two verifier bins) build against the unchanged API.
  `axiomregent` also consumes only the preserved API; it could not be built in
  the authoring environment because of a pre-existing missing `onnxruntime`
  native lib (unrelated to this change), and CI has it.

## Provenance

The extracted source carried `AGPL-3.0-or-later` in OAP. Relicensing to
Apache-2.0 is the sole copyright holder's authorized act, recorded in each
extracted repo's `NOTICE`. Spec 231 is the OAP-side record of the vend, the
analog of spec 219 for tenant-tail. The OAP-specific proof-record fields, the
`PolicyBundle` config model, and OAP's six domain checks stayed in OAP.

## Not in scope

The `audit.rs` file writer / rotation, the spec-068 permission-runtime family,
and `provenance_policy.rs` stay in OAP. No consumer API change; no wasm-target
change (the pre-existing `getrandom` wasm posture is unaffected).

title: fix(124): fail loud on init_pipeline failure + factory.event correlation diagnostics
body:
## Context

Follow-on to #569 (stagecraft-web gate delivery), in the same `commands/factory.rs` run-integration surface. Diagnostics + fail-loud only; no behavioural change to the correlation itself.

## Why

The `factory.event` gate handler resolves a web-side approval by matching the inbound `pipeline_id` against the run's `stagecraft_pipeline_id`. That field is set from the `init_pipeline` response in a fire-and-forget task whose failure was a silent `warn`-and-continue, so a run that fails `init_pipeline` executes with `stagecraft_pipeline_id = None` and can never match a web approval, looking identical to a healthy run in the UI. Diagnosing a stuck run (approvals on the web not reaching OPC) was near-impossible from the logs.

## Change

- **Fail-loud `init_pipeline` error:** `warn` → `error` + a `factory:stagecraft_correlation_failed` UI event. The success path now logs the id triad (`pipeline_id`, local `run_id`, `platform_run_id`) so a repro can correlate the web-shown run id against the pipeline id gate approvals key on.
- **Correlation-miss trace:** `apply_factory_event`'s no-matching-run branch (previously a bare `return`, indistinguishable from an ordinary org broadcast) now logs the unmatched `pipeline_id` at debug.

## Deferred (intentionally)

The identity question between the reservation `platform_run_id` shown in the web UI and the `init_pipeline` `pipeline_id` (observed as `614d76b2` vs `eff4ea20`) is deferred to an end-to-end `tauri dev` repro before any behavioural correlation change. `factory.event` carries `pipeline.id` (stagecraft `factory.ts`), so the correlation is structurally correct *if* the web-confirmed pipeline equals the one `init_pipeline` created; these diagnostics make that determination conclusive.

## Verification

`cargo check` green; spec-code coupling gate "no drift"; spec 124 amended, shards regenerated.

title: fix(187): bootstrap default Secret Service collection for e2e nightly (#567 item 1)
body:
## Summary

- The OPC e2e nightly's seed writer (`e2e_seed_session`) needs a **default Secret Service collection** to write the fake session token into. A fresh runner has none, so `echo -n "" | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock` (zero bytes / immediate EOF) failed with `Secret Service: no result found`, failing the seeding fixtures `ac8` and `208`.
- The e2e run step now bootstraps the default collection in two layers: **(1)** a newline-terminated empty password (`printf '\n' | gnome-keyring-daemon --daemonize --unlock`, the keyring-rs CI pattern) so the daemon creates + unlocks the login keyring and registers it as `default`; **(2)** a fallback via `secret-tool store` (`libsecret-tools`) if the alias still did not materialise.
- Scoped the FR-T5(e) "Open issue on failure" step to `github.event_name == 'schedule'` so manual `workflow_dispatch` bring-up iterations do not each auto-file a regression issue.

## Verification

`workflow_dispatch` run **29075858753** (on this branch) verifies the fix:

| fixture | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `208/org-halt-drill` (2 tests) | fail (`no result found`) | **pass** |
| `183/ac8-precondition-loss` | fail (`no result found`) | **pass** |
| `183/ac7-boot-sticky` | pass | pass |
| `183/ac9-no-orphan-on-quit` | fail | fail (contract 3, out of scope) |

Overall `3 failed | 1 passed` -> `1 failed | 4 passed`. The `Secret Service: no result found` class is gone; the sole remaining failure is `ac9` (element-click-intercept / session-terminated), which is contract 3 / #567 item 2 and stays tracked. The "Open issue on failure" step correctly reported `skipped` on this dispatch run.

Verification was push-then-observe against CI because the failure mode is Secret-Service-only and does not reproduce on the macOS `apple-native` keychain.

## Spec alignment

- Spec: `specs/187-opc-e2e-test-harness/spec.md` (§3.5.2 records contract 2 verified; completion now hinges only on contract 3). Coupling gate clean (`spec-spine couple: OK, no drift`); no waiver required.

## Change classification

- [x] Bug fix — corrects incorrect behavior

## Checklist

- [x] Changes align with the referenced spec (or no spec applies)
- [x] Spec-compiler output unchanged (or spec frontmatter was intentionally modified)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or API keys committed
- [x] Tests pass locally (N/A: Secret-Service-only, verified in CI run 29075858753)

Addresses **#567 item 1** (default Secret Service collection). Item 2 (`ac9` element interactions) remains open.

title: fix(124): deliver stagecraft-web gate approvals to OPC runs; resume + handshake hardening
body:
## Problem

A factory run triggered from stagecraft sat at `Processing 0/6, waiting for agent output` and never advanced once its gates were approved on the stagecraft **web** UI. Stagecraft publishes gate decisions as `factory.event { event_type: "stage_confirmed" | "stage_rejected", … }` (`api/factory/factory.ts`), but OPC registered **no handler** for the `factory.event` envelope kind, so every one was dropped (`received factory.event, no handler registered`, confirmed in `opc.log`). The local pipeline blocks on a per-run oneshot (`TauriGateHandler.pending`) that only the OPC-local Confirm dialog resolved, so a web-side sign-off never reached it. (The run context already tracked `stagecraft_pipeline_id`, showing this routing was anticipated but never wired.)

## Fix

1. **`factory.event` handler (the core fix).** Register a dispatch handler mirroring `register_factory_run_handler`. It routes by `stagecraft_pipeline_id` to the matching run's `TauriGateHandler` and applies `stage_confirmed` to approve / `stage_rejected` to reject. Stage ids are normalised to their `sN` prefix (`stage_prefix` / `match_pending_stage`) so the OPC vocabulary (`s4-api-specification`) joins stagecraft's (`s4-api-spec`) and the `s1`/`s2`/`s3` sign-off labels. Echoes of a locally-resolved gate find no pending gate and no-op. This is the reverse of the OPC-side dual-write already present in `confirm_factory_stage`.
2. **Resume path.** `list_factory_runs` emitted the stagecraft project UUID as `project_path`, so Resume ran `PathBuf::from(uuid).canonicalize()` (ENOENT) and surfaced a raw OS error. It now emits no local path; `resolve_resume_project_path` returns an actionable message, and `PipelineHistory.tsx` falls back to the real clone path or disables Resume with a "Clone locally to resume" hint.
3. **Governance handshake fail-loud.** `send_and_await_reply` bounded only the reply wait, not the outbound send on the bounded duplex channel; a stalled WebSocket writer could block the send indefinitely, wedging a run before governance completed (the "Waiting for agent output" silent stall). The outbound send is now bounded (10 s), so the run-grant handshake fails closed with an actionable error.
4. **`business_docs`.** `extract_factory_run` silently dropped the envelope's explicit `business_docs`; it now surfaces them in the log. Full materialisation from the bare `storage_ref` (presigning in the stagecraft relay, as knowledge bundles already get) is a scoped follow-up; no confirmed live caller populates the field today.

## Verification

- `cargo check` clean; **34 factory-module tests pass** (new: `stage_prefix_normalises_across_vocabularies`, `match_pending_stage_reconciles_drifted_ids`, `resolve_resume_project_path_rejects_missing_and_accepts_existing`); `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Spec-code coupling gate green (specs 124 + 076 amended).
- **Not yet proven end-to-end**: "web approval unblocks the run" needs a **packaged OPC release build against a live cluster** (a `tauri dev` build has `opc://` deep-link + duplex reachability differences). The changes are additive (a new handler for a previously-ignored envelope kind; no existing code path changes), which bounds the risk.

title: fix(106): map M2M sub claim so deployd accepts stagecraft deploy tokens
body:
## Problem

Every tenant deploy triggered from stagecraft failed with diagnostic `token missing subject claim` (deployd-api `routes.rs`). deployd-api's `create_deployment` owner-bind guard rejects any bearer token without a `sub` claim, but Rauthy's `client_credentials` grant (stagecraft's machine-to-machine deploy dispatch, `api/deploy/oidcM2m.ts`) sets `sub = None` by default because that grant has no end-user subject. Nothing wired the one Rauthy flag that maps a subject onto M2M tokens, so this failed for **every** deploy, on any environment, mock or Rauthy tenant auth alike (it is orthogonal to tenant auth, and predates spec 225).

## Fix

Enable `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_MAP_SUB` on the rauthy StatefulSet via a new `access.clientCredentialsMapSub` chart value (default `true`), mirroring the existing `DISABLE_REFRESH_TOKEN_NBF` wiring. Rauthy then maps `sub = <client id>` onto `client_credentials` tokens, satisfying deployd's guard. The flag landed in Rauthy v0.34.0; the chart image is 0.35.0.

Chart-only change; no deployd-api code change (the guard already documents this assumption in `auth.rs::is_owner_or_admin`).

## Verification

- `helm template rauthy platform/charts/rauthy` renders `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_MAP_SUB: "true"`.
- Confirmed the flag exists in Rauthy >= 0.34.0 against the vendored source (`token_set.rs` / `rauthy_config.rs`).
- Spec-code coupling gate green (spec 106 amended).

## Operational (post-merge)

1. Redeploy rauthy (`helm upgrade`) so the StatefulSet picks up the env var.
2. Restart stagecraft so its cached M2M token is re-minted with the `sub` claim (the token is cached until near expiry).
3. Retry a tenant deploy.

title: OPC e2e nightly: complete first-green bring-up (Secret Service collection + per-AC element interactions)
body:
## Context

The OPC E2E nightly (spec 187) has never had a genuinely-green run. Before #508 the e2e step **masked** vitest failures (`npm run test:e2e | tee` returned tee's exit code), so a run with failing fixtures still exited 0. #508 added `set -eo pipefail` (unmasking) alongside the seeding fixtures, and the bundler bug (#564) then failed the `tauri build` step every night until it was fixed. Spec 187 §6 explicitly defers `implementation: complete` to "the first green nightly."

## Fixed (PR #566, verified by nightly run 29042838102)

**WebDriver session creation.** WebdriverIO v9 negotiates WebDriver BiDi by default (`webSocketUrl: true`); tauri-driver proxies to WebKitWebDriver on Linux, which has no BiDi and rejected the session with `session not created: Failed to match capabilities`. Fix: `wdio:enforceWebDriverClassic: true` in `fixtures/_session.ts` + pin `tauri-driver@2.0.6` / `webdriverio@9`. Result: `4 failed` -> `3 failed | 1 passed`; **`ac7` passes** and the capabilities error is gone.

## Remaining (this issue)

### 1. Secret Service default collection (`ac8`, `208`)

The seed writer fails with:
```
e2e_seed_session set failed (dev.opc.stagecraft/session):
Couldn't access platform secure storage: Secret Service: no result found
```
`gnome-keyring-daemon --daemonize --unlock --components=secrets` on a fresh runner does not establish a **default** Secret Service collection for the `keyring` crate's `set` to write into.

Proposed next steps (untried here to avoid landing unverified CI changes):
- Match the keyring-rs CI pattern: single daemonized invocation with a **newline-terminated** empty password (`printf '\n' | ...` or `<<< ''`) rather than `echo -n ""` (no byte on stdin).
- If that is insufficient, `apt-get install libsecret-tools` and bootstrap the default collection with a `secret-tool store` before the fixtures run.

(The error itself confirms #564's `[[example]]` move works: the harness finds and runs the relocated binary.)

### 2. Per-AC element interactions (`ac9`, and `ac8`/`208` once past keyring)

With a session created, `ac9-no-orphan-on-quit` fails at an element click:
```
element click intercepted ...
session deleted because of page crash or hang
```
This is per-fixture app/interaction bring-up under xvfb (an overlay intercepting the click, or the WebView crashing on Quit), not an environment pin. Needs per-AC debugging.

## Non-gating

The nightly is not a per-PR gate (FR-T5), so this blocks nothing. It is the remaining work to reach the first genuinely-green nightly and flip spec 187 `implementation: complete`.

title: fix(187): fix nightly e2e WebDriver session creation (classic WebDriver + pins)
body:
## What this fixes

The OPC E2E nightly's `tauri build` unblocked once #564 landed, and the e2e-fixture step then ran for the first time in days. **Record correction:** these fixtures are *not* a runner-drift regression. The 07-04 "green" run masked failures (`npm run test:e2e | tee` returned tee's exit code; 2 test files were failing yet it exited 0). `set -eo pipefail` (unmasking) landed in #508 alongside the seeding fixtures, so the first honest signal only surfaced now. Spec 187 §6 always deferred `implementation: complete` to "the first green nightly," which has never happened — this is **initial bring-up**, not a regression.

This PR lands the **one contract I could fix and verify**:

**WebDriver session creation.** WebdriverIO v9 negotiates WebDriver BiDi by default (`webSocketUrl: true`); tauri-driver proxies to WebKitWebDriver on Linux, which has no BiDi and rejected the session with `session not created: Failed to match capabilities`. Fix: `wdio:enforceWebDriverClassic: true` + pin `tauri-driver@2.0.6` / `webdriverio@9` (a tauri-driver bump is a known cause of this error class, tauri-apps/tauri#8828).

**Verified** by nightly run 29042838102: `4 failed` → `3 failed | 1 passed`; **`ac7` passes** and the "failed to match capabilities" class is gone.

## What this does NOT fix (tracked in #567)

Two contracts are deeper than an env pin, so per a bounded remit they are tracked, not churned:
1. **Secret Service default collection** — `ac8`/`208` still fail the seed `set` with "no result found" (`gnome-keyring --unlock` doesn't establish a default collection on the fresh runner). The keyring init is left at the original invocation here to avoid landing an unverified change.
2. **Per-AC element interactions** — `ac9` fails at an element click (`click intercepted` / `page crash or hang` under xvfb): per-fixture app bring-up.

## Non-gating

The nightly is not a per-PR gate (FR-T5). spec 187 §3.5.2 records contract 1 as fixed-and-verified and contracts 2/3 as open. Coupling clean (3 paths, all owned by spec 187).

title: feat(227): wire opt-in Redis end to end; complete create-project infra projection (Stage 4)
body:
## Stage 4: Redis Infrastructure resource end to end

Closes the final stage of spec 227. The opt-in Redis Infrastructure resource now flows from the create-project form through to a provisioned dev instance, satisfying FR-004/FR-005/FR-006 and flipping spec 227 to `status: approved` / `implementation: complete`.

### What lands

- **Form (`app.projects.new.tsx`)** — the Infrastructure "Redis / cache" row becomes a live checkbox (single topology only; dual keeps the disabled composition-guard row, FR-008). Selecting it submits `data-redis`, so the scaffold composes factory-encore's `data-redis` module and bakes a `redis` block into the app's `apps/api/infra.config.json`. Its dedicated `redis` state is distinct from the cron stage's `selectedModules` transitive-requires closure, so there is no double-submit.
- **Persistence (`schema.ts` + migration 4)** — `projects` gains a `uses_redis` column (default false), set at create from the opt-in selection. Under Option A the topology is build-time, so the selection is fixed at scaffold.

Non-development environments supply an external Redis as runtime env; deployd never provisions it for them (FR-005).
- **Chart (`deployment.yaml` / `values.yaml`)** — inject `REDIS_USER` (default `default`, the built-in Redis ACL user the `--requirepass` preview workload authenticates as) alongside the Stage 3 `REDIS_HOST`/`REDIS_PASSWORD`, matching the exact `${REDIS_HOST}`/`${REDIS_USER}`/`$env:REDIS_PASSWORD` triple the app's baked `redis` block resolves.

### Dependency

factory-encore spec 008 (data-redis promotion) is the adapter-side dependency, already merged.

title: fix(187): make e2e_seed_session a cargo example so Tauri stops bundling it
body:
## Problem

**Release Desktop** failed on all three platforms, and **OPC E2E Nightly** has failed every night since 2026-07-05:

```
failed to bundle project Failed to copy binary from
".../target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/e2e_seed_session": does not exist
Error failed to bundle project ...
##[error]Command "pnpm ["tauri","build",...]" failed with exit code 1
```

## Root cause

#508 (2026-07-04) registered the e2e keychain seed helper as a `[[bin]]` in the opc crate, gated behind `required-features = ["e2e-seed"]`. That gating correctly keeps it out of shipping builds, but **Tauri's bundler enumerates every `[[bin]]` of the packaged crate** and copies each from the release target dir. A required-features bin the release `cargo build` never compiles makes the bundler fail with "does not exist".

This broke:
- the **Release Desktop** workflow (first run since #508 → this failure), and
- the nightly's own `tauri build` step (OPC E2E Nightly went ✅→❌ the first night after #508: green 07-04, red every night 07-05 onward).

## Fix

Keep the helper **in the opc crate** (the same-`keyring` guarantee is load-bearing; the header comment explains a standalone helper crate would forfeit Secret-Service attribute compatibility) but declare it as a cargo **`[[example]]`** under `examples/e2e_seed_session.rs`. Tauri does not bundle examples, so `tauri build` is clean, while the nightly still builds it explicitly with `--example e2e_seed_session --features e2e-seed`.

Verified via `cargo metadata`: the target is now `kind=example`, so it is no longer in Tauri's bin set (`opc`, `opc-web` remain the only bins, both build in release).

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: `[[bin]]` → `[[example]]`; feature comment updated.
- Move `src/bin/e2e_seed_session.rs` → `examples/e2e_seed_session.rs` (git rename).
- Harness `seedBinPath()` → `target/release/examples/`; spawn error hint → `--example`.
- Harness unit test regex → `examples/` path.
- `opc-e2e-nightly.yml` seed-helper build step → `--example`.
- spec 187: `establishes` path + new **§3.5.1** recording the "example-not-bin" invariant and why.

## Validation

- `cargo metadata` confirms `e2e_seed_session` is `kind=example`.
- featuregraph golden unchanged; coupling gate clean (6 paths, all owned by spec 187).
- I am dispatching `opc-e2e-nightly.yml` on this branch to exercise the exact `tauri build` + `--example` build steps end-to-end before merge.

---

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `src/bin/e2e_seed_session.rs` is renamed to `examples/e2e_seed_session.rs` (a cargo bin→example conversion). title: fix(136): pin deployd-api builder to rust:1.95-bookworm for runtime glibc parity
body:
## Problem

The `deploy-hetzner` job has been failing on every CD run. The deployd-api pod is in **CrashLoopBackOff**:

```
=== Pod logs (latest) ===
deployd-api: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found (required by deployd-api)
deployd-api: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.39' not found (required by deployd-api)
```

(observed on run 28989144206, image `sha-a2235ad`.)

## Root cause

#558 bumped the Dockerfile builder `rust:1.88 -> rust:1.95` for the hiqlite 0.14 / serde_rusqlite 0.43 MSRV. The bare `rust:1.95` tag tracks **Debian Trixie** (glibc 2.41), but the runtime stage is `debian:bookworm-slim` (**glibc 2.36**). A Trixie-built binary links against `GLIBC_2.38`/`GLIBC_2.39` symbols the Bookworm runtime does not provide, so the container fails at start.

The `1.88` tag was still Bookworm-based, which is why the deploy had been green before the bump. This is a **runtime** failure: the Docker build and CI both pass; it only surfaces at deploy time.

## Fix

- Pin the builder to `rust:1.95-bookworm` so builder and runtime glibc stay in lockstep (glibc 2.36 on both). Same rustc 1.95.0, older Debian base.
- Record the builder/runtime glibc-parity constraint as a clarification in spec 136 (which `extends` this Dockerfile) so the next MSRV bump does not silently reintroduce the skew.

## Validation

This CD workflow auto-triggers on push to `main` for `platform/services/deployd-api-rs/**`, so merging rebuilds the image and redeploys to Hetzner. The definitive check is `deploy-hetzner` showing the pod reach **Ready** instead of CrashLoopBackOff. I will shepherd that run after merge.

Coupling gate: clean (Dockerfile edit coupled to spec 136).

title: fix(034): align featuregraph scanner SPEC_REGEX to canonical specs/ layout
body:
## Summary

The featuregraph scanner's `SPEC_REGEX` required the `// Spec:` header directive to match `spec/<path>.md` (singular `spec/`, `.md`, no trailing content), the pre-`specs/` layout shape. Current-layout headers `// Spec: specs/NNN-slug/spec.md` (optionally annotated with the FR or section a file implements) were rejected as `INVALID_HEADER_FORMAT`, so the committed golden accepted **225** such entries as expected state, blinding the featuregraph-golden CI gate to any *new* malformed header.

This lands as a spec 034 amendment (a `refines:` edge over `scanner.rs`, aspect `scanner-spec-directive-canonical-layout`):

- **Widen `SPEC_REGEX`** to `specs?/[...]\.md(\s.*)?$`: accept the canonical `specs/` prefix (still tolerating legacy `spec/` so no currently-parsing header regresses) plus an optional whitespace-separated trailing annotation. Capture group 2 still yields only the path.
- **Migrate the featuregraph crate's own six headers** off dead `spec/core/*.md` paths onto `specs/034-featuregraph-registry-scanner-fix/spec.md` (both `FEATUREGRAPH_REGISTRY` and `GOVERNANCE_ENGINE` are this spec's `code_aliases`), removing six `SPEC_PATH_MISMATCH` warnings.
- **Regenerate the golden.** `INVALID_HEADER_FORMAT` 225 to 57, `SPEC_PATH_MISMATCH` 49 to 43; 3 files reclassify `INVALID_HEADER_FORMAT` to `DANGLING_FEATURE_ID` (net error-severity 225 to 60), surfacing a latent wrong Feature token (`SCHEDULING`, whose registry alias is `SCHEDULED_AGENT_EXECUTION`) deferred to spec 079.

The 57 residual `INVALID` plus 3 `DANGLING` are genuinely-malformed headers (bare-id tokens, a `.yaml` reference, comma-joined paths, a wrong Feature token), now clearly visible instead of buried under 168 false positives. Fixing them is a per-file convention migration that belongs to the owning specs, deferred to a follow-up. The amendment accounts for the full residual, so the golden's ability to surface a *new* malformation is restored without pretending the backlog is empty.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p featuregraph`: 21 unit tests + golden green.
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (9 paths, no drift).
- `oap-registry-enrich validate-graph`: graph well-formed (231 specs, edges resolve, supersession acyclic).
- Local adversarial review (correctness + docs + cold finders, then per-finding refuters): 3 findings confirmed and fixed (DANGLING accounting, comment whitespace precision, marker-glyph wording); remainder refuted; every quantitative claim verified exact against the regenerated golden.

title: fix(196): allow ACME HTTP-01 solver into monitoring; close deploy validation
body:
## Summary

Fixes the FR-006 NetworkPolicy gap that blocked Grafana TLS on the Hetzner cluster and closes spec 196's deploy-time validation.

- **Bug fix.** `monitoring`'s default-deny admitted ingress-nginx to Grafana (`:3000`) but had no allow for the ephemeral cert-manager HTTP-01 solver pods (`:8089`). On this cluster the netpol controller rejects rather than drops, so every ACME challenge for a `monitoring` ingress failed with a 502 and Grafana's Let's Encrypt certificate could never issue. Adds `allow-acme-solver-from-ingress-nginx` (solver label + `:8089` only; receiver isolation SC-008 untouched). The certificate then issued immediately.
- **Validation closure.** V001-V012 ran end-to-end against the live Hetzner cluster, so `implementation:` flips `pending -> complete` (`status:` stays `draft`; approval is a separate ratification act). Per-SC evidence recorded in `spec.md` §Deploy-time validation record.
- **Doc accuracy (from local adversarial review).** Folded the solver flow into FR-006's enumerated list as (d); credited the SC-005 negative probe; corrected an inaccurate lifecycle-precedent note (196 is the first `draft`+`complete` spec, not a 199/201/211 precedent, which are `approved`); tracked the same solver gap in `stagecraft`/`deployd`/`rauthy` as a follow-up owned by those specs (196 does not `establishes:` their policy files).

## Testing

- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (4 paths, no drift).
- featuregraph golden regenerated and deterministic (`cargo test -p featuregraph`).
- NetworkPolicy correctness verified: wired into `platform/k8s/policies/kustomization.yaml`; solver label + port correct (cert-manager v1.19.3, acmesolver `:8089`); scoping does not widen the `:9090` receiver or `:3000` Grafana surface; additive semantics leave unlabeled pods under default-deny.
- Deploy-time V001-V012 executed against the live Hetzner cluster (evidence in `spec.md`).

Branch re-homed onto current `origin/main` (#558); all derived artifacts regenerated fresh.

title: deployd-api: hiqlite 0.14 WAL serialization change may brick boot on pre-existing single-node state
body:
## Summary

The hiqlite `0.14` bump that landed in #558 (`a2235ad7`) changed the
on-disk WAL/logs-store serialization: `hiqlite-wal` dropped `rkyv` in
favour of `bincode`/`serde`. `deployd-api-rs` runs hiqlite as a
**single node** with an embedded Raft store, and its boot path treats a
`start_node` failure as fatal. An existing deployd data directory written
by a pre-`0.14` hiqlite therefore risks a hard boot failure after the
upgrade, and hiqlite's `auto-heal` feature does **not** cover this case.

This is an operational upgrade caveat, not a code bug. Filing it so the
next deployd rollout against a persistent data dir has a tracked home
before someone hits it.

## Why deployd is exposed

- **Single-node topology.** `store.rs` pins one node:
  `HQL_NODES = "1 127.0.0.1:7001 127.0.0.1:7002"`
  (`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/src/store.rs:78`).
- **Fatal boot on store error.** `init_db` propagates a `start_node`
  error with `?` and has no deployd-level move-aside / retry:
  `let client = hiqlite::start_node(config).await?;`
  (`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/src/store.rs:22-28`). `main.rs:44`
  awaits `init_db` at startup, so a store-open error aborts the process.
- **auto-heal does not cover a format change.** deployd enables
  hiqlite's `auto-heal` feature (`Cargo.toml:17`,
  `features = ["sqlite", "backup", "s3", "auto-heal"]`), and that feature
  does extend into the WAL layer (`hiqlite/Cargo.toml:24`:
  `auto-heal = ["hiqlite-wal/auto-heal"]`). But the WAL-layer heal path
  (`hiqlite-wal/src/wal.rs:110-157`) only recovers from a **bad CRC /
  torn write**: it rolls the last log ID back to the last valid record
  and expects the truncated tail to be **re-synced from another cluster
  member**. A serialization-format change is not a CRC failure (the
  reader cannot parse the old record framing at all), and even if the
  heal path engaged, deployd is single-node and has **no peer to
  re-sync from**.

## Impact

A deployd instance whose hiqlite data dir persists across the `0.14`
upgrade (any PVC-backed dev/staging deployment via the Azure AKS or
Hetzner K3s paths) may fail to boot with a store-open / integrity error
and no automatic recovery. deployd's Raft store is deployment
orchestration state (a cache derivable from the live cluster + Helm
releases), not an irreplaceable source of truth, so the data loss is
tolerable; the failure mode (a crash-looping pod on rollout) is the
concern.

## Mitigation (rollout runbook)

- **If S3 backups are configured** (`DEPLOYD_BACKUP_*`): restore the
  latest snapshot into a **fresh** data dir via the existing
  `HQL_BACKUP_RESTORE=s3:<key>` path (`store.rs:86-110`; validated by the
  `restore_from_env_var` ignore-gated test at `store.rs:439-455`). This
  reconstitutes `state_machine/db/deployd.db` from a sqlite snapshot and
  sidesteps replaying the incompatible WAL.
- **Otherwise**: wipe / reprovision the deployd hiqlite data dir on the
  `0.14` rollout. deployd re-derives its orchestration state.

## Optional durable fix (defer until scheduled)

If a persistent, migration-safe deployd store is wanted later:

- Detect an unreadable / format-incompatible store at boot and move it
  aside + reinit with a clear diagnostic, rather than crash-looping
  (the pattern axiomregent already uses with its port sidecar).
- Or document a mandatory pre-upgrade S3 snapshot + fresh-dir restore
  step in the deployd chart upgrade notes.

Either is a code/docs change to a spec-governed path
(`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/`), so it should graduate to a draft
spec when prioritized, not be bolted on here.

## Not yet verified

- The exact hiqlite version deployd ran **before** #558 (the pre-bump
  pin), and thus the precise from/to WAL format delta. The rkyv-drop
  fact comes from the `0.14` changelog investigation during #558; the
  local hiqlite source confirms `hiqlite-wal` now serializes via
  `bincode`/`serde` with no `rkyv`.
- Whether any live deployd instance currently holds pre-`0.14` state
  (project is pre-alpha, single-developer, no public releases), i.e.
  whether this is latent or immediate.

## References

- #558 (`a2235ad7`): the hiqlite `0.14` consolidation bump.
- Related MSRV fallout already fixed in the same PR: deployd Dockerfile
  `FROM rust:1.95` (`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Dockerfile:12`),
  since hiqlite `0.14` raised its MSRV.

title: chore(deps): consolidate non-spec-spine Dependabot bumps
body:
## Summary

Consolidates every open Dependabot dependency bump **except the
`spec-spine-*` crates** into one author-owned PR (Dependabot PRs run
without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so their `ai-review` / `ci-gate` fails; a
human PR gets the secrets). No product source-code changes were
required for any bump: each is a manifest version bump plus a scoped
lockfile regeneration, verified by builds and tests. The one code edit
is a build-toolchain pin bump forced by a raised MSRV (below).

### Root Cargo workspace (`crates/*`)
- **ed25519-dalek 2 → 3** (policy-kernel, factory-engine). Used API
  surface unchanged in 3.0; MSRV 1.85 already satisfied (edition 2024).
- **hiqlite ~0.13 → ~0.14** (axiomregent, orchestrator). 0.14 pins
  rusqlite ^0.40, collapsing orchestrator's `>=0.39, <0.41` range to
  `0.40` so the whole graph agrees on one rusqlite major (libsqlite3-sys
  single-`links` rule). This resolves the long-standing deferral noted
  in `orchestrator/Cargo.toml`.
- **octocrab 0.53 → 0.54** (axiomregent). Sole breaking change (typed
  `PullRequest` fields) does not apply; the client reads raw
  `serde_json::Value`.
- **jsonschema 0.46 → 0.47** (factory-engine). `validate()` unchanged.

### deployd-api-rs (isolated workspace)
- **hiqlite 0.13.2 → 0.14.0** (+ rusqlite 0.40.1, libsqlite3-sys 0.38.1).
- **Dockerfile `rust:1.88` → `rust:1.95`**: hiqlite 0.14 /
  serde_rusqlite 0.43 raised MSRV to 1.95.0. The non-Docker Rust jobs
  pass on `rust-toolchain.toml` (already 1.95.0); the Docker build
  context excludes that file, so its base image rustc had to move.

### opc src-tauri (isolated workspace, lock-only)
- **ed25519-dalek 3 / jsonschema 0.47** (transitive via path-deps) plus
  the cargo-minor-patch group (**bytes 1.12.1, cc 1.2.66**).

### stagecraft (npm)
- **recharts 2.15.4 → 3.9.2** (React 19 satisfies the peer; adds
  `react-is`; dashboard usage untouched by the 3.0 removals).
- npm-minor-patch group: **@aws-sdk/client-s3 + s3-request-presigner
  3.1082**, **@react-router/{dev,node,serve} + react-router 8.2.0**,
  **isbot 5.2.0**. Lock regenerated fresh with npm 10 / node 22.

## Superseded Dependabot PRs
Closes #546, #547, #549, #550, #551, #552, #553, #554, #555, #556, #557.

**Intentionally excluded** (per request): #545, #548
(`spec-spine-types` / `spec-spine-core` 0.10.0) — the spec-spine pin is
owned by spec 217 and moves on its own cadence. (This PR merges main's
spec-spine 0.10.0 bump from #544; it does not re-pin it.)

## Testing
- `cargo check --locked` green on all three Cargo workspaces (root,
  deployd-api-rs, opc), including after merging main's spec-spine 0.10.0.
- `cargo test -p factory-engine -p open_agentic_policy_kernel`: 295 + 68
  pass, incl. ed25519 sign/verify roundtrip, tamper-detection, and
  resign-attack cases.
- `npm ci` (npm 10 / node 22) validates the stagecraft lock clean;
  `react-router build` bundles the recharts-3 dashboard successfully.
- deployd docker build fixed by the rust:1.95 base bump (was failing on
  the 1.95.0 MSRV wall).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: dependency version bumps touch spec-owned manifests (Cargo.toml, package.json), their lockfiles, and (where a bump raises a crate's MSRV) the build-toolchain pin in platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Dockerfile, with no change to any spec's design. Editing the owning specs to satisfy the coupling gate would be a CONST-005 violation (mass spec edits whose rationale is "satisfy a gate"). This waiver is the established mechanism for Dependabot consolidation PRs (precedent #299, #385).

title: chore(deps): update hiqlite requirement from ~0.13 to ~0.14 in /crates/axiomregent
body:
Updates the requirements on [hiqlite](https://github.com/sebadob/hiqlite) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from hiqlite's releases.

v0.14.0

Breaking

NodeConfig::from_toml and NodeConfig::from_toml_table take a new secrets: Option<toml::Table> argument (after table / table_name, before the optional enc_keys). Existing callers can pass None to keep the previous behavior.

Raft Rate-Limiting

You can now rate-limit all Raft write actions. These are things like cache PUT or e.g. execute queries. This limit does not affect read actions, since they are local and do not travel through the network. With this rate-limiting, if tuned properly for your deployment, you can guarantee that you never saturate your disk, and therefore can never get in a situation where you overwhelm the cluster, no matter how high requests might spike.

Just as a very rough guideline: When you only write tiny queries that INSERT 3 columns per row, and you limit the Raft to 50.000 requests / s, your disk already writes 350+ MB/s. How you want to tune this value depends a lot on how much your server can handle and how expensive your queries are. It's impossible to provide a reasonable default value here.

Each client has its own rate-limiter. This is crucial. If the leader enforced it, all limited requests would need to travel through the network only for getting limited. This means if you have a traffic spike that your deployment cannot handle, it would still flood the network. Instead, each client enforces this locally BEFORE sending out any network requests. At the same time, this means if you limit to e.g. 100 RPS while having a 3-node cluster, it will effectively mean ~300 RPS for the whole cluster (assuming even load alancing).

You have new config values:

# To guarantee the stabiliy of your Raft cluster, you can
# rate-limit all write operations to the Raft (excluding
# management overhead). This is in request per second. It
# guarantees that the cluster can never be overwhelmed
# because maybe the disks cannot keep up. Usually, when
# this happens, you would see dropped or missing heartbeats
# and errors that the leader is down, even when the cluster
# is healthy.
# The burst can usually be 2-2x the rps.
#
# default: not set
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_RPS
rate_limit_cache_rps = 50000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_BURST
rate_limit_cache_burst = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_RPS
rate_limit_db_rps = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_BURST
rate_limit_db_burst = 200000

Learner-Only mode

Added NodeConfig::learner_only, learner_only, and HQL_LEARNER_ONLY to let newly joining nodes stay learners during startup reconciliation instead of being promoted to voting members. This makes it possible to add read-only cluster members.

New feature: in-memory-snapshots

By default, even if you set cache_storage_disk = false to keep the WAL in-memory, Cache snapshots will still be written to disk into a temp file. This means the data_dir must be writable. Snapshots are only necessary if a new node joins the Raft cluster, and then only the leader needs to stream the latest snapshot to the new node. This means in most cases, you never need them. Writing them into a temp file is the most efficient solution. However, with this feature, you can opt-in to keep snapshots in-memory as well. This will not need any disk at all (as long as you don't enable sqlite of course). This is costly, though, because you effectively double your memory requirements for each single cache entry.

Improvements for stack sizes

Quite a few tasks were pretty big and consumed a lot of space on the stack. Some even so much that tokio auto-boxed them. All of them were tuned to not throw warnings anymore. There are a few left inside openraft. To my knowledge, we cannot control these sizes indirectly with our trait impl's. This needs some further investigation.

title: chore(deps): update hiqlite requirement from ~0.13 to ~0.14 in /crates/orchestrator
body:
Updates the requirements on [hiqlite](https://github.com/sebadob/hiqlite) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from hiqlite's releases.

v0.14.0

Breaking

NodeConfig::from_toml and NodeConfig::from_toml_table take a new secrets: Option<toml::Table> argument (after table / table_name, before the optional enc_keys). Existing callers can pass None to keep the previous behavior.

Raft Rate-Limiting

You can now rate-limit all Raft write actions. These are things like cache PUT or e.g. execute queries. This limit does not affect read actions, since they are local and do not travel through the network. With this rate-limiting, if tuned properly for your deployment, you can guarantee that you never saturate your disk, and therefore can never get in a situation where you overwhelm the cluster, no matter how high requests might spike.

Just as a very rough guideline: When you only write tiny queries that INSERT 3 columns per row, and you limit the Raft to 50.000 requests / s, your disk already writes 350+ MB/s. How you want to tune this value depends a lot on how much your server can handle and how expensive your queries are. It's impossible to provide a reasonable default value here.

Each client has its own rate-limiter. This is crucial. If the leader enforced it, all limited requests would need to travel through the network only for getting limited. This means if you have a traffic spike that your deployment cannot handle, it would still flood the network. Instead, each client enforces this locally BEFORE sending out any network requests. At the same time, this means if you limit to e.g. 100 RPS while having a 3-node cluster, it will effectively mean ~300 RPS for the whole cluster (assuming even load alancing).

You have new config values:

# To guarantee the stabiliy of your Raft cluster, you can
# rate-limit all write operations to the Raft (excluding
# management overhead). This is in request per second. It
# guarantees that the cluster can never be overwhelmed
# because maybe the disks cannot keep up. Usually, when
# this happens, you would see dropped or missing heartbeats
# and errors that the leader is down, even when the cluster
# is healthy.
# The burst can usually be 2-2x the rps.
#
# default: not set
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_RPS
rate_limit_cache_rps = 50000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_BURST
rate_limit_cache_burst = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_RPS
rate_limit_db_rps = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_BURST
rate_limit_db_burst = 200000

Learner-Only mode

Added NodeConfig::learner_only, learner_only, and HQL_LEARNER_ONLY to let newly joining nodes stay learners during startup reconciliation instead of being promoted to voting members. This makes it possible to add read-only cluster members.

New feature: in-memory-snapshots

By default, even if you set cache_storage_disk = false to keep the WAL in-memory, Cache snapshots will still be written to disk into a temp file. This means the data_dir must be writable. Snapshots are only necessary if a new node joins the Raft cluster, and then only the leader needs to stream the latest snapshot to the new node. This means in most cases, you never need them. Writing them into a temp file is the most efficient solution. However, with this feature, you can opt-in to keep snapshots in-memory as well. This will not need any disk at all (as long as you don't enable sqlite of course). This is costly, though, because you effectively double your memory requirements for each single cache entry.

Improvements for stack sizes

Quite a few tasks were pretty big and consumed a lot of space on the stack. Some even so much that tokio auto-boxed them. All of them were tuned to not throw warnings anymore. There are a few left inside openraft. To my knowledge, we cannot control these sizes indirectly with our trait impl's. This needs some further investigation.

Quite a few tasks were pretty big and consumed a lot of space on the stack. Some even so much that tokio auto-boxed them. All of them were tuned to not throw warnings anymore. There are a few left inside openraft. To my knowledge, we cannot control these sizes indirectly with our trait impl's. This needs some further investigation.

Secrets from file

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from hiqlite's changelog.

v0.14.0

Raft Rate-Limiting

You can now rate-limit all Raft write actions. These are things like cache PUT or e.g. execute queries. This limit does not affect read actions, since they are local and do not travel through the network. With this rate-limiting, if tuned properly for your deployment, you can guarantee that you never saturate your disk, and therefore can never get in a situation where you overwhelm the cluster, no matter how high requests might spike.

Just as a very rough guideline: When you only write tiny queries that INSERT 3 columns per row, and you limit the Raft to 50.000 requests / s, your disk already writes 350+ MB/s. How you want to tune this value depends a lot on how much your server can handle and how expensive your queries are. It's impossible to provide a reasonable default value here.

Each client has its own rate-limiter. This is crucial. If the leader enforced it, all limited requests would need to travel through the network only for getting limited. This means if you have a traffic spike that your deployment cannot handle, it would still flood the network. Instead, each client enforces this locally BEFORE sending out any network requests. At the same time, this means if you limit to e.g. 100 RPS while having a 3-node cluster, it will effectively mean ~300 RPS for the whole cluster (assuming even load balancing).

You have new config values:

# To guarantee the stabiliy of your Raft cluster, you can
# rate-limit all write operations to the Raft (excluding
# management overhead). This is in request per second. It
# guarantees that the cluster can never be overwhelmed
# because maybe the disks cannot keep up. Usually, when
# this happens, you would see dropped or missing heartbeats
# and errors that the leader is down, even when the cluster
# is healthy.
# The burst can usually be 2-2x the rps.
#
# default: not set
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_RPS
rate_limit_cache_rps = 50000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_CACHE_BURST
rate_limit_cache_burst = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_RPS
rate_limit_db_rps = 100000
# overwritten by: HQL_RL_DB_BURST
rate_limit_db_burst = 200000

Learner-Only mode

Added NodeConfig::learner_only, learner_only, and HQL_LEARNER_ONLY to let newly joining nodes stay learners during startup reconciliation instead of being promoted to voting members. This makes it possible to add read-only cluster members.

New feature: in-memory-snapshots

  • Fix a data modeling error in the serde feature pointed out by Trevor Perrin which caused points and scalars to be serialized with length fields rather than as fixed-size 32-byte arrays. title: chore(217): bump spec-spine 0.8.0 -> 0.10.0 (CLI pin + crate deps)
body:
## What

Advance the `spec-spine` toolchain pin from **0.8.0 to 0.10.0** in lockstep across both surfaces spec 217 governs, so the installed build tool and the linked library never skew.

**CLI install pin** (installed `spec-spine-cli` version):
- `Makefile` `SPEC_SPINE_VERSION`
- 4 CI workflows that install it (`ci-crates`, `ci-featuregraph-golden`, `ci-spec-code-coupling`, `spec-conformance`)
- `make setup` / docs / rules / githook install hints (`README.md`, `docs/OVERVIEW.md`, `.claude/rules/{build-commands,governed-artifact-reads}.md`, `.claude/skills/setup/SKILL.md`, `.githooks/{pre-commit,merge-derived-index.sh}`, `website/docs/**`, stagecraft `registryReader.ts`)

**Library crate deps** (`spec-spine-core` / `spec-spine-types = 0.10.0`) in the six consumers spec 217 enumerates:
`featuregraph`, `factory-engine`, `oap-registry-enrich`, `oap-code-index-enrich`, `opc/src-tauri`, `opc-decomposition-pipeline` + regenerated `Cargo.lock` (root + opc).

Spec 217's pin section is updated to record the advance.

## Why

0.10.0 ships the library's cargo + GitHub-Actions dependency **auto-waiver**: dependabot cargo and workflow bumps self-clear without a human `Spec-Drift-Waiver`, and a `Cargo.toml` dependency bump no longer stales the codebase index (its dependency table is stripped from the hashed governance projection, mirroring `package.json`). This directly reduces OAP's recurring dependabot friction.

## Risk

Schema and grammar are **unchanged** between 0.8.0 and 0.10.0 (registry + index schema both stay `1.1.0`), so committed shards read identically. The one deterministic, one-time effect is the 0.10.0 index-hash projection recomputing every `codebase-index` `shardHash` once with **content unchanged** (49 shards; verified `shardHash`-only, same class as the spec 188 config-hash rehome). The `Cargo.toml` dep bumps are invisible to the index content hash (spec 030 stripped-projection, confirmed locally).

## Verification (local, on 0.10.0)

- `cargo build --workspace` (root) + `cargo build` (opc standalone) — both clean
- `cargo test` on the 5 spec-spine-linked crates — pass
- `spec-spine compile` (231 specs, 0 warnings) + `spec-spine index` (fresh, 0 error diagnostics)
- `featuregraph` golden test — pass; golden file unchanged
- `spec-spine index check` — fresh; only the `217` registry shard changed (spec 222 freshness satisfied)
- Coupling gate: 20 mechanical violations, all cleared by the waiver below (exit 0)

## Note

The stagecraft `*.generated.json` public-page projections are intentionally **not** regenerated here: they are a deploy-time refresh with no PR-time gate and are already 10 spec-editing commits behind, so regenerating in this pin-bump PR would mix in unrelated drift. They refresh on the next stagecraft deploy (spec 228).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Mechanical spec-spine toolchain pin bump 0.8.0 -> 0.10.0 (CLI install pin + spec-spine-core/types library crate deps). No spec design changes; the pin is narratively owned by spec 217, whose pin section is updated here. All flagged paths are version-string / dependency-line edits, plus the deterministic 0.10.0 index shardHash rechurn. Verified green: full root workspace + opc desktop build, spec-spine-linked crate tests, registry+index recompile (shardHash-only churn), featuregraph golden.

title: feat(210): Build Spec agentic_posture field + certificate binding + SBOM cross-check verifier
body:
## Summary

Refines spec 210 from sketch to implementation-ready and lands FR-001 through FR-004 in one OAP-side change: a produced application's agentic surface becomes a declared, falsifiable contract fact (Least Agency applied to outputs).

- **FR-001**: `agentic_posture: none | declared | governed` (with enumerated surfaces; governed surfaces carry an inline governance envelope) added to `build-spec.schema.yaml` (1.1.0 -> 1.2.0) and the Rust twin `factory-contracts::build_spec`, with `AgenticPosture::validate`.
- **FR-002**: the posture is bound into the governance certificate as the optional `agenticPostureBinding` block (cert **1.8.0 -> 1.9.0**, inside the hash + signature, skip-when-absent), read off the frozen Build Spec by the `build-certificate` emitter. `defaulted: true` distinguishes "authored none" from "nobody asked".
- **FR-003**: `verify-certificate` rejects a self-inconsistent binding and, under `--sbom-dir`, cross-checks a `none` posture against the produced app's CycloneDX BOM. A watchlisted agent/LLM SDK dependency contradicts the declaration (exit 1, names the package). The watchlist is versioned data at `standards/schemas/factory/agentic-sdk-watchlist.yaml`, embedded into the verifier. A watchlist miss is a stated residual (absence of a match is not proof of absence of agency).
- **FR-004**: a `governed` surface's inline envelope is shape-validated against the spec 198 `GovernanceEnvelope`.

## Compatibility

Additive and byte-compatible when absent: a posture-free certificate (including the delivered spec 220 tenant cert, which is emitted by the separately published `tenant-emit` and unaffected by this change) is byte-identical and still verifies. A regression test asserts this.

## Tests

- `factory-contracts`: posture type + `validate` (none / declared / governed, envelope shape, round-trip, version-pin 1.2.0).
- `factory-engine` lib: cert binding round-trip + tamper + the 220-regression byte-compat guard; internal-consistency verify; SBOM cross-check + watchlist matcher.
- `spec_210_agentic_posture.rs` (end-to-end via the real `build-certificate` / `verify-certificate` binaries): AC-2 (authored recorded / omitted field defaulted-none), AC-3 (none + `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gives exit 1 naming the package; clean BOM passes; declared + SDK passes).
- featuregraph golden regenerated (210 draft -> approved); clippy clean under the CI-parity invocation.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: mechanical compile-fix. `crates/factory-contracts/src/adapter_registry.rs` and `crates/factory-engine/src/policy_shard.rs` each gain a single `agentic_posture: None` line in a `#[cfg(test)]` BuildSpec helper literal, forced by the additive optional field on `BuildSpec` (FR-001). Those files are owned by the adapter-registry / policy-shard specs (074/197/198/... and 075/197/202/...); the edit is a Rust exhaustive-struct-literal requirement, not a semantic change to any of their concerns, so no spec edit is warranted and spec 210 does not claim ownership.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: reverse-coupling over-fire. `specs/212-factory-schema-lockstep-ci/spec.md` changes only to bump `pinned_ref` (427f499 -> a87daf6), which is spec 212's own FR-007 operational config, done here because the lockstep reads the pin from the PR head tree. The gate flags it against spec 214 solely because 214 carries a non-owning `references` edge (role `lockstep-philosophy-precedent`) at 212's spec.md; that citation does not make 214 an owner of 212's pin, so no 214 edit is warranted.

## Cross-repo mirror (resolved)

`build-spec.schema.yaml` is a Floor-mode file in the spec 212 `factory-schema-lockstep` set, so OAP cannot carry `agentic_posture` unless the upstream `factory` contract mirrors it. That mirror landed: `stagecraft-ing/factory-encore#21` adds the identical `agentic_posture` object + `schema_version` bump (all checks green, merged), and this PR's second commit bumps spec 212's `pinned_ref` to the merged upstream commit `a87daf6`. Floor parity was re-verified locally with the `factory-schema-lockstep` tool (holds on every mode), so the lockstep CI lane is expected green.

title: feat(227): surface cron capability in create-project (spec 230 cron stage)
body:
## What

The OAP-side companion to **factory-encore PR #20** (the `cron` scheduler module, factory-encore spec 009 / OAP spec 230). Wires the create-project form to surface `cron` as a first-class Application feature. This is the cron-capability stage of spec 227 (§6).

## Changes

- **`moduleCatalog.ts`**: `cron` gains a `PRESENTATION` overlay entry (`displayName: "Cron Scheduler"`, `category: "Application"`) so it renders in the Application-features section instead of falling to the "Other" fallback. Its `description`/`requires`/`status` derive from the admitted manifest (`requires: ["data-postgres"]`, `optionalPeers: ["data-redis"]`).
- **`app.projects.new.tsx`**: selecting cron pulls `data-postgres` into the selection via `applyModuleToggle`, but infra modules are not rendered feature checkboxes (and disabled/auto checkboxes do not submit), so the requirement would be dropped and the generator would reject the cron install. The form now emits the **transitive infra-requires closure** as hidden `modules` inputs (the same closure-as-hidden-inputs pattern the `/connectivity` gateway already uses), so the scaffold composes `data-postgres` ahead of `cron`.
- **Scale tiers.** The **Small** (Postgres atomic-claim lock) tier is active. The large-scale Redis distributed lock rides `REDIS_URL`, provisioned by the Redis Infrastructure resource, which is **Stage 4** (the Infrastructure Redis row stays "Planned"). cron's manifest description states both tiers honestly.

## Scope / sequencing

- **End-to-end composition activates once factory-encore #20 merges and the org substrate admits the cron manifest** (the create-project catalog derives from the substrate, so cron appears in the picker only after admission). Before then the form degrades cleanly (cron simply absent from the catalog).
- `deploy.ts` and the Redis end-to-end path remain **Stage 4**. `227` `implementation:` stays `pending`.

## Validation

title: docs(230): tenant self-hosted cron via in-app scheduler (design spec)
body:
## Summary

Design spec (like 229 for auth) for **tenant self-hosted cron**. Encore's `CronJob` is a no-op on self-hosted targets (no Encore Cloud scheduler), so every tenant `CronJob` deployed via deployd is silent today. Spec 230 gives each tenant app working self-hosted cron via an **in-app scheduler** baked into the generated Encore app, with **no per-tenant Kubernetes CronJob**.

This is **distinct from spec 224** (stagecraft's OWN control-plane sweepers, which correctly stay on K8s CronJobs). Tenant apps cannot be required to provision K8s CronJobs, so tenant cron runs in-app.

## The decided lock/scale model

- Cron **always requires `data-postgres`** (schedule store + small-scale Postgres atomic-claim lock).
- `data-redis` is an **optional peer** for the **large-scale** distributed lock (production/enterprise-grade, multi-replica).
- The scheduler **auto-detects `REDIS_URL`** to pick the backend, mirroring the existing `data-redis` idiom. Tenant chooses **Small (Postgres)** or **Large (Postgres + Redis)** in create-project.

Postgres is already default-on and Redis already opt-in + provisionable via the merged `previewRedis` path (spec 227), so this reuses existing provisioning.

## Shape

- New factory-encore `cron` adapter module: `requires: [data-postgres]`, `optionalPeers: [data-redis]`, ships the scheduler service (`~/DevExperiment/encore-cron-scheduler-ts`: schedule table + `cron-parser` register + polling daemon + atomic claim + fire).
- Surfaced on the create-project **Infra axis** (spec 227), the third axis alongside topology and auth (spec 229).

## Scope

Design spec only. The factory-encore module implementation and the create-project form wiring land in follow-on PRs (a factory-encore spec + a spec-227 stage). The only in-PR code delta is the featuregraph golden node (`extends 034`).

## Evidence

title: docs(229): auth-driver model correction (mock|rauthy; IdPs via Rauthy)
body:
## Summary

Amendment spec **229** records a 2026-07-08 design decision and amends the auth-driver registry triplet (**148/149/150**) to match it, without changing the registry pattern or spec 147's proving-ground.

**The model:** app-level `AUTH_DRIVER` has exactly two values, `mock` (zero-dependency dev/test identity) and `rauthy` (the single production driver). Every real IdP (GitHub, Google, Auth0, Entra ID, and SAML-requiring tenants) federates *inside* Rauthy as an upstream provider, not as a peer `AUTH_DRIVER` member. SAML needs no OAP driver and no Rauthy SAML code (Rauthy has zero SAML): SAML tenants enter Rauthy as a `Custom`/`Google` OIDC upstream via Google Workspace SSO with custom OIDC profiles (Google, Dec 2024 open beta).

## Changes

- **148** (registry): `default: rauthy-oidc` -> `rauthy`; membership clarified to `mock|rauthy`; upstream federation stated as Rauthy-internal.
- **149** (SAML capability): relabeled as a spec-kind-grammar fixture (OAP ships no standalone SAML driver).
- **150** (example profile): reaffirmed as a synthetic proving-ground profile; `selects:` unchanged.
- **229** (new): the amendment spec of record.

Amend-and-relabel, **not** supersession, so 149/150 stay live V-013/14/15/17 fixtures for spec 147.

title: fix(227): single substrate load per create + prototype-safe catalog
body:
## What

The four remaining #533 ai-review findings the Stage 1 PR adjudicated
non-blocking, as a focused follow-up ahead of the Stage 2 form reframe.

## Changes

- **Single substrate load per create (#1).** `createFactoryProject` loaded the
  org substrate twice: `loadModuleCatalogForOrg` (via `loadOrgView`) and
  `loadFactoryAdapter` (via `loadSubstrateForOrg`). It now loads one `OrgView`,
  derives the catalog via a new exported `deriveModuleCatalogFromView`, and
  threads that substrate into `loadFactoryAdapter` (new optional
  `preloadedSubstrate` param). The per-org cache (`moduleCatalogCache.ts`) now
  serves only the read endpoint / page loader. Net effect is also a strict
  admission improvement on create: the catalog is derived from a fresh
  `OrgView`, not the up-to-60s cache, while `isFactoryAdmitted` stays fresh.
- **Prototype-safe presentation lookup (#2).** The `PRESENTATION` overlay in the
  pure `moduleCatalog.ts` is a `Map`, so an externally-authored module named
  `__proto__`/`constructor` misses cleanly (`.get` returns undefined) rather
  than resolving to a truthy prototype value that left `displayName`/`category`
  undefined. Regression test added.
- **stagecraft/CLAUDE.md (#4).** The `moduleCatalog.ts` description is refreshed
  to the Stage 1 derived API (the stale `MODULE_CATALOG`/`INSTALL_ORDER`
  listing). Spec 227 additively co-authors that doc file (138 already claims it).

## Finding #3 re-examined, not "fixed"

The #533 review called the `extrasFor` exact-order test fragile. The local
adversarial review re-derived `deriveInstallOrder` and confirmed the install
order is a **deterministic** alphabetical-within-dependency-level contract, so
the exact assertion is correct and worth pinning. I kept it (with a comment
explaining the guarantee) rather than loosening it.

## Governance

Refinements to already-claimed spec-227 paths (create.ts, both `moduleCatalog.ts`,
scaffold test) plus an additive `extends 138` claim on `stagecraft/CLAUDE.md`.
No new `establishes:`; `implementation:` stays `pending`.

## Testing

- stagecraft `vitest`: 42 pass (scaffold incl. the new prototype-safe test +
  the retained exact-order test; `moduleCatalogCache`; `module-selection`).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean on every touched file (11 remaining errors are
  pre-existing stale `encore.gen` for `monitor`/`site`; CI regenerates codegen).
- coupling gate: OK, 7 paths, no drift.

Note: a direct unit test for the new `deriveModuleCatalogFromView` seam is
deferred, tracked in the spec log: it is exported from an Encore endpoint module
so it needs the `encore test` runtime lane (plain vitest cannot load it); the
extraction is behavior-preserving and stays transitively covered by
`deriveModuleCatalog`'s pure tests.

title: fix(227): transitive module selection + cached per-org catalog
body:
## What

Pulls the two Stage-2-deferred ai-review nits from #533 forward into a
standalone spec-227 PR, ahead of the larger form reframe (Stage 2).

## Changes

- **Transitive module selection.** New pure, tested `applyModuleToggle`
  (`web/app/lib/module-selection.ts`) resolves the `requires` DAG in both
  directions. Unchecking now drops the full dependent closure (the flagged
  #533 bug: the prior `m.requires.includes(id)` pass only removed direct
  dependents, so an `A -> B -> C` chain left `A` checked after unchecking
  `C`). Checking pulls the full requires closure, which also fixes a latent
  server-side under-install: `perRequestScaffold` installs
  `selectedModules` verbatim with no closure expansion, so the old
  direct-only toggle silently under-installed >1-hop chains. The route's
  `toggleModule` now delegates to the helper.
- **Per-org catalog cache.** `loadModuleCatalogForOrg` gains a 60s per-org
  cache (`api/factory/moduleCatalogCache.ts`, pure module mirroring the
  `extractionPolicy.ts` idiom), removing the substrate load + admission
  check that ran on every create POST. Signature unchanged, so `create.ts`
  is untouched; the `GET /api/factory/module-catalog` endpoint benefits too.

## Governance

Spec 227 `establishes:` the four net-new files (2 source + 2 test). Both
touched pre-existing paths were already claimed by 227 (establishes

`implementation:` stays `pending` (Stage 2 form reframe and Stage 4 wiring

title: feat(227): derive create-project module catalog from the adapter manifest (stage 1)
body:
## What

Stage 1 of spec **227-create-project-infra-config-projection** (FR-001, SC-001): replace the two hand-mirrored `MODULE_CATALOG` copies (frontend route const + backend `moduleCatalog.ts`) with a runtime derivation from the adapter's substrate module manifests, so the drift-prone module prose (notably the retired `data-redis` rate-limit-backend false label) can no longer diverge from the adapter by construction.

## Changes

- **`api/projects/scaffold/moduleCatalog.ts`** is now **pure** (no Encore imports): `deriveModuleCatalog(rows)` maps each module `manifest.json` to a descriptor; `deriveInstallOrder` topo-sorts over `requires` (security-core before api-gateway); `isKnownModule`/`extrasFor` take the derived catalog. `id`/`description`/`requires`/`conflicts`/`status` derive from the manifest; a thin **transitional** `PRESENTATION` overlay supplies `displayName`/`category` (no manifest source), which Stage 2's re-sectioning reworks.
- **New `api/factory/moduleCatalog.ts`**: `loadModuleCatalogForOrg` + admission-gated `GET /api/factory/module-catalog`, reusing `browse.ts`'s `loadOrgView`/`servableRows` (single admission gate). Module manifests land in the catch-all `reference-data` kind, so they're selected by path regex `^adapters/*/modules/*/manifest.json$`.
- **`create.ts`** loads the derived catalog per-org and threads it through scaffold; the **frontend route** deletes its hand-copy const and consumes the endpoint via its loader (a rejected/empty fetch degrades to an **empty picker, not a 500**).

## Scope boundary

`PROFILE_MODULES`/`PRESETS` profile defaults and the "auto for Internal" surfacing are **Stage 2** (the form reframe) — deferred and noted in-code. The adapter manifest's `scaffold.profiles[].modules` (`internal` ships `user-management`) drifts from the current empty `PROFILE_MODULES`, but the runtime dedupe in `perRequestScaffold.readInstalledModules` keeps composition correct, so **behavior is unchanged** here. The false `data-redis` label is corrected by factory-encore **008** at the manifest source; Stage 1 removes the hand-copy so stagecraft can't drift from it.

## Governance

Promotes spec 227 `references:` to authoritative relationships: `establishes` the new endpoint; `extends 138` (create/scaffold surface), `extends 199` (the thin-consumer browser whose admission gate the endpoint reuses), and `extends 112` (scaffold test files).

## Gates (local)

- `tsc --noEmit`: **clean on every touched file** (the 11 remaining errors are pre-existing stale `encore.gen` for the unrelated `monitor`/`site` services; CI regenerates codegen)
