title: docs(227): create-project as an Encore infra-config projection (design spec)
body:
## Summary

Design/contract spec (`227`) that reframes the stagecraft **Create New Project** surface as a projection of vocabulary that already exists, replacing a hand-mirrored, drifted module catalog.

**Why it's needed:** the catalog is hardcoded in two independently-maintained copies (`app.projects.new.tsx`, `moduleCatalog.ts`) that have diverged and gone stale. They still offer a "Redis" module whose factory-encore source is an inert marker with a false label (it claims a Redis rate-limit backend that does not exist; the baseline limiter is Postgres). One checkbox UI conflates three kinds of thing (inert markers, base-app knobs, one real feature module), and the "Variant" selector fuses factory-encore's two orthogonal axes and drops the default profile.

## What this spec commits to

- **Derived catalog:** feature modules from the adapter manifest, infrastructure resources projected from the app's committed `apps/api/infra.config.json` (Encore `infra.schema.json`). Eliminates both hardcoded copies (constitution Principle II).
- **Two-axis selector:** auth `{public, internal}` plus topology `{single, dual}`. `minimal` is not offered at the OAP surface.
- **Infrastructure section:** read-only projection of the baked topology; Postgres default-on, Redis opt-in.
- **Option A (topology parity):** the `infra.config.json` topology is read-only across environments; per-environment hosts/credentials/secrets are runtime env via GitHub Environments (dev owned by OAP/deployd; staging/prod by the tenant). One portable image; no per-environment config files.
- **deployd `previewRedis`:** a dev-only Redis provisioning path mirroring `previewDatabase`.

## Coupling posture

Design-only, following the 226 precedent: no code path is claimed via `establishes:`; governed paths sit under `references:`; the only in-PR code change is the featuregraph golden node (`extends: 034`). Implementation is staged across follow-on PRs (catalog derivation, form reframe, deployd previewRedis).

## Validation

- `spec-spine compile`: clean (228 specs, 0 warnings)
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- spec-code coupling gate: exit 0

## Companion

factory-encore spec `008-data-redis-promotion-dual-composition` owns the adapter-side changes (data-redis promotion, dual module composition, CORS knob). Design record: `docs/analysis/create-project-encore-config-reframe.md`.

title: chore(213,deps): bump oap-build.yml seed actions (checkout v7, docker/login v4.4.0)
body:
## What

SHA-pins / bumps the GitHub Actions in the workflows that `repoInit.ts` seeds into every produced tenant repo:

- `oap-build.yml`: `actions/checkout` `df4cb1c` (v6) → `9c091bb` (v7.0.0), both occurrences (detect + build jobs); `docker/login-action` `650006c` (v4) → `af1e73f` (v4.4.0)
- `oap-verify.yml`: `actions/checkout@v4` (a mutable floating tag) → the same immutable `9c091bb` (v7.0.0) SHA pin

After this, every seeded action ref in `repoInit.ts` is SHA-pinned to a full commit SHA (`setup-node@v6` was already pinned and current).

## Why here, not in the produced repo

Dependabot raised the `oap-build.yml` bumps on a produced tenant repo (`stagecraft-ing/spec220-ac2-single-4` #1 and #2), but that repo is a generated artifact. The workflows are authored by `platform/services/stagecraft/api/github/repoInit.ts`, so fixing the seed makes every future scaffold born with current, immutable pins. The `oap-verify.yml` floating-tag pin was surfaced by the AI review on this PR (same file, same hardening intent).

title: fix(220): harden the Encore CLI download (timeout, cleanup, provenance)
body:
Follow-up to #524 addressing its AI review. Rebased onto `main` after #524 merged: the node-fetch+tar base landed in #524 (`c8a60621`), so this PR now carries only the hardening delta on top (a single commit touching `templateCache.ts`).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `templateCache.ts` is a scaffold-warmup path that specs 138/140/220 `extends`. This change is a pure robustness hardening (fetch timeout, always-clean tarball, defensive version-read warning, provenance/integrity doc-comments); it does not alter any owning spec's contract (the warmup still provisions the same pinned Encore CLI, and spec 220's emit+verify cert chain is unchanged), so no authoring spec edit is warranted. The spec.md attempt-7 note that previously satisfied the gate on this branch landed in `main` via #524.

## Applied (verified-real findings)
- **Fetch timeout** (Sec 1): `AbortController` + 300s timeout so a stalled CDN cannot hang the warmup pod.
- **`rm` in `finally`** (Perf 1): the ~160MB tarball is always cleaned off the PVC, including on a fetch/extract failure.
- **Version-read warning** (Bug 2, defensive): `resolveEncoreCliVersion` now warns instead of silently falling through, so a stale/mismatched pin is diagnosable.
- **Provenance + integrity docs** (Sec 4 / Sec 2): the comment documents the CloudFront URL source (Encore's own install.sh), the verified flat layout, and the TLS-only integrity posture.

## Refuted (verified, no change)
- **Bug 1 (nested tarball layout / `--strip-components`)**: re-verified twice; the tarball is flat-rooted (`./bin/encore` at the archive root), so `tar -C installRoot` already lands `installRoot/bin/encore`.
- **Bug 2 ordering**: `ensureEncoreCli` runs *after* `ensureTemplateCache` in `runWarmup`, so the version read is never pre-cache.
- **Sec 3 (version injection)**: the reviewer agrees the `/(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)/` extraction is safe.

## Deferred (documented)
- **Checksum verification** (Sec 2): Encore's own installer does not checksum, and Encore publishes no per-release SHA-256 at a stable URL to verify against; TLS to the CDN is the baseline. Documented in-code as the deferral rationale rather than inventing a check against a nonexistent source.

Typecheck clean; coupling gate satisfied via the waiver above.

title: fix(220): provision the Encore CLI via node fetch + tar (no curl in the stagecraft pod)
body:
The first live re-scaffold after #519 merged failed at `regenerateProducedClient` with `npm run gen:client exited 127: sh: 1: encore: not found`, orphaning the job before push.

## Root cause (a bug in the #519 Option C code)
`ensureEncoreCli` provisioned the CLI with `curl -fsSL https://encore.dev/install.sh | bash`, but the stagecraft runtime image is slim and ships **no curl/wget**. The missing-curl failure was **masked**: a `curl | bash` pipeline exits with bash's status (0 on empty stdin), not curl's, so the warmup logged `encore CLI: ready` and wrote the idempotency marker while the binary was never installed. Confirmed on the pod: `.encore/bin/` absent, `command -v curl` → none; `bash`, `node v22`, `tar`, `gzip` present.

## Fix
Download the pinned release tarball (`https://d2f391esomvqpi.cloudfront.net/encore-<version>-linux_amd64.tar.gz`) with node's global `fetch`, streamed to disk (avoids buffering ~160MB), and extract with `tar`. **Verify `encoreBin` exists before writing the marker** so a partial/failed install can never masquerade as ready (the guard the `curl | bash` recipe lacked). Arch mapped from `process.arch`.

Everything else in the Option C path validated in-cluster on the #519 deploy (caches refreshed to the merged SHAs, all prebuilds published) — this is the one provisioning-mechanism defect. Typecheck clean, coupling gate clean.

After merge: redeploy stagecraft → warmup re-provisions the CLI (correctly this time) → re-scaffold Single internal → verify the whole born-with ci-gate. (An empty orphan repo `spec220-ac2-single-4` from the failed attempt needs reclaiming.)

title: feat(220): regenerate born-with typed client + close AC-2 cert chain (tenant-tail 0.3.0)
body:
Closes the two born-with blockers the live AC-2 run surfaced, so a re-scaffolded produced app runs its whole ci-gate green (not just the cert chain).

## Cert chain (#8) — tenant-tail 0.3.0 seal-by-default
tenant-tail 0.3.0 inverted its default to **seal-required**, so `verify-certificate` rejects the unsealed-by-design tenant cert. This spec amends **AC-2 / AC-5 / FR-004 / Out-of-scope** to the 0.3.0 contract (`--allow-unsealed` opt-out) and records the live-attempt log. It is a faithful contract-sync: the tenant cert is genuinely unsealed (AC-5, Out-of-scope), so accepting it with `--allow-unsealed` aligns the ACs with both the tool's deliberate hardening and the spec's own model. The born-with verify step passes `--allow-unsealed` in **stagecraft-ing/template-encore** (paired PR).

## Typed client (#9, Option C) — regenerate at scaffold time
A profile that composes `user-management` ships a client missing the `user_management` namespace, failing the produced app's own `Typed client up-to-date` gate. The scaffold runs the generator under `NO_INSTALL` and cannot run `encore gen client` offline, so:

- `templateCache.ts` `ensureEncoreCli` provisions the pinned Encore CLI into the warmup PVC (official install.sh, egress over the NetworkPolicy's general-HTTPS rule; version read from the template's `encore.dev` pin so the scaffold-time client matches the CI's regen).
- `perRequestScaffold.ts` `regenerateProducedClient` runs `npm install` + `npm run gen:client` per `apps/api` with the pinned CLI on PATH, over the FINAL composed graph, before the index regen.
- `create.ts` wires the step in; spec 220 extends the two spec-112 scaffold files and establishes the new unit test in its relationship graph.

Empirically validated locally: `encore gen client` runs headless (no auth), produces the correct client. New unit tests (`regenerateProducedClient.test.ts`) pass; coupling gate clean.

## Landing order
Merge **template-encore** (`fix/born-with-unsealed-verify-and-cli-pin`) first (its verify step + `encore-install` pin ride into the produced app at scaffold time), then this PR, then redeploy stagecraft and re-scaffold to verify AC-2 green. **factory-encore** (`fix/setup-app-gen-client-path`) is an off-critical-path latent-bug cleanup.

title: docs(226): address #516 AI-review comments (contract precision)
body:
Second review round on spec 226, following #515 (base spec) and #516 (round-1 hardening), both merged. Amends the design-only spec in place with the AI review of #516; all findings are contract-precision tightenings (no new architectural surface).

## Resolved

- **FR-009 crash window fully closed** — intent is written **in the same transaction** as the delete (the in-tx `project.delete` audit row commits atomically), not merely "immediately after"; only best-effort outcomes can be lost, and those are recoverable.
- **FR-007a / FR-008 delete-once is idempotency, not atomicity** — the empty-namespace check need not be atomic; namespace DELETE is idempotent (404 -> success), so a racing double-delete is benign and no distributed lock is required. Dropped the "exactly once" over-claim.
- **FR-010 org-scope reaffirmed (IDOR)** — the existing `(id, orgId = auth.orgId)` scope bounds all three toggle legs; `project:delete` is evaluated org-scoped, never as a global "admin somewhere" check, so a repo/namespace in another org is never acted on.
- **FR-004 immutability at the DB layer** — `origin` is write-once via a DB-level trigger, not application code alone, so an ad-hoc migration or hotfix cannot relabel a row and bypass the provenance gate.
- **FR-011 exact token match** — the typed confirmation MUST be exact, case-sensitive string equality against the project slug (never substring / case-insensitive).
- **FR-006 timeout ceiling** — per-call (<= 30s) and total (<= 120s) bounds so best-effort cannot block indefinitely on a hung deployd; the capability-probe result MAY be cached.

Recorded in a `Review follow-ups (AI review of #516)` section. Refuted / no-change: the "permanent Review-follow-ups section" style note (spec-lint accepts it; spec 225 uses the identical pattern).

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 227 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden`: pass
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (OK: 1 path, no drift)
- No em dashes; FR/SC cross-references intact

title: docs(226): address #515 AI-review comments (teardown hardening)
body:
Follow-up to #515 (spec 226 landed there). Amends spec 226 in place with the AI review's design points, mirroring the `#509 -> #510` pattern (land the spec, address review comments in a follow-up PR). Design-only; the sole in-PR code change is the featuregraph golden (the new `depends_on: 137` edge), claimed via `extends: 034`.

## Contract tightenings (rigor fixes)

- **FR-004** `project_repos.origin` is now MUST-**immutable** after creation, so no path can relabel an `imported` repo `factory-created` and bypass the provenance gate.
- **FR-010 / FR-011** authorization made explicit (destructive toggles inherit the base `project:delete` admin/owner gate; no new tier invented) and the typed confirmation for `deleteNamespaces` promoted **SHOULD -> MUST**, enforced at the API boundary (not UI-only).
- **FR-009** records the *requested* toggles as intent at commit, then per-resource outcomes as each leg settles, closing the crash window between the DB commit and the outcome write.
- **FR-003** takes the pre-transaction snapshot only when at least one toggle is set (toggle-free delete pays nothing).
- `depends_on += 137-tenant-environment-access-gates` (co-author of `uninstall_with_gate`, which FR-006 routes through).

## Architectural decisions (delegated on this PR)

- **Namespace-delete ordering -> deployd-side empty-namespace check** (FR-007a / FR-008). deployd, not stagecraft, decides a namespace is safe to delete (only when no deployd-managed release remains in it). This dissolves the concurrent-teardown "who is last?" race and makes partial failure correct: a failed/racing sibling leaves the namespace non-empty, so it is not deleted. stagecraft just sets the flag on every teardown; deployd deletes exactly once.
- **Teardown execution -> synchronous, bounded-concurrent** (FR-006); async `202` is a compatible future change if env counts grow.
- **PR-ordering enforcement -> runtime capability probe** of deployd, so an older deployd disables the `deleteNamespaces` checkbox rather than silently no-opping.

New success criteria SC-007 (authorization), SC-008 (typed confirmation enforced server-side), SC-009 (empty-check ordering under failure + concurrency). All dispositions recorded in a `## Review follow-ups (AI review of #515)` section.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 227 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden`: pass
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (OK: 2 paths, no drift)

title: docs(226): complete project teardown spec (3 opt-in delete toggles)
body:
## Summary

`deleteProject` today is a DB + object-storage delete only. It silently orphans two real resources:

- the **GitHub repository** (it drops the `project_repos` link row but never deletes the repo), and
- any **live Kubernetes deployment** (CASCADE removes the `environments` rows, but nothing calls deployd's teardown, so the helm release and tenant namespace linger).

Spec 226 makes teardown complete via three opt-in, **default-off** destructive toggles on the delete request, each mapped to one destroyed resource and each independently opt-in because all three are irreversible at escalating blast radius:

| Toggle | Destroyed resource | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| `deleteRepo` | GitHub repository (provenance-gated to repos OAP created) | `deleteGithubRepo` |
| `destroyDeployments` | helm release(s) across environments | `destroyPreviewDeployment` -> deployd `delete_deployment` |
| `deleteNamespaces` | tenant namespace(s) + PVCs | new deployd namespace-delete capability |

Every toggle runs after the DB commit and is best-effort (mirroring the existing storage sweep); teardown targets are snapshotted before the delete transaction. Toggle 3 promotes spec 225's deferred "Namespace deletion on teardown" item into a first-class, gated contract.

**Design-only PR.** No runtime code ships here; the sole in-PR code change is the featuregraph golden node (`extends` 034). Implementation lands as two follow-on PRs (PR A: stagecraft flags + `project_repos.origin` provenance + repo/deployment legs; PR B: deployd namespace-delete capability, the delivery of spec 225's deferred item), each promoting the referenced code paths to authoritative relationships.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 227 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden`: pass
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (OK: 2 paths, no drift)
- Local adversarial review (docs-accuracy warm finder + cold consistency finder): 8 confirmed findings, all fixed pre-commit. The spec's factual claims about `deleteProject`, `deleteGithubRepo`, `destroyPreviewDeployment`, deployd `delete_deployment`, `is_valid_tenant_namespace`, `preview_database`, and the `project_repos` schema were verified against the code.

title: fix(225,deployd): sanitize untrusted RBAC-error text in audit events
body:
## Summary

Post-delivery hygiene follow-up to #513 (FR-007 teardown self-provision), addressing the non-blocking nits from that PR's automated review.

- **Event-detail sanitization.** `sanitize_event_detail` flattens control characters and caps length on the untrusted error cause (`kube::Error::to_string()`, which can embed an API response body) before it lands in the append-only event store, on **both** the deploy and teardown RBAC-failure paths. This prevents an API error body from injecting newlines (splitting an audit-log line) or unbounded content into a deployment's audit trail.
- **63-char boundary test** for `is_valid_tenant_namespace` (the max DNS-1123 label length is accepted, guarding the `> 63` bound against an off-by-one drift).
- **Spec 225** records the delivered hygiene items and the deferred ones with rationale.

### Deferred (tracked in spec 225, not in this PR)

- **Shared kube `Client` in `AppState`** — trades the deliberate lazy/probe pattern (tolerates booting without cluster access) for startup cluster coupling; deletes are not latency-sensitive.
- **Namespace deletion on teardown** — a teardown-semantics / blast-radius change that warrants its own decision.
- **TOCTOU error variant** — cosmetic (best-effort teardown proceeds either way); distinguishing it would complicate the shared create helper the deploy path also uses.

## Testing

- `cargo test` (deployd-api-rs): 61 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (S3-gated)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate OK (3 paths, no drift), index regenerated

Depends on #513 (merged): spec 225's authority over `rbac.rs` / `routes.rs` and the FR-007 code both land there.

title: feat(225,deployd): self-provision RBAC on the teardown path (FR-007)
body:
## Summary

Delivers spec 225 FR-007, the staged teardown-path self-provision. Once the cluster-wide workloads fallback is dropped (`rbac.selfProvision: true`), a namespace created before the flip and never redeployed has no `deployd-controller-workloads` RoleBinding, so its `helm uninstall` fails `Forbidden` and the best-effort delete swallows it, orphaning the namespace's k8s resources. `delete_deployment` now provisions the RoleBinding before uninstall so the first delete tears the namespace down cleanly.

Design, kept honest against the deploy path:

- **Existing-namespace-only.** The teardown variant never recreates a namespace that is already gone (that would orphan an empty namespace + RoleBinding, the very leak this closes).
- **Reserved-namespace guard.** The RBAC write is gated on `is_valid_tenant_namespace` (the same guard `create_deployment` applies). The delete path derives the namespace from the recorded column or the `app_id-env_id` fallback and the chart `bind` grant is cluster-wide, so a legacy row resolving to `kube-system` must not receive a deployd RoleBinding.
- **Best-effort.** A failure is logged and recorded as an `rbac_warning` event; the delete stays idempotent, matching the uninstall it precedes.

Spec 225: FR-007 moved from staged to delivered (Edge Cases, Cutover, Acceptance Scenario 6, Review follow-up updated). Frontmatter now authoritatively claims `rbac.rs` (establishes) and `routes.rs` (extends), retiring #503's Spec-Drift-Waiver on the mechanism code.

Follows the spec-225 chain: #503 (mechanism), #509 (chart flip), #510 (review follow-ups), this (FR-007 code follow-up).

## Testing

- `cargo test` (deployd-api-rs): 58 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (S3-gated)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate OK (3 paths, no drift), index regenerated
- `spec-lint`: clean
- featuregraph golden: passes

Note: this is code + spec, so unlike the #509 chart-only flip it needs a deployd-api-rs image rebuild + CD deploy to take effect on the cluster. No live-cluster action is implied by merging alone.

title: fix(220,112): bump stagecraft base to node:22-trixie-slim for glibc 2.39
body:
## What

Bump the stagecraft runtime base image from `node:22-slim` (Debian bookworm, glibc 2.36) to `node:22-trixie-slim` (Debian 13, glibc 2.41).

## Why

The spec 112 regenerate-index step (#504) runs the produced app's **pinned** `@spec-spine/cli-linux-x64` inside the stagecraft container at scaffold time, so commit #1 of a scaffolded tenant ships a fresh, committed `.derived` index (spec 220 AC-2 born-green). Born-with fidelity requires the produced app's own pinned binary, so we cannot substitute stagecraft's host `spec-spine`.

That npm binary is built on `ubuntu-latest` (glibc 2.39), and spec-spine ships glibc-only linux binaries by design (spec 007; musl deliberately refused). On the old bookworm base (glibc 2.36) it aborts:

```
@spec-spine/cli-linux-x64/bin/spec-spine:
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.39' not found
```

which halted the AC-2 re-scaffold. The 0.10.0 dependency-chain rollout (tenant-emit / tenant-tail / template-encore / factory-encore) does **not** resolve this: every spec-spine version's linux binary carries the same 2.39 floor because the release build runner (`release.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) is unchanged across 0.8 to 0.10.

trixie's glibc 2.41 clears the 2.39 floor and is forward-compatible for the two Rust helpers baked into the base (their glibc floor sits below 2.36, which is why they run fine on bookworm today).

## Deploy path

`cd-stagecraft.yml` delegates to the `encore-build` composite action, which builds the runtime base from `Dockerfile.base` and passes it via `--base`. Merging to `main` therefore triggers: base rebuild on trixie, encore image, GHCR push, Hetzner deploy. No `PREV_IMAGE` bump is needed (that field feeds only the manual hotfix `Dockerfile`, which CD does not use).

## Validation

- `node:22-trixie-slim` tag confirmed published on Docker Hub (glibc 2.41).
- Spec 160 claims `platform/services/stagecraft/` by directory prefix (`unit: { kind: directory, path: platform/services/stagecraft }`), so the coupling gate fires on `Dockerfile.base`; resolved by the waiver below rather than a gate-satisfying edit to spec 160 (whose factory-adapter-relocation design is unrelated to the container base image). `Dockerfile.base` is not a hashed index input, so no codebase-index regen is required.
- Post-merge + deploy: re-scaffold a tenant and confirm the regenerate-index step completes green (AC-2 born-green closure).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: platform/services/stagecraft/Dockerfile.base base-image glibc bump (node:22-slim -> node:22-trixie-slim) serves specs 112/220 AC-2 born-green; it does not alter spec 160's factory-adapter-stagecraft-relocation design.

title: feat(208): drill the org kill-switch pull-and-lift over the e2e mock seam (T021)
body:
## What

Spec 208 Phase 5 (PR-5), **T021**: the org kill-switch pull-and-lift drill
(FR-005 / AC-5). Exercises the org halt against a live, seeded cockpit over the
spec-187 `mock_stagecraft` seam. "A kill switch that has never been pulled is
decoration," so the drill is an acceptance criterion.

## How

- **Harness (`mock_stagecraft.ts`)** gains `push()` / `inboundFrames()` /
  `waitForFrame()` plus socket retention, so the duplex stays bidirectional
  after `sync.hello`. The four spec-187 handshake modes are untouched. `stop()`
  force-terminates any retained socket so a still-open client never wedges
  `http.Server.close()` on teardown.
- **Fixture (`fixtures/208/org-halt-drill.e2e.ts`)**:
  - **connected leg**: push `org.halt.activated` (org scope) and assert the
    **real** `org.halt.ack` emitted by the OPC-side `on_org_halt_activated`
    (`live_sessions.rs`); then push `org.halt.lifted` and assert the lift ack.
    These are the FR-003/FR-004 audited per-engine ack timestamps.
  - **disconnected leg**: a halted server refuses the reconnect handshake
    (`handshake-rejects`); the OPC has no local halt-awareness, so the boot gate
    stays sticky. Assert it never advances to cockpit.

## Scope, kept honest

- The literal pause-and-checkpoint of a *running* session is **not** asserted:
  seeding a live session requires a Tauri invoke the harness cannot reach
  (`withGlobalTauri` is off, no `window.__TAURI__`). The ack is the FR-003
  propagation-bound evidence, so that is what the drill measures.

title: feat(225,deployd): drop the cluster-wide workloads grant when selfProvision is on
body:
Lands spec 225 as the design home for deployd's self-provisioned RBAC mechanism (shipped mechanism-only in #503 under a Spec-Drift-Waiver) and the now-validated flip that drops deployd's cluster-wide workloads grant.

## What changes

- **`templates/rbac.yaml`**: the cluster-wide `deployd-controller-workloads` ClusterRoleBinding else-branch is suppressed when `rbac.selfProvision: true`. deployd's standing workload authority drops from **every namespace on the cluster** to **only the namespaces it self-provisions at deploy time**. The chart default is untouched (`selfProvision:false` + `namespaces:[]` still renders the fallback), so nothing changes for any environment that doesn't opt in.
- **`values-hetzner.yaml`**: `rbac.selfProvision: true`, enabling the flip on Hetzner via values, never by changing the chart default.
- **`specs/225-...`**: establishes `rbac.yaml`, refines `values-hetzner.yaml` (new `deployd-selfprovision-rbac` aspect), extends the featuregraph golden against 034, references the unchanged `rbac.rs`/`routes.rs` mechanism.

No `Spec-Drift-Waiver`: spec 225's authority edges cover every changed path, so `spec-spine couple` is clean (4 paths, no drift).

## Why this is safe to drop the fallback

#503 added the mechanism opt-in and default-off and deliberately kept the cluster-wide fallback, because dropping it was gated on validating the `bind`-verb escalation on a real cluster (only kind-proven then). That validation is now done.

**Validated 2026-07-04 on `oap-hetzner-master1` (real K3s):** with `rbac.selfProvision=true` applied to the live deployd (rev 80, the #503 image `sha-918b0c7`), impersonating `deployd-api-sa`, the exact `ensure_workload_rbac` operation succeeded (created a throwaway namespace, then the `bind`-gated `deployd-controller-workloads` RoleBinding referencing it, then cleaned up). The `bind` verb is load-bearing (kind negative control: no bind verb gives `Forbidden`). deployd's Rust code path is unchanged from #503, so what kind proved runs identically here.

`helm template` verified across all three cases: `selfProvision:true`+`namespaces:[]` yields 1 ClusterRoleBinding (namespaces only); chart default yields 2 (namespaces + workloads fallback); explicit `namespaces` allowlist yields per-namespace RoleBindings.

## Cutover behavior (read before merge)

When this deploys to Hetzner, helm **deletes the cluster-wide workloads ClusterRoleBinding**. deployd then self-heals per namespace on each deploy (`ensure_workload_rbac` runs before helm, idempotent). Two things to know:

1. **Existing tenants self-heal on next deploy, not instantly.** There is exactly one live tenant today (`oap-stagecraft-ing-single-simple-dev`). Recommended cutover: after CD deploys the flip, redeploy it once to provision its RoleBinding.
2. **Teardown gap (FR-007, staged).** Only the deploy handler self-provisions; `delete_deployment` shells `helm uninstall` directly without it. A DELETE of a namespace never redeployed since the flip would hit `Forbidden` on uninstall, which the delete path treats as best-effort (ignored) and would orphan k8s resources. The durable fix (call `ensure_workload_rbac` in the teardown path) is FR-007, deferred as a code follow-up since this PR is chart+spec only. The cutover redeploy in step 1 also closes this for the live tenant.

The spec's Cutover section documents the transitional `rbac.namespaces` allowlist option for operators who can't redeploy all tenants at cutover.

## Gates
- spec-lint `--fail-on-warn`: clean
- `spec-spine couple`: OK, 4 paths, no drift (no waiver)
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden`: green

title: feat(187): headless auth-state seeding, un-skips the 183 AC-8 e2e drill
body:
Closes the spec 187 `[[opc-e2e-auth-state-seeding]]` follow-up (§8), the last
blocker on the harness's `implementation: complete`. It un-skips the spec-183
AC-8 fixture (cockpit reverts to `<BootGate>` on sidecar kill), which has sat
`describe.skip` since spec 183 for lack of a way to reach a signed-in cockpit
headlessly.

This is the prerequisite the 208 kill-switch drill (PR-5) needs; a follow-up PR
extends the mock with frame push/observe and adds the 208 drill on top.

## Why pure seeding works

Reaching a signed-in cockpit would otherwise require the full GitHub OAuth/PKCE
flow against Rauthy (no dev bypass). But OPC's boot path only DECODES the stored
session JWT's claims and never verifies its signature
(`stagecraft_client.rs::decode_jwt_claims`: "Signature is intentionally not
verified here") or calls Rauthy's JWKS. The mock duplex ignores the bearer. So
the entire signed-in state is **one keychain entry** holding a fake, unsigned
JWT whose payload carries an `exp` in the future and a `custom.oap_org_id` claim
(which flips `org_session_ready = has_org && sync_hello`).

## What landed

- **`e2e_seed_session` bin** (`src-tauri/src/bin/`, feature-gated `e2e-seed`):
  writes/clears the keychain entry via the **same** `keyring` crate/version the
  app reads back with, so read-back is guaranteed. Nothing in the production
  feature set enables `e2e-seed`, so the shipping `opc` binary is byte-for-byte
  unchanged.
- **`seedSignedInSession` / `buildSeedJwt` / `clearSeededSession`**
  (`tests-e2e/harness/seed_session.ts`): build the fake JWT and shell the bin.
  Wired into `launchOpc` via a `seedSession` option that seeds BEFORE the binary
  boots (so the token is present when Rust `setup()` and React `AuthContext` read
  the keychain at t=0) and clears on teardown.
- **`killProcess({name})`** (`tests-e2e/harness/kill_process.ts`): SIGKILL a
  sidecar by name (comm), the same OS-portable basis `process_tree.ts` matches on.
- **Un-skipped `fixtures/183/ac8-precondition-loss.e2e.ts`**: seed a session,
  wait for `cockpit`, `killProcess({name: "axiomregent"})`, assert `<BootGate>`
  reasserts within the AC-8 window.
- **Nightly** (`opc-e2e-nightly.yml`): builds the seed bin with `--features
  e2e-seed`, and runs the e2e step inside `dbus-run-session` with an unlocked
  gnome-keyring so the `keyring` crate's Linux Secret Service backend is
  available to both the seed writer and the OPC binary.
- **9 harness unit tests** (JWT claim shape / base64url, bin-path resolver, kill
  no-match) pass locally on plain Node.

## Verification posture

Per spec 187 FR-T5, the binary-driving fixtures run **only** in the Linux
nightly (tauri-driver has no macOS WebView backend), so the AC-8 fixture and the
D-Bus/keyring bootstrap are verified by the first green nightly, not locally.
Locally green here: `cargo check --bin e2e_seed_session --features e2e-seed`,
`tsc` (harness scope), the 9 harness unit tests, `make pr-prep` coupling (10
paths, no drift), the featuregraph golden, and index freshness.

`implementation: complete` for spec 187 is intentionally **not** flipped: §6
defers it to a small follow-up after the first green nightly confirms
AC-5/AC-7/AC-9 (now including AC-8) on Linux.

## Coupling

Spec 187 `establishes:` the seed bin (it brought it into existence; it lives in
the opc crate only to link the app's exact `keyring` dep) and adds a `refines:`
aspect for the manifest's `[[bin]]`/`[features]` registration. The harness and
fixture files sit under directories 187 already establishes. No waiver.

title: chore(deps): bump Encore to 1.57.9 (lib + CLI + integrity digest in lockstep)
body:
Coordinated bump of Encore from 1.57.8 to 1.57.9 across every surface that must move together. This is the follow-up flagged in #496 (which held `encore.dev` at 1.57.8) and depends on #498 (which made the Encore CLI download integrity check load-bearing and fail-closed).

## Why coordinated

`encore build` fails closed when the `encore.dev` library is newer than the pinned CLI (`installed 'encore.dev' package version (1.57.9) newer than 'encore' release`). And per `encore-install`'s own contract, bumping `ENCORE_VERSION` without updating the integrity digest fails closed at install time. So library, CLI pin, and digest are a single atomic unit.

## Surfaces changed

- `platform/services/stagecraft/package.json`: `encore.dev` `^1.57.8` -> `^1.57.9`.
- `platform/services/stagecraft/package-lock.json`: regenerated with **npm@10** (`npx npm@10 install --package-lock-only --force`) to match CI's node 22 / npm 10 dedup; minimal 4-line delta pinning `encore.dev@1.57.9`.
- `ENCORE_VERSION` `1.57.8` -> `1.57.9` in `cd-stagecraft.yml`, `cd-tenant-app.yml`, `ci-stagecraft.yml`, `ci-stagecraft-encore.yml`.
- `.github/actions/encore-install/action.yml`: default `encore-sha256` updated to the real published digest of `encore-1.57.9-linux_amd64.tar.gz` (`dfd43dcd456f91414a823315480da921333e6d1e3535ab48c47c09225d022af5`), verified against the CloudFront tarball.

`cd-tenant-app.yml` is in the set, so produced tenant apps move to 1.57.9 in lockstep.

## Not changed (deliberate)

- `web/app/lib/client.ts` generated header still reads `v1.57.8`: it is codegen output, not CI-enforced for freshness, and a patch bump does not change the generator output meaningfully. Left for the next natural codegen pass.
- `specs/211-encore-test-ci-job/spec.md` mention of "Encore CLI 1.57.8" is a historical record of the first encore-lane execution and is left intact.

## Validation

- `1.57.9` confirmed published on npm (latest) and as the CloudFront CLI tarball; digest computed locally.
- `make pr-prep`: index staleness gate fresh; coupling gate drift is dependency/wiring only (waiver below).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Coordinated Encore 1.57.9 version bump (npm lib + ENCORE_VERSION CLI pin + integrity digest). It advances a dependency version and its matching CLI and digest pins across manifests, the lockfile, workflow env, and the install action, and changes no governed workflow behavior or any owning spec's narrative (118, 177, 211, 214, 116, 160, 220). Editing those owning specs purely to satisfy the gate would be the mass-edit-to-satisfy-a-gate anti-pattern (CONST-005). Verified locally: `spec-spine couple` exits 0 with this waiver.

title: feat(208): harden the org-halt ack ledger against replay (Phase 3.1)
body:
Implements spec 208 Phase 3.1 (T023/T024), the ack-ledger hardening
follow-ups from the PR #502 reintegration fix. Stacked on the doc PR #505,
which records the `## Deferred hardening (Phase 3.1)` spec section.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: the coupled spec 208 change (the `## Deferred hardening (Phase 3.1)` section + T023-T025 tasks) lands in the stacked base PR #505; this PR is its implementation. No drift -- `make pr-prep` (coupling vs main) is clean because spec and code are coherent; the gate flags this PR only because its base is #505's branch, so the spec half is in the base rather than this PR's diff.

## T023 -- symmetric halt-ack write-path guard

PR #502 guarded the *lift*-ack write on `state === "reintegrating"`. A late
*halt*-ack replayed via the outbox-durable resync after the scope moved to
`reintegrating`/`lifted` was appended unchecked. For a client not already in
the ledger (the idempotency check misses it) that widens the recorded
halt-acker set: the phantom acker is then expected to lift-ack, holding the
scope in `reintegrating` indefinitely. Fail-safe in direction (over-count,
never a premature `lifted`), but a stuck reintegration is still a defect.

Mirror the lift-ack guard: append a `kind:'halt'` ack only while the scope is
`halted`; drop it otherwise as a benign no-op. The engine re-acks on the next
broadcast per the resync-replay contract, so the drop is lossless.

## T024 -- dropped-ack audit trail

The three benign drop paths (a duplicate replay, the T023 stale halt-ack, a
stale lift-ack) only `log.info`d. A dropped ack was invisible to the audit
chain the rest of the switch preserves. Add a `FACTORY_ORG_HALT_ACK_DROPPED`
audit action, written inside the txn on each drop path with the drop `reason`
in metadata. The duplicate path records this explicit drop marker instead of
a misleading second `engine_ack` (still one `engine_ack` per real ack, still
no jsonb growth).

## Tests (encore lane, spec 211)

- a stale halt-ack while `reintegrating` does not widen the halt-acker set,
  proven behaviourally: the sole real acker's lift-ack still completes
  reintegration (if the stale ack had leaked in, the halt would stay
  reintegrating);
- the same while `lifted` (guard covers the lifted branch);
- each drop path (`not-halted`, `not-reintegrating`, `duplicate`) writes an
  `ack_dropped` audit row with the expected reason.

## Coupling

Both source paths are already 208-owned: `api/sync/service.ts` is the
`org-halt-propagation` refine aspect, `api/factory/auditActions.ts` the
`org-halt-audit-actions` refine aspect. No frontmatter change; `spec-spine
index` unchanged. Flips T023-T025 in `tasks.md`.

title: feat(112,220): regenerate produced-app .derived index at scaffold time
body:
## What

Closes the spec 220 AC-2 blocker where **every produced app is born with a red CI**: the scaffold pipeline ships no committed `.derived/codebase-index`, so the produced app's born-with `spec-spine index check` gate exits 3 (index not found), which aborts the whole `spec-spine` job before the spec 220 certificate-emission step ever runs.

The generator (factory-encore `born-with.ts`) strips the template's `.derived/` **on purpose**: it must be recomputed against the PRODUCED tree, which differs from the template (seeded specs, born-with `Makefile` + `tools/lint`, the added `.github/workflows/oap-build.yml`, per-profile modules). Nothing recomputed it, so it was simply absent. This PR adds that regeneration.

## Change

- `create.ts`: a new `regenerate-index` scaffold step runs the pinned `spec-spine compile` + `index` + `index check` over the final tree, after every tree mutation (scaffold, add-module, kernel stamp, oap-build.yml seed, artifact extraction), before the initial push. **Fail-closed** (spec 209 posture, no skip-as-pass): a scaffold that cannot produce a fresh index orphans the job rather than pushing a red-on-arrival repo.
- `perRequestScaffold.ts`: exported `regenerateProducedIndex` (reuses the existing `spawnAndCapture` + `tooledEnv`; **not** called by `scaffoldFromPrebuilt`, so the VCS-free copy-behavior unit test is unaffected).
- `templateCache.ts`: `specSpineBin(workspace)` resolves the pinned `spec-spine` binary the warmup installed into the template cache, so the committed shards match the exact version the produced app's own CI runs `index check` with.
- `types.ts`: new `regenerate-index` `ScaffoldStep`.
- `regenerateProducedIndex.test.ts`: verifies the compile -> index -> index-check sequence and the fail-closed contract against a stub binary.
- Spec 112 §5.3 (Net additions): documents the regenerate-index step.

## Verification

Local: stagecraft vitest for the new test + the affected `perRequestScaffold`/`create` suites (7 passed), no new TypeScript errors (the residual `~encore/*` alias errors are environmental, resolved by `encore check` in CI), OAP `spec-spine compile`/`index check` fresh, coupling gate green with the waiver below.

End-to-end proof that the emitted chain works once a produced tree carries a fresh index: a scaffolded tenant's born-with CI (with all three source fixes applied) emitted a signed certificate and `tenant-tail verify-certificate` accepted it green (`governance certificate VERIFIED`, corpus + SBOM bindings VERIFIED).

## Companions

Two companion PRs complete the born-with fix: `factory-encore` (carry `Makefile` + `tools/` forward) and `template-encore` ci.yml (`secrets: inherit` for the cert-emit leg + parentless-commit routing). Propagation to fresh scaffolds also requires the warmup to rebuild the prebuilt from the updated template + generator (and the factory-encore lockstep pin to advance, spec 006 Phase 3).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: edits spec 112's own spec.md to document the scaffold regenerate-index step. Specs 138/199/215 carry `references` edges to 112, so the coupling gate names them as owners of 112's spec.md (references-edge reverse-coupling), but their contracts are unaffected by this documentation addition, so no authoring edit to them is warranted.

title: feat(deployd): self-provision per-namespace RBAC (additive, opt-in)
body:
Lands the first clause of the third #494 follow-up ("the deployd code change that self-provisions per-namespace RoleBindings") as an **additive, opt-in, default-off** mechanism. The second clause (flipping `rbac.namespaces` to scoped) is intentionally deferred and cluster-gated, per the approach chosen for this follow-up.

## Background

The deployd-api chart (from #494) splits its permissions into two ClusterRoles: `deployd-controller-namespaces` (cluster-scoped, always bound cluster-wide) and `deployd-controller-workloads` (namespaced, bound per-namespace via `rbac.namespaces` or cluster-wide as a fallback). The cluster-wide workloads fallback exists **only** because deployd creates tenant namespaces on demand and had no code path to grant itself workload rights in a namespace it just created. The chart's `rbac.yaml` header flagged closing that gap as residual work needing a deployd code change. This is that change.

## What changed

- **`deployd-api-rs/src/rbac.rs`** (new): when `DEPLOYD_SELF_PROVISION_RBAC` is on, `ensure_workload_rbac()` creates the target namespace (idempotent) and a RoleBinding granting deployd's own ServiceAccount the `deployd-controller-workloads` ClusterRole, before helm runs there. Wired into the deploy handler (`routes.rs`) ahead of `helm upgrade --install`; on failure the deploy fails fast (`FAILED` + event) rather than letting helm fail mid-install with an opaque "forbidden".
- **chart**: `rbac.selfProvision` (default `false`) gates (a) the `rolebindings` create + `bind` verb on the workloads ClusterRole that K8s privilege-escalation prevention requires, and (b) the `DEPLOYD_*` env driving the code (SA name, pod namespace via the downward API, ClusterRole name).

**Default off ⇒ inert**: with `rbac.selfProvision: false`, the chart renders exactly as before and the code path is a no-op, so the working cluster-wide fallback is completely untouched.

## Why the flip is deferred

Flipping `rbac.namespaces` to scoped removes a currently-working fallback; if the self-provisioning were subtly wrong, every tenant deploy would break. The chart header and the spec-136 Phase 3 precedent both treat that flip as cluster-validation-gated. This PR lands and proves the mechanism so the flip becomes a safe, small follow-up.

## Testing

- **`cargo test`** (deployd-api-rs): 57 passed, incl. 5 new `rbac` unit tests (env parsing, `enabled` only on `true`/`1`, RoleBinding shape/roleRef/subject, disabled no-op).
- **`helm template`**: default renders no new RBAC or env; `--set rbac.selfProvision=true` renders the `rolebindings` rule, the `bind` verb (`resourceNames: [deployd-controller-workloads]`), and the env vars.
- **kind cluster (real Kubernetes RBAC escalation proof)**, SA in scoped mode (namespaces ClusterRole + `rolebindings`/`bind`, **no** cluster-wide workloads binding):
  - **With** the `bind` grant: SA creates a namespace → self-provisions the RoleBinding → then creates a Secret and a Deployment there (granted only via that RoleBinding). ✅
  - **Without** the `bind` grant: RoleBinding create is `Forbidden` (*"attempting to grant RBAC permissions not currently held"*), and workload access is denied. ✅ This proves the `bind` verb is load-bearing, not incidental.

## Follow-up (cluster-gated)

- Flip `rbac.namespaces` default to scoped (drop the cluster-wide workloads ClusterRoleBinding) once self-provisioning is validated against the real target cluster. That behavior-changing PR is the natural home for a spec establishing this mechanism.

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: additive, opt-in, default-off RBAC self-provisioning mechanism. With `selfProvision: false` (the default) the chart and code are inert, so no owning spec's current narrative changes. The touched paths are owned structurally by several deployd/tenant specs (073 retroactive, 136, 137, 145, 146, 196, 214), none of which is about RBAC self-provisioning; #494 documented this only as chart-comment residual work. The spec-worthy change is the deferred, behavior-changing flip, which will carry its own spec. Editing several unrelated structural owners purely to satisfy the gate would be the mass-edit-to-satisfy-a-gate anti-pattern (CONST-005).

title: fix(208): drop lift-acks that arrive when a halt is not reintegrating
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a reintegration-ledger bug shipped in #495: a lift-ack was recorded after only the D2 admission check, with no guard on the halt's current state. A cycle-1 lift-ack still in flight when the operator re-pulls (the D3 path, which resets the ack ledger) lands while the halt is `halted`, is written unconditionally, then miscounted as a completed lift in the next reintegration cycle. That can flip a halt to `lifted` for an engine that never lift-acked that cycle (premature reintegration). Reachable by ordinary timing, no adversarial input.
- The completion computation was already gated on `state === "reintegrating"`, but the ledger write above it was not. This adds the matching write-path guard in `orgHaltAckDispatch`: a lift-ack is a benign no-op unless the halt is actively reintegrating. The engine re-acks on the next `lifted` broadcast per the resync-replay contract, so ignoring it is lossless. Halt-acks are unaffected.
- Adds two regression tests (a direct guard assertion and the full cross-cycle contamination scenario), and clarifies spec 208 FR-004 to document the completion-count windowing invariant the fix enforces.

Follow-up to #495. The bug was found by #495's own adversarial AI-review pass, but #495 merged before the fix landed.

## Spec alignment

- Spec: `specs/208-org-agent-kill-switch/spec.md` (FR-004 clarification)

## Change classification

Select one:

- [ ] Feature: new capability backed by a spec
- [ ] Enhancement: improvement to existing feature
- [x] Bug fix: corrects incorrect behavior
- [ ] Refactor: internal restructure, no behavior change
- [ ] Docs: documentation only
- [ ] Chore: build, deps, tooling, CI

## Checklist

- [x] Changes align with the referenced spec (or no spec applies): the FR-004 clarification documents the invariant the code now enforces
- [x] Spec-compiler output unchanged (or spec frontmatter was intentionally modified): registry + codebase-index shards for 208 regenerated and committed
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or API keys committed
- [x] Tests pass locally: my files typecheck clean. The DB-bound `orgHalt.test.ts` (incl. the 2 new tests) runs in CI's `encore-test` lane; the two source paths are owned by spec 208 and the coupling gate is clean (3 paths, no drift).

title: docs(202): withdraw AC-6 pt2 (total_tokens is not a redundant counter)
body:
> **Stacked on #497.** Base is the `202-audit-log-approval-velocity-index` branch; GitHub will retarget this to `main` once #497 merges. Merge #497 first.

## What

Reframes spec 202's **AC-6 pt2**. It was tracked as a mechanical follow-up (this was the original "PR1b") to remove `FactoryPipelineState.total_tokens` as a counter redundant with the `RunBudgetMeter` tokens axis. **No code changes** — spec.md + plan.md only.

## Why the original plan was wrong

Implementation-time investigation of the OPC read path shows the two accumulators are **not redundant**; they live in different scopes and serve different jobs:

| | `pipeline_state.total_tokens` | `RunBudgetMeter` tokens axis |
|---|---|---|
| Lifetime | **persisted** (`.factory/pipeline-state.json`) | in-memory, per-spawn local (`factory.rs:1393`) |
| Purpose | UI-facing token total | budget gate (FR-002) + cert snapshot (FR-005) |
| Read by | `build_status_response` → `PipelineStatusResponse.total_tokens` (`factory.rs:1005`); `emit_terminal_completed` (`factory.rs:1832`) | `budget_meter.consumption()` for the cert only (`factory.rs:1841`) |
| In scope at status endpoint? | yes | **no** (meter is gone after the spawn returns) |

`total_tokens` is the persisted value the desktop polls and displays. The meter is a per-run in-memory accumulator that never persists and isn't reachable from the status-poll command. Removing `total_tokens` would break 3 read sites plus the desktop `PipelineStatusResponse` contract; making the meter a true replacement means persisting it and threading it into the status path — a behavior-bearing refactor, not the mechanical cleanup the flip anticipated.

## What changed

Per CONST-005 (don't delete a live UI-surfaced field as if it were dead code), pt2 is **withdrawn**, not executed. Reframed across:

- **spec.md**: the frontmatter `implementation:` note, the Status section, the **AC-6 criterion** itself (dropping the false "no two accumulators coexist" clause), and the "Implementation status (AC-6 residual)" blockquote (now records the investigation with `path:line` evidence).
- **plan.md**: the Slice B AC-6-status blockquote, the code-reality row's forward claim, and the Summary.

Outcome: `total_tokens` is **kept by design** as the UI/persistence surface, and **AC-6 is satisfied by pt1 alone** (the dead `max_total_tokens` stub was already retired in PR1 #469).

## Gates run locally

- `spec-spine compile`: 0 warnings; `implementation:` value unchanged (`complete`), so the featuregraph golden is untouched
- `spec-spine couple`: OK, no drift
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `spec-spine index`: regenerated (shard staged)

title: fix(opc): source agent-auth org id from the stagecraft session
body:
Closes the fourth #494 follow-up: "set `PLATFORM_ORG_ID` on the desktop so the per-org agent block policy binds."

## Problem

#494's Seam D agent-authorization pre-flight (`execute_agent` → `check_agent_authorized` → stagecraft `isAgentAuthorized`) requires the caller's org id as a UUID query param, but only read it from a `PLATFORM_ORG_ID` env var that the desktop never sets. With it unset the request omitted `orgId`, stagecraft returned 400, and the outcome degraded to `Unavailable` — so an org's agent **block** policy never actually bound on the desktop.

## Fix

Rather than depend on a manually-configured env var the app can derive itself, resolve the org id from the **authenticated stagecraft session** (`StagecraftState.current().org_id()` — the same lookup `sidecars.rs::boot_gate_status` already uses) and pass it into `check_agent_authorized`. `PLATFORM_ORG_ID` is kept as an override / fallback for headless or pre-login contexts.

Now the per-org block policy binds automatically once a session is established.

This composes with the sibling follow-up (`agent_policies` default-org backfill, #499): that migration puts stranded policies under the real org; this makes the desktop query with the real org.

## Testing

- `cargo check` (src-tauri): clean.
- `check_agent_authorized` has a single caller; `org_id()` returns an owned `String` and `current()` an owned `Arc<StagecraftClient>`, so the session lookup borrows nothing (compiles without lifetime gymnastics).

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `agents.rs` is owned structurally by several desktop specs (032, 035, 111, 119, 178, 180, …), none of which describe this #494-era security seam (added ad-hoc in the security sweep). The seam's contract — block policies bind per-org — is unchanged; only the org-id source is corrected so the policy actually binds. Editing unrelated structural owners purely to satisfy the gate would be the mass-edit-to-satisfy-a-gate anti-pattern (CONST-005). The semantic home (spec 208, org-agent-kill-switch) is not a path owner of this file and is mid-flight in #495.

title: fix(stagecraft): backfill agent_policies rows stranded on org_id='default'
body:
Closes the second #494 follow-up: the per-org cutover stranded legacy `agent_policies` rows on `org_id='default'`.

## Problem

#494 made every agent-policy read and write org-scoped by the caller's real org UUID (`api/agents/agents.ts`: `isAgentAuthorized` now requires a UUID `orgId`; `listAgentPolicies` / `upsertAgentPolicy` / `deleteAgentPolicy` filter by `auth.orgId`). Rows created before that cutover carry `org_id='default'` (the column default), which no UUID-scoped query can match. They are invisible to the admin CRUD and — the real hazard — a **block** policy stranded on `'default'` is no longer enforced for any real org.

## Fix

`migrations/2_backfill_agent_policies_default_org.up.sql`, guarded to the single-tenant case (exactly one organization):

1. **Delete** legacy `'default'` rows whose slug the real org already governs. The real-org row is authoritative and the only one the app reads, so the `'default'` duplicate is dead data; removing it lets step 2 satisfy `UNIQUE(org_id, slug)` and is behaviour-neutral.
2. **Reassign** the remaining (non-conflicting) `'default'` rows to the real org so they are enforced and visible again.
3. With **zero or multiple** orgs the target is absent or ambiguous, so rows are left untouched for explicit operator resolution (a multi-tenant backfill needs a per-row org mapping this migration cannot infer).

## Testing

Verified against Postgres 17 in a throwaway DB with the real DDL (including `UNIQUE(org_id, slug)`) across three scenarios:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| One org, mixed non-conflict + conflict + real-org rows | non-conflict reassigned (blocked preserved), conflicting `'default'` deleted, real-org row kept, **0** `'default'` rows left |
| Two orgs | `'default'` rows **untouched** |
| Zero orgs | `'default'` rows **untouched** |

The DB-bound `stagecraft-encore` lane applies this migration in CI.

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: data-only backfill migration completing #494's per-org agent-policy cutover. The migration path is owned structurally by specs 119 and 160 (the `api/db` schema baseline), whose narratives this data change does not alter. The enforcement-semantics home is spec 208 (org-agent-kill-switch), which is not the path authority and is mid-flight in #495; the narrative note belongs there once that reintegration settles. Editing 119/160 purely to satisfy the gate would be the mass-edit-to-satisfy-a-gate anti-pattern (CONST-005).

title: ci: make the Encore CLI download integrity check load-bearing
body:
Closes the first #494 follow-up: fill the real Encore CLI sha256 so the download integrity check in the `encore-install` composite action stops skipping with a warning and becomes load-bearing.

## What changed

`encore-install` shipped in #494 with a placeholder digest (`REPLACE_WITH_PUBLISHED_SHA256`) that skipped verification, because no caller passed a digest. This fills in the authentic published sha256 for the pinned Encore version:

- **default `encore-sha256` = `59ac867590cb5572410b8b911c28f8263aeb0df5a9eccd2042a6a64a26597d4e`** — sha256 of `encore-1.57.8-linux_amd64.tar.gz`, downloaded over HTTPS from the same CloudFront URL the action installs from and verified locally to be a valid gzip tarball containing `./bin/encore`.
- All four callers (`ci-stagecraft`, `ci-stagecraft-encore`, `cd-stagecraft`, `cd-tenant-app`) pin `ENCORE_VERSION` 1.57.8 and inherit this default, so the integrity check now engages on every Encore install path.
- **Fail-closed coupling:** bumping `ENCORE_VERSION` in a caller without updating this digest fails closed at install time (the new tarball's hash won't match) — version and digest must move together, by design.
- The explicit empty-value opt-out and the placeholder fallback branch are retained; the warning wording now reflects that skipping is a deliberate opt-out rather than the default state.

## Testing

- Downloaded the pinned tarball and computed the digest locally; confirmed it is a valid Encore gzip tarball (`./bin/encore` present).
- This PR's own `ci-stagecraft` / `ci-stagecraft-encore` jobs exercise `encore-install` with the real digest, so a green run is end-to-end proof the check passes.
- `spec-spine couple`: 0 paths checked, no drift — `.github/actions/**` composite actions are empty-authority-by-rule (spec 152 §3.2), so no spec edit or waiver is required.

title: perf(202): index audit_log for the FR-004 approval-velocity read
body:
## What

Adds `2_audit_log_actor_action_created_idx.up.sql` — the composite btree index `(actor_user_id, action, created_at)` on `audit_log`. This is the first stagecraft migration since the #454/#455 baseline reset.

## Why

Spec 202 Slice G (FR-004) added the approval-velocity governance-drift counter. Its DB read, `api/factory/approvalVelocity.ts::loadActorApprovalTimestamps`, runs on **every gate approval** and filters `audit_log` on equality `(actor_user_id, action)` plus a `created_at >= cutoff` range (joining `factory_runs` for org scoping). `audit_log` carried **zero indexes**, so this (and every other `audit_log` read) was a sequential scan over an append-only, monotonically growing table.

This was net-new (spec 202 did not previously disclose it as a residual); the queue-storm gate's read is already served by `factory_runs_org_in_flight_idx`, so approval-velocity is the one unindexed `audit_log` read the governor introduced.

## Verification

Applied `1_baseline.up.sql` then this migration to a fresh Postgres 16 in real sequence, seeded 102,015 `audit_log` rows, `ANALYZE`, and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`'d the exact FR-004 query:

| | plan | `audit_log` access | buffers | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **with index** | `Index Scan using audit_log_actor_action_created_idx` | Index Cond on all three columns; `target_type` post-filter | 4 | **0.033 ms** |
| **without index** | `Parallel Seq Scan`, 51k rows removed/worker | full 102k scan | 1928 | **6.195 ms** |

Same 15-row result both ways. The planner picks the index automatically for the exact predicate; the gap widens as `audit_log` grows.

## Design notes

- **Migration-only**, matching the `factory_runs_org_in_flight_idx` precedent (performance indexes live in SQL, not the Drizzle query model). The schema-drift gate (`api/db/schemaDrift.test.ts`) checks columns/enums, not indexes, so no `schema.ts` change is needed.
- **Plain `CREATE INDEX`** (not `CONCURRENTLY`) so it applies inside Encore's transactional migration runner.

## Governance

`platform/services/stagecraft/api/db` is co-owned by spec 119's directory claim. Rather than a Spec-Drift-Waiver (the #454 mechanical-consolidation path) or an off-topic edit to spec 119, spec 202 gains a **file-level `establishes`** for the migration plus a body note under FR-004. The coupling gate then resolves ownership to the motivating spec, mirroring how spec 205 claimed its specific `api/db` files (`schema.ts`). `spec-spine couple`: OK, no drift.

## Gates run locally

- `spec-spine couple`: OK, 2 paths, no drift
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh (regenerated shard staged)
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- `spec-spine compile`: 0 warnings
- Featuregraph golden: unaffected (establishes-edge change; not a golden-tripping field)

The encore-lane (`encore test` applying the migration + `approvalVelocity.test.ts`) is CI-verified.

title: chore(deps): consolidate Dependabot cargo + npm bumps (#487-#491)
body:
Consolidates the four open Dependabot dependency PRs onto one branch so they clear the spec/code coupling and supply-chain gates together instead of each tripping them individually.

## Bumps

**Cargo** (`product/apps/opc/src-tauri`):
- `sysinfo` 0.38.4 → 0.39.5 (#491)
- `window-vibrancy` 0.6.0 → 0.7.1 (#489) — direct dep; `tauri` 2.11.5 still depends on `^0.6`, so both versions coexist in the lock, exactly as Dependabot resolves it
- `cargo-minor-patch` group (#488): `ignore` 0.4.27, `jsonschema` + `referencing` 0.46.8, `tauri` 2.11.5, `tauri-runtime-wry` 2.11.4, `tree-sitter` 0.26.10

**npm** (`platform/services/stagecraft`) — `npm-minor-patch` group (#487): **12 of the 13** declared updates: `react-router` (+ `/dev`, `/node`, `/serve`, `/express`) 8.1.0, `vite` 8.1.2, `knex` 3.3.0, `@aws-sdk/client-s3` + `s3-request-presigner` 3.1078.0, `prettier` 3.9.4, `@tanstack/react-query` 5.101.2, `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.2.

### `encore.dev` held at 1.57.8 (deliberately not bumped to 1.57.9)

The Encore CLI is pinned at **1.57.8** across all four workflows (`ENCORE_VERSION`), and `encore build` **fails closed** when the `encore.dev` runtime package is newer than the CLI:

```
ERR installed 'encore.dev' package version (1.57.9) newer than 'encore' release, run 'encore version update' first
```

(This is exactly what the first push of this branch tripped in the `stagecraft` encore jobs.) Bumping `encore.dev` to 1.57.9 therefore requires a **coordinated CLI bump** — `ENCORE_VERSION` in `ci-stagecraft`, `ci-stagecraft-encore`, `cd-stagecraft`, `cd-tenant-app`, plus the `encore-install` digest (see #498). That coordinated bump is left as a follow-up; this PR holds `encore.dev` at 1.57.8 to stay in lockstep.

## Method

The cargo lock was regenerated with `cargo update --precise` per package to hit each Dependabot target without over-bumping. The npm lock was regenerated **under npm 10** (CI runs node 22 / npm 10; the dev machine's npm 11 dedupes differently and drops the peer-pulled `typescript@5.9.3` node, which fails CI's `npm ci` sync check) via an incremental update, so the tree stays minimal.

## Testing

- `cargo check` (src-tauri): clean against sysinfo 0.39 + window-vibrancy 0.7.
- `npm@10 ci` (stagecraft): clean, 0 vulnerabilities, react-router family consistent at 8.1.0, `encore.dev` pinned 1.57.8.
- `spec-spine index`: regenerated (`opc` shard); `spec-spine index check`: fresh.
- `spec-spine couple`: 4 dependency-manifest drift violations, all covered by the waiver below.

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Dependabot-surfaced cargo + npm minor/patch bumps only (#487, #488, #489, #491). They advance dependency versions in manifests and lockfiles and change no governed workflow behavior, so no owning spec's narrative changes. Editing the ~15 owning specs purely to satisfy the gate would be the mass-edit-to-satisfy-a-gate anti-pattern (CONST-005). Verified locally: `spec-spine couple` exits 0 with this waiver.

## Follow-up

- Coordinated Encore 1.57.9 bump: raise `ENCORE_VERSION` to 1.57.9 in the four workflows, refresh the `encore-install` digest (built on #498), and bump `encore.dev` to 1.57.9 in the same PR.

Supersedes #487, #488, #489, #491.

title: feat(208): agent-profile kill-switch seam + staged reintegration (Phase 3)
body:
## Summary

- Closes AC-3 (all three kill-switch scopes now enforced) and AC-4's reintegration leg for the org-agent kill switch, and adds AC-7 (reintegrating-state refusal).
- Agent-profile seam (option a): the engine resolves the profile about to execute a stage from its reservation-time stage-agent map and presents it on `factory.run.grant_renew` (`FACTORY_RUN_GRANT_ENVELOPE_VERSION` 1 to 2), so an agent-profile-scoped halt refuses renewal. Enforcement is at grant renewal only: issuance carries no single profile (a run spans several over its life) and the first renewal fires before s0, so a halted profile is refused before any agent output. `pullHaltCore`'s Phase-1 agent-profile rejection is removed.
- Staged reintegration (FR-004): `reintegrating` to `lifted` completes only when every engine that halt-acked has also lift-acked (computed over the acks ledger, no migration), and a lift-ack counts only after a fresh admission re-validation (D2 two-sided check). A new OPC `org.halt.lifted` dispatch handler sends the lift-ack. Re-halt (D3): a pull on a reintegrating scope re-asserts `halted`, adopts the new reason, and resets the ack ledger.

Closes #433.

## Spec alignment

- Spec: `specs/208-org-agent-kill-switch/spec.md` (Phase 3)

## Change classification

Select one:

- [x] Feature: new capability backed by a spec
- [ ] Enhancement: improvement to existing feature
- [ ] Bug fix: corrects incorrect behavior
- [ ] Refactor: internal restructure, no behavior change
- [ ] Docs: documentation only
- [ ] Chore: build, deps, tooling, CI

## Checklist

- [x] Changes align with the referenced spec (or no spec applies)
- [x] Spec-compiler output unchanged (or spec frontmatter was intentionally modified): spec 208 frontmatter intentionally updated; registry + codebase-index shards regenerated and committed
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or API keys committed
- [x] Tests pass locally: OPC Rust lib suite 188/188 (5 new). The DB-bound `orgHalt.test.ts` (7 tests) typechecks clean and runs in CI's `encore-test` lane (spec 211), since it needs live Postgres.

## Notes

- Coupling gate clean: 13 paths, no waiver. Three new `extends:198` edges for the OPC grant-renewal files.
- No new coupling edges from reusing the admission primitives inline in `sync/service.ts` (avoids the deliberate `service` to `grantDuplexHandlers` to `orgHalt` to `service` import cycle documented in-tree).
- Envelope version bump: `FACTORY_RUN_GRANT_ENVELOPE_VERSION` 1 to 2.

title: fix(security): close cross-stack auth, tenancy, and traversal gaps
body:
## Summary

Cross-stack security hardening from an adversarial scan of the repository, followed by a decorrelated pre-merge review whose confirmed findings were fixed in the same branch.

- **opc-web**: `/ws/claude` and `/api/*` now sit behind the control-token middleware with a localhost Origin allowlist; default bind moved to `127.0.0.1` (the `--host` flag was parsed but ignored before); the ungoverned `--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypass is refused on network-facing execute paths; the control token is embedded in the served HTML only on a loopback bind (logged to stderr otherwise); constant-time token comparison; `fs` capability narrowed off `read-all`/`write-all`/`scope-home-recursive`.
- **deployd-api**: deployments are owner-bound (`owner_sub`, rejecting a token with no subject), the read handlers are scope-gated, owner-mismatch returns 404 (no existence oracle), the caller-supplied namespace is validated and reserved/platform namespaces are blocked, empty required-scope fails closed, and hiqlite secrets are required (dev-only fallback behind `DEPLOYD_DEV`) with a per-namespace RBAC lever.
- **stagecraft**: authorization added to the agent-policy, github-token, audit, policy, and grants endpoints; `actorUserId` derived from the authenticated identity; the GitHub token broker verifies org ownership.
- **crates**: axiomregent path-traversal write fixed (lexical normalize + reject escape), factory path-component validation, audit-rotation errors logged, mutex-poison recovery.
- **k8s/helm**: default-deny NetworkPolicies for the app namespaces, rauthy and tenant-Postgres securityContext hardening, oauth2-proxy fails closed instead of `--email-domain=*`, service-account token automount disabled where unused.
- **ci/docs**: the release-tag `workflow_dispatch` input routed through `env:`, the encore binary download sha256-verifiable (opt-in), the `settings.json` execute allowlist narrowed, README/CLAUDE spec counts corrected.

24 owning specs carry dated coupling amendments per the spec 127 gate.

## Testing

- `cargo check`/`test`/`clippy` green across the crates workspace, deployd-api (52 tests), and opc `src-tauri`.
- stagecraft `tsc`/vitest: only pre-existing unrelated failures (`@opc/carrier-gate`/`libsodium`).
- `helm template` / `kubectl kustomize` / `terraform validate`: clean.
- `spec-spine index check` (staleness) and `spec-spine couple` (coupling, 82 paths): green; `make pr-prep`: clean.

## Declared trade-offs

- WebSocket control token is passed as a `?token=` query param because browsers cannot set custom WS handshake headers; it is per-session and reaches only loopback/served clients.
- An absent `Origin` on the WS upgrade is allowed so non-browser clients can authenticate via the control token.
- Tenant egress to 443/5432 is destination-open (port-scoped) because tenant apps need external HTTPS and managed databases.
- `owner_sub` binds the M2M caller identity, not the individual tenant behind a shared M2M credential; per-tenant isolation still relies on stagecraft's upstream project-membership checks.
- The `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID` fallback is gated by `NODE_ENV`, following the service's existing convention.
- Encore digest verification is opt-in (a placeholder digest skips with a warning) to avoid breaking existing CI until a real digest is supplied.

## Follow-ups (non-blocking)

- Fill the real Encore CLI sha256 to make the download integrity check load-bearing.
- Backfill stagecraft `agentPolicies` rows from `orgId = "default"` to real org ids (the per-org cutover strands legacy rows).
- Land the deployd code change that self-provisions per-namespace RoleBindings, then flip the `rbac.namespaces` default to scoped.
- Set `PLATFORM_ORG_ID` on the desktop so the per-org agent block policy binds.

title: feat(202): approval-velocity governance-drift counter (FR-004) + flip 202 complete
body:
## Spec 202 Slice G: FR-004 approval-velocity counter + flip 202 complete

Final slice of the **Run Blast-Radius Governor** (ASI08). Implements FR-004 and flips spec 202 to `status: approved` / `implementation: complete`.

### What FR-004 does

Bulk rubber-stamping is ASI08's governance-drift signature: an actor clicking APPROVE far faster than any real review of the spec 201 `ApprovalSummary` could take. The counter measures an actor's org-scoped `gate_approved` ratifications per rolling window and surfaces / records anomalous velocity. **Detection-only: records, never blocks an approval** (depth of approval policy is org-filed, the spec 198 FR-013 posture).

### Design (as-built refinements of the plan sketch, documented like Slices D/E/F)

- **Surface, not hash.** Velocity is a read-only `approvalVelocity` field on the `GET .../approval-context` response, **not** folded into the hashed `ApprovalSummary`. It is actor- and time-dependent, so hashing it would break the spec 201 FR-003(b) replay guard. `approvalSummary-pure.ts` (the hashed contract) is untouched.
- **Record on write, measure on read.** The `POST .../approve` path records a `factory.run.approval_velocity_anomaly` audit row after the `gate_approved` insert (fully fail-open, so a detection hiccup can never undo the committed approval). The GET path only measures (read-only, preserving FR-003 preview purity).
- **Org scoping via the run join.** `audit_log` has no `org_id` column, so approvals are fenced to the caller's org by joining `gate_approved` rows (`targetType = "factory_runs"`) to `factory_runs`. The join filters `targetType` explicitly as defense-in-depth.
- **Thresholds are platform config** (`STAGECRAFT_FACTORY_APPROVAL_VELOCITY_WINDOW_SEC` / `_THRESHOLD`, defaults 60s / 10), the same posture FR-003(c) landed with.

### Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `approvalVelocity-pure.ts` | NEW: env readers + pure classifier (`anomalous = count >= threshold`) |
| `approvalVelocity.ts` | NEW: `measureApprovalVelocity` (read-only) + `detectApprovalVelocity` (records), both fail-open |
| `approvalSummary.ts` | refined: `approvalVelocity` response field + the two call sites |
| `auditActions.ts` | `FACTORY_RUN_APPROVAL_VELOCITY_ANOMALY` constant |
| `vite.config.ts` / `CLAUDE.md` | encore-lane test entry + env-knob docs (covered by Slice F edges) |
| `approvalVelocity-pure.test.ts` / `approvalVelocity.test.ts` | pure (bare vitest) + DB integration (encore lane) |

### The `implementation: complete` flip and the AC-6 residual (honest disclosure)

All five FRs have landed (PR1 #469, C #472, D #481, E #486, F #492, G this PR). The flip is user-ratified (2026-07-01). One acceptance criterion is **not** fully discharged and is recorded honestly rather than hidden:

> **AC-6 pt2** (subsume `FactoryPipelineState.total_tokens` into the meter's `tokens` axis so no two token accumulators coexist) is a tracked follow-up, **PR1b**. As of this flip, `total_tokens` + `add_tokens()` still exist in `crates/factory-engine/src/pipeline_state.rs` and are wired in `bin/factory_run.rs`, read for a diagnostic `eprintln!` only. This is a redundant-counter cleanup, **not** a governance behavior gap: the `RunBudgetMeter` tokens axis (FR-002) is already the authoritative accumulator. AC-6 pt1 (retire the `max_total_tokens` stub) landed in PR1.

The disclosure is threaded through the `implementation:` frontmatter comment, spec.md's "Implementation status (AC-6 residual)" callout, the FR-004/Sequencing notes, and plan.md's Slice B pointer + Summary.

### Evidence (local)

- `spec-spine couple`: **OK, 10 paths, no drift** (`make ci-spec-code-coupling`)
- `spec-spine index check`: **fresh**; both `.derived/**/by-spec/202-*.json` shards regenerated and committed
- `tsc --noEmit`: **zero errors in touched files** (14 pre-existing env-noise errors in unrelated modules)
- Pure test: **10/10** (`npx vitest run approvalVelocity-pure.test.ts`)
- DB integration test: **encore-lane (CI-only)**, same posture as Slice F #492 (local env has no live Postgres)

### Review

Two decorrelated reviewers (correctness/security + spec-coherence/CONST-005), each finding adversarially verified:
- **Correctness reviewer: APPROVE WITH NOTES.** Verified fail-open contract, join-cast safety, boundary logic, test validity, GET-path purity. Applied its `targetType`-filter defense-in-depth suggestion.
- **Coherence reviewer: caught a real blocker** (the tracked codebase-index shard was not yet regenerated for the new edges) plus a plan.md Slice B stale-AC-6 claim and a prose `Status: Draft` line. **All three fixed** in this PR.

### Deferred (tracked, non-blocking)

- **PR1b** (AC-6 pt2): remove the vestigial `total_tokens` accumulator.
- **`audit_log` composite index** `(actor_user_id, action, created_at)`: both this counter and the queue-storm gate add unindexed `audit_log` query shapes; a `CREATE INDEX` migration deserves its own PR. Failure mode today is latency at scale on a HITL surface, not correctness.

title: feat(202): queue-storm detection at run submission (FR-003c, detection-only)
body:
## Slice F of spec 202 (Run Blast-Radius Governor): FR-003c queue-storm gate

Platform-side runs-in-flight counter at factory-run reservation. Fourth ASI08 detector after FR-002 budgets (#469), FR-003b oscillation (#481), FR-003a intent-dedup (#486). This is the first spec-202 code in stagecraft.

### What it does
A new `api/factory/queueStormGate.ts` counts the submitting org's in-flight `factory_runs` (`queued` + `running`, served by the existing `factory_runs_org_in_flight_idx` partial index) inside `reserveRunCore`, after the idempotent fast-path and before the substrate load. At or over the configured ceiling it emits `log.warn` + a `factory.run.storm_detected` audit row; the run is still admitted. The staleness sweeper (`runsScheduler.ts`) is untouched.

### Detection-only by design (locked decision)
The spec's FR-003c body calls it "a count gate", but the Sequencing says "(c) detection-only ... thresholds from platform config until the envelope carries them ... behind a non-blocking flag." Since the ceiling is platform config (`STAGECRAFT_FACTORY_MAX_RUNS_IN_FLIGHT`, default 25), not an admitted `budgets:` envelope value, refusing on it would block work the org never admitted. So this slice detects (log + audit) and admits; enforcement (a 429-class refusal) is deferred to the envelope-carried threshold, the same cross-cutting follow-up budgets/oscillation/intent-dedup already defer. The spec.md FR-003c body is amended to record this, superseding the plan-time 429 sketch (kept visible in a `<details>` block).

### Review (decorrelated finder + adversarial verification)
Applied before commit:
- **Fail-open** (my finding): the module doc claimed "never throws, never blocks" but the two awaited DB ops had no try/catch. Wrapped so a detection error is logged (via `errorForLog`) and swallowed; the reservation is never blocked by its own observation.
- **W1** (finder): the audit row paired `targetType: "factory_runs"` with an org id. Fixed to `targetType: "organization"` (webhook.ts precedent) so `(targetType, targetId)` resolves consistently.
- **W2** (finder): the fail-open catch logged a raw `unknown`; switched to `errorForLog(err)` (pat.ts idiom) so the one diagnostic this path has is informative.

Verified clean: detection-only integrity (idempotent replays skip the count), count correctness (excludes terminal states, correct ceiling boundary), coupling frontmatter (multi-`refines` on the co-authored `runs.ts` follows the spec-200 precedent), CONST-005 (honest refinement).

### Gates (local)
- `make pr-prep` coupling gate: **OK, 8 paths, no drift** (the co-authored `runs.ts` edge is accepted).
- `tsc --noEmit`: 14 errors, all pre-existing and unrelated (missing `@opc/carrier-gate` / `libsodium-wrappers` in local `node_modules`); **zero** referencing the new files.
- `vitest` (bare): 610 pass; the new `queueStormGate.test.ts` is correctly excluded (encore-test-only).
- **encore-lane DB integration tests are CI-verified** (the local encore-test env is missing the same two packages; this matches the established posture for prior stagecraft slices).

### Deferred (tracked, not blockers)
- Enforcement (429) rides the envelope-carried threshold, part of the shared "thread declared envelope values through the detectors" follow-up.
- Pre-existing: `stagecraft/CLAUDE.md` "Reference" points at a non-existent `docs/encore-ts-reference.md` (unrelated doc drift, left for a separate fix).
