title: fix(220): broker `secrets: write` so FR-003 can set OAP_SIGNING_KEY
body:
## What

The stagecraft Create flow's FR-003 signing-key provisioning (spec 220, merged in #485) 403'd on the first live scaffold. The GitHub App installation token was brokered with `{contents, administration, actions, workflows}` but **not** `secrets`, so `provisionTenantSigningKey` -> `setRepoActionsSecret` failed at `GET /repos/{repo}/actions/secrets/public-key` with `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, fail-closing the scaffold before commit #1 (repo created, never pushed, job orphaned).

GitHub governs `/repos/{repo}/actions/secrets/*` under the dedicated `secrets` fine-grained permission, **not** `actions`. The `tenantSigningKey.ts` comment claiming `actions: write` sufficed was wrong; the unit tests mock `fetch`, so only a live create surfaced it.

## Change

- `create.ts`: add `secrets: "write"` to the brokered installation token.
- `tenantSigningKey.ts`: correct the permission comment.
- spec 220 FR-003: document the `secrets` permission prerequisite; a dated status note records the live AC-2 attempt-1 finding (the prior "the code path is complete" claim was falsified by the live run).

## Also required (not code)

The OAP GitHub App must be granted the **repository** "Secrets: Read and write" permission, and the org owner must approve it on the `stagecraft-ing` installation. Repository-level only; the org Secrets permission is not used by this flow. If the App still lacks it after this merges, the brokered token exchange fails cleanly with **422** instead of the 403.

## Closing spec 220 AC-2

After this merges and deploys:
1. Delete the orphaned empty repo `stagecraft-ing/cert-ac2-demo` (or use a new name on retry).
2. Retry Create -> the born-with CI emits a governance certificate the spec 209 verify step accepts green -> 220 flips to `complete`.

## Tests

- `tenantSigningKey.test.ts` 5/5 pass (unchanged; they mock `fetch`).
- Coupling gate: `spec-spine couple: OK, no drift`.

title: feat(202): intent-hash dedup detector via peer envelope field (FR-003a)
body:
## Slice E of spec 202 (Run Blast-Radius Governor): FR-003a repeated-near-identical-intent detection

Closes the FR-003a signature (a) of ASI08 fan-out detection. Third detector in the family after FR-002 budget metering (#469) and FR-003b oscillation (#481).

### What it does
An `IntentDedupGate` (peer `PreStepGate`) hashes each dispatched step's `goal_id + normalize(instruction)` (step id **excluded** so dynamically-generated near-twin steps collide, mirroring `derive_goal_id`) and pauses the run fail-closed when one signature recurs past its ceiling. Composes with `BudgetGate` + `OscillationGate` via `ChainedPreStepGate` on the CLI dispatch path and all four OPC chains (fresh/resume x governed/ungoverned).

### Design decision (peer field, not a budget axis)
The intent-repeat threshold is a **peer envelope field** (`IntentDedupThreshold`), not a `RunBudgetAxis` variant. Same reasoning `run_budget.rs` documents for oscillation: the six axes are monotonic run-total accumulators bound into the certificate's per-axis consistency invariant; a windowed per-signature repeat count is non-monotonic and stays a peer field. The spec's FR-003 preamble is **amended honestly** to record that signature (a), like (b), is a peer field, refined against the oscillation precedent rather than the `budgets:` axis it originally proposed (this is a code-reality refinement, not spec-as-obstacle drift, per CONST-005).

### AC-7 schema lockstep
Governance-envelope schema bumps **1.2.0 -> 1.3.0** in both the YAML (`governance-envelope.schema.yaml`) and the Rust twin (`GOVERNANCE_ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION`), plus the `sibling_contract_schema_versions_are_pinned` literal, all in this changeset.

### Review (2 decorrelated finders + adversarial verification)
Every finding verified before applying. Resolved in-PR:
- **Off-by-one (`>` vs `>=`)**: confirmed *correct* -- `IntentDedupGate` follows `BudgetGate`'s `actual > ceiling` ceiling convention with the documented §Code reality 4 one-step overshoot (the `>=` sibling is `OscillationGate`'s streak model, a different quantity). Added a doc note to preempt the confusion.
- **Blank/whitespace-only instruction collision**: added a guard so an instruction normalizing to empty is a no-op (like `None`), with a test.
- **Non-deterministic breach reporting**: `before_step` now names the worst offender (highest count) deterministically instead of an arbitrary HashMap entry, with a test.
- **Missing wired-through-dispatch coverage**: added `wired_intent_dedup_gate_pauses_dispatch_on_repeated_instruction` proving the real `dispatch_manifest` loop threads `step.instruction` through `after_step`.

Verified clean by the finders: FR-003a compliance, CONST-005 (legitimate refinement), spec-code coupling (all changed paths covered), featuregraph golden (unaffected).

### Gates (local)
- `make pr-prep` coupling gate: **OK, 11 paths, no drift**
- `cargo test -p factory-contracts -p orchestrator`: **all pass** (fc 143, orch 172 lib + integration)
- `cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo check --workspace`: clean

### Deferred follow-ups (not blockers, tracked)
- Declared (non-default) `intent_dedup:` / `oscillation:` / `budgets:` envelope values are not yet threaded through the live gates (all call sites use `apply_*_default(None)`, platform-default fail-closed). Pre-existing cross-cutting gap shared by all three detectors; a single follow-up should thread declared values for all.
- `plan.md` Slice A text overstates AC-7 enforcement (claims schema-parity 125/191 enforces the governance-envelope YAML<->Rust parity; it actually checks the unrelated spec-124 `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION`). The real guard is the pinned-literal test. Pre-existing Slice A wording; a small spec-correction PR should fix it.

title: feat(224,143): revive the factory-runs staleness sweeper on self-hosted via a K8s CronJob
body:
## What

Revives the **spec 124 factory-runs staleness sweeper** on the self-hosted target, and lands the new **spec 224** that spec 143 §12 **FU-003** mandated.

Encore's `CronJob` primitive is a silent no-op without Encore Cloud, so the `factory-runs-staleness-sweeper` has never fired on Hetzner. Stuck `queued`/`running` rows are never recovered, which surfaces as permanently-stuck runs in the OPC Runs tab (the OPC "Idle"/"Processing" confusion + the D2 factory stall). The sweep logic (`sweepStaleFactoryRuns`) already existed and was correct; only the self-hosted scheduling path was missing.

This mirrors exactly what spec 143 FR-010 did for its own orphan sweeper.

## Changes

- **`specs/224-self-hosted-sweeper-cron-revival/`** (new sibling spec). Delivers the factory leg (FR-001..005), codifies the systemic rule (FR-006: any Encore `CronJob` on a self-hosted target MUST provision a sibling K8s CronJob), and **stages** the spec 115 extraction + spec 087 connector-sync legs as FR-007/008 so the systemic finding stays in one spec.
- **`api/factory/runsScheduler.ts`**: the sweep endpoint flips to `expose:true` + `validateM2mRequest(…, "platform:factory:sweep")`; a new parameterless `-cron` endpoint serves the local-dev Encore cron. Shared kernel; `sweepStaleFactoryRuns` unchanged.
- **`cronjob-factory-runs-sweeper.yaml`** + **`external-secret-factory-sweeper.yaml`**: new Helm templates mirroring the knowledge sweeper (15m cadence, per-purpose Secret, no cross-purpose mount; ExternalSecret only under the `eso` provider).
- **`setup.sh`**: factory-sweeper Secret + required-var gate + Rauthy client instructions. Terraform + `.env.example` already carried the `STAGECRAFT_FACTORY_SWEEPER_*` slots (FU-003 pre-staged them).
- **spec 124**: amendment callout + `amended`/`amendment_record` recording the revival.

## Deploy-time prerequisite (operator action)

This depends on **#480** (the gateway M2M-auth fix) having reached the cluster. Before the CronJob can run, the operator must create the `stagecraft-factory-sweeper-m2m-app` Rauthy client with **Default Scope** `platform:factory:sweep` (not just Allowed Scope, per spec 143 §12 L-006) and fill `STAGECRAFT_FACTORY_SWEEPER_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET` in `.env`, then run `setup.sh`.

## Gates

- `spec-spine compile`: 225 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-lint`: exit 0
- coupling gate: clean (7 paths, no drift)
- `helm lint` + `helm template`: clean; ExternalSecret correctly gated (skipped under `k8s`, rendered under `eso`)
- featuregraph golden regenerated (spec 224 node)
- `tsc`: zero new errors (the 12 present are pre-existing `@opc/carrier-gate` + stale-codegen noise)

## Test posture

No new endpoint test: the sweep kernel is covered by `runsScheduler.test.ts` and M2M auth by `m2mAuth.test.ts`; the thin `expose:true` wiring is an exact mirror of the knowledge sweeper's `runOrphanImportedSweep`, which is itself untested at the endpoint layer. Matching that established posture.

title: fix(124): remove XDG_DATA_HOME data race in replay-queue tests
body:
## Summary

The OPC replay-queue tests isolated their spool directory by mutating the process-global `XDG_DATA_HOME` via `std::env::set_var`. That is a data race against every sibling test that reads any env var concurrently (UB in Rust 2024). It flaked `run_emitter_spools_to_disk_when_disconnected` in the merge queue, where the full desktop test binary runs, repeatedly ejecting product-touching PRs.

This routes the queue directory through a synchronized, panic-safe test override instead of env:

- `ReplayQueueDirGuard` (RAII) acquires the serialization lock and installs an in-process directory override; on drop it clears the override and releases the lock, so a panicking assertion cannot strand a deleted temp dir.
- The path precedence is split into a pure `resolve_replay_queue_dir(...)` with a lazy data-dir fallback, so the honours-XDG test drives it by argument and the production short-circuit is preserved.
- Production `replay_queue_dir()` is byte-identical in non-test builds: `XDG_DATA_HOME`, then `dirs::data_dir()`, then `temp_dir()`. The override branch is `#[cfg(test)]` only. No `unsafe`, no `std::env::set_var`, and no environ mutation remain in either file.

Hardening from local adversarial review: poison-resilient override locks (`unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())`), `#[must_use]` on the guard, and a new test that drives `replay_queue_dir()` through the override branch to restore entrypoint coverage.

## Testing

- `cargo test --manifest-path product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib` -> 185 passed, 0 failed (was 184; +1 new coverage test).
- The four replay-queue tests pass individually.
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- -A dead_code -D warnings` -> clean (CI-matched).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Test-harness-only stabilization. Replaces process-global XDG_DATA_HOME mutation (UB against concurrent env readers) with a synchronized in-process test override. No production behavior or contract change; replay_queue_dir precedence is byte-identical in non-test builds. Touches only #[cfg(test)] isolation code plus a behavior-preserving refactor. Editing one of the ~13 owning spec.md files to document a test detail would be spec pollution.

title: fix(214): auto-provision a preview database for dev/preview tenant deploys
body:
## Problem

With the image-pull chain fixed, `single-simple` finally pulls and **runs**, but
crash-loops immediately:

```
Error: failed to initialize runtime: unable to initialize sqldb proxy
Caused by: failed to resolve password: environment variable not found
```

The acme-vue-encore scaffold is an Encore app with a `SQLDatabase("app")`, so it
cannot boot without a database. The chart's `previewDatabase` block (spec 214
FR-006) shipped, but **nothing ever set `previewDatabase.enabled`** — a
UI-triggered deploy dispatched with no DB and no external DSN, and the tenant
namespace had only the Deployment + Service (no Postgres).

## Fix (auto-provision for dev/preview; reject otherwise)

Threaded `preview_database` end to end:

- **deployd-api:** `DeployExtras.preview_database` + `DeploymentRequest.preview_database`
  render `previewDatabase.enabled: true` in `build_values`. Two new unit tests;
  `cargo check` + `cargo test` green.
- **stagecraft:** `buildTriggerDeploydBody` sets `preview_database: true` for
  `development` and `preview` environments so an Encore tenant boots
  self-contained (the chart renders the single-replica Postgres + injects the
  `POSTGRES_*` env the Encore runtime resolves). For `staging`/`production` it
  **rejects** the dispatch (they need an external DSN the trigger doesn't model
  yet) rather than deploying a DB-less app — satisfying FR-006's
  reject-when-no-DB requirement for the trigger path. The reject message reaches
  the toast via #465.

The raw `/v1/deployments` proxy is unchanged (external callers manage their own
database); an external-DSN dispatch field is a documented follow-up.

Once merged + deployed, re-triggering single-simple's deploy provisions its
preview Postgres and the app boots.

Coupling gate: clean, no waiver.

title: feat(202): oscillation detector via circuit breaker (FR-003b, AC-2)
body:
## Summary

Spec 202 Slice D (FR-003b, AC-2): wires the previously-unwired `circuit_breaker.rs` into dispatch as a **peer** `OscillationGate`, detecting consecutive retry-heavy steps.

- **Peer, not a 7th axis.** The trip threshold is a new top-level `oscillation:` envelope field (`OscillationThreshold`), not a `RunBudgetAxis`. Rationale: a failure streak resets on success and trips on `>=` within a window, unlike the six monotonic axes; modelling it as an axis would force it into every certificate (via Slice C's `admitted_axis_names` derived from `RunBudgetAxis::ALL`), require a `CERTIFICATE_VERSION` bump, and collide with verify's strict `breached == (actual > ceiling)`. **The certificate is untouched (stays 1.8.0).**
- **`OscillationGate`** (a `PreStepGate`) wraps `CircuitBreakerState` unmodified, composed via `ChainedPreStepGate` alongside the budget gate at all 4 run entry points (CLI both phases with a shared breaker, OPC start + resume, governed + ungoverned arms). `before_step` fails closed when tripped; `after_step` records a "wobble."
- **Detector input is `retry_count`** (user-ratified reframing). The orchestrator halts on the first hard step failure (spec 075 / orchestrator rule 4), so a literal inter-stage failure loop cannot arise; the realizable cross-step signal is consecutive steps that each needed an intra-step retry (`retry_count > 0`) but eventually succeeded. `StepActuals` gains `retry_count`.
- **Envelope schema `1.1.0 -> 1.2.0`** (Rust twin `GOVERNANCE_ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` in lockstep; Tier-B advisory in factory-schema-lockstep). Cert version unchanged.

### Spec coherence
AC-2 amended to state the halt-on-failure reality (inter-stage failure loops precluded; `retry_count` is the input). FR-003 preamble reconciled ("declared as envelope fields": budgets axis for a/c, peer `oscillation:` for b). FR-003b note documents the reframing + the `1.2.0` bump. plan.md Slice D rewritten from the rejected axis design to the delivered peer design. This is a more-truthful amendment (aligned with real dispatch behavior), not a weakening.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p factory-contracts` (139) + `-p orchestrator` (164 lib + integration) green; `cargo build` (3 crates) + OPC `cargo check` (`opc v0.4.0`) green.
- New tests: `apply_oscillation_default_is_tighten_only`, `oscillation_threshold_round_trips`, 2 envelope round-trip tests, `oscillation_gate_trips_after_threshold_wobbles`, `oscillation_gate_resets_on_clean_step`, `chain_fires_oscillation_before_wall_clock_budget` (literal AC-2: trips with wall-clock actual far below its 3600s ceiling), `wired_oscillation_gate_pauses_dispatch_when_tripped` (integration through `dispatch_manifest`).
- `make pr-prep`: coupling clean (11 paths, **zero new frontmatter edges**).

Note: +588 lines trips CONST-004's 500-line soft warn (mode: warn); one cohesive slice across schema + Rust twin + gate + wiring + spec/plan reconciliation.

## Known limitations (tracked)
- The declared `oscillation:` field is not yet threaded to the OPC (every site uses `apply_oscillation_default(None)` = platform default), exactly like the six budget axes today (RunGovernance carries only `envelope_hash`, PR1). Declared-value admission threading is a shared follow-up for all axes + oscillation.
- `window_secs` is platform-fixed this slice (a declared value is ignored; tighten-direction deferred). Documented in the type + schema.

## Local review
Adversarial review (correctness + docs-coherence + cold). Correctness finder cleared all code logic (retry_count threading, inert Err-branch, fail-closed poison, all-4-site wiring, version lockstep). Confirmed + fixed: spec/plan coherence reconciliations (FR-003 preamble, 1.2.0 documentation, plan.md rewrite, FR-003b header) and doc cleanups; removed an unused `OscillationBreach`. Refuted: resume-reset (AC-5 posture), hard-failure-never-trips (the ratified design), threshold-0 deadlock, poison cascade, window-unenforced. Evidence posted as a comment.

title: fix(080,143): auth handler returns null for M2M tokens instead of 401
body:
## Problem

Every platform machine-to-machine seam is broken in production. The
knowledge-orphan-imported sweeper pods `Error` every 30 minutes with
`curl: (22) 401`, and stagecraft logs:

```
JWT rejected: audience mismatch (aud: stagecraft-knowledge-sweeper-m2m-app, expected: stagecraft-server)
```

## Root cause

The Encore **gateway auth handler** (`api/auth/handler.ts`) runs for *every*
request carrying an Authorization header, including the platform's
`expose: true` / `auth: false` M2M endpoints (audit, policy, grants, spec
143's `/internal/knowledge/orphan-imported-sweep`). Those endpoints validate
their own `client_credentials` token via `validateM2mRequest`, but the token's
audience is the caller's own client (not `stagecraft-server`), so the gateway's
session validator (`validateJwt`) returns null and the handler **threw** — 401
before the endpoint's own M2M check ever ran.

## Fix

On `validateJwt`-null, the handler now **returns `null`** (unauthenticated)
instead of throwing. Encore's `authHandler` type is `Promise<AuthData | null>`,
and null is the documented "no authenticated user" signal:

- `auth: true` user endpoints still reject the request (no AuthData → 401).
- `auth: false` M2M endpoints proceed to their scope-checked
  `validateM2mRequest`.

The disabled-user check (spec 080 Phase 6) and the valid-session path are
unchanged. Regression cover in `api/auth/handler.test.ts` (encore lane, since
the module constructs a `Gateway` at import): null-return for a rejected token
and for an expired session cookie, plus AuthData for a valid session JWT.

## Why two specs

Spec **080** owns `api/auth` (the authoring edit). Spec **143** already
documented (§12 L-004) that self-host Encore crons no-op and its sweeper was
moved to a K8s CronJob against the M2M endpoint; this PR adds the empirical
correction that the CronJob fix was insufficient until the auth handler stops
rejecting M2M tokens. **This is the precondition for reviving the spec 124
factory-runs staleness sweeper** as a K8s CronJob (the next follow-up).

Coupling gate: clean, no waiver.

title: fix(214): materialize the ghcr-pull reflector source so tenant pods can pull
body:
## Problem

The `single-simple` tenant deploy dispatched, ran helm, and then timed out
(`context deadline exceeded`) because its pod never became Ready. Root cause on
the cluster: `FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret (ghcr-pull)` and the pull returns
`NotFound` for `sha-0841f821d6e9` — GHCR masks a **private** image as
"not found" when the pull is unauthenticated. The tenant namespace has **no**
`ghcr-pull` secret (only the wildcard TLS cert is reflected in).

## Root cause

Spec 214 FR-005 shipped the reflector-source manifest
`platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/ghcr-pull-secret.yaml`, but the setup.sh step
that materializes it was **never added** (the deferred SC-005 item). So on the
live cluster the `kube-system/ghcr-pull` source secret is absent, reflector has
nothing to clone, and deployd-api renders `imagePullSecrets: [ghcr-pull]` on
every tenant Deployment pointing at a secret that never exists. Every tenant
hits ImagePullBackOff.

The manifest also had a latent bug: it put the raw dockerconfigjson under
`stringData` inside a double-quoted scalar, which cannot hold the JSON.

## Fix

- `setup.sh` builds the base64 dockerconfigjson from `GHCR_PAT` and
  `sed`-substitutes it into the manifest before `kubectl apply` — matching how
  every other credential secret is materialized (cloudflare-api-token,
  rauthy-secrets, ...), so no `envsubst` dependency.
- The manifest's `.dockerconfigjson` moves from `stringData` to `data` (base64).
- kubernetes-reflector then auto-clones `ghcr-pull` into every namespace,
  existing and future, mirroring `tenants-wildcard-tls`.

Verified locally: the rendered YAML parses as a valid `dockerconfigjson`
Secret, and `oap:<PAT>` round-trips through both base64 layers.

## Operational

The live cluster still needs the source secret applied once (setup.sh only runs
at bootstrap); that command is handled separately and will let reflector heal
`single-simple` (and every other tenant namespace) immediately.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `setup.sh` is co-owned by infra specs
(072/106/137/143/151/196/221) via file-level authority, but this change is the
completion of **spec 214** FR-005 (the ghcr-pull materialization for the
manifest 214 establishes), and the edited hunk is in the GHCR-secrets block,
outside every named co-authority region. 214's spec.md carries the authoring
edit; amending an unrelated infra spec purely to satisfy the file-level gate
would be the anti-pattern CONST-005 warns against.

title: feat(204): no-self-ingestion guarantee + session quarantine (freeze)
body:
## Summary

Spec 204 FR-005 (no self-ingestion) + FR-006 (segmentation / quarantine), AC-5.

**FR-005** is enforced by the trusted-boundary model already in place (agent
writes are machine-harvested, trust is derived from the actor, importance is
clamped, promotion is capped). So an agent reading its own harvested memory and
re-storing a paraphrase cannot launder it to a higher trust class. This PR adds
the explicit read-then-rewrite self-ingestion test.

**FR-006** segmentation: cross-project reads are refused at the storage layer
(query/list match `project_scope` exactly). Migration v3 adds a `quarantined`
flag; `getBySession` enumerates a session's writes (a poisoned session may span
projects), `quarantineSession` bulk-quarantines it, `releaseSession` restores it.

**Quarantine is a full FREEZE** (hardened after local review found the gaps): a
quarantined entry is inert pending human review, excluded from every read
(query, list, count, and therefore session injection) and frozen from all
lifecycle housekeeping: not promoted, not decayed, not expiry-swept, and **not
deletable via the agent-facing `memory_delete` tool** (so a poisoning agent
cannot destroy the evidence). Only `releaseSession` restores normal lifecycle.

The operator surface that invokes the quarantine controls (a cockpit review UI)
is future work; this PR delivers the storage-layer primitive and its contract,
consistent with the package's current not-yet-wired state.

Completes the FR surface of spec 204 (the lifecycle flip to approved follows).

## Testing

- 173 session-memory tests green: the freeze (a quarantined entry is not
  counted / promoted / decayed / swept / deleted), a real read-then-rewrite
  no-self-ingestion case, bulk-quarantine + read exclusion + release, the
  quarantined-not-injected integration path, and cross-project isolation.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; coupling gate clean (5 paths, no waiver).
- Adversarial local review caught 1 CRITICAL (agent could delete a quarantined
  entry via memory_delete) + 1 HIGH (expiry sweep / decay / promotion mutated
  quarantined entries); both fixed by the full-freeze model before this PR.

title: feat(204): human-gated retention boundary (write + promotion) + trust-weighted decay
body:
## Summary

Spec 204 FR-003 (AC-3) retention boundary + FR-004 (AC-4) trust-weighted decay.

**The retention boundary is enforced at BOTH the write path and promotion** so
machine-harvested content can never reach a human-gated tier (long-term /
permanent) with no human in the loop:

- `storage.store()` clamps a machine-harvested write to the machine-harvested
  ceiling (`medium-term`). This closes the write-time bypass, which local review
  flagged as the real ASI06 hole: an agent storing at `permanent` via the MCP
  `importance` input, **and the harvester's own builtin rules** (which request
  `permanent`/`long-term` for `note-remember` / `preference-*`), can no longer
  land at a human-gated tier.
- `runPromotion()` refuses to promote a machine-harvested entry across the
  boundary; no sequence of automated accesses reaches long-term/permanent.

Reaching a human-gated tier requires human-curated or verified trust.
`markVerified` is the trusted human-verify action (never exposed via MCP); a
verified entry crosses the boundary and is exempt from decay.

**Trust-weighted decay (FR-004 AC-4):** a pass demotes stale machine-harvested
entries one tier (at most one per horizon) and expires them at the floor.
Human-curated and verified entries are exempt. Decay targets disuse; an accessed
machine-harvested entry is bounded instead by the write-time ceiling.

Builds on the trust classes (PR #474). Next: no-self-ingestion + quarantine.

## Testing

- 168 session-memory tests green: the write-time clamp (agent + harvester
  clamped, human reaches permanent), the promotion boundary (no automated
  sequence reaches a human tier), decay demotion + floor expiry + no-cascade,
  and the human / verified / recently-accessed decay exemptions.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; coupling gate clean (9 paths, no waiver).
- Adversarial local review caught 3 CRITICAL findings (all variants of the
  write-time boundary bypass, including the harvester's builtin permanent-tier
  rules) and they are fixed here before this PR was opened.

title: feat(204): stamp provenance + trust class on every session-memory write
body:
## Summary

Spec 204 FR-002 (provenance stamp) + FR-003 (trust-class schema), AC-2.

Migration v2 adds `actor_kind`, `source_attribution`, `content_hash`, and
`trust_class` to `memory_entries`. It runs in a transaction (ADD COLUMN is not
idempotent, so a crash mid-migration rolls back cleanly); pre-v2 rows are
backfilled with a real SHA-256 on open, made O(1) by a partial index.

Provenance is set at the **trusted storage boundary**, not the agent surface:

- `storage.store()` stamps a sha256 content hash, the origin session id, the
  actor kind, optional source attribution, and a trust class **derived** from
  the actor (human → human-curated; agent/harvester → machine-harvested), and
  validates `actor_kind` at write time.
- The harvester stamps `actorKind=harvester` + a harvest-rule attribution.
- The **untrusted MCP `memory_store` tool** does NOT accept `actorKind` /
  `sourceAttribution` / `sourceSessionId`; it forces the server's trusted
  session, so an agent cannot self-assert `human` to launder its output to a
  higher trust class (FR-005 foundation). `verified` is reachable only through
  an explicit human verify action (a later slice).

Provenance and trust are exposed via the MCP query surface (AC-2). Builds on
PR #473; next is the promotion boundary + trust-weighted decay (FR-003/004).

## Testing

- 153 session-memory tests green: content-hash stamping, actor/trust
  derivation, storage-boundary actor validation, MCP non-laundering, harvester
  provenance, the v1→v2 backfill, migration idempotency, and query exposure.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; coupling gate clean (8 paths, no waiver).
- Adversarial local review caught and fixed 2 CRITICAL (trust laundering via
  an MCP-exposed `actorKind`; non-atomic migration) and 1 HIGH (harvested
  entries mislabeled `agent`) before this PR was opened.

title: feat(204): gate every session-memory write against the shared carrier rules
body:
## Summary

Spec 204 FR-001 on the memory surface: every memory write passes a
deterministic, fail-closed gate before it can be persisted.

- The carrier-class / secret / UTF-8 rules are the SHARED canonical set from
  `@opc/carrier-gate` (the same rules the factory substrate gate enforces, spec
  198), imported not copied. AC-1 is proven by importing the shared
  `CARRIER_FIXTURE` and asserting the memory gate refuses every sample: if the
  two gates ever diverged, that test breaks.
- The memory-specific size ceiling is checked first, so an oversized write
  fails fast before the carrier regexes scan it.
- The gate is wired at `storage.store()`, the single write chokepoint, so an
  explicit `memory_store` and a harvested-signal write routed through `store()`
  are gated identically.
- Content AND tags are gated: both are persisted and re-injected into later
  sessions' prompts (`formatMemoriesForPrompt`), so both carry the poisoning
  risk FR-001 defends against.
- Refusals throw `MemoryWriteRefused` (rule id + detail) and surface
  attributably at the MCP layer as a JSON-RPC error with `data.ruleId`.

Builds on `@opc/carrier-gate` (PR #470). Next: provenance + trust classes
(FR-002/003).

## Testing

- 143 session-memory tests green, including AC-1 shared-fixture parity, the
  byte-based ceiling proven with multi-byte UTF-8, tag gating, the
  harvested-signal path through `store()`, and MCP-layer attribution.

title: feat(202): bind run budget consumption into governance certificate
body:
## Summary

Spec 202 Slice C (FR-005 / AC-4): binds run budget-consumption actuals into the governance certificate, building on the wired governor from #469.

- **Certificate `budgetConsumption` record** inside the signed payload (covered by content hash + Ed25519 signature): `{axis, ceiling, actual, source, breached}` per admitted axis, from the run's `RunBudgetMeter` snapshot at termination. Cert version `1.7.0 -> 1.8.0` (cascades after spec 203 #466 took 1.7.0 for `sbomArtifactBinding`; the shared version-pin test now documents 218=1.6 / 203=1.7 / 202=1.8).
- **`verify-certificate` integrity checks** (after the signature check): per-axis consistency (`breached` iff `actual > ceiling`, finite non-negative magnitudes), completeness derived from `RunBudgetAxis::ALL` (drift-proof, so Slice D's 7th axis auto-extends it), and closed-set (reject unknown / duplicate axis), each with an axis-named diagnostic.
- **`RunBudgetMeter::consumption()`** exports the per-axis snapshot; threaded into OPC start/resume and CLI emission, recovering a poisoned meter (`into_inner`) rather than silently emitting an unmetered cert.
- Backward-compatible: `Option` + `skip_serializing_if=None`, so pre-1.8.0 (unmetered) certs stay byte-identical and still verify.

### Trust model (stated honestly)
verify catches raw byte tamper (signature) and a record made internally inconsistent or structurally malformed. A self-consistent forgery of an `actual` by the signing producer is bounded by the same key-trust model as `corpusBinding` / `sbomArtifactBinding` (a self-signed receipt). FR-005's numeric per-stage corroboration is NOT implemented: the cert's `StageRecord` carries no per-axis token/cost totals to cross-sum, so it needs a data-model change (tracked follow-up).

## Testing
- `cargo test -p factory-engine --lib` = 283 passed, incl. 7 budget tests: verify/round-trip, inconsistent-tamper, missing/unknown/duplicate axis, absent-compat, and a From-path serde-contract test locking `RunBudgetAxis` snake_case to the completeness list.
- `cargo test -p orchestrator` green (`consumption()` test); `cargo check` OPC (`opc v0.4.0`) green.
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (6 paths).

Note: +521 lines trips CONST-004's 500-line soft warn (mode: warn); the change is one cohesive feature, ~370 of it in `governance_certificate.rs` (verify logic + 3 new tests + docs).

## Local review
Adversarial review (correctness + security + cold). 1 MEDIUM (axis-list drift) + LOWs confirmed and fixed (closed-set/finite checks, poison-recovery, honest doc wording, From-path coverage). Refuted: snake_case mismatch, format-args, float-boundary, unwrap-default, None-fail-open (same named-absent model as corpus/sbom), version-bump-rejects-old (by-design). Evidence posted as a comment.

body:

title: feat(202): wire Run Blast-Radius Governor live into factory dispatch
body:
## Summary

Wires the spec-202 Run Blast-Radius Governor (ASI08) live into the factory dispatch path. The `RunBudgetMeter` + `BudgetGate` mechanism (landed in #421 / #424) was unwired until now, so production runs could not fail-closed on a budget breach.

- **Governor is live on every run** under platform-default budgets (`apply_defaults(&[])`): OPC `start_factory_pipeline`, OPC `resume_factory_pipeline`, and the CLI `factory-run` (both phases). On governed runs the budget gate composes AFTER the grant-renewal gate via `ChainedPreStepGate` (grant-first, budget-second, short-circuit on first `Err`); on ungoverned/bypass and CLI runs it rides alone (`BudgetGate` has no grant-chain dependency). Absent budgets are fail-closed, not exempt (FR-001 / FR-002 / AC-3).
- **AC-6 (first half): retire the dead `max_total_tokens`** field from `FactoryEngineConfig` and its six call sites; it was declared, always `None`, and read nowhere. The `total_tokens` / `add_tokens` single-accumulator subsumption (AC-6 second half) is deferred to a focused PR1b (it spans two crates and a serialized checkpoint struct).
- **AC-1 / AC-5 are now real, not just unit-tested**: a wired-dispatch test drives the `ChainedPreStepGate` through `dispatch_manifest` and asserts the run fails closed with an axis-named error on a token breach; the meter remains structurally incapable of self-raising (AC-5).

### Delivered
FR-002 (engine-side metering + circuit break, wired), AC-1 (pause fail-closed), AC-3 (platform defaults on absent budgets), AC-5 (no self-raise), AC-6 first half.

### Deferred (tracked)
- PR1b: `total_tokens` subsumption (AC-6 second half).
- Declared-envelope budgets are not yet threaded to the OPC (RunGovernance carries only the envelope hash today); OPC meters at platform defaults. Certificate binding of consumption actuals is Slice C (FR-005 / AC-4).

## Testing
- `cargo test -p orchestrator` (full suite + new wired test) green; `cargo test -p factory-contracts -p factory-engine` green (incl. integration).
- `cargo check` on the OPC Tauri crate (`opc v0.4.0`) green.

Adversarial review (3 warm finders + cold). One CONFIRMED fail-open (ungoverned OPC runs skipped budget metering) is fixed in this PR by riding the budget gate on the ungoverned arm too, matching the CLI. title: fix(124): render in-flight factory runs as Processing, not Idle
body:
## Problem

The OPC Factory Pipeline history showed genuinely `queued`/`running` platform
runs with an **"Idle"** badge (visible in the reported OPC screenshots).

## Root cause

`list_factory_runs` (`src-tauri/src/commands/factory.rs`) mapped
`factory_runs.status` `queued`/`running` to the literal phase string
`"running"`. The desktop's `FactoryPhase` union (`components/factory/types.ts`)
has no `"running"` member, so `PipelineHistory.tsx`'s `PHASE_BADGE[phase] ??
PHASE_BADGE.idle` fell back to the **Idle** badge for every in-flight run. The
sibling projection `build_status_response_from_platform` in the same file
already maps both to `"process"` — the two functions read the identical field
and disagreed. Latent since the Phase 7 history table landed.

## Fix

Map `queued`/`running` to `"process"` in `list_factory_runs`, matching the
sibling, so an in-flight run correctly renders "Processing". Display-only.

## Scope note

This corrects the **label**. It does not by itself make a stalled pipeline
run its agent — that separate functional issue (the governance grant
handshake never reaching stagecraft, so no stage dispatches and 0 agent
output) is tracked separately and needs the instrumented OPC rebuild +
reproduce to pin down. Takes effect after the next OPC build.

title: fix(215): surface deploy build-body preconditions in the redeploy toast
body:
## Problem

Clicking Redeploy on a gate-enabled environment showed the opaque toast
`{"code":"internal","message":"an internal error occurred","details":null}`,
even though the deployment card below it showed the real diagnostic
(`RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL is required when a tenant access gate is enabled`).

## Root cause

`triggerDeployment` (`api/deploy/deploy.ts`) records the real reason on the
deployment record's `diagnostic` (hence the correct card), but when
`buildTriggerDeploydBody` returns `{ ok: false }` it threw
`APIError.internal(message)`. Encore **sanitizes** `internal` errors to
`"an internal error occurred"` before they reach the client, so the toast lost
the reason.

## Fix

A build-body failure is an unmet deploy **precondition** (missing config), not
an internal fault. Throw `APIError.failedPrecondition(message)` instead, which
Encore forwards to the client verbatim, matching the existing
`image not built yet` precondition throw a few lines up. The record's
`diagnostic` is unchanged. Spec 215 Edge Cases gains a companion amendment
next to the 2026-06-30 timeout-race one.

Coupling gate: clean, no waiver. (The second commit refreshes two
codebase-index shards; the 137 shard was stale on `main` and pr-prep
regenerates it deterministically.)

title: fix(137): wire RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL into stagecraft so gate deploys dispatch
body:
## Problem

With `single-simple`'s access gate enabled, redeploys failed with the
diagnostic **`RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL is required when a tenant access gate is
enabled`**. `deploy.ts` refuses a gate-enabled dispatch unless
`RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL` is set, but the value was **wired nowhere**: it is absent
from the `stagecraft-api-secrets` bootstrap in
`platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh`, so the deployed stagecraft ran with
`RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL=""`. Spec 137 Phase 4 added the requirement; the chart/secret
wiring was never landed.

## The value form is load-bearing

`oauth2-proxy` uses `--oidc-issuer-url` as **both** the discovery base **and**
the expected issuer, and validates the returned `issuer` claim against it
exactly. Verified against live Rauthy:

- issuer claim (root **and** `/auth/v1/` discovery) = `https://auth.stagecraft.ing/auth/v1/`
- the bare host (`https://auth.stagecraft.ing`, the old chart example) would
  pass discovery but **fail** issuer verification.

deployd-api's own M2M path is unaffected because `auth.rs` reads the issuer
from the discovery document rather than trusting the configured endpoint.

## Fix

- `setup.sh`: derive `RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL="${RAUTHY_URL%/}/auth/v1/"` into
  `stagecraft-api-secrets` (env-overridable); consumed via the chart's existing
  `envFrom: secretRef: stagecraft-api-secrets`, so no `deployment.yaml` change.
- `oauth2-proxy-gate` chart: correct the misleading `rauthy.issuerUrl` example
  to the full issuer form.
- Spec 137: empirical correction documenting the wiring and the value form.

## Note

The **live** `stagecraft-api-secrets` still needs the key patched in + a
stagecraft rollout for the running cluster (setup.sh only affects fresh
bootstraps); that operational step is handled separately.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: The only coupling flag is that editing `specs/137/spec.md`
requires an edit to its amender spec 214 (214 `amends: [137]` and claims
137's spec.md as a unit). This change is a 137-internal empirical correction
about RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL, entirely unrelated to 214's chart-supersession
concern; editing 214 here would be an unrelated gate-satisfying edit. The
chart (established by 137) and setup.sh changes are covered by the 137 edit.

title: fix(213): record artifacts only for default-branch push builds
body:
## Problem

The `single-simple` tenant deploy was stuck trying to pull
`ghcr.io/stagecraft-ing/single-simple:sha-8c65109b6020`, an image tag that
**does not exist in GHCR**. The previous session read this as an operational
"missing image" blocker. It is not: it is a phantom `project_artifacts` row.

`8c65109b6020` is the head of an **open, failing Dependabot PR** on
`single-simple` (its `ci` check is red, so it never merged). `main` is still at
`0841f821d6e9`, whose image **does** exist (`sha-0841f821d6e9`, pushed by the
push-triggered `oap-build`).

## Root cause

`handleWorkflowRunCompleted` (`api/github/webhook.ts`) recorded a
`project_artifacts` row for **every** successful `oap-build` run, including
`pull_request` ones, keyed on `run.head_sha`. On a PR run the workflow checks
out the ephemeral merge commit, so its `Push sha tag` step publishes
`sha-<mergesha>` plus the `pr-<n>` alias, **never** `sha-<head_sha>`. So the
recorded row pointed at a tag GHCR never had, and because it was the newest
`builtAt`, `resolveLatestArtifact` selected it over the valid default-branch
image and the pull failed. This contradicts spec 213's own convention: "sha
tags on every default-branch push, pr-N alias tags [on PRs]".

## Fix

- New pure gate `isDefaultBranchPush(run, defaultBranch)`: record only when
  `run.event = push` and `run.head_branch = repository.default_branch`; fail
  closed when the default branch is unknown.
- `webhook.test.ts`: accept path + PR-event / non-default-branch /
  unknown-default / missing-run rejections (the PR-event case is the direct
  regression cover for `sha-8c65109b6020`).
- Spec 213 FR-006, acceptance scenario 1, and a new Edge Case document the
  push-only recording rule and the regression.

## Note

The existing phantom row must still be removed from the live stagecraft DB so
the deploy re-selects `sha-0841f821d6e9`; that operational cleanup is handled
separately. This PR stops new phantoms at the source.

title: fix(214,215): resolve deploy timeout race so failures surface the real reason
body:
## Problem

Redeploying a tenant environment showed **REQUEST_FAILED** with diagnostic **`fetch failed`** after ~5 minutes. \"fetch failed\" is undici's bare transport-error string, so the real cause was invisible.

Empirically root-caused on the live cluster:
- deployd-api is healthy; the M2M token + deployd hops both succeed from the stagecraft pod.
- The tenant pod is in **ImagePullBackOff** (its image is genuinely `NotFound` in GHCR), so `helm --wait` can never converge.
- The PENDING→REQUEST_FAILED gap is **exactly ~5 min** = undici's 300s headers timeout.

## Mechanism

`deployd::create_deployment` holds the HTTP connection open for the whole synchronous `helm upgrade --install --wait`, and stagecraft's `fetch` inherits undici's **300s** headers timeout. With deployd's old **5m** `--wait` default the two ~300s windows raced: when undici lost, stagecraft recorded `REQUEST_FAILED: fetch failed` *before* deployd could return its `FAILED` + helm stderr (which would have named the ImagePullBackOff).

## Fix

- **deployd** (`helm.rs`): default `--wait` timeout drops `5m` → `3m` (still overridable via `DEPLOYD_HELM_TIMEOUT`) so deployd reliably wins the race and its `FAILED` + helm diagnostic reaches the UI. New unit test guards the `<300s` race margin.
- **stagecraft** (`deploydClient.ts`): new `describeTransportError` unwraps `err.cause`, so a genuine transport failure now reads `fetch failed (ECONNREFUSED: ...)` / `fetch failed (UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT: ...)` instead of a bare `fetch failed`. Used in the `REQUEST_FAILED` catch in `deploy.ts`.
- Amends specs **214** (helm-runner timeout edge case) and **215** (dispatch edge cases).

## Tests

- deployd `cargo test helm::` 24/24 (incl. new `from_env_default_helm_timeout_is_under_undici_300s`); `cargo clippy` clean.
- stagecraft `api/deploy/` vitest 39/39 (incl. new `deploydClient.test.ts` covering `describeTransportError`).

## Scope note

This makes deploy failures **legible**. The separate **operational** blocker (the `single-simple` tenant image is not present in GHCR, and `ghcr-pull` is not reflected into the tenant namespace) is a tenant-repo/cluster concern, not OAP code, and is unaffected by this PR. Reported separately.

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `deploydClient.test.ts` is a new test for spec-215 functionality (it tests `deploydClient.ts`, which spec 215 owns). The coupling gate attributes it to spec 160's over-broad `platform/services/stagecraft/**` path claim, not to a real 160 ownership of deployd-client diagnostics; editing 160 would be dishonest coupling. The implementation files (`deploy.ts`, `deploydClient.ts`, `helm.rs`) are coupled to their owning specs 214/215.

title: fix(137): recover Rauthy client secret via POST /clients/{id}/secret
body:
## Problem

\"Enable access gate\" fails with:

> Rauthy admin call failed; gate not enabled: createRauthyClient tenant-gate-… succeeded but response contained no client secret (expected 'secret' or 'client_secret' field). Rauthy admin contract drift — re-run T003 smoke against this Rauthy version to capture the new shape.

The `#458` self-heal (delete + recreate) re-enters the same dead end, so the gate can never go green.

## Root cause (verified against rauthy v0.35.0 source)

`POST /auth/v1/clients` on Rauthy 0.35 returns a `ClientResponse` that has **no secret field at all** (21 fields, none is a secret). The confidential-client secret is exposed only by a dedicated endpoint:

- `POST /auth/v1/clients/{id}/secret` (a POST on purpose so the sensitive read gets a CSRF check), handler `get_client_secret`, **reads** (does not rotate), returns `ClientSecretResponse { id, confidential, secret }`.

The original T003 smoke recorded only create timing plus a GET read-back schema, so it never actually observed a secret on create. The \"capture it from the POST response\" contract was never true on 0.35.

## Fix

- `createRauthyClient` now creates, then reads the secret back from `POST /auth/v1/clients/{id}/secret`. Back-compat: it still tries `secret`/`client_secret` on the create body first, for a forked Rauthy that inlines it.
- New `fetchRauthyClientSecret(clientId)` helper.
- `accessGates` self-heal recovers an orphaned client's secret **non-destructively** via that endpoint, falling back to delete+recreate only if the endpoint yields nothing (recreate rotates the secret, breaking any live gate).
- Corrects spec 137's empirical-contract note with the verified 0.35 shape.

## Tests

- `api/auth/rauthyAdminClients.test.ts`: 21/21 pass. New coverage: 0.35 create→secret-endpoint path, true fail-loud (neither yields a secret), and direct `fetchRauthyClientSecret` (read + 404→null).

## Coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: the spec.md edit is a self-contained correction of spec 137's own Rauthy admin secret-retrieval contract. The coupling gate flags it because spec 214 carries a file-level `amends: 137` unit on specs/137/spec.md (gate-anchor amendment), which is orthogonal to this Rauthy-secret correction; editing 214 would be dishonest coupling.

title: fix: deployd RBAC for tenant chart resources + tenant-gate secret self-heal
body:
Follow-up to #457, driven by the now-visible diagnostics. Two contract-preserving fixes.

## A — tenant deploy was failing on RBAC (the real root cause)
#457's diagnostic surfacing revealed the actual helm error:

> `serviceaccounts "single-simple" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:deployd-system:deployd-api-sa" cannot get resource "serviceaccounts" in namespace "oap-stagecraft-ing-single-simple-dev"`

The `deployd-controller` ClusterRole could manage namespaces, services, secrets, deployments, statefulsets and ingresses, but the tenant chart (acme-vue-encore) also creates a **ServiceAccount** and a Postgres **StatefulSet** (PVCs via volumeClaimTemplates). Added `serviceaccounts` + `persistentvolumeclaims` to the core rule and a read-only `pods` rule for `helm --wait`. The deployd-api CD reapplies this ClusterRole on merge.

## B — "Enable gate" second failure (self-heal)
#457's name-sanitize let the gate provision, exposing a pre-existing state bug: an orphaned Rauthy client from an earlier attempt makes provision return `action='updated'` with no secret, and the descriptor has no prior secret, so the `enabled_requires_secrets` CHECK can never pass. Since Rauthy 0.35 never returns a client secret on GET/PUT, the fix deletes the orphaned client and recreates it to recapture a fresh secret (the recovery the old error told the operator to do by hand).

## Verification
- stagecraft: `tsc` clean; accessGates + rauthy admin tests green (30/30).
- ClusterRole change validated against the live forbidden-resource error.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: contract-preserving fixes (deployd RBAC for chart-created resources; tenant-gate secret recapture self-heal); no owning-spec contract changed.

title: fix: deploy gate + factory flow bugs (Rauthy gate name, Clone&open, deploy diag, governance logging)
body:
Fixes a batch of issues surfaced while exercising the stagecraft → OPC factory flow on the deployed cluster. Each is a contract-preserving bug or diagnostics fix; no spec contract changes.

## What's fixed

**B — "Enable gate" Rauthy 400 (spec 137).** `accessGates.ts` built the tenant-gate Rauthy client name as `Tenant Gate · <env-id>`; the `·` (U+00B7) is outside Rauthy 0.35's name regex `[a-zA-Z0-9À-ɏ-\s]{2,128}`, so the create was rejected and the gate never enabled. Added a `sanitizeRauthyClientName()` boundary helper (applied in `buildTenantGateClientPayload`) plus a clean `-` separator at the call site, and regression tests.

**E — Projects "Clone & open" no-op (OPC).** The handler called `window.location.assign(opc://…)`, which the Tauri webview cannot route to the OS URI handler, so the click did nothing. It now re-emits the same `project-open-request` event the OS deep-link dispatcher fires, landing in the proven Resolve → Clone → Open inbox handoff.

**A — deploy failure was undiagnosable (spec 215).** A failed dev deploy showed only "deployd reported FAILED (see deployd logs)" while the deployd pod logged nothing. deployd-api now `tracing::error!`s the helm stderr it already captured; stagecraft now fetches deployd's `failed` event via the existing `/status` endpoint and stores the real reason as the deploy diagnostic (`DeploydStatusResult.failedReason`).

**D — factory pipeline stalls on "Waiting for agent output" (spec 198).** Instrumentation only: the spawned governance task and `run_governance::establish()` had no entry/phase logging, so a stall left no trace of which phase blocked. Added INFO logging across task start + establish phases so the next reproduce pinpoints the blocking phase. Root-cause fix is a follow-up.

## Verification
- stagecraft: `vitest` rauthy admin (18/18) + deploy (34/34) green; `tsc` clean.
- deployd-api: `cargo check` clean.
- OPC: `tsc` clean; `cargo check` clean.

## Not in this PR
- **C — Google login `invalid_client`**: Rauthy's Google upstream-provider client secret is stale. Rauthy 0.35 gates provider management behind an interactive admin session (API-Key rejected), so it's a manual admin-UI update, not a code change.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: contract-preserving bug + diagnostics fixes (Rauthy gate name sanitize, Clone&open event emit, deploy-failure surfacing, governance phase logging); no owning-spec contract changed.

title: feat(106): self-healing GitHub installation reconcile at login
body:
## Problem
`resolveMembership` reads `github_installations`, which is written **only** by the GitHub App installation webhook (a one-time delivery). A DB reset or a missed webhook leaves a still-installed App invisible, so login dead-ends on the "No connected organization" screen with no self-heal. We hit this immediately after the clean-slate DB reset, and `oap-bootstrap` stand-ups will hit it every time.

## Fix
When `resolveMembership` finds zero active installations, it reconciles from GitHub (the source of truth) before giving up:
- sign an App JWT, `GET /app/installations`, and upsert the org + `github_installations` rows (mirroring the webhook's `installation.created` path), then re-load.
- Best-effort: any GitHub or signing failure logs and returns 0, so login degrades to the existing `no_installed_orgs` path rather than erroring.

Result: a fresh database self-heals on first login instead of requiring a manual webhook redelivery or reinstall.

Spec 106 §13 amendment documents the change (coupling: `membershipResolver.ts` is owned by 106).

## Notes
- Single-file change plus the spec amendment; no schema change.
- Follow-up worth considering: extract the shared org+installation upsert so the webhook and the reconciler stop duplicating it.

title: chore(stagecraft): clean-slate reset prep (db rename, monitor/site removal, baseline fixes, drift gate)
body:
Prepares the deployed stagecraft instance for a clean-slate database reset (purging legacy substrate contamination so create-project works), and folds in adjacent cleanups discovered along the way.

## What's in here
- **DB rename `auth` -> `stagecraft`** across `drizzle.ts`, `infra.config.json`, `STAGECRAFT_DB_URL`, the bitnami `auth.database`, and the drift-guard `psql` check.
- **Remove the Encore uptime-monitor tutorial scaffolding** (`api/monitor`, `api/site`): unused services, their pubsub topics, the slack uptime subscription, the `createdb` bootstrap. `slack.ts` keeps `notify` + the real factory subscription.
- **Baseline fixes** (`1_baseline.up.sql`): add the missing `'cancelled'` to `factory_pipeline_status` (latent runtime bug), drop vestigial `agent_catalog_migration_30_log` + the redundant `project_repos` triple-unique; align `schema.ts` `size_bytes` to `bigint`. Verified: baseline applies clean to a real Postgres (51 tables, seeds present).
- **schema.ts <-> SQL drift gate**: `api/db/schemaDrift.test.ts` (DB-bound) checks every Drizzle table's columns + every pgEnum's labels against the migrated schema. Removes the phantom `check.test.ts` glob and orphaned test-fixtures.
- **Single `infra.config.json` substrate for all clouds** (retire `infra.config.hetzner.json`; repoint Makefile/docker-build/mirrord).
- **Operator state** (kubeconfig + .env) moved out of the repo tree to `$OAP_HETZNER_DIR` (`~/.config/oap/infra/hetzner`); never clobbers `~/.kube/config`.
- **deployd-api**: disable S3 backup projection in `values-hetzner.yaml` so a fresh install starts (the four non-optional `backup-*` secretKeyRefs were the kubelet start blocker); re-enable tracked separately.

## Deploy coordination (IMPORTANT, post-merge)
This PR ships the renamed image but does **not** itself reset the DB. Because the new image expects DB `stagecraft`, the deploy must be coordinated with a one-time DB reset:
1. Merge -> CD `build-and-push` builds the sha-tagged image; the `deploy` job waits on the `production` environment approval.
2. Before approving: `pg_dump auth` (safety) -> scale `stagecraft-api` to 0 -> `CREATE DATABASE stagecraft` -> patch `STAGECRAFT_DB_URL` secret to `/stagecraft` -> `DROP DATABASE auth`.
3. Approve the deploy -> pre-upgrade migrate hook applies the baseline to the empty `stagecraft` -> pods boot. Then re-login + factory Sync.

## CI heads-up
Large surface across many spec-claimed paths, so the spec-code coupling gate will likely flag paths needing spec edits or a waiver.

title: fix(stagecraft): factory-sync + signin + migration-baseline rebuild prereqs
body:
## Summary

Rebuild prerequisites for the stagecraft factory and signin, found during an end-to-end walkthrough of the deployed instance. Four fixes, one commit each; all coupling-clean.

## Fixes

- **#5 `fix(199)`** Factory sync no longer wedges on binary upstream files. `website/` is excluded from ingest in both repos, any NUL-byte file is skipped, and `failRun` sanitizes the error so a poison payload can never block the status transition. Root cause: `template-encore/website/static/img/favicon.ico` aborted the UTF-8 TEXT substrate insert and then the failure-recording write, leaving the run stuck `running` (observed in prod 2026-06-27).
- **#1 `feat(106)`** Signin offers "Continue with Google" (new `/auth/google` route via Rauthy `idp_hint=google`) and drops the enterprise-email SSO box. Backend OIDC endpoints stay for admin-configured providers.
- **#4 `refactor`** Consolidate the 53 stagecraft migrations into a single verified `1_baseline.up.sql`, and purge the legacy `legacy-mixed`/`legacy-template-mixed` source-ids (now `factory`/`template`) plus the aim-vue-node/goa seed. The baseline was generated mechanically (pg_dump of the full-53 run) and verified SCHEMA_IDENTICAL by re-apply + diff. Dangling migration-path claims were removed from 19 specs; the index is clean.
- **#2 `feat(109)`** A `factory_sync_runs` staleness sweeper (cron, every 1 minute) recovers orphaned syncs the CAS guard cannot, mirroring the spec 124 sweeper.

## Verification

- typecheck at baseline (0 new errors); translator suite 12/12.
- migration baseline: SCHEMA_IDENTICAL vs the full 53-migration schema (re-apply + `pg_dump --schema-only` diff, empty).
- coupling gate exits 0 with the waiver below; spec index fresh (0 diagnostics).
- the full `encore test` suite runs in CI.

## Deferred (to the oap-bootstrap rebuild)

The file-format contract (knowledge/requirements Markdown-only; artifacts pdf/docx/xlsx/csv/pptx/pbix/json) and the import-path rebuild are deferred: they need a typed ingest taxonomy (artifact vs knowledge vs requirement) that does not exist in the data model yet, plus a client-coordinated upload API change. They belong with the from-scratch rebuild.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Consolidates the 53 incremental stagecraft migrations into one verified baseline (1_baseline.up.sql) and purges legacy source-id naming ahead of the oap-bootstrap from-scratch rebuild. The deleted migration files are derived artifacts absorbed into the baseline (verified SCHEMA_IDENTICAL by re-apply + schema diff); their owning specs are unchanged and remain the design record, with the now-dangling migration-path claims removed from 19 specs so the index stays clean.

  1. Switch to a new branch from main.
  2. Run npm test to ensure all tests are passing.
  3. Update the version in https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/package.json.
  4. Run npm run build to update the compiled files.
  5. Update this https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/RELEASES.md with the new version and changes in the ## Changelog section.
  6. Run licensed cache to update the license report.
  7. Run licensed status and resolve any warnings by updating the https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/.licensed.yml file with the exceptions.
  8. Commit your changes and push your branch upstream.
  9. Open a pull request against main and get it reviewed and merged.
  10. Draft a new release https://github.com/actions/cache/releases use the same version number used in package.json
    1. Create a new tag with the version number.
    2. Auto generate release notes and update them to match the changes you made in RELEASES.md.
    3. Toggle the set as the latest release option.
    4. Publish the release.
  11. Navigate to https://github.com/actions/cache/actions/workflows/release-new-action-version.yml
    1. There should be a workflow run queued with the same version number.
    2. Approve the run to publish the new version and update the major tags for this action.

title: docs: add factory system current-state map
body:
## Summary

Adds `docs/analysis/factory-system-current-state.md`: a single ground-truth inventory of the factory pathway across three repos (`stagecraft-ing/factory-encore`, `stagecraft-ing/template-encore`, and the in-repo stagecraft service) for the **sync**, **create project**, and **module selection** flows.

The doc surfaces every structural misalignment, legacy remnant, and outdated concept so a remediation plan can be devised against it. Headline findings include:

- Modules declared in four places; the generator honours none of them.
- Two generators (`setup-app.ts` / `setup-dual-app.ts`) that should be one.
- Adapter-name authority split across three gates.
- The substrate now mirrors generator source code it never reads.

Also adds a "Current successor" pointer to the superseded 2026-06-09 `factory-encore-sync-current-state.md` so readers land on the live map.

## Provenance

Assembled from eight read-only investigation agents plus three targeted misalignment hunts across the three repos, with `file:line` citations throughout.

**Supersedes** the 2026-06-09 sync map (predates the spec 199 thin-consumer cutover and the generator-product split). **Companion** to `acme-vue-encore-generator-product-split.md` and `governance-envelope-unification.md`.

title: feat(112): stagecraft two-cache warmup + sha-stamped prebuilds (§5.3.1)
body:
## Summary Implements spec 112 §5.3.1 (generator-product-split scaffold warmup) in stagecraft, and lands the §5.3.1 spec refinement alongside it. - **Two-cache warmup.** Clone factory-encore (`_factory-cache`: generator + module catalog + tsx) and template-encore (`_template-cache`: the `--source` baseline); run the adapter's manifest-declared entry point (`setup-app.ts --profile

--source _template-cache`; `setup-dual-app.ts` for dual). This fixes the live break where warmup ran the moved generator scripts from the template clone. - **Generator-reads-manifest.** The generator reads `profiles[].modules` itself, so warmup passes only `--profile` (no `--with` translation): an `internal` prebuild ships `user-management` because the generator composed it. - **Concurrency-safe prebuilds.** Profile trees are SHA-stamped immutable snapshots (`_prebuilt//`) behind an atomically-swapped `current` pointer, with a single-flight warmup guard and a keep-`{new, previous}` GC. A per-request copy resolves the snapshot once and reads an immutable tree, so a 30-minute refresh can never expose a half-written prebuild to an in-flight copy (the prior in-place rm-then-regenerate could). Per-request `mkdtemp` isolation plus single-pod warmup (RWO PVC, `replicaCount=1`) cover concurrent different-profile creates. - **perRequestScaffold.** Resolves the current snapshot, runs `add-module` from the factory cache, and filters out modules the profile already shipped (read from the copied `template.json`) so a profile default is never double-composed. - **scheduler.** Resolves the factory upstream from the `legacy-mixed` row and adds a `no-factory-source` warmup blocker. Adversarial-review fixes folded in: the PAT is redacted from the spawn-failure error message; the snapshot GC uses a deterministic keep-set; cache shas are validated as hex before use as a path component. ## Testing - `tsc` is clean for the changed files. (The 41 `~encore/* TS2307` errors are the pre-existing `encore.gen` virtual-module gap, generated by `encore gen` in CI, not from this change.) - New `parity.test.ts`: stagecraft's `ensurePrebuilts` produces a tree byte-identical to a direct generator run (internal verified; all four profiles built; public ships no user-management). Self-skips when local factory-encore / template-encore checkouts are absent. - `perRequestScaffold.test.ts` updated to the sha-stamped snapshot layout; the 30 non-DB scaffold tests pass. ## Spec-Drift-Waiver `specs/112-factory-project-lifecycle/spec.md` is reported by the coupling gate as owned by its amenders (138-stagecraft-create-realised-scaffold, 199-factory-thin-consumer-sync, 215-stagecraft-deploy-trigger-ux). This change is a 112 self-amendment refining §5.3.1 (the generator-reads-manifest mechanism and the concurrency-safe prebuild design) and does not change the designs of 138/199/215. The code it touches (`platform/services/stagecraft/api/projects/scaffold/**`) is owned by 112 and changes together with this spec edit. Spec-Drift-Waiver: specs/112 self-amendment (§5.3.1); owners 138/199/215 designs unchanged; the scaffold/ code is owned by 112 and changes with it.

title: factory: amend spec 112 scaffold warmup (generator-product split) + retire dead OAP-native adapter path
body:
## Summary

Two factory-cleanup changes, one self-consistent commit each.

1. **Spec 112 scaffold-warmup amendment** (`docs(112)`, new §5.3.1). The generator-product split moved the generator + module catalog out of `template-encore` into the `factory-encore` adapter, which breaks the create-project warmup: it still runs the generator from the cloned *template* repo. The amendment records the corrected two-cache warmup (clone `factory-encore` for the generator + modules + `tsx`; clone `template-encore` as the `--source` baseline; run the manifest-declared entry point). Factory coordinates resolve from the existing `legacy-mixed` `factory_upstreams` row, so no admission or DB-schema change is needed. Profile module sets become manifest-authoritative. `implementation` flips `complete` to `in-progress`: the spec now describes a fix the code does not yet implement (implementation is a follow-up).

2. **Retire the dead OAP-native adapter path** (`chore(factory)`). Delete `createOapNative.test.ts` (the `next-prisma` / `scaffold_source_id`-probe E2E test for a concept retired by spec 199; `factory-encore` + `template-encore` are OAP's native factory implementation). Remove its now-empty entry from the `vite.config.ts` encore-test exclude list (a glob matching no file fails the lane-coverage guard), keeping `dispatch.test.ts`. Reword a stale OAP-native comment in `scaffold.test.ts`; record the retirement in spec 211's incident log and spec 139's T042.

- `spec-spine compile`: 224 specs, 0 warnings.

title: fix(deps): bump pdf-extract to patched lopdf 0.42 (RUSTSEC-2026-0187)
body:
## Summary

`cargo-deny` started failing on `main` and every open PR after **RUSTSEC-2026-0187** was published: a denial-of-service in `lopdf`. Its `load_mem` / `load*` entry points parse nested PDF arrays and dictionaries with unbounded recursion, so a ~21 KB crafted PDF (a ~10k-deep nested array in the Catalog) exhausts the call stack and aborts the process with `SIGABRT`. Because it is a stack overflow rather than a panic, `catch_unwind` cannot contain it. Fixed in `lopdf` 0.42.0.

`lopdf` is transitive in this tree:

```
artifact-extract -> pdf-extract 0.7.12 -> lopdf 0.34.0
```

`pdf-extract` 0.12.0 is the first release requiring `lopdf ^0.42`, so this bumps `artifact-extract`'s `pdf-extract` requirement from `"0.7"` to `"0.12"`, pulling the patched `lopdf` into both the root and `opc/src-tauri` workspaces. `artifact-extract` uses a single stable API (`extract_text_from_mem`), unchanged across the jump.

## Verification

- `cargo deny check` clean (exit 0) on all three checked manifests: root, `deployd-api-rs`, `opc/src-tauri`. RUSTSEC-2026-0187 no longer fires.
- `artifact-extract` builds in both workspaces; 16/16 unit tests pass.
- Codebase index regenerated (`by-package/artifact-extract`).

## Scope

Project-wide supply-chain fix. Unblocks `main` and every open PR (including #442, the spec-208 propagate PR, which is otherwise green).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: crates/artifact-extract/Cargo.toml and product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.lock change only to bump the transitive pdf-extract/lopdf versions for RUSTSEC-2026-0187. This is a mechanical security dependency bump with no change to spec 120's extraction-stage contract (the only API used, extract_text_from_mem, is unchanged) or to any opc spec's behavior. The root Cargo.lock carries the same transitive bump.

title: fix(ci): narrow opc-bench in-job path guard to benched source (spec 180 FR-T9)
body:
## What

The opc-bench Tier 2 gate's in-job path guard (FR-T9, amended 2026-06-10) skipped the same-runner measurement only when `base..head` touched neither `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/**` (the whole crate directory) nor the workflow. That directory also holds `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, and `tauri.*.conf.json`, so a **deps-only or config-only diff still ran the gate** and stayed exposed to the residual intra-runner temporal variance the 2026-06-10 amendment documents (+28.2% on a zero-opc diff).

This is the class that forced manual intervention recently: the lockfile-only bump #441 ran the gate, and the #437/#438 consolidation needed a branch-protection bypass to land past a spurious regression flag.

## Change

Narrow the in-job benchable set to the **benched source** (`src-tauri/src`), the **bench harness** (`src-tauri/benches`), and this workflow. Deps/config-only diffs now skip the same-runner measurement on both `pull_request` and `merge_group`. The in-job filter is now deliberately **stricter** than `ci.yml`'s `src-tauri/**` route filter, which still dispatches the job (it exits early without measuring).

This is a scoped, documented coverage reduction, **not** silent disablement (spec 180 §5.4): the gate still fires fully on any change to the benched source or harness, and the nightly N=2000 trend (non-gating) remains the safety net for a genuine dependency-driven regression. The threshold (+25%) and the relative-only discipline (FR-T10) are unchanged.

## Spec

`spec 180 FR-T9` carries the dated 2026-06-25 amendment; §5.3 updated to reflect the stricter-than-route in-job filter. The regenerated `180-*` registry + index shards are committed alongside.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: editing `specs/180-opc-shell-codification/spec.md` trips reverse-coupling from non-owning `references:` file-unit edges in specs 181/183/217 (which name 180's spec.md as a referenced unit per spec 156 grammar; non-owning per spec 154 §4). Those specs' contracts are unaffected by an FR-T9 path-guard narrowing; editing them to satisfy the gate would be gratuitous. spec-127 references-edge non-owning waiver, not a spec amendment of 181/183/217.

The workflow file (`.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`) is included in this branch but could not be pushed due to GitHub App workflow permission constraints. **A maintainer must add this file manually** or grant workflows permission. The file content is:

```yaml
name: Deploy docs to GitHub Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["website/**", ".github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: website
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: website/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: website/build
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

title: feat(208): org-agent kill-switch Phase 2 propagate (duplex broadcast + engine ack)
body:
## Spec 208 Phase 2 — Propagate (PR-2, tasks T008-T014)

Phase 1 (#435) made the org-wide halt *enforced* (the `org_halts` record + fail-closed grant/serve/bind/registration consults). Phase 2 makes it *propagated*: a pull now reaches every connected engine, the engine pauses at its next boundary and self-checkpoints before yielding, and acks so the realized propagation bound is an audited fact on the quarantine record (FR-001/FR-003, AC-1, the AC-4 halt-ack leg).

### Server (stagecraft)
- **types.ts (T008):** `org.halt.activated` / `org.halt.lifted` (server) and `org.halt.ack` (client) envelope variants + `ORG_HALT_ENVELOPE_VERSION`. The free-form reason rides the shared `detail` field (the `reason` wire field is the closed nack/resync union); the ack's halt-vs-lift discriminator is `haltKind` (the envelope `kind` is reserved).
- **service.ts (T009/T010):** `broadcastOrgHalt` over the outbox-durable `dispatchServerEvent`, and an inbound `org.halt.ack` arm that appends a per-engine `{clientId, ackedAt, kind}` timestamp to `org_halts.acks` and audits `factory.org_halt.engine_ack`. `clientId` is stamped from the authenticated session, never self-reported on the wire.
- **orgHalt.ts:** `pullHaltCore` / `liftHaltCore` broadcast after the row commits, on a fresh pull only. Enforcement is independent of the broadcast, so a missed broadcast degrades safely to a pause at the next grant renewal; a reconnecting engine replays the halt off the outbox on resync.

### Engine (OPC, Rust)
- **sync_client.rs (T008/T011):** the `org.halt.*` wire twin, `OutboundFrame::OrgHaltAck` + `send_org_halt_ack`, and a mirrored `ORG_HALT_ENVELOPE_VERSION` (build-time skew guard).
- **live_sessions.rs (T012):** halt-aware termination (PD-D), the inverse of force-disconnect: a cooperative `{"type":"halt"}` bridge signal then a self-checkpoint **before** yield, so containment preserves forensic state. Force-disconnect stays the no-ack fallback. Phase 2 acts on the `org` scope only; `project`/`agent-profile` sibling isolation is Phase 3 (AC-3).
- **lib.rs:** registers the `org.halt.activated` dispatch handler at startup (the spec 207 command-registration precedent).

### Tests
- DB-bound (stagecraft, encore lane): the AC-4 halt-ack leg (per-engine timestamp + `engine_ack` audit) and cross-org isolation. 19/19 in `orgHalt.test.ts` pass (16 Phase-1 preserved + 3 new).
- Rust unit: envelope-version lock, ack wire-shape, and the halt-vs-abort IPC distinction. `cargo check`/clippy clean, 4/4 new tests pass.
- `tsc` clean, schema-parity green (envelope v=2), coupling gate green with the waiver below.

The engine-side three-session pause/refuse/reconnect integration is the FR-005 drill (Phase 5); AC-3 scope-lattice and the lift-ack/reintegration leg are Phase 3.

### Notes
- `web/app/lib/client.ts` is the generated Encore client. Regenerating it for the new duplex surface also catches up the Phase-1 `pullHalt`/`liftHalt` verb endpoints that #435 left ungenerated (its committed copy had none), which is why that diff is larger than PR-2's hand-written surface.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: web/app/lib/client.ts is the generated Encore client regenerated for the new duplex envelope surface (spec 160 owns the path; PR-2 does not change its domain). commands/factory.rs gains only halt_id/scope/scope_key None in three ServerEnvelopeWire test constructors, mechanical collateral of the wire-struct field addition declared in the 208-owned sync_client.rs.

title: fix(ci): force same-runner checkouts in opc-bench baseline (spec 180 FR-T9)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a deterministic bug in the spec-180 opc-bench same-runner harness. After `cargo bench` on the base commit rewrites `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` (when the base lock is bench-incomplete), the non-forced `git checkout --detach "$HEAD_SHA"` aborts with *"local changes would be overwritten by checkout"*, hard-failing the job and `ci-gate` on a harness fault rather than a code regression.

Both same-runner checkouts now pass `--force`, discarding build-induced lockfile churn before the commit switch. The benchmark, the +25% threshold, and the relative-only discipline (FR-T10) are unchanged.

Surfaced by the dependabot-consolidation PR #437, which hit this deterministically (its head lock was bench-complete; the `main` base lock was not) while its 6.8 ms benchmark passed under the threshold. Unblocks #437 on rebase.

## Testing

- Diagnosed from CI logs: the benchmark passed (6.8 ms); the failure was `git checkout` aborting on a cargo-modified `src-tauri/Cargo.lock`. Confirmed deterministic (failed identically on rerun).
- spec 180 FR-T9 carries the dated amendment (2026-06-24) documenting the fix; `make pr-prep` regenerated the registry + index shards.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: spec 180 self-amendment (FR-T9 force-checkout harness robustness fix) plus the workflow it establishes (ci-opc-bench.yml), both edited together in this PR. The lone remaining coupling hit is specs 181/183/217 reverse-coupling via their references/refines edges to specs/180/spec.md (181 references it as its canonical regression case; 183 refines spec 180; 217 amended it during the engine swap), not a real authority edit; those specs need no change for a prose amendment to spec 180. spec-127-FR-005 reverse-coupling waiver, not a spec edit to satisfy a gate.
