title: feat(222): registry-shard freshness gate (PR-time staleness block for by-spec shards)
body:
## Summary

Closes the silent-drift hole this session surfaced: PR #422 squash-merged a refined spec 208 while landing a registry shard generated from an earlier draft, and it merged undetected because `spec-conformance.yml` runs `spec-spine compile` **only as a smoke test** (it proves the registry emits, then discards the result). There is no native check verb either: `spec-spine compile` has no `--check`, and the `registry` consumer surface is read-only.

This adds a PR-time + `merge_group` freshness gate: recompile, then `git diff --exit-code .derived/spec-registry/by-spec/`, failing on any drift with an actionable message.

### Why a gate here is safe (and not a re-run of the 188 tension)
- Spec 188 moved **broad codebase-index** freshness post-merge because the *monolithic* `index.json` carried one global hash and caused O(N²) cross-branch conflicts.
- Spec 217 re-committed the registry as **conflict-free per-spec shards**; each shard is a pure function of its own `spec.md` (only outbound relationship edges, no inbound backlinks — verified). Different branches editing different specs never collide.
- So this is the registry analogue of **spec 184's narrow `claude-config` slice** (a conflict-free PR-time block on a committed governance artifact), not of 188's broad gate.
- **Index shards stay out of scope on purpose**: their input set is broad (every `Cargo.toml`/`package.json`/workflow/`​.claude/**`), so gating them *would* reintroduce 188's churn. Registry shards are cheap to gate because their only input is the owning `spec.md`. The spec's Out-of-scope section documents this boundary.

### Changeset
- `specs/222-registry-shard-freshness-gate/spec.md` (new spec; `extends:` 177 workflow + 034 golden)
- `.github/workflows/spec-conformance.yml` (the gate step, right after the existing compile)
- `.derived/spec-registry/by-spec/222-*.json` + `.derived/codebase-index/by-spec/222-*.json` (new shards)
- `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` (new 222 row)

The mechanism is a git-layer equality check, not JSON parsing, so it stays within `governed-artifact-reads.md` (no `python`/`jq`/`awk`/`sed` over `.derived/**`).

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 223 specs, 0 warnings.
- `spec-spine lint`: 0 errors (10 pre-existing L-001 warnings on other specs; none on 222).
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (3 paths checked, 0 drift); codebase-index regenerated.
- Featuregraph golden regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`; the 222 row is present and the golden test passes.
- Gate self-test: `git diff --exit-code -- .derived/spec-registry/by-spec/` is clean after a fresh compile (a fresh compile reproduces the committed shards byte-for-byte). The drift-detection direction is the same `git diff` that surfaced the original #423 shard drift earlier in this session.

Note: the new step runs from the merge-queue instance onward (GitHub resolves `pull_request` workflow definitions from the base branch); the changeset is internally consistent regardless, so the PR is clean either way.

title: feat(208): org-agent kill-switch Phase 1 enforce (org_halts + fail-closed seams)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 (PR-1) of spec 208 (Org-Wide Agent Kill Switch, ASI10 containment). The admin-gated org halt verb and its fail-closed enforcement, composing primitives that already ship (revocation check sites, run-grants, duplex) rather than adding a parallel control plane.

First of four PRs driving 208 to conclusion (Phase 4 / NHI credential closure stays deferred behind spec 205):
- **PR-1 (this) — Enforce**: `org_halts` record + verb + fail-closed seams.
- PR-2 Propagate: duplex broadcast + OPC halt-aware termination.
- PR-3 Scope/reintegrate: scope-lattice proofs + staged lift (+ closes the #433 reintegrating-enforcement AC gap).
- PR-5 Drill: e2e pull-and-lift in the nightly lane.

### What lands
- **`org_halts` quarantine record** (migration 53): a partial UNIQUE index on the active `(org_id, scope, scope_key)` is both the liveness lookup and the one-active-halt-per-scope backstop.
- **`pullHalt` / `liftHalt` verb**: `factory:configure` + human-actor gate (service identity rejected, AC-4 leg); transactional row+audit; idempotent pull; `halted -> reintegrating` lift as a compare-and-swap.
- **`isHaltedInScope`** wired fail-closed at the three reused check sites: grant issuance/renewal, new-session registration, serve/bind.
- **Scope**: org + project enforce in Phase 1; **agent-profile is rejected at the verb** until a profile-carrying seam lands (no false containment). FR-002 ships the degraded grant+session path (keyless posture, 198 FR-014).

### Acceptance (Phase 1 legs)
- **AC-2**: grant issuance and renewal refused under a halt, naming the quarantine record (DB-bound tests drive the real handlers).
- **AC-3** (org+project legs): project-scope precision proven (a sibling halt leaves the grant working; a same-project halt refuses). The agent-profile leg moves to the phase that adds its seam.
- **AC-4** (Phase 1 leg): lift requires a human actor; a service / cross-org identity is rejected.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean across the stagecraft service.
- Coupling gate (`make pr-prep`): 14 paths checked, no drift.
- DB-bound `orgHalt.test.ts` (encore-test lane, spec 211, live DB): scope-lattice matrix, verb lifecycle + audits, end-to-end grant refusal + project-scope precision.
- Local adversarial review (4 decorrelated finders + refuters): 6 findings confirmed and fixed in this PR; 2 refuted; 7 in the trade-offs ledger (see the Local Review Evidence comment).

  • timeout: add DeadlineBody for non-resetting body timeouts, applied via the new RequestBodyDeadlineLayer and ResponseBodyDeadlineLayer (#688)

    Unlike TimeoutBody, which resets its deadline on every frame, DeadlineBody caps the total time of a body transfer. A slow client trickling one byte at a time never trips an idle timeout but will trip a deadline.

    use std::time::Duration;
use tower::ServiceBuilder;
use tower_http::timeout::RequestBodyDeadlineLayer;

    // Abort the request body transfer after 30s total, regardless of how
    
// frequently data arrives.
    
let service = ServiceBuilder::new()
    
.layer(RequestBodyDeadlineLayer::new(Duration::from_secs(30)))
    
.service_fn(handler);

title: docs(208): record halt-pull authz AC gap + re-halt transition in plan.md
body:
## Summary

CI ai-review on #423 raised three design observations about the merged spec 208. Verified each against the actual spec text and recorded the two genuine ones in `plan.md`'s existing `Known gaps and their carriers` list (spec.md delegates refinement to plan.md; plan.md is not a registry-shard input, so no shard churn):

1. **Halt-pull authorization has no negative-test AC.** FR-001 requires `factory:configure`; AC-4 gives the *lift* path a negative test (service identity rejected) but there is no symmetric AC for the *pull* path. Carrier: add the AC alongside the halt-verb tasks. Authorization is already specified in FR-001, so this is a test-coverage gap, not a design hole.
2. **Re-halt during `reintegrating` is implied, not drawn.** The record-based model already fails closed (a `reintegrating` scope is still enforced; a second halt writes another record), but the diagram shows no explicit `reintegrating to halted` re-assertion. Carrier: make it explicit when PD-E resolves the `org_halts` record shape.

The third review point (spec-205 degraded mode "invisible") is **not** recorded: FR-002 and Out-of-scope already document degraded mode thoroughly; only the one-line summary omits it, which is expected for an abstract.

No FR, AC, or relationship edge changed; this is plan.md narrative only.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: no registry-shard change (plan.md is not a shard input).
- `make pr-prep`: codebase-index regenerated (0 errors), coupling gate clean (1 path checked, 0 drift).

title: feat(202): RunBudgetMeter + budget PreStepGate mechanism (Slice B core)
body:
## Spec 202 Run Blast-Radius Governor: Slice B (core mechanism)

FR-002 (engine-side metering + circuit break), landed as the self-contained
`orchestrator` mechanism. Follows Slice A (#421: RunBudget* types + envelope
schema 1.1.0).

### What this delivers

- **`RunBudgetMeter`** accumulates the per-step actuals the dispatch loop
  already collects (tokens, cost, `num_turns`, dispatched-step count, run-level
  wall-clock) against the admitted per-run ceilings produced by Slice A's
  `apply_defaults`.
- **`BudgetGate`** wraps the meter behind the existing `PreStepGate` trait:
  - `after_step` records each completed step into the meter.
  - `before_step` fails the next step **closed** when a ceiling is exceeded,
    with an error naming axis, ceiling, and actual (**AC-1**).
  - The meter exposes no ceiling-raising method, so a run cannot loosen its own
    budget (**AC-5**).
- **`ChainedPreStepGate`** composes the budget gate with `GrantRenewalGate`
  (spec 198 FR-005) without changing the single-`Option` `pre_step` dispatch
  API.
- **`PreStepGate::after_step`** is a new defaulted (no-op) trait method wired
  into both dispatch loops; existing gates (`GrantRenewalGate`) inherit the
  default unchanged, so there is zero behavior change for current runs.

`orchestrator` takes a leaf, acyclic `factory-contracts` dependency for the
`RunBudget*` types.

### Tests

10 `budget_gate` unit tests (token / spawned-agents / tool-invocations breach,
under-ceiling pass, file-mutations-never-breaches, AC-5 no-self-raise, platform
defaults, chain short-circuit / forward / compose) plus 1 dispatch-loop
integration test proving `after_step` fires per completed step. Clippy clean.

### Scope boundary (deferred to the follow-up slice)

This PR ships the **mechanism**, not its installation on production dispatch
paths. Deferred:

- Installing `BudgetGate` on the CLI (`factory_run.rs`) and OPC dispatch paths.
- **AC-6** dead-stub discharge (`FactoryEngineConfig.max_total_tokens`,
  `FactoryPipelineState.total_tokens`), which crosses into the **standalone OPC
  crate** (it reads `total_tokens`) and wants the default ceilings validated
  against real-run telemetry before hard enforcement lands (the
  `tool_invocations` axis approximates summed `num_turns` at the 200 default,
  which could false-positive on legitimate multi-step runs).

`implementation:` stays `pending`; the flip to `complete` follows the remaining
slices.

### Coupling

Gate clean (`5 paths checked, no drift`). `establishes` `budget_gate.rs`;
`refines` `orchestrator/src/lib.rs` and `orchestrator/Cargo.toml` under
`run-budget-metering`.

title: chore(208): resync registry shard with merged spec.md refinement

## Summary

PR #422 squash-merged the refined 208 `spec.md` (implementable form: rewritten section headings, summary punctuation normalized) but landed a stale `spec-registry` shard generated from an earlier draft (shardHash `0239e6bf`). main's registry therefore described an older version of the spec than the one actually on main.

This regenerates the shard via `spec-spine compile` so main's registry matches its own `spec.md` (shardHash `c3232c1d`). Single file, isolated: a full recompile against current main touches only this shard.

Root cause: `spec-conformance.yml` runs `spec-spine compile` as a smoke test only (no committed-shard freshness gate), so a stale registry shard can merge silently. A follow-up could add a shard-freshness gate; out of scope here.

- `spec-spine compile`: 222 spec(s), 0 warning(s); working tree clean after compile (no other shard drifted).

title: docs(208): refine kill-switch spec to implementable + plan/tasks; add OVERVIEW.md
body:
## Summary

Two related docs changes (no code, no lifecycle flips):

**Spec 208 (org-wide agent kill switch) graduated from sketch to implementable.** Its sequencing gate (spec 198 `implementation: complete`) is now green, so:
- De-hedged FR-001..FR-005 and AC-1..AC-6 from "sketch" to normative/testable; added AC-6 (CI/parity/coupling gate).
- Locked the state machine (scope view `active`/`halted`/`reintegrating`; record lifecycle `halted`/`reintegrating`/`lifted`) and the scope lattice (`org`/`project`/`agent-profile`).
- Added a composition-over-new-mechanism design model mapping each reused primitive to its existing home.

**Authored `plan.md` + `tasks.md`**, resolving the two decisions the spec deferred:
- *Storage*: a dedicated `org_halts` table, with enforcement reusing the existing fail-closed check sites (`grantPreflight`, serve/bind). Rejected overloading `factory_revocations.scopeKind` (a revocation row cannot hold per-engine ack timestamps or a `reintegrating` substate).
- *Propagation*: an outbox-durable `dispatchServerEvent` broadcast (replays to engines that reconnect).
- 22 tasks across 5 PR-mapped phases, grounded in a seam survey of `grantDuplexHandlers.ts`, `sync/service.ts`, `live_sessions.rs`, `schema.ts`. FR-002 degrades to grant+session revocation until spec 205 lands.

**Added `docs/OVERVIEW.md`**: a citation-backed orientation document mapping OAP's three planes plus the portable spec engine, with explicit accuracy notes where a capability is partial/roadmap, and a capability-status table keyed to the spec corpus.

Status stays `draft`/`pending`; no code touched.

## Testing

title: feat(177): ai-review resilience: pass with visible notice on Claude API failure
body:
## What

Makes the `ai-review` gate immune to Claude **API outages**: a transient API failure now **passes `ci-gate` with a loud, visible notice** instead of red-gating the PR. A genuine config problem (secret unset / auth error) still hard-fails.

Motivated by today's Anthropic incident ("elevated error rate", 14:19-14:53 UTC), which made `claude -p` exit non-zero and blocked merges on any PR scanned during the window (this is exactly what bit #413).

## Behavior (Run AI Review step classifies the failure)

| Failure | Result |
|---|---|
| Secret unset (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) | **hard fail** (config bug; unchanged) |
| Auth / permission (`authentication_error`, 401/403, invalid/expired token) | **hard fail** (a broken token must be fixed, not masked) |
| Anything else (`overloaded_error`, `rate_limit`, 5xx, timeout, network, unclassified) | **PASS** + `::warning::` + PR notice comment |

The pass is **never silent**: a "## AI Code Review: SKIPPED (Claude API failure)" comment is posted with the error excerpt, same posture as the existing oversized-diff skip notice. This preserves the anti-silent-green guard the 2026-05-31 fold installed (a green-but-dead review), while ensuring a third-party outage can't block merges.

spec 177 amended: the ci-gate claim gains a fourth disjunct (visibly-passed-because-the-Claude-API-failed).

## What

Lands `specs/203-produced-app-sbom-attestation/plan.md` for spec 203 (produced-app SBOM + dependency-audit attestation). Spec 203 splits across two lanes: the **cert/verify** half (this lane: audit-chain, specs 207/218/219) and the **kernel/emit** half (Dev2 lane). This PR settles the cert-side contract on paper and records the emission findings for Dev2 so they survive the session.

## Why a PR for a plan-only change

The session that scoped 203 surfaced a load-bearing correction to the emission hook point that must not be lost when this lane closes. Putting it on `main` makes it discoverable to Dev2 in normal history rather than stranded on a branch.

## Handoff findings (plan.md "Cross-lane handoff" section)

- **F1 (verified):** `emit_kernel` is born-with *seeding*, not scaffold completion. It creates `target_root` fresh and `refuse_existing_kernel` aborts on an existing kernel; `engine.rs:340-342` documents that pipeline timing is the caller's and "the method itself is pure". At seeding time there is no lockfile, so FR-001's "BOM from the committed lockfile at scaffold completion" must NOT hook in `emit_kernel` or every BOM is an empty stub. Phase 2 and Risk #3 in the plan are corrected on this basis.
- **F2 (open for Dev2):** where `emit_project_kernel` actually fires in the s0-s6 stage list, and whether a committed `package-lock.json` exists at that point. Candidate hook: the terminal stage `s6h-final-validation` (`engine.rs:448`). The trace is left to the kernel/emit lane.

- **F4 (cert-side contract, settled):** `SbomArtifactBinding { bom_hash, audit_hash, bom_tool_version }` parallel to spec 218's `CorpusBinding`, read-never-recompute `verify_sbom_binding` (four-outcome, fail-closed), `--sbom-dir` on `verify-certificate`, cert version `1.6.0 -> 1.7.0`. title: Reconcile spec 216 relationship graph after spec 217 deleted its in-tree implementation
body:
## Context

Discovered during the spec-lifecycle reconciliation sweep (PR #403). Spec **216-spec-spine-library-grammar-adoption** cannot be flipped `draft -> approved` because its claimed implementation no longer exists.

## The problem

216 `establishes`/`refines` paths under the in-tree spec-compiler:
- `tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/src/lib.rs` (refines)
- `tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/tests` (extends, directory)

Both were **deleted by spec 217's engine swap** (#387, `145b6fc3` — "delete 4 in-tree engine crates, repoint to published spec-spine CLI"). Only `tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/target/` (build artifacts) remains.

Draft status tolerates the dangling claims, but `approved` enforces path existence, so flipping 216 produces blocking index diagnostics:
- `I-004 ... file unit 'tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/src/lib.rs' does not exist`
- `I-007 ... directory unit 'tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/tests' is not a directory`

## Why this happened

217's collapse subsumed 216's entire mechanism. 216's goal was to converge OAP's in-tree spec-compiler grammar (V-033/V-034 etc.) onto the standalone spec-spine library; 217 achieved that convergence by deleting the in-tree compiler outright and adopting the published library. 216's relationship graph was never reconciled to that.

## Options to decide

1. **Supersede 216 by 217** — `status: superseded`, `superseded_by: 217`. Cleanest if 217 is judged to fully replace 216's mechanism. Caveat: 216 also did corpus `amends`-edge work on specs 130/154/133/181/188 that may stand independently of the deleted code.
2. **Repoint 216's claims** — drop the deleted spec-compiler units, keep the surviving in-repo surfaces (`standards/schemas/spec-spine/registry.schema.json`, `tools/shared/spec-types/src/lib.rs`, the featuregraph golden), then approve. Overlaps spec 217 Phase 2 territory.

Until resolved, 216 stays `draft` (its current, coherent state).

title: feat(218): bind run cert to spec-spine corpus attestation (read, never recompute)
body:
## Summary

Binds the governance run certificate to the spec-spine ledger-seal corpus attestation (spec 218), forming a two-link audit chain: the corpus link is reproducible by any third party (`spec-spine verify-attestation --recompute`); the run link is signed-but-not-reproducible (factory-engine). The cert gains an additive, optional `corpus_binding` block `{ corpus_attestation_hash, spec_spine_version }` inside its hash + Ed25519 signature (version `1.5.0` -> `1.6.0`). An absent binding is the named "unbound" state and serialises byte-identically to pre-1.6.0 payloads.

- **Read, never recompute (FR-002).** The cert builder records an attestation hash it is GIVEN (via `OAP_CORPUS_ATTESTATION_PATH`) and calls only `attestation_hash`; it never recomputes the corpus. The boundary is enforced structurally in two layers: a cargo-deny ban on `spec-spine-cli` (extends spec 116's ban list) plus a clippy `disallowed-methods` ban on the corpus-compile + attestation-emit functions (`attest`, `attest_json`, `verify_recompute`, `verify_attestation_json`, `compile`, `compile_json`). The reader seam (`attestation_hash`, `load_committed_registry`) stays permitted.
- **Emit.** `factory_run.rs` applies the binding on both the chain-success and chain-failure paths so an operator-configured binding is never silently dropped; unbound emits a visible notice.
- **Verify (FR-003/FR-004).** `verify-certificate --corpus-attestation <file>` checks the link by reference with four fail-closed outcomes (verified / mismatch / present-but-unverified / unbound); it delegates the attestation's own truth to `spec-spine verify-attestation`.

Spec 218's FR-002 is amended to the post-spec-217 single-crate dependency reality (`open_agentic_spec_registry_reader` no longer exists; the published `spec-spine-core` carries reader + emit in one crate, which is why the boundary needs the symbol-level clippy layer alongside the crate-level cargo-deny layer).

## Testing

- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/factory-engine/Cargo.toml` — all pass, including 4 new corpus-binding tests (AC-1..AC-5).
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` — clean; all six disallowed-method bans resolve (a probe call was verified to fire the lint).
- `cargo deny check bans` — ok (`spec-spine-cli` ban valid; current graph clean).
- featuregraph golden — no drift.
- `make pr-prep` — codebase index regenerated, coupling gate clean (7 paths, no drift).

title: feat(207): OPC countersign client closes tamper-evident audit chain AC-4
body:
## Summary

Closes **AC-4 end-to-end** for spec 207 (tamper-evident audit log chain): the OPC desktop now anchors session-scoped audit segments via the platform countersign, completing the producer/server work already on `main` (#390, #392, #394, #398).

- **sync_client.rs** — on `sync.hello` (when the duplex session id arrives), a **single-flight** sweep enumerates closed segment heads (`permissions.jsonl.1..5`) off the shared axiomregent chain dir (recomputed from the same `app_data_dir` the sidecar pins as `AXIOMREGENT_DATA_DIR` — no IPC), skips already-sealed segments, and submits the rest over the duplex `audit.segment.countersign_request` using the proven `send_and_await_reply` correlation. Each returned countersignature is persisted to a local seal store.
- **audit_unanchored_window** Tauri command — exposes the FR-004 residual: the open segment plus any closed-but-uncountersigned segments (the unanchored window is queryable).
- The local side holds no signing keys (spec 198 FR-014): it attests the head hash + metadata; stagecraft signs. The seal upsert is idempotent on `(org, session, segment)`, so reconnect resubmission is safe.
- **spec 207** — two `refines` edges (sync_client.rs, lib.rs); `implementation` flipped to `complete` (all five ACs landed).

### Hardened after local adversarial review (5 finders)
- Single-flight sweep guard (no overlapping sweeps on reconnect churn).
- Blocking file I/O offloaded to `spawn_blocking` (matches the file's keychain precedent).
- Atomic seal-store write (temp+rename) that reports persist success; no silent drop.
- Read size cap (producer rotates at 10 MB).

## Testing

- `cargo check` (opc lib): clean, no warnings.
- `cargo test --lib sync_client`: **46 passed** (8 new for the AC-4 client, incl. round-trip, refusal mapping, seal-store atomicity, segment enumeration).

## Public-cleanup: remove government references, finish aim-to-acme rename

This branch makes the open-agentic-platform tree read as a generic enterprise
product by removing old Government-of-Alberta / Government-of-Canada references
and finishing the partial `aim-vue` to `acme-vue` adapter rename.

### What changed

- **Genericized the GoA forensic.** The "CFS / 1GX / Treasury Board /
  shelter-society" scenario was the foundational worked example across the
  factory, provenance, and stakeholder-doc subsystems. It is now a generic
  `Globex / Initech / Acme` scheme across spec prose, test fixtures, test data,
  schema comment examples, and coverage docs. The `provenance-validator` and
  `factory-engine` fixtures were renamed (`cfs-1gx-fabrication` to
  `payment-scope-fabrication`, `cfs-stage-cd-1gx` to `payment-scope-stage-cd`)
  and the `sc001_cfs_audit.rs` test file to `sc001_audit.rs`.
- **Finished the aim-vue to acme-vue rename.** Uppercase identifiers
  (`AIM_VUE_ENCORE_*` consts), spec `code_aliases`, display names, and the
  retired `AIM_VUE_NODE_CONFIG` references that the lowercase pass missed.
- **Genericized remaining government framing** in `README.md`, specs (088, 115,
  120, 121, 148, 150, 183), and docs; **deleted** the government-origin history
  doc `docs/stagecraft/factory/factory-evolution.md`.
- **Fixed two stale references** introduced by the test-file rename
  (`sc001_cfs_audit.rs` to `sc001_audit.rs`) in a featuregraph golden and two
  coverage docs.

### Retained by design (not a miss)

The spec-197 FR-005 **GoA-concept guard** (specs 197/212,
`factory-schema-lockstep`, the lockstep workflow, the Makefile) names GoA
tokens (`Protected B`, the GoA service catalogue) deliberately: the guard's job
is to **reject** those tokens from the open contract, so naming them is what
enforces government-agnosticism. Genericizing them would break the guard and
its tests and desync spec from code. The provenance allowlist keeps the generic
`government` jurisdiction noun for the same functional reason.

### Verification

No spec design or code behavior changed. All affected suites pass:
`provenance-validator` (75), `factory-engine`, `factory-contracts` (125),
`featuregraph` (22, golden regenerated), `opc` vitest, `assumption-cascade-check`,
`stakeholder-doc-lint`. Spec registry and codebase index regenerated; staleness
gate is fresh.

### Coupling-gate waiver

The change touches many spec-claimed code paths and several specs that other
specs claim, but every edit is a prose/test-data rename with no design or
behavior change. Per CONST-005, editing the ~50 owning specs solely to satisfy
the gate would be spec-gaming; a blanket waiver is the principled resolution
(matching the spec 091 / 127 precedents for mechanical cross-cutting changes).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: repo-wide public cleanup; prose/test-data genericization and aim-to-acme rename only, no spec design or code behavior changed (all affected suites green).

## Spec 207 Phase 2b: producer-first (this is PR B2a of B2a then B2b)

### Why

The Phase 2b client plan ("the local side accumulates unanchored segment heads, submits them at reconnect") presumed a running local session audit chain. There was none. Phase 1 built the hash-chained `AuditLogger`, but nothing in production instantiates it:

- `PermissionRuntime::with_audit_logger` has **zero callers**
- `PermissionRuntime` is **constructed nowhere** outside its own definition
- the OPC desktop / axiomregent have **zero** `AuditLogger` usage

The live governed-tool permission path is axiomregent's `policy_preflight_response` / `audit_tool_dispatch`, not the dormant spec-068 runtime. A consumer-only client PR would be a dead consumer, so the work is split producer-first: this PR (B2a) wires the producer; B2b wires the OPC duplex client that consumes it.

### What

- **`policy-kernel`**: `AuditLogger::log_value(Value)` content-agnostic core; `log(AuditEntry)` is now a thin wrapper over it (behaviour byte-identical, guarded by the Phase 1 chain tests). Same primitive-reuse posture as Phase 2a's run-audit chain.
- **`axiomregent` Router**: chains every governed tool-dispatch decision (allowed / denied / allowed_no_lease / denied_no_lease / policy_denied) via a new `record_audit` helper that forwards (Seam B) AND chains. Attached by `set_audit_chain` (mirrors the existing `set_preflight_checker` setter) at `<AXIOMREGENT_DATA_DIR>/audit/permissions.jsonl`.
- **Cross-process handoff to B2b**: the producer runs in the axiomregent subprocess; the client runs in the OPC Tauri process. They share disk (the Tauri parent pins `AXIOMREGENT_DATA_DIR` under `app_data_dir`, so the desktop recomputes the identical chain path to read closed segment heads). No IPC. Keyed by the agent process instance, since the duplex `sessionId` only arrives at `sync.hello`, after the sidecar is spawned.

### Verification

- `policy-kernel`: 68 lib + 4 CLI tests pass (the refactor is byte-identical for `log`)
- `axiomregent`: producer integration test (`session_audit_chain_test.rs`) + affected suites pass; all test targets compile
- Coupling gate clean (`6 paths checked, no drift`); index + registry fresh

### Coupling

- `establishes:` `crates/axiomregent/tests/session_audit_chain_test.rs`
- `refines:` the spec-073-owned `router/mod.rs` + `main.rs` (behaviour-refined, authority not evolved)
- `audit.rs` rides the existing `hash-chained-audit-records` refines edge

### Not in this PR

PR B2b: the OPC Tauri duplex client that reads closed segment heads and submits `audit.segment.countersign_request` (the proven `send_and_await_reply` reply-correlation), stores the returned countersignature, and exposes the unanchored window. Completes AC-4 end-to-end.

title: spec(220): tenant-emit governance certificate (R-2 emit leg)
body:
## What

Spec 220 (`tenant-emit-governance-certificate`): the residual R-2 emit spec deferred by spec 209 FR-003 and spec 219. It lets a produced app **emit** its own governance certificate (it could already verify one via tenant-tail), closing the audit chain across the tenant boundary and activating spec 209's currently-dormant `verify-certificate` CI step.

**Design:**
- **Post-hoc emission** via `build-certificate` (reads a finished `.factory/runs/<run-id>/` dir + a signing key; needs none of factory-engine's pipeline orchestration). This is what makes tenant emission tractable.
- The emitter is a **separate distributable, never a tenant-tail verb** (preserves spec 219's structural verify-only boundary). Packaging is OQ-1.
- **Signer / key custody:** operator-supplied Ed25519 secret outside the agent's write scope (spec 102 FR-008.1 / 198 "agents are keyless"); an attributable principal; **anonymous signing halts before emit** (168 FR-007 fail-closed).
- **Unsealed-but-verifiable:** no platform countersign (a tenant run is outside OAP's admission/grant flow); the cert is Ed25519-signed and verifies offline as "verifiable-but-unsealed" (198 FR-014 AC-4).

**Also amends spec 168 (clarification):** 168's FR-001/FR-002 were capability-complete in-engine but never delivered tenant-side (219 vended verify-only; 209 FR-003 deferred emit). The amendment clarifies that 168's `implementation: complete` is capability-level, with the tenant emit leg delivered by 220. No status flip, no format change.

**Open questions** (deferred, not hand-waved): OQ-1 emit packaging, OQ-2 emitter licensing, OQ-3 key-provisioning UX, OQ-4 in-engine tenant-mode flag.

## Verification
- `spec-spine compile` clean (221 specs); `lint` clean on 168 + 220; `index check` fresh; `couple` OK (no drift, **no waiver** — the `extends: 034-featuregraph` edge couples the golden bump).
- featuregraph golden regenerated (new spec).

Status: `draft` / `implementation: pending`. Closure is gated on AC-2: a real produced app emitting a certificate the spec 209 CI step verifies green (also spec 209's own AC-1).

title: fix(213): one repo -> one project, kill cross-project build mis-attribution (FR-009)
body:
## What

A GitHub repo could be linked by more than one project, so a build event was attributed to an **arbitrary** project and the deploy path resolved another project's image.

**Observed live (Hetzner):** spec215-verify's manual "Preview in Deployd" dispatched `ghcr.io/stagecraft-ing/example-project:sha-a4858104a46f-public` (the *other* project's image) and failed on the cluster.

## Root cause

Two unscoped `.limit(1)` repo->project lookups plus no uniqueness on `project_repos`:

1. The `repository.created` webhook auto-linked a newly-created repo to an arbitrary project in the org (`webhook.ts`), racing that repo's own project creation. It wrote a stray `project_repos` row (spec215-verify -> example-project) three seconds before example-project's project existed. **This is the poisoning step.**
2. `findRepoRow` then returned an arbitrary matching row, so example-project's build was recorded under spec215-verify's `project_artifacts`.
3. The manual deploy correctly resolved spec215-verify's "latest built image" and got the poison.

## Fix (FR-009: one repo -> one project)

- Unique index on `project_repos(github_org, repo_name)` via migration 50, which is self-healing: it keeps the primary link, drops non-primary duplicates, and fails loud when a duplicate group has zero or multiple primaries.
- `repository.created` no longer speculatively links a new repo; the create/clone/import flow owns the primary `project_repos` row.
- `findRepoRow` is deterministic and fails loud on genuine ambiguity, preferring the primary link.
- DB-backed regression test, gated to the encore-test lane.
- spec 213 FR-009 + edge case + relationship-graph edges.

## Validation

- Local gates green: tsc, spec/code coupling (no drift), codebase-index regen, spec-spine compile (220, 0 warnings), spec-lint (exit 0).
- `webhook.test.ts` is DB-bound and runs in the **encore-test CI lane** (spec 211); it was not executed locally.

## Not in this PR (deliberate fast-follow)

- **Observability pair**: deployd should log the helm error (`routes.rs:309`), and stagecraft should surface deployd's returned diagnostic instead of hardcoding "deployd reported FAILED (see deployd logs)" (`deploy.ts:819`). These fall under specs 214/137/215, not 213.
- The separate **cluster-side helm pre-install failure**: yesterday's *correct*-image deploy also failed (no release, no namespace created), and that reason is still trapped by the observability gap above.

## Operator note (prod data)

Migration 50's dedup removes the poison `project_repos` link on deploy. The two poison `project_artifacts` rows for spec215-verify are outside its scope; delete them so spec215-verify resolves its own image:

```sql
DELETE FROM project_artifacts
 WHERE project_id = '1a613ceb-f75e-405f-8b5c-b5aac28f5378'
   AND image_ref LIKE 'ghcr.io/stagecraft-ing/example-project:%';
```

title: spec-213: GitHub App not subscribed to `workflow_run` → oap-build artifacts never recorded (deploy path blocked)
body:
## Summary

Spec 213's artifact recorder (`platform/services/stagecraft/api/github/webhook.ts:266`, the `workflow_run.completed` case → `insert(projectArtifacts)` at :685) is **dead in production**: the OAP GitHub App is not subscribed to the `workflow_run` webhook event, so GitHub never delivers it. `project_artifacts` is therefore never populated, and the deploy path is blocked for **every** project — `resolveLatestArtifact` always returns null, so spec 215's "Preview in Deployd" always reports "image not built yet" even when the image exists in GHCR.

## Evidence (Hetzner, 2026-06-19)

- Default-branch `oap-build` for a freshly scaffolded project **succeeded** (image pushed to GHCR); a clean re-run also succeeded.
- `select count(*) from project_artifacts` stayed **0** after both.
- `webhook.ts:78` logs `"GitHub webhook received"` for every delivery; **zero** webhook log activity in the window covering the build completion, while `pull_request` events ARE delivered + logged (they create the preview-deploy rows). → `workflow_run` is not being delivered.
- Nothing in `platform/**` (terraform/manifests) declares the App's subscribed events, so the subscription was never added when 213 shipped the recorder.

## Fix

1. **Immediate (App settings):** in the OAP GitHub App → Permissions & events → set Repository permission **Actions: Read** (required for `workflow_run`) and subscribe to the **Workflow run** event. Existing installations must accept the new permission.
2. **Durable (declare as code):** capture the App's webhook event subscriptions + permissions as code (terraform/app manifest) so a recorder can't ship without its event. Spec 213 amendment or a small new spec.

## Discovered by

Live end-to-end verification of spec 215 (deploy trigger UX). 215 itself is verified working; this 213 gap is the sole blocker to SC-001's positive rollout.

title: feat(stagecraft): platform countersign for audit segments (spec 207 AC-4, server side)
body:
## Summary

Spec 207 **Phase 2b (server side)**: the stagecraft half of AC-4. The platform can now seal a session-scoped audit segment head, giving session-scoped audit chains the external trust root the open chain lacks (spec 198 FR-014: **the platform signs, the local side is keyless**). Faithfully mirrors the existing run-grant `countersignRunCertificate` flow.

- New duplex message `audit.segment.countersign_request` carrying `{sessionId, segmentId, segmentHeadHash, segmentRecordCount, first/lastRecordAt}`.
- `auditSegmentHandlers.ts` signs the head with a new domain typ `oap-audit-segment-countersign+jws` via the existing `signFactoryJws`, and persists a row in the new `factory_session_audit_seals` table (**migration 50**), **idempotent** on `(org_id, session_id, segment_id)` so reconnect / at-least-once resubmission is safe. Dispatch wired in `sync/service.ts` exactly like the grant path (targeted reply, correlationId).
- The new typ is an **additive** member of the spec-198-owned `FactoryJwsTyp` (declared via an additive `extends` edge on 198 — uses the signing authority, does not evolve it).

## Design note (deliberate)

Unlike the run-grant countersign, this handler does **not** gate on factory admission/revocations. Audit sealing is universal observability, not an execution grant, so gating it on an active factory admission would be wrong. The submitted head hash is taken on trust: the seal attests *platform observation* of that head at `iat`, not its content; a bogus hash gains nothing because the local audit chain must still terminate at the sealed head for verification to pass. The authenticated org/session comes from the duplex auth layer. (Residual: distinct-`segment_id` spam is a mild DoS vector, matching the existing grant-request exposure; rate-limiting is a future hardening if needed.)

## Testing

- `encore test api/factory/auditSegmentHandlers.test.ts`: **5/5** (positive, idempotent resubmit, distinct segments, distinct sessions, refusal-when-unconfigured).
- `encore test api/factory/grantDuplexHandlers.test.ts`: **17/17** (no regression).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: no new errors; wire-assignability gates pass.
- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (10 paths, no drift).

## Coupling

`establishes:` the handler + test + migration up/down; additive `extends:` on spec-198 `signing-pure.ts` (the new typ); `refines:` `sync/types.ts`, `sync/service.ts`, `schema.ts`, `auditActions.ts` (upgraded from a context reference). No waiver.

## Follow-up

**Phase 2b client side (PR B2)** completes AC-4 end-to-end: the OPC-side accumulates unanchored segment heads, submits them at reconnect, stores the countersignatures, and exposes the unanchored window. Sequenced after the active stagecraft (215) deploy/verify settles. Design in `specs/207-tamper-evident-audit-chain/plan.md`.

title: fix(215): register env-detail deploys route (FR-004/FR-006 UI was 404)
body:
## Found via live verification

Verifying spec 215 end-to-end on the Hetzner cluster (running the merged image `sha-ad1428e`), the env-detail page `/app/project/:projectId/deploys/:envId` returned **404 for everyone** — both via in-app Link and direct navigation.

**Root cause:** `web/app/routes.ts` is an explicit route config. It registered the deploys **list** (`deploys.tsx`) but never the env-**detail** route (`app.project.$projectId.deploys.$envId.tsx`). That page hosts **both** spec 137's access-gate UI **and** spec 215's FR-004 deployment card + FR-006 trigger button, so the detail page, the trigger UI, and the success-page "View Deployd" link / "Preview in Deployd" button all 404'd. This is a **pre-existing gap from spec 137** (the file was created but never wired into the route table), inherited and surfaced by 215. `tsc` compiles the component and the encore-test lane never loads the router, so neither local gate could catch it — only live E2E did.

## Fix

Register `deploys/:envId` as a **sibling** of the list (`deploys.tsx` is a leaf with no `<Outlet/>`). Spec 215 now claims `routes.ts` via an additive `extends` edge on the app route table established by spec 087.

```ts
route("deploys", "routes/app.project.$projectId.deploys.tsx"),
route("deploys/:envId", "routes/app.project.$projectId.deploys.$envId.tsx"),  // added
```

## What live verification already confirmed (and what this unblocks)

Working on the live cluster:
- FR-003 migration 49 applied (table + indexes + CHECK constraints exact)
- FR-001 success-page "Preview in Deployd" row renders
- FR-004 deploys-**list** status badges render (red FAILED on the preview envs)
- FR-005 webhook record path writes `environment_deployments` rows live

This fix makes the FR-004 detail page and FR-006 trigger reachable. The SC-001 positive path (trigger → ROLLED_OUT → URL) still needs a built image (`oap-build` artifact) once this is deployed; that's the remaining live check.

Coupling gate OK (2 paths, no drift); spec-lint `--fail-on-warn` clean; registry compiles with 0 warnings.

title: feat(factory-engine): run-audit chain anchored in run cert (spec 207 AC-3)
body:
## Summary

Spec 207 **Phase 2a (AC-3)**: closes the run-scoped half of the open-segment residual by giving the factory run audit an external trust root (the run governance certificate).

- A run's audit trail is serialized as a **hash-chained segment** at `<run_dir>/run-audit/run-audit.jsonl`, each record carrying `previous_record_hash` + `record_hash` via the **same** `policy_kernel::proof_chain::link_record_hash` primitive the permission chain uses (FR-001: one chain shape, not two). Genesis link is `genesis:<run_id>`; `verify_audit_chain` (content-agnostic) validates it.
- `emit_certificate` writes the segment, then builds the certificate with stage list `OAP_STAGE_IDS + "run-audit"`. The existing `stage_record_for` scan binds the segment's SHA-256 into the cert and the existing `verify_certificate` artifact-hash loop catches any tamper (**FR-002, AC-3**). **No bespoke certificate code** — the segment is just a stage artifact.
- The run accrues a `StageConfirmed` per phase boundary into a binary-local `Vec<AuditEntry>`. The factory-run CLI's `FactoryPipelineState` is distinct from the harness `PipelineState` that carries the OPC-side audit vec (which is why `record_audit` was an unwired stub); per-gate recording in the dispatch path is a deliberate follow-up.

## Testing

- `crates/factory-engine/src/run_audit_chain.rs`: 3 unit tests (chain verifies, tamper breaks it, empty segment).
- `crates/factory-engine/tests/run_audit_anchoring.rs`: **end-to-end AC-3** — a clean cert verifies; tampering the segment on disk fails `verify_certificate` with the segment named in the diagnostic.
- Full `cargo test -p factory-engine` passes (incl. all 35 `governance_certificate` regression tests; the stage-scan change only affects the real `emit_certificate` path, not the byte-equivalence test path).
- `cargo clippy --bins -- -D warnings` clean; `make pr-prep` coupling gate clean (6 paths, no drift).

## Coupling

`establishes:` the run-audit chain writer + the anchoring test; `refines:` `factory_run.rs` (emission/anchoring) + the factory-engine `lib.rs` module registration. No `governance_certificate.rs` change (the stage scan is reused as-is). No waiver.

## Follow-up

**Phase 2b (AC-4)** — session-scoped segments countersigned by stagecraft (spec 198 FR-014), offline-first with retroactive anchoring — lands in a separate PR after the active stagecraft (215) deploy/verify settles. Design recorded in `specs/207-tamper-evident-audit-chain/plan.md`.

title: feat(policy-kernel): tamper-evident audit log chain (spec 207 Phase 1)
body:
## Summary

Spec 207 Phase 1: make the permission audit log tamper-evident by hash-chaining records, reusing the spec 047 proof-chain link primitive rather than inventing a second chain shape.

- **FR-001** every audit record carries `previous_record_hash` + `record_hash`; a shared `link_record_hash(value, field)` in `proof_chain.rs` backs both chains (`compute_record_hash` becomes a thin wrapper, byte-identical, regression-guarded by the existing spec 047 tests).
- **FR-002 (local half)** rotation closes a segment with a head record (`segment_id`, `record_count`, time range); the next segment's genesis binds the prior head (continuity), and the count is the closed-segment truncation tripwire.
- **FR-003** new independent `verify_audit_chain` binary (sister to `verify_proof_chain`) walks a segment and exits non-zero naming the first broken record.
- **FR-004** the open-segment-without-anchor residual is stated honestly.

Cross-repo anchoring (run certificate + platform countersign, AC-3/AC-4) is **Phase 2**, deferred per the spec sequencing.

A local adversarial review (correctness / security / concurrency / cold finders) drove fixes folded into this PR: write-failure chain-head guard, poisoned-lock recovery, rotate-then-restart continuity recovery, verifier input-size cap, and a corrected over-narrow "tamper-evident" framing. title: feat(215): Stagecraft Deploy Trigger UX (Preview in Deployd / View Deployd)
body:
Implements spec **215-stagecraft-deploy-trigger-ux**, the third of the deploy-path trilogy (consumes 213 artifact resolution and 214 dispatch contract). The manual, human-triggered precursor to the spec 112 §11 automated terminal deploy stage.

## What this delivers

All eight FRs, built on one branch as ordered commits:

- **FR-007 client consolidation** (`215b`): `deploydClient.ts` is now the single deployd-api client. M2M secret resolution + token cache resolve there once (`getDeploydAuthHeader`, `DEPLOYD_URL`, plus new `dispatchDeployment` / `getDeploymentStatus` transport); `deploy.ts` deletes its duplicate.
- **FR-003 record module** (`215b`): `api/deploy/deployments.ts` owns all writes to `environment_deployments` (the wip table + migration 49). Pure DB, exercised against live Postgres by `deployments.test.ts` (registered in the spec-211 encore-test lane).
- **FR-006 authorization** (`215b` + `215c`): the `auth: false` `/v1/deployments` raw proxy now requires a Rauthy M2M JWT (`platform:deploy:write`); the new UI trigger is `auth: true` with an org-scoped environment lookup as the membership gate, and `requiresApproval` environments refuse direct dispatch.
- **FR-002 dispatch path** (`215c`): `POST /api/projects/:projectId/envs/:envId/deployments` resolves the built image from the artifact record (spec 213), records the dispatch up-front, enriches the deployd body from stagecraft records (chart, namespace, derived host, access gate per spec 214), dispatches via the consolidated client, and reconciles the record from the synchronous deployd response. Idempotent replay returns the existing `ROLLED_OUT` record. A `deploy.triggered` audit row is written.
- **FR-008 reconciliation** (`215c`): `GET .../deployments/latest` lazily reconciles a stale `PENDING` record against deployd-api status before answering (no background poller).
- **FR-005 webhook fix** (`215d`): PR-open records each preview dispatch keyed to deployd's real `rel_<uuid>`; PR-close resolves the stored id and destroys THAT, then marks `DESTROYED`. The constructed-string destroy (which 404'd while previews leaked) is gone.
- **FR-001 / FR-004 web tier** (`215e`): the project-created success page gains a "Preview in Deployd" row (trigger + View Deployd link); the env detail page renders a Deployment card (status, commit, image, endpoints, FAILED diagnostic) with a never-deployed empty state and a trigger/redeploy button; the deploys list shows per-environment latest-status badges. `projects-api.server.ts` gains `createDeployment` / `getLatestDeployment`.
- **Spec finalize** (`215f`): `implementation: complete`; planned-establishes converted to `establishes` (modules + migration 49); `vite.config.ts` lane-assignment `refines` edge added.

## Gates (locally verified)

- Coupling gate: `OK: 14 path(s) checked, no drift`
- Registry compile: 0 warnings; spec-lint `--fail-on-warn`: clean
- stagecraft tsc (`api/`): clean; pure deploy vitest: 34/34
- Registry + codebase-index by-spec shards regenerated and committed

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Pre-existing spec-217 fallout (not this PR):** the featuregraph golden test (`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden.rs:17`) still guards on the removed monolithic `registry.json`, so it silently skips post-217 for every PR. The golden's 215 row is stale (`pending`); left untouched (not gate-blocking, skips in CI too). Worth a separate one-line guard fix.
- **FR-001 nuance:** the success-page trigger surfaces "image not built yet" on click (the endpoint guards with `failedPrecondition`) rather than pre-disabled; the success page has no loader to check artifact existence at render.
- **CI-only validation:** `encore build`/`gen` acceptance of the two new typed endpoints, and the `deployments.test.ts` run in the encore-test lane, are exercised by CI (need the Encore daemon + Docker), not locally.

title: spec(209): refine FRs against vended tenant-tail; FR-004 npm-pin amendment
body:
## What

Refine spec 209 (tenant kernel CI enforcement) off its sketch state now that the tenant-tail vend blocker is cleared (spec 219 published tenant-tail 0.1.0 + its platform packages to npm).

- FR-004 rewritten to the npm-pin / npm-ci sha512 integrity model spec 219 FR-006 established, replacing the "content hash against .kernel-version" wording (the amendment spec 219 explicitly tracked against 209). Scoped honestly: .kernel-version records the born-with spec-spine pin, so CI asserts spec-spine equality there; tenant-tail integrity rests on the npm ci lockfile sha512 (it is not in the stamp). OQ-1 records adding the tenant-tail pin to the stamp as a future hardening.
- FR-001 / FR-005 grounded on tenant-tail's actual verbs and exit-code contract (verify-provenance --fail-on-rejected, conditional verify-certificate, the --require-sealed posture).
- FR-003 reframed as deferred to the emit spec (residual R-2): tenant-tail is verify-only by construction.

FR-002 already landed (PR #366). The cross-repo CI activation (FR-001/004/005) lands in template-encore's spec-spine.yml (separate PR, GovAlta-Pronghorn/template-encore).

## Why the waiver

The coupling gate's index resolver treats spec 219's references:role:context edge over specs/209-tenant-kernel-ci-enforcement/spec.md as ownership and over-fires. The registry authority resolver (oap-registry-enrich by-authority) confirms NO spec claims authority over 209's spec.md: a references edge is non-owning by design (spec 154). There is no owning spec to co-edit; forcing an edit into the non-owning referrer (draft spec 219) would entrench the resolver divergence rather than fix it.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: refining spec 209's own FRs; the only spec referencing 209/spec.md does so via a non-owning references:role:context edge (by-authority confirms no owner). Known index-vs-registry resolver divergence; no owning spec exists to co-edit.

title: feat(217): spec-spine engine swap and collapse (delete 4 in-tree engine crates, repoint to published spec-spine CLI)
body:
## Spec 217: Spec-Spine Engine Swap and Collapse

Replaces OAP's four in-tree spec-spine engine binaries with the published `spec-spine` CLI (crates.io 0.8.0). The generic compile / registry / index / couple engine is no longer vendored; OAP keeps only its overlay tools and the `spec-lint` overlay.

Implements [`217-spec-spine-engine-swap-collapse`](specs/217-spec-spine-engine-swap-collapse/spec.md). Base is `main`. This branch incorporates the Phase 1 spec amendment `d261ea43` (currently draft #386); **#386 can be closed in favour of this PR.** The workstream-checkpoint commits are labelled WIP and are intended to squash-merge.

### What changes

- **Delete (Phase 3 / FR-301):** `tools/spec-spine/{spec-compiler, registry-consumer, codebase-indexer, spec-code-coupling-check}` plus their `[workspace] members` entries. `spec-lint` survives. `cargo build --workspace` passes (AC-301).
- **Repoint 8 consumers (Phase 2):** featuregraph, factory-engine, opc/src-tauri, oap-registry-enrich, oap-code-index-enrich, opc-decomposition-pipeline onto `spec-spine-core` 0.8.0 `default-features = false` (the `load_committed_registry` / `load_committed_index` / `couple_with` read path; tree-sitter symbol-resolution is feature-gated to avoid the `links` conflict with xray's 0.26 pin). policy-compiler is a no-op (the overlay-types crate survives).
- **oap-registry-enrich** absorbs the `by-authority` authority verb (FR-302; re-implements spec 181 over the typed library `Registry`).
- **Rewire 56 call sites (Phase 4 / FR-401..404):** Makefile, 6 workflows, `.claude/`, `.githooks/`, the stagecraft TS reader, docs, standards. `spec-compiler -> spec-spine compile`, `codebase-indexer -> spec-spine index`, `registry-consumer -> spec-spine registry` / `oap-registry-enrich`, `coupling-check -> spec-spine couple`.
- **Commit the shard trees (Phase 3 / FR-303):** the per-unit `by-spec` / `by-package` shards are now committed (499 files), restoring present-on-clone (spec 101 SC-06) in a conflict-free per-spec form that supersedes spec 188 Phase 4b's de-commit. `.gitignore` re-includes them; the `.gitattributes` merge driver repoints to shard globs; the monolithic `codebase-index.schema.json` (3.1.0) is dropped for the library shard schemas (1.0.0), with its 5 owning claims reconciled (101/129 re-anchor onto the surviving overlay schema `codebase-index-oap.schema.json`; 154/156/188 strip the edge). 217 gains the `amends: 188` edge.
- **FR-101 overlay slim:** `tools/shared/spec-types` drops the now-dead generics (Severity, ViolationCode + the V/W/L registry, LogicalUnit, ProvenanceKind, RESOLVER_EXCLUSIONS); 1085 -> 230 lines. The four downstream path-dep consumers compile without modification (AC-101); `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` exits 0 (AC-102). spec-lint's primary spec is repointed off superseded 006 to live 147.
- **Governance wave (Phase 5 / FR-501/502):** 57 spec.md. Full-supersede 6 (001/002/006/133/176/181) + bulk-supersede the 007-031 registry-consumer series (25) + amend 24 survivors (deleted-crate / dropped-schema units stripped). 217 carries 31 supersedes + 23 amends edges.
- **Blast-radius (Phase 6 / FR-BLAST):** the before/after `authorities(P)` diff via `oap-registry-enrich by-authority` is GO; no surviving path unexpectedly loses all live owners.

|---|---|
| `spec-spine compile` | 220 specs, 0 warnings |
| `spec-spine index` | 0 error diagnostics |
| `spec-spine index check` | fresh |

| `cargo build --workspace` (AC-301) | exit 0 |
| `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --pr-body <this body>` (AC-502) | exit 0 |

### Follow-ups (tracked, not in this PR)

- **FR-102 library-lint merge** (fold the generic L-001..L-004 pass into the OAP gate, drop the now-redundant V-020/V-031, retire OAP's obsolete L-005): deferred to its own pass because the L-001-vs-V-020 reconciliation is a behavior-and-corpus change. AC-102 holds with `spec-lint` unchanged. See spec 217 §1.7.
- **spec-spine library brief #3** (exact-lockfile-claim-over-bypass): the durable fix for the `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` waiver below; until it ships, that lockfile couples to spec 178's directory ownership.

### CI fixups (after the initial push)

The first CI run surfaced three root causes across five jobs, now fixed:

- **`slices.json` not committed** (failed `spec-conformance` + `parity`). The spec-184 config-slice gate (`spec-spine index check --slice claude-config`) reads `.derived/codebase-index/slices.json` as its committed reference; Workstream D had left it gitignored, so a fresh CI clone had no reference. Un-ignored and committed it (the `config-hash.json` precedent; ci-parity's producer/consumer gate flagged it precisely).
- **featuregraph test fixture on the retired monolith** (failed `crates` + `axiomregent`). `axiomregent`'s `mcp_featuregraph_test` fixture wrote the monolithic `registry.json`; the post-217 scanner reads the `by-spec/*.json` shard tree via `load_committed_registry`. - **stale factory-engine template tests** (the `crates` job's second cause). Workstream E repointed `tenant.makefile.tmpl` off the deleted binaries onto the `spec-spine` CLI (dropping the `@@binaries_dir@@` placeholder), but the `kernel_emission::templates` tests still asserted `tools/spec-spine` / `vendor/spine`. title: spec(217): amend Phase 1 to empirical 0.6.0 reality + seam corrections
body:
## What this PR does

Amends spec 217's Phase 1 to match the empirically-verified reality of the published `spec-spine` 0.6.0 library. This is `spec.md` only; the engine-swap code lands as a follow-on consolidated bundle (see "Phase-model consequence" below).

## Verified on spec-spine 0.6.0 (installed from crates.io)

- **FR-000 green:** `spec-spine compile` exit 0 (220 specs, 0 warnings); `spec-spine index` exit 0 (0 errors, 94 accepted `W-002` unresolved-file warnings, surfaced not skipped per P2). Honest note recorded for the 94-vs-95 / single-`W-002` corpus-drift delta.
- **API:** `spec-spine-core` supports the swap; consumers use `load_committed_registry` / `load_committed_index` / `couple` (corrected from the draft's `load_registry` / `couple_with`).
- **Edition 2024 / MSRV 1.85** compatible (rustc 1.95; all crates already edition 2024).

## Seam corrections (why the draft's "mechanical re-export" premise was false)

- **Section 1.6 (spec-types):** 4 of 5 generic primitives (`LogicalUnit`, `split_frontmatter_*`, `ProvenanceKind`, `RESOLVER_EXCLUSIONS`) are INCOMPATIBLE with a `spec-spine-types` re-export. The overlay keeps OAP types; the library dep moves to the Phase-2 consumers. FR-101/AC-101 corrected (AC-101 holds because OAP types are kept, not swapped).
- **Section 1.7 (lint):** the library lint emits a different `L-001..L-005` namespace; `L-005` collides with OAP's; library `L-001` is stricter than OAP's `V-020`, so `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn` fails on 8 legitimately non-owning specs. Annotating them to pass would be CONST-005 drift. Library-lint integration defers to the Phase 3+5 bundle. FR-102/AC-102 corrected.

## Phase-model consequence

Three Phase-1 elements each dissolved into the wave on contact with the library's stricter or different semantics and OAP coupling governance. The spec now records that the realistic landing is a consolidated Phase 2-5 bundle (consumer repoints, engine deletion, and the supersession/amendment wave together), not thin per-phase PRs. This PR is Phase 1's coupling-clean deliverable: the reality-aligned plan plus the FR-000 green result.

## Coupling

`spec.md` only; coupling-clean (spec.md is not an implements claimant, section 7). `make pr-prep` clean: coupling gate OK, 1 diff path checked.

Draft: the follow-on bundle PR carries the code (8 consumer repoints, 4-crate deletion, ~40-spec wave).

title: fix(stagecraft): direct upstream login via idp_hint with resolved provider id
body:
## Problem

Signing in via "Continue with GitHub" on stagecraft.ing forced a **second**
provider click. The authorize URL set `upstream_auth_provider_id=github`, a
query param Rauthy does not read, so the user landed on Rauthy's own login
card (e-mail + provider buttons) instead of being forwarded straight to
GitHub, then had to click GitHub again.

Two bugs in one place:
- **Wrong param name.** Rauthy's direct-login hint is `idp_hint`
  (Rauthy Book: "Direct Login with idp_hint"). `upstream_auth_provider_id`
  is read nowhere in Rauthy.
- **Wrong value.** `idp_hint` takes the upstream provider's **id** (a random
  string assigned at provider creation), not its name. We were passing the
  literal `"github"` / the provider's `name`, which could never match.

## Fix

- `buildAuthorizationUrl` now emits `idp_hint`.
- New `resolveUpstreamProviderId(name)`: a cached (1h TTL) lookup that lists
  Rauthy's providers (`POST /auth/v1/providers`, admin auth, mirroring
  `scripts/seed-rauthy.mjs`) and maps name -> id. On miss/error it returns
  `null` and the caller omits the hint, so Rauthy renders its normal
  selection page: the pre-fix behaviour, **never worse**.
- All four call sites resolve name -> id before building the URL: the
  `rauthyCallback` GitHub web path, the `oidc` enterprise SSO path, and the
  `desktop` default + enterprise paths. The redundant manual param appends in
  `oidc.ts` / `desktop.ts` are removed.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: zero errors in the four edited files (the repo's standing
  unresolved `~encore/*` generated-type errors are pre-existing and unrelated).
- No tests referenced the old param or the builder; behaviour is unchanged
  whenever the provider cannot be resolved.

## Known caveat / follow-up

With Rauthy 0.35 the `idp_hint` forward is client-side, so the Rauthy login
card may flash briefly before redirecting to GitHub. A true server-side 302
is a separate upstream Rauthy change, not in scope here.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Runtime bug fix correcting a non-functional OIDC query parameter (upstream_auth_provider_id, which Rauthy never reads) to the one Rauthy honours (idp_hint), plus a cached provider-id resolver. No spec design changes. rauthy.ts is spec 106 territory and the fix honours its FR-004 single-click upstream login; desktop.ts/oidc.ts/rauthyCallback.ts are claimed only by broad-containment specs 080/087/160 (github-onboarding, workspace-architecture, factory-adapter-relocation), none related to OIDC param handling, so editing them would be gate-chasing rather than honest amendment.

title: spec(217): honest Phase 0 scope + Track 1 spec-spine.toml manifest-discovery fix
body:
## What

Phase 0 of the spec-spine engine swap (217), driven against the published spec-spine 0.5.0 (sharded). Two changes:

1. **Track 1 config fix (`spec-spine.toml`).** The committed config mis-declared manifest paths: `standalone_rust_workspaces` listed `Cargo.toml` files (the library joins `<member>/Cargo.toml`, yielding `.../Cargo.toml/Cargo.toml`), and npm packages were routed through `product/pnpm-workspace.yaml` (whose globs the library resolves against repo-root, not `product/`). Result: the `opc`/`deployd-api-rs` crates and all 25 npm packages were undiscovered. Correcting both clears 16 index diagnostics (**116 -> 101**) and discovers **63 packages (was 38)**.
2. **Spec 217 amendment.** Records the honest Phase 0 finding: the engine-swap premise was validated on registry `compile` only, never the index. New section 1.5 documents the verified three-track split, policy decisions P1 (references-edge truth lives inline; the edge is supplementary) and P2 (draft/pending units warn, never skip), the revised FR-000 (zero errors + zero un-accepted warnings; not relaxed), and the `spec-spine index` command-name correction.

## Scope boundary

This **does not complete Phase 0's gate.** 101 diagnostics remain: **Track 2** (95, OAP corpus drift the in-tree indexer never validated) and **Track 3** (6, spec-spine 0.5.1 library defects). FR-000 goes green only after all three land.

## Verification

- `make pr-prep` clean (in-tree index regenerated/gitignored per 188 4b; coupling gate OK, 2 diff paths).
- Track 1 effect measured: 116 -> 101, I-003 and I-005 fully cleared.
- No on-disk schema or behaviour change to current CI (the in-tree engine does not read `spec-spine.toml`).

---

Spec-Drift-Waiver: git2 0.21 security upgrade (RUSTSEC-2026-0183 Remote::list UB, RUSTSEC-2026-0184 BlameHunk/Signature UB; deny.toml forbids ignoring unsound advisories). `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` is a dependency version bump and `src/commands/git.rs` adapts to git2 0.21's Option->Result API change on `Reference::shorthand` / `Commit::summary` with no behaviour or design change. No spec design changed, so no edit to specs 032/172 is warranted; waived per the dependency-security-upgrade pattern.

Release notes

Sourced from @​aws-sdk/client-s3's releases.

v3.1071.0

3.1071.0(2026-06-17)

New Features
  • client-partnercentral-selling: Cosell Resonate AND Prospecing API Launch with ARN correction (7e8c98ab)
  • client-compute-optimizer-automation: This launch adds IfExists comparison operators to Compute Optimizer Automation rule criteria, so a rule can include recommended actions whose specified attribute isn't present. (ab2c616d)
  • client-bedrock-agent: Launching Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases. Added support for resource-based policies on Knowledge Base resources, enabling cross-account access for Managed Knowledge Bases. (de0affe4)
  • client-securityagent: Updated AWS Security Agent SDK model with new APIs for threat modeling, code review, security requirements, and additional integration providers. (9c3d3351)
  • client-opensearch: Adds support for configuring IAM Identity Center options on existing OpenSearch applications via the UpdateApplication API. (94f06a20)
  • client-glue: This release adds support for Search and Discovery in AWS Glue, letting you and your applications search Data Catalog assets such as table and enrich them with business context and glossary terms. (b394fc0b)
  • client-bedrock-agentcore-control: AgentCore Gateway now supports inference targets to LLM providers (direct config or built-in connectors), HTTP passthrough targets with session stickiness, runtime target API schemas, AWS WAF web ACL association with configurable fail-open or fail-close modes, and interceptor payload filtering. (75f1d588)
  • client-devops-agent: Adds support for Remote A2A (Agent-to-Agent) agent registration and management. Adds new Release Readiness Review and Release Testing capabilities. Adds support for Git managed skills in AWS DevOps Agent. (ebc040e1)
  • client-bedrock-agentcore: AgentCore Harness service will be Generally Available at NYS 2026 with this Treb release. Harness will support invoking specific endpoints via the qualifier parameter, AWS Skills for pre-built agent capabilities, and improved validation for skill git source URLs. (5bf9fccc)
  • client-ecs: Releasing the ability to bring-your-own task-definition for CreateExpressGatewayService and UpdateGatewayExpressService (b7b9cb4f)
  • client-mq: This release adds private networking support for Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ. You can now associate AWS RAM resource shares with your broker and retrieve shared resource details using the new DescribeSharedResources API. (e96af450)
  • client-bedrock-agent-runtime: Adds new AgenticRetrieveStream API for managed knowledge bases to use conversation history and autonomously plan for multi-hop multi-KB reasoning with built-in evaluation and access-control. Updates Retrieve API for access-control-based filtering for managed knowledge bases. (557f7b32)
Tests
  • core:
    • prebuild before integration and e2e (#8111) (363f3fb7)
    • prebuild core before unit tests (#8108) (5f789e7f)

For list of updated packages, view updated-packages.md in assets-3.1071.0.zip

v3.1070.0

3.1070.0(2026-06-16)

Chores
  • scripts: speed up esm-to-cjs transform (#8107) (9063e305)
New Features
  • clients: update client endpoints as of 2026-06-16 (dc044784)
  • client-sagemaker: Add EnableDetailedObservability to Endpoint MetricsConfig. Publishes GPU, host, and framework-native inference metrics to CloudWatch with per-inference-component, availability-zone, and instance dimensions. Adds Inference Component provisioning lifecycle and multi-AZ placement metrics. (97bb02cf)
  • client-outposts: Adds support for creating an order from quotes. (d4389889)
  • client-s3vectors: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports paginated QueryVectors requests, returning up to 10,000 results per query. (8b2ef7f2)
  • client-partnercentral-selling: Added Prospecting APIs to convert engagements into AI-enriched leads with scoring insights. Extended Engagement APIs with ProspectingResult and Lead contexts. Added CoSell Scoring to GetAwsOpportunitySummary- quality score, trend, agent-driven recommendations, and engagement classification. (c6c54ef0)
  • client-route53resolver: Adds supports for PartnerManagedRules (b76e2eed)
  • client-direct-connect: Added VIF rate limiting support for AWS Direct Connect, allowing customers to set bandwidth allocations on virtual interfaces to manage traffic on dedicated connections. (73df9383)
  • client-s3: Added support for annotations. You can now attach up to 1000 annotations (up to 1 MB each) directly to objects and create, retrieve, list, and delete them using new annotation APIs. Also added support for configuring an annotation table in S3 Metadata. (c5558746)

Updates `@tailwindcss/vite` from 4.3.0 to 4.3.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​tailwindcss/vite's releases.

v4.3.1

Added

  • Add --silent option to suppress output in @tailwindcss/cli (#20100)

Fixed

  • Remove deprecation warnings by using Module#registerHooks instead of Module#register on Node 26+ (#20028)
  • Canonicalization: don't crash when plugin utilities throw for unsupported values (#20052)
  • Allow @apply to be used with CSS mixins (#19427)
  • Ensure not-* correctly negates @container queries, including style(…) queries (#20059)
  • Ensure drop-shadow-* color utilities work with custom shadow values containing calc(…) (#20080)
  • Fix 'Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect' warnings when using @tailwindcss/vite (#20103)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/webpack can be installed in Rspack projects without requiring webpack as a peer dependency (#20027)
  • Canonicalization: don't suggest invalid calc(…) expressions (e.g. px-[calc(1rem+0px)] → px-[calc(1rem+0)]) (#20127)
  • Canonicalization: avoid suggesting large spacing-scale values for arbitrary lengths (e.g. left-[99999px] → left-[99999px], not left-24999.75) (#20130)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode recovers when a tracked dependency is deleted and restored (#20137)
  • Ensure standalone @tailwindcss/cli binaries are ignored when scanning for class candidates (#20139)
  • Ensure class candidates are extracted from Twig addClass(…) and removeClass(…) calls (#20198)
  • Don't crash in the Ruby or Vue preprocessors when scanning files containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (#19588)
  • Allow @variant to be used inside addBase (#19480)
  • Ensure @source globs with symlinks are preserved (#20203)
  • Ensure later @source rules can re-include files excluded by earlier @source not rules (#20203)
  • Upgrade: don't migrate empty class rules to invalid @utility rules (#20205)
  • Ensure transitions between inset-shadow-none and other inset shadows work correctly (#20208)
  • Ensure explicitly referenced @source directories are scanned even when ignored by git (#20214)
  • Ensure @source globs ending in **/* preserve dynamic path segments to avoid scanning too many files (#20217)
  • Canonicalization: don't fold calc(…) divisions when the result would require high precision (e.g. w-[calc(100%/3.5)] → w-[calc(100%/3.5)], not w-[28.571428571428573%]) (#20221)
  • Serve ESM type declarations to ESM importers of @tailwindcss/postcss (#20228)

Changed

  • Generate 0 instead of calc(var(--spacing) * 0) for spacing utilities like m-0 and left-0 (#20196)
  • Generate var(--spacing) instead of calc(var(--spacing) * 1) for spacing utilities like m-1 and left-1 (#20196)

tower-http-0.7.0

Changes since 0.6.11

Added

  • csrf: add cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection middleware, porting the cross-origin protection scheme introduced in Go 1.25 (#699)

    use tower::ServiceBuilder;
use tower_http::csrf::CsrfLayer;

    // Rejects cross-origin state-changing requests using Sec-Fetch-Site,
    
// an Origin allow-list, and an Origin/Host fallback. No per-request
    
// token state required.
    
let layer = CsrfLayer::new().add_trusted_origin("https://example.com")?;
    

    let service = ServiceBuilder::new().layer(layer).service_fn(handler);

  • timeout: add DeadlineBody for non-resetting body timeouts, applied via the new RequestBodyDeadlineLayer and ResponseBodyDeadlineLayer (#688)

    Unlike TimeoutBody, which resets its deadline on every frame, DeadlineBody caps the total time of a body transfer. A slow client trickling one byte at a time never trips an idle timeout but will trip a deadline.

    use std::time::Duration;
use tower::ServiceBuilder;
use tower_http::timeout::RequestBodyDeadlineLayer;

    // Abort the request body transfer after 30s total, regardless of how
    
// frequently data arrives.
    
let service = ServiceBuilder::new()
    
.layer(RequestBodyDeadlineLayer::new(Duration::from_secs(30)))
    
.service_fn(handler);

  • fs: add strong ETag support to ServeDir, including If-Match and If-None-Match precondition handling per RFC 9110. 304 Not Modified responses now carry the ETag and Last-Modified validators (#691)

  • fs: add a Backend trait to make ServeDir work with non-filesystem sources (e.g. embedded assets or object storage). The default TokioBackend preserves existing behavior. Use ServeDir::with_backend() to plug in custom implementations (#684)

    use tower_http::services::fs::ServeDir;

    // MyBackend implements tower_http::services::fs::Backend.
    
// The default ServeDir::new() continues to use TokioBackend (local FS).
    
let service = ServeDir::with_backend("assets", MyBackend::new());

  • body: UnsyncBoxBody::new() constructor and From<ServeFileSystemResponseBody> conversion to avoid double-boxing when combining ServeDir responses with other body types (#537)

title: chore(deps): bump kube from 3.1.0 to 4.0.0 in /platform/services/deployd-api-rs
body:
Bumps [kube](https://github.com/kube-rs/kube) from 3.1.0 to 4.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from kube's releases.

4.0.0

New Major

As per the release schedule to match up with the latest Kubernetes ハル release. Lots of fixes and improvements. Thanks to everyone who contributed!

Kubernetes v1_36 support via k8s-openapi 0.28

Please upgrade k8s-openapi along with kube to avoid conflicts.

CEL Validation

A new optional crate kube-cel is being re-exported through kube::core::cel via kube-rs/kube#1954

Kubernetes CRDs support CEL validation rules via x-kubernetes-validations, and were supported from 3.0 via KubeSchema, but these rules could only be evaluated server-side by the API server.

The new crate allows evaluating these rules locally using rules matching the upstream Kubernetes CEL libraries.

While low-level, a higher-level CEL validator integrates with CustomResource via #[kube(cel)] from kube-rs/kube#2011 and can be used as;

#[derive(CustomResource, Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, KubeSchema)]
#[kube(group = "example.com", version = "v1", kind = "Foo", namespaced)]
#[kube(cel, validation = "self.spec.replicas >= 0")] // cel trigger + validation rule
struct FooSpec { replicas: i32 }

let foo = Foo::new("test", FooSpec { replicas: -1 });
foo.validate_cel()?;                     // new impl; checks creation rules
new_foo.validate_cel_update(&old_foo)?;  // new impl; checks transition rules

See examples/crd_derive_cel.rs for more details.

This is available under the kube/cel feature, courtesy of @​doxxx93.

Config

A lot of improvements to config handling;

  • better error handling of malformed client certs in kube-rs/kube#1966
  • add missing Kubeconfig fields in kube-rs/kube#1965
  • Kubeconfig future key compatibility for new fields by adding catch-all other key via kube-rs/kube#1964
  • deserialization changed from serde-yaml to serde-saphyr to get rid of the long-deprecated dependency. kube-rs/kube#1975

Retry and Timeouts

Better timeout and retry handling to better deal with flaky network conditions, and busy or initializing apiservers.

  • default global read timeouts has been unset in favor of watcher level timeouts in kube-rs/kube#1945 (see kube-rs/kube#1798 for context)
  • regular (non-watch) queries now respect the RetryPolicy - now enabled by default in kube-rs/kube#2007.

title: spec(217): make the engine swap sharding-aware; supersede 188 Phase 4b
body:
## What

Text-only update to spec 217 (engine swap, draft) so it is sharding-aware and 4b-aware, making 217 the single accurate home for OAP's adoption of spec-spine per-spec index sharding (spec-spine spec 024).

## Why

217 was drafted against spec-spine 0.4.0 (monolithic index) and before spec 188 Phase 4b. Since then: 4b de-committed the monolithic `index.json` (gitignored, rebuilt on demand), and spec-spine 024 shards both registry and index. 217's index handling (FR-303, Phase 0/3/4) was stale.

## Changes (spec text only)

- **§1**: a sharding-model note (target the sharded spec-spine release, commit shard trees, supersede 4b) + the overlay open item.
- **Phase 0 / FR-000**: target the SHARDED spec-spine release (not 0.4.0); re-run the dry run and assert a sane shard set.
- **FR-303 / Phase 3**: commit the sharded `by-spec/`/`by-package/` trees, not a monolithic `index.json`; restore present-on-clone (spec 101 SC-06) in a conflict-free form, superseding 188 Phase 4b's de-commit.
- **Phase 4**: repoint the `oap-index-regen` merge-driver globs to the shard paths; drop OAP's overlay `codebase-index.schema.json` for spec-spine's shard schemas.

## Not in this PR (intentionally)

- 217's implementation (the engine swap migration) and the `amends: 188` edge + the SC-06 restoration: those land when 217 is executed (relationship-graph current-truth discipline), not in this draft.
- Execution is gated upstream on spec-spine cutting a release that includes sharding and approving its spec 024.

## Validation (local)

`spec-compiler compile` clean; `spec-lint` exit 0; featuregraph golden unchanged; coupling OK (the `spec.md` edit self-claims, no code paths). No code changes; the index is gitignored post-4b, so nothing derived enters the diff.
