title: feat(188): Phase 4b de-commit broad codebase index for clean auto-merge
body:
## What

Implements spec 188 Phase 4b (the one item it left deferred): the broad `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` is now **gitignored and rebuilt on demand**, never committed.

## Why (clean auto-merge)

A committed monolithic index with one global content hash is a per-PR merge-conflict point: every spec PR rewrites it, GitHub's server-side merge (web button and merge queue) does not run the local `oap-index-regen` driver, so it reports a conflict and the merge queue ejects sibling PRs whose speculative merge collides on it. De-committing it removes that shared byte surface, so the queue forms clean speculative stacks and **auto-merge stops throwing off other in-flight PRs**.

The coupling gate already rebuilds the index ephemerally in CI (`ci-spec-code-coupling.yml`), and the governed slice (`claudeConfigHash`) already lives in its own committed `config-hash.json` (Phase 4a), so the broad index carried nothing governed: only present-on-clone convenience (spec 101 SC-06), which this reverses.

## Changes

- `.gitignore`: drop the `index.json` re-include (`config-hash.json` stays committed).
- Untrack `index.json`; retire `cd-index-staleness-report.yml` (nothing committed to report staleness on).
- Makefile (`pr-prep`, `ci-tools`, `ci-fast-tools`): drop the broad staleness `check`; `setup` / `validate-and-fix` skills: `codebase-indexer compile`, not `check`.
- `ci-parity-check`: model the `check-config` step as reading the tracked `config-hash.json` (not the now-untracked `index.json`), fixing its fresh-clone precondition.
- Amend spec 101 (SC-06 present-on-clone reversed), spec 188 (Phase 4b to done), spec 182 (records that it owns the two skill-doc updates).

## Validation (local)

`spec-compiler compile` clean; `spec-lint` exit 0; featuregraph golden matches; `ci-parity-check` live drift OK; `index.json` absent from the change set (untracked). Merged latest `main` (#366) and kept `index.json` deleted (the transitional modify/delete race a concurrent spec PR causes; it ends once this PR lands and `main` stops committing the index).

## Successor / relationship to the merge queue

Per-spec index sharding (spec-spine, planned) will restore a committed-but-conflict-free present-on-clone form, superseding this reversal. It complements the merge queue rather than replacing it: sharding removes spurious index ejects; the queue still catches genuine "green alone, broken together" conflicts.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: spec 188 Phase 4b. The Makefile recipe edits (removing the retired broad `codebase-indexer check` from the ci-tools / ci-fast-tools / pr-prep targets) incidentally fall in the `registry` and `spec-lint` co-authority sections, owned by specs (102/160, 128/147) unrelated to the codebase index; the substantive design change is amended into specs 101 and 188, and no behavior owned by those section-owner specs changes.

body:
## What

Files the OAP half of the certificate/attestation vending architecture (ADR 0002 follow-on), grounded against the real repos by the R-1 read.

- **ADR 0002** (`docs/adr/`): the run certificate is run-provenance (factory-engine), not spec-spine's authority-ledger domain; the fix is a second vended distributable, not spec-spine subcommands.
- **spec 218 — run-cert corpus binding**: an additive, optional `corpus_binding` chain edge on the governance certificate that references the spec-spine ledger seal's `attestation_hash` by value, plus a read-not-recompute dependency deny-rule (the cert crate may keep the registry reader but never a corpus-compile/attestation-emit edge). Two-link audit chain: a reproducible corpus link and a signed run link.
- **spec 219 — tenant-tail verifier toolkit**: vend the run-side verify surface as a separate `tenant-tail` repo (mirroring spec-spine's npm distribution). Per the R-1 read, two verify cores exist and extract cleanly today, so the toolkit ships **two verbs now** (`verify-certificate`, `verify-provenance`); `verify-sbom` is forward-declared and staged (spec 203 is unimplemented and, by its own design, its verify side extends the cert core). Retires the stale `cargo install --git` template path (FR-006).

## R-1 grounding (residuals note, "R-1 read: findings")

- `FactoryPipelineState` is a genuinely slim carrier (serde+std); ADR 0002 OQ-1 refuted.
- Cert core sheds as a bounded module set; provenance core is already its own crate (`crates/provenance-validator`).
- The only spec-spine seam is `validate_spec_id_resolution`, warn-only (no verdict change), feature-gated off for the vended build.

## Validation (local)

- `spec-compiler compile` clean; 218/219 register.
- `spec-lint` exit 0 (fail-on-warn).
- featuregraph golden regenerated (both specs present); `cargo test -p featuregraph` passes.
- codebase index regenerated; `codebase-indexer check` fresh.
- coupling gate OK against `origin/main` (4 paths).

## Cross-repo context (not in this PR)

- The spec-spine **ledger seal** (`023-ledger-seal`) is a ready-to-file artifact for a spec-spine-rooted agent (cross-corpus dep tracked in prose, never as a registry edge).
- The **tenant-tail** repo is scaffolded separately; its verifier implementation is a separate handoff. Its CI would be red until that lands, so it is intentionally not PR'd here.

title: feat(213): tenant repo image build and artifact-ref record

## Summary

Closes the deferral spec 137 recorded as "CI / container-build for tenant repos (separate spec)". A factory-created project repo previously received only the `oap-verify.yml` governance stub: nothing built an OCI image for the scaffolded commit, and the GitHub webhook preview-deploy path assumed a `ghcr.io` image tag no workflow produced. This spec seeds an active container-build workflow into created repos, locks the image-ref naming convention, and gives stagecraft a `project_artifacts` record plus a deterministic artifact-ref derivation so the deploy path (spec 215) can resolve "the image for this commit" without guessing.

First of the deploy-path trilogy (213 this, 214 chart supersession, 215 deploy-trigger-ux). Independent of 214; both are prerequisites of 215.

The seed lives on the per-request scaffold path (the one that actually has an `apps/api` to build), extending the spec 138 / 112 scaffold assembly.
- **`schema.ts` + `migrations/48_project_artifacts.{up,down}.sql`**: the `project_artifacts` table (establishes the migration pair) recording built image refs per project.
- **`deploy/artifacts.ts`** (+ 11 tests): deterministic artifact-ref derivation (`deriveArtifactRef` / `derivePreviewRef` / tri-state `artifactExists`), FR-005 / FR-006.

title: spec(217): Phase 1b @opc package ownership edges (L-001 15→8)
body:
## Phase 1b: @opc package ownership edges

Continues the spec-spine-library migration (spec 217). Phase 1a (#363)
cleared the 47 L-004 short-id edges and ran the corpus-wide full-id
migration. Phase 1b resolves the L-001 (no-ownership-edge) warnings the
spec-spine 0.4.0 library lint emits, **reducing L-001 from 15 to 8.**

### What L-001 catches

The 0.4.0 library lint flags a spec that declares no ownership edge
(`establishes` / `extends` / `refines` / `supersedes` / `amends` /
`co_authority` / `constrains`) and is not `origin: retroactive`. It is
stricter than the in-tree V-020: `references:` (spec-156 provenance)
does not count as ownership. In-tree CI is unaffected (V-020 already
fires on zero specs).

### Disposition (three buckets)

**Fixed (7): under-annotated specs that own live code.**
Six `@opc/*` package specs carried only stale `references: historical`
pointing at pre-relocation paths that no longer exist, while their code
lives in `product/packages/*` (1.3k to 3.7k LOC each) whose
`package.json` `oap.spec` already names the spec as owner. The
frontmatter under-claimed; the fix reconciles it with the manifest.

| Spec | Edge added | Package |
|---|---|---|
| 056 session-memory | establishes | product/packages/session-memory |
| 057 notification-system | establishes | product/packages/notification-orchestrator |
| 058 file-mention-system | establishes | product/packages/file-mention |
| 060 panel-event-bus | establishes | product/packages/panel-event-bus |
| 061 conductor-track-lifecycle | establishes | product/packages/conductor-track |
| 062 multi-model-chaining | establishes | product/packages/multi-model-chaining |
| 070 prompt-assembly-cache | extends 046 | product/packages/prompt-assembly |

070 uses `extends: 046-context-compaction` because 046 already
`establishes` `@opc/prompt-assembly`; 070 additively built the cache
layer on it. (A pre-existing graph-vs-manifest divergence remains here:
`oap.spec` says 070 but the establishes edge is on 046. Flagged for
separate reconciliation, not silently rewritten in this PR.)

**Left flagged (8): honestly territory-less, L-001 is correct.**
038 / 040 / 088 (superseded), 066 (vscode-extension, deferred), 081
(factory work absorbed upstream by spec 108, its directory removed),
148 / 149 / 150 (spec-147 proving-ground specimens). Making these green
would require faking `origin: retroactive` (reserved for bootstrap, a
CONST-005 violation) or a library-policy change. Per the agreed Phase 1b
disposition they stay flagged. Whether the library lint becomes a hard
CI gate, and how superseded/specimen specs are classified, is deferred
to the engine-swap CI wiring (spec 217 Phase 4).

### Validation

- spec-spine 0.4.0 `lint`: L-001 15 to 8 (all 7 targets cleared)
- in-tree `validate-graph`: passed
- in-tree `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0
- featuregraph golden: stable (no drift)
- coupling gate: OK, 8 paths, **no waiver needed** (spec.md files are not
  claimants; no code path changed; `index.json` regenerated)

Unit kind is `kind: directory, path: product/packages/X` so the edges are
existence-checked by both the in-tree indexer and the future library,
independent of the unresolved `@opc` package-discovery gap (the separate
I-003 bucket).

title: feat(209): born-with kernel completeness + spec_spine_version pin (foundation)
body:
## Summary

Spec 209 (tenant-kernel-ci-enforcement) **foundation** increment: the
OAP-resident, tenant-emitter-independent slice. The tenant-side certificate
legs are deferred (see Residuals). Specs 203 and 210 are **not** in this PR; the
branch name is the umbrella for the ASI-forward arc, but only 209's foundation
is included here.

## What landed

- **FR-002 reframed (CONST-005 resolution).** The sketch FR-002 said the
  project-creation pipeline transition invokes kernel emission and "closes the
  spec 167 production pipeline auto-fire deferral." That contradicted approved
  spec 167 §2.4/§7, which deliberately leaves the engine `emit_project_kernel`
  auto-fire **unwired** to avoid a double-emit (the live emission layer is the
  stagecraft TypeScript Create flow, not the engine transition). FR-002 is
  reframed to deliver the same fail-closed *guarantee* against the live TS path:
  `perRequestScaffold.ts` re-reads `.kernel-version` after writing it and
  refuses to complete creation with a missing or partial kernel.
- **`KernelOrigin.spec_spine_version`** (`version.rs`): the Rust struct now
  round-trips the npm pin the TS stamp already writes (FR-004 OAP half) instead
  of silently dropping it. A test pins the TS/Rust `.kernel-version` schema gap
  (the TS stamp omits `source_hash`/`factory_engine_version`, so a full Rust
  read still fails) so the residual stays visible, not silent.
- **`emit.rs`**: threads `spec_spine_version: None` through the non-npm engine
  fallback.
- **spec 209 frontmatter**: refines edges retargeted off the retired `emit.rs`
  vendored-CI premise onto live production surfaces (`perRequestScaffold.ts`,
  `version.rs`, `emit.rs`); `implementation: in-progress`.

## Verification (local)

- factory-engine: version tests 6/6, kernel_emission lib 25/25, tenant_emission
  integration 7/7
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (stagecraft)
- spec registry compiles; spec-lint clean
- codebase index regenerated; `check` fresh
- spec/code coupling gate: OK (5 paths)
- featuregraph golden regenerated (diff scoped to 209's `implementation` field;
  claimed by 209's `extends` edge, no waiver needed)

## Residuals (the regroup driver)

The npm tenant toolchain (`spec-spine` CLI) exposes only
`compile/registry/index/lint/couple/init` with no certificate emit/verify, so
the tenant-side legs are blocked until that surface exists:

- 209 FR-001 verify-certificate step; FR-003 tenant-emit auto-fire
- 203 FR-003 and 210 FR-002/FR-003 tenant-side cert binding + cross-check

`tenant-tail` (the new tool providing `verify-certificate / verify-provenance /
verify-sbom`) is the surface that closes this. 203 and 210 are deferred pending
re-analysis against tenant-tail.

title: feat(214): tenant app chart supersession Stage 1 (additive aim-vue-encore deploy path)

## Summary

The destructive retirement of tenant-hello (the supersession itself) is **Stage 2, a follow-up PR**.

This is the second of the deploy-path trilogy (213 tenant-repo-image-build, 214 this, 215 deploy-trigger-ux). 213 is on its own branch.

## What lands (FR mechanisms, all additive)

- **`platform/charts/aim-vue-encore/`** (FR-001/003/006): single-image Encore API + bundled SPA chart. Port 4000, non-root + read-only rootfs, `/health/liveness` + `/health/readiness` probes, ConfigMap-free env-var runtime config, opt-in preview Postgres (StatefulSet + Service + generated-credentials Secret), the spec-137 access-gate annotation seam ported verbatim, and ingress TLS.

- **`ci-tenant-app.yml`** + `ci.yml` route: helm lint + renders (default / gate+tls / preview-db) and the **FR-011 gate-seam render-parity check** that gates the Stage 2 retirement (tenant-hello vs aim-vue-encore: the 3 `auth-*` annotations + the TLS `secretName` asserted byte-identical, with an empty-extraction guard).

## Gates (green locally)

title: fix(116): pnpm audit advisory response (form-data/vite/protobufjs high GHSAs)
body:
## Summary

Unblocks the merge queue. `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` (the spec 116 supply-chain gate) fails on the product (pnpm) workspace for **every** candidate, because three high-severity advisories landed in transitive deps no recent PR touched. Surfaced on the #363 merge_group run, but pre-existing on `main`.

| Package | Vulnerable | Fixed | Advisory |
|---|---|---|---|
| form-data | <4.0.6 | 4.0.6 | GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx |

| protobufjs | <=7.6.0 | 7.6.4 | GHSA-wcpc-wj8m-hjx6 |

All three patched releases are clean in-major bumps with no known regression against the OPC build, so each is taken via `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `overrides` (a real fix), not an audit ignore. Merge this first to green the queue, then re-enqueue #363 (which fails only on this pre-existing advisory, not its own content).

title: spec(217): keystone + Phase 0 config + Phase 1 hygiene + corpus-wide full-id migration
body:
## Summary

Foundation PR for the spec-spine engine-swap-collapse mission. Three things:

1. **Keystone + Phase 0 config** for spec 217.
2. **Phase 1 corpus hygiene** (the L-004 edge cleanup the library 0.4.0 audit surfaced).
3. **Corpus-wide full-id migration** to make the corpus ready for short-id resolution being removed at the `spec-spine` library level.

It does **not** delete any in-tree engine crate or rewire call sites (Phases 2 through 6).

## Corpus-wide full-id migration (commit 2)

The library is dropping short-id resolution. Beyond the `amends` edges fixed in commit 1, the library currently silently resolves short ids in `depends_on` / `superseded_by` / `supersedes`, and the OAP indexer resolves `amendment_record`. None of those tripped a lint, but all break the moment resolution is removed.

This expands **all 410 quoted bare short-ids (`"NNN"`) to full slugs (`"NNN-slug"`) across 108 specs**, frontmatter only. Every occurrence was in exactly four id-reference fields: `depends_on` (395), `amendment_record` (10), `superseded_by` (4), `supersedes` (1). No body prose touched; zero false positives (every quoted bare-number frontmatter token was an id reference). After this, **no spec frontmatter uses a short id anywhere**.

## Keystone + Phase 0 config (commit 1)

- **specs/217**: the 7-phase plan to replace OAP's in-tree generic spec-spine engine with the published `spec-spine` library. Establishes `spec-spine.toml`; extends spec 034's featuregraph golden. The supersession/amendment wave (section 6) is a documented plan, deliberately **not** in frontmatter yet (CONST-005: the relationship graph is current truth, not declared intent).
- **spec-spine.toml**: root config (namespace=oap, 4 domains, 16 kinds, dual standalone Rust crates, product/ pnpm workspace, stagecraft standalone-npm). Library 0.4.0 compiles the full 218-spec corpus 0/0.

## Phase 1 corpus hygiene (commit 1, clears all 47 library L-004 warnings)

- Expand 43 short-numeric `amends` ids to full slugs across 22 specs (string-not-object grammar preserved).
- Remove the erroneous `105-axiomregent-sidecar` co-authority member from specs 127/128/134/135. Spec 105 owns the Makefile `axiomregent-build` section, not the four sections it was copy-pasted into; the member lists were already asymmetric.

## Verification

- Library 0.4.0: `compile` 0/0; `lint` 0 errors, **0 L-004**.
- In-tree: `spec-compiler compile`, `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`, `registry-consumer validate-graph` all exit 0.
- `codebase-indexer check` exit 0; codebase index + featuregraph golden regenerated.
- Spec/code coupling gate: **OK, 114 paths, exit 0** (coupling-clean, no waiver).

## Deferred to Phase 1b

The 15 remaining library L-001 (no-ownership-edge) warnings need per-spec honest dispositions: 7 are genuine owners missing a typed `establishes` edge (056/057/058/060/061/062/070); 6 are honestly territory-less (066 deferred; 148/149/150 kind-grammar specimens; 038/040/088 superseded); 081 needs investigation. CONST-005-sensitive (no fake edges to silence the lint); lands separately.

title: feat(216): Phase 2b supersession filtering in authorities(P)
body:
Completes spec 216 Phase 2b: the consumer-side supersession filtering. Phase 1 (#360, bare-id `amends` + V-033) and Phase 2a (#361, typed `supersedes` parse + V-034 + structured emission) are merged; this finishes the trilogy.

## What this does

Spec 133 §3 has *always* defined `authorities(P)` to exclude superseded predecessors (the `¬ ∃ later_spec` clause), but the coupling gate's `legitimate_owners` never implemented it: a superseded spec conferred authority exactly as a live claimant. Phase 2b makes the runtime match the spec.

- **codebase-index** (FR-010): `TraceMapping` gains an additive `supersedes` field carrying each spec's **partial**-scope edges (predecessor id + `unit:` resolved to physical paths). `SCHEMA_VERSION` 3.0.0 → 3.1.0 (the gate's compat check is major-only, so this is backward-compatible); `codebase-index.schema.json` widened additively. Full supersession is *not* carried here: it is represented by the predecessor's `spec_status`.
- **gate** (FR-011/FR-012): a `SupersessionFilter` drops fully-superseded predecessors (via `spec_status`) from every path, and partially-superseded ones over the unit's paths (containment-aware, mirroring `claim_matches`) from `legitimate_owners` and the section-aware resolver. The live successor stays the owner (it already claims the path via the folded supersedes unit).
- **registry-consumer** (FR-013): `by-authority` gains a `supersedes` matcher and removes the partial predecessor, so it reports the same `authorities(P)` the gate enforces (closing the supersession slice of the gate/by-authority read divergence). `show-relationships` surfaces the unit-resolved path.

## Corpus verification (the load-bearing check)

**Zero paths lose all live owners.** Verified via `by-authority` on every at-risk path:

- **Full:** 038/040/088 claim no code; 044's three `crates/orchestrator/*` paths each retain live co-owners (092/094/097/098/099/100/102/198/202). Note: 044 is caught by `spec_status`, not an edge: its successor 089 carries no `supersedes:` edge, so the status-based filter is strictly more robust than §3's literal edge-based clause.
- **Partial:** 114→113 `clone.ts` and 214→136's four `tenant-hello` units now resolve to the live successor (`via: supersedes`); 199→{108,140,141} are note-only and a no-op.

## Coupling

No waiver needed. Each touched source file is cleared by amending its existing owner's `spec.md`: 133 (gate `authority-derivation` region + the §3 clause it specifies), 154 (indexer + index-schema unit surface), 181 (registry-consumer authority resolver), 188 (set the schema to 3.0.0 in Phase 4a and owns the version-assertion test). Spec 216 stays `draft` pending approval.

## Tests

- Gate: 6 supersession fixtures (full drop, partial path-scoped, note-only no-op, dead-successor inert, directory-containment, end-to-end gate).
- registry-consumer: 3 `by-authority` supersedes fixtures (partial unit, path-scoped, full-string-confers-nothing).
- All three crates green; `validate-graph` clean; `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` exit 0; coupling gate clean; featuregraph golden unchanged.

title: feat(216): supersedes typed parse + V-034 + structured emission (Phase 2a)
body:
## What

Implements **Phase 2a** of spec 216: converge OAP's spec-compiler `supersedes` parse onto the standalone spec-spine library. A bare id is full-scope shorthand; a `{spec, scope, unit?, note?, rationale?}` object carries partial scope. This replaces the silent-drop `optional_string_list` site (`lib.rs:282`) — the `supersedes` analogue of the spec 125 `amends` defect — which discarded **every structured partial entry** to `null`.

This is the **producer side**. Phase 2b (the consumer side: coupling-gate `legitimate_owners()` supersession filtering + registry-consumer reader `paths`->`unit` alignment) is the authority-semantics change and is sequenced separately (spec §2.4) for its own review pass. Phase 2a changes no gating decision today (the gate ignores `supersedes`), so it is safe ahead of 2b.

## Changes (mapped to FRs/ACs)

- **FR-005/006/007** `spec-compiler/src/lib.rs`: `parse_supersedes` + **V-034**. Full-scope entries (bare string, `{spec}`, `{spec, scope: full}`) normalise to a bare id; partial entries emit `{spec, scope: partial, unit?, note?, rationale?}`. Malformed envelopes (missing `spec`, bad `scope`, unknown key, non-string-non-map) reject with V-034; the `unit:` shape is still validated by V-021..V-024. `Feature.supersedes` widens `Option<Vec<String>>` -> `Option<Value>` (the `establishes` precedent). Partial does **not** require `unit:` (a prose `note:` suffices — spec 199 is the live precedent).
- **FR-008** `registry.schema.json`: `supersedes.items` widened to `oneOf:[string, supersedeScopedItem]` (new `$def`). Strictly additive per **spec 153**; authorised by 216's new `extends:{nature: additive, unit: registry.schema.json}` edge (the **spec 154** precedent on this same file). No `specVersion` bump.
- **FR-009** `spec-types/src/lib.rs`: corrected the `supersedes` known-key comment. **spec 130 §2.4**: reconciled the doc-template `paths:` -> canonical `unit:` (spec 154 §6); amendment recorded in 130's `amendment_record`.
- **AC-007..012** `tests/v034_supersedes_typed.rs`: partial-unit records structured; partial-by-`note` (no unit) is clean; all full-scope forms normalise to one bare-string list; malformed-envelope matrix rejects with V-034.
- Regenerated codebase index + featuregraph golden. **Spec 214**'s four partial entries and **spec 199**'s note-scoped partials now emit structured (were `null`); **073/108/154** full entries emit bare strings.

## Verification

- `cargo test` spec-compiler: green (4 new v034 tests + existing suite)
- `spec-compiler compile`: exit 0 — embedded-schema self-validation passes on the structured registry (AC-011); no V-034 on the real corpus
- `spec-lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0 · `registry-consumer validate-graph`: clean (AC-010)
- `spec-code-coupling-check` (local pr-prep): clean, 8 paths · `cargo clippy`: clean

## Scope / risk note

Phase 2a is intentionally **not** registry-byte-identical (it is an authority-*representation* change): specs that already author structured partial `supersedes` move from `null` to the form they always meant. No previously-*valid* `supersedes` document changes meaning (the widen is additive; bare strings and full objects still normalise to the same bare strings). The load-bearing `authorities(P)` change is deferred to Phase 2b.

title: feat(216): amends bare-id grammar adoption (Phase 1) with loud V-033
body:
## What

Implements **Phase 1** of spec 216 (`spec-spine-library-grammar-adoption`): converge OAP's spec-compiler `amends` parse onto the standalone spec-spine library. `amends` is **bare-id only**; a non-string (object) entry is now a hard **V-033** compile error instead of the former silent empty-list collapse (the latent spec 125 defect PR #358 corrected).

This is behaviour-preserving for the real corpus: zero live object-form `amends` remain after #358, so the registry is byte-identical and the corpus compiles clean.

## Changes (mapped to FRs/ACs)

- **FR-001/FR-002** `tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/src/lib.rs`: new `parse_amends` + V-033 error-severity violation. Distinguishes *absent* (ok, empty) from *present-but-non-string* (rejected), mirroring the library's reject-on-object behaviour. The malformed field is dropped so the registry stays schema-conformant (the V-007 precedent); V-033 is the source of truth. Message names the bare-id / `refines` / `amends_sections` remediation verbatim.

title: fix(125): structured amends → bare-id + refines (WS-B Phase 1 prep)
body:
First corpus-hygiene step toward consuming the standalone **spec-spine 0.3.0** library (the in-tree-engine collapse, WS-B). Behavior-preserving for OAP today; clears the last *compile* blocker when the corpus is compiled by the library.

## What

Spec 125 authored its two code-unit claims on `amends`:

```yaml
amends:
  - spec: "120-factory-extraction-stage"
    unit: { kind: file, path: tools/oap/schema-parity-check/index.mjs }
  - spec: "120-factory-extraction-stage"
    unit: { kind: file, path: platform/services/stagecraft/api/knowledge/extractionOutput.ts }
```

Rewritten to a bare-id `amends` plus two `refines` units:

```yaml
amends:
  - "120-factory-extraction-stage"
refines:
  - aspect: "schema-parity-walker"
    unit: { kind: file, path: tools/oap/schema-parity-check/index.mjs }
  - aspect: "schema-parity-walker"
    unit: { kind: file, path: platform/services/stagecraft/api/knowledge/extractionOutput.ts }
```

## Why

`amends` grants co-authority over a predecessor's **spec.md**, not its code — and OAP's coupling gate derives authority from `establishes`/`extends`/`refines`/`co_authority`/`constrains`, **not** `amends`. So the amends-units were decorative (type-checked, no authority). Moving them to `refines` puts the claims on a behavior edge and correctly makes 125 a coupling owner of the parity-walker files it rebuilt. The bare `amends: ["120-…"]` preserves 125's amendment relationship to 120.

This is also the structured form the generic spec-spine grammar rejects (`amends` is an id-list there) — the single remaining compile error when the OAP corpus is compiled by the library.

## Validation

- `make pr-prep`: coupling gate clean (9 paths checked); codebase-index refreshed.
- Registry now records bare `amends` + the two `refines` units; index fresh; only `spec.md` + the tracked `index.json` change.
- spec-spine 0.3.0 compiles the full OAP corpus with **0 errors, 0 warnings** after this fix.

body:
## What

Full implementation of spec 200 (`substrate-override-async-scanner`, ASI06 model-assisted detection) — all four phases in the spec's order — plus the spec's own `implementation: pending → complete` flip with frontmatter edges for every established/refined unit, the §Sequencing gate-discharge note, and the interim OQ-1 resolution.

## The cross-cutting principle, preserved verbatim

> A model may **detect**; only rules may **block**.

Every enforcement surface is a deterministic DB read; the scanner never rejects a write synchronously and never lifts its own quarantines; the quarantine key is provably sourced from the run row, never from model output (AC-7 fixture).

## Phases

1. **Rules first (FR-003/004/006)** — consumed-override hashes join the revocation sweep at serve (`collectConsumedOverrides`, checked before the verified predicate — quarantine wins), grant issue/renew (`sweepCompositionRevocations` extends its key set with active override hashes), the spec 201 approval-summary parity replica (inline, cycle-avoidance), and the FR-003(c) user-authored agent serve paths named per the FR: `runAgentRefs.ts` (new `QuarantinedAgentError` → `failedPrecondition`) and `opcBundle.ts::loadPublishedAgents`. `liftRevocation` becomes mode-sensitive (revoked: never; quarantined: human + `factory:configure` + deterministic gate re-run + unverified reset). `verifyOverrideCore` pre-flights the quarantine.

title: fix(196): withdraw isolating cross-ns NetworkPolicies; unblock TSDB PVC
body:
## Incident

Within minutes of #345 reconciling, all four public hosts went down with Cloudflare 521 (origin connection refused): `stagecraft.ing`, `auth.`, `deploy.`, `minio.`. `CD stagecraft` failed at the `seed-rauthy` job (run 27427072672); the `knowledge-orphan-imported-sweeper` cron failed every cycle. (`CD deployd-api-rs` run 27427072405 failed separately on a GHA cache-export flake, `error writing layer blob: not_found`; unrelated, rerun.)

## Root cause

The three policies in `namespace-baseline/networkpolicy-allow-metrics-egress.yaml` shipped under a false premise the file itself documented: that allows are "dormant-additive" until a namespace gains default-deny. A NetworkPolicy isolates every pod it selects for the listed policy type, so:

1. `ingress-nginx` (`podSelector: {}`, Ingress, allow only monitoring:10254): controller rejected 80/443 from the Hetzner LB. k3s netpol REJECTs rather than drops, hence 521 not 522.
2. `stagecraft-system` (`podSelector: {}`, Egress, allow only monitoring:9090): every stagecraft pod lost DNS, in-namespace Postgres, Rauthy, GitHub (the seeder's `fetch failed`).
3. `deployd-system` (`app=deployd-api`, Ingress, allow only monitoring:8080): blocked nginx ingress on the shared :8080.

## Fix

- Delete the file; reduce the `policies` apply set to `monitoring/networkpolicy-monitoring.yaml`. The monitoring-namespace objects (default-deny + named flows) are correct and stay; their halves carry today's traffic end to end because no other namespace is isolated.
- FR-006/SC-005 corrected in spec 196 + incident addendum: outside-`monitoring` halves land WITH their namespace's enforced default-deny under its own spec, where the full legitimate flow set is enumerated together.
- Bonus unblock: `cleanPrometheusOperatorObjectNames: true`. The 71-char operator-default PVC name overflowed hcloud's 63-char volume-label cap (`invalid input in field 'labels'`), so the TSDB PVC never bound. PVC name drops to 48 chars; the chart-owned `monitoring-prometheus` Service (FR-001 remote_write literal) is unchanged.

## Post-merge (T042, V011/V012)

Resume the `policies` Flux Kustomization (suspended during mitigation), confirm the three objects stay pruned and public hosts return non-5xx, rerun the failed CD jobs, confirm TSDB PVC `Bound`.

Coupling gate: clean (6 paths). Featuregraph golden: unchanged.

title: spec(202): refine blast-radius governor from sketch to implementable FRs
body:
## What

Spec 202 (`run-blast-radius-governor`, the ASI08 residual owner) was filed 2026-06-11 with FRs and ACs explicitly marked "sketch — refine before implementation". This PR is that refinement pass: spec text only, no code, no lifecycle change (stays `draft` / `implementation: pending`), sequencing gate on spec 198 `implementation: complete` intact.

## Why now

Refinement is the spec's own designated next step and is not gated; only implementation is. Doing it pre-gate means the FRs are implementable the day 198 flips.

## What changed

- **New §Code reality** — five surveyed findings that shape the design: `PreStepGate` is the step-shaped instruction boundary (with `GrantRenewalGate` as the 198 FR-005 pause precedent); per-step actuals (`tokens_used`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `num_turns`, `retry_count`) exist but never accumulate run-level; `max_total_tokens` is a declared-but-unenforced stub; in-step opacity limits enforcement to step entry (the bounded-overshoot contract is now stated, not implied); the platform `runsScheduler` is a staleness sweeper, so FR-003's queue-storm lever is a new submission-time count gate.
- **FR-001** — now honours 198 P-2 predicate shape: `per_run` + uniform `per_stage` ceilings only; stage-id-keyed maps inadmissible (stage ids are run topology). Five axes defined with their concrete observation points. Schema 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 with the Rust twin same-PR (compile-time const); Tier B lockstep posture (212) noted, so the addition is OAP-unilateral.
- **FR-002** — names the seam (budget gate implementing `PreStepGate`, ordered after `GrantRenewalGate`) and the granularity contract; discharges the `max_total_tokens` stub (new AC-6).
- **FR-003** — detection split into (a) near-identical intents, (b) inter-stage oscillation (rewiring the today-unwired `circuit_breaker.rs` library, 102 FR-032/FR-035), (c) platform-side runs-in-flight gate.
- **FR-005** — certificate binding pinned inside the signed payload (1.5.0 → 1.6.0) with per-axis `{ceiling, actual, source, breached}`; `verify-certificate` gains presence + consistency checks.
- **New §Overlaps** — keeps the governor from duplicating existing per-step timeout/retry machinery.
- ACs sharpened from five sketches to seven testable criteria; `references:` gained three non-owning survey pointers (pause-channel precedent, certificate extension target, trip-pattern library).

Also fixed a pre-existing fixture-org collision between `dispatch.test.ts` and `approvalSummaryEndpoint.test.ts` (both used `88888888-…`).

## Evidence

The edits re-seed/repair those suites against the schema as already cut over by migrations 34/35/38 and the spec-199 reservation rewrite; no design of any claiming spec changes. The rot inventory and per-file disposition are recorded in spec 211 §Implementation log, which this PR amends.

title: feat(212): widen lockstep gate to dual_stack; implementation complete
body:
## What

Widens the spec-212 factory-schema-lockstep gate's section-scoped compare for `adapter-manifest.schema.yaml` from `{schema_version, governance}` to `{schema_version, governance, dual_stack}`, and closes spec 212 (`implementation: complete`).

## Why

The OPC "adapter not found" failure (fixed by #344) was stack→variant model drift in `dual_stack` — OAP's mirror sat on the legacy `audience_to_stack`/`stacks` model while factory-encore's manifest had moved to `audience_to_variant`/`variants`. That drift was invisible to the gate because spec 212 excluded `dual_stack` from the adapter-manifest compare. The `dual_stack` audience→variant mapping is consumed by OPC's adapter loading path: it is cross-repo contract surface, not an adapter-determined detail.

## Changes

- `tools/oap/factory-schema-lockstep/src/lib.rs` — `"dual_stack"` joins `include_top_keys`; two unit tests (drift flagged, aligned passes).
- `tools/oap/factory-schema-lockstep/tests/run_check_integration.rs` — baseline manifest now carries an aligned variant-model `dual_stack`; new integration test proves stack-model drift fails through `run_check` end-to-end.

title: feat(196): platform metrics stack — kube-prometheus-stack via Flux, hybrid ingestion, OIDC-only Grafana
body:
## Summary

Implements **spec 196** (platform-metrics-stack) per its locked `plan.md` — Prometheus + Grafana for the **platform control plane** (stagecraft + deployd-api + Flux + ingress-nginx oversight), Dev1 lane of the 2026-06-12 relay.

Both plan phases land as manifests in one PR: the Phase-2 boundary is the **operator's manual Rauthy-client step** (Grafana blocks on the `grafana-oidc` Secret until `.env` is filled and `setup.sh` re-run — the documented `[manual]` OIDC-client convention, same contract as `rauthy-smtp-secret`), not a second code drop.

## What this does

- **Hybrid ingestion (FR-001/002/003):** one Prometheus *server* (`kube-prometheus-stack 86.2.2`, pinned) receives stagecraft's Encore `remote_write` push (`infra.config.hetzner.json` gains the `metrics` block — the first field to ever diverge the two infra configs) and scrapes the pull targets via an annotation-keyed job over an enumerated namespace allowlist.
- **OIDC-only Grafana (FR-004):** native `generic_oauth` against Rauthy; `role_attribute_path` on `custom.platform_role` (the spec-106 `custom.*` nesting, verified in `auth.server.ts`), locked map `owner|admin → Admin`, `member → Viewer`, `role_attribute_strict`; login form/basic/anonymous off; `disable_initial_admin_creation` — no local credential ever exists. Client creds ride a Secret, never git.
- **Receiver isolation (FR-006/SC-008):** `monitoring` ships with the deployment's **first enforced default-deny**; the unauthenticated remote_write port is reachable from `stagecraft-system` (and intra-ns) ONLY; Grafana only from ingress-nginx; egress port-bounded. Policies reconcile via a new declarative Flux `policies` tier — deliberately *not* by growing post-create.sh (spec 151 retires imperative mutation).
- **Governed knobs:** admin API explicitly off (FR-002), Alertmanager off + ~100 bundled rules pruned + kube-mixin dashboards off (FR-008), CRDs `CreateReplace` against helm-controller's silent-Skip upgrade default (FR-007), retention 15d/20Gi (FR-010).

## Current-state corrections (recorded in spec.md)

The implementation survey falsified three filing-time claims; the design is unchanged, the starting-state description is corrected:

1. **deployd-api-rs had no `/metrics` endpoint** ("already expose /metrics" was false) → endpoint **created**: `src/metrics.rs`, hand-rolled exposition, zero new crates, public beside `/healthz` (Prometheus can't do OIDC; containment is the FR-006(b) NetworkPolicy) + chart pod annotations.
2. **ingress-nginx metrics were not enabled** → `controller.metrics.enabled` + annotations in the spec-151 HelmRelease (196 `refines:` edge).
3. **No namespace had default-deny applied** (post-create.sh skips it "for MVP") → SC-005 rescoped; the stagecraft-system egress allow is declared, dormant-additive.

## Spec spine

title: fix(198): realign adapter-manifest dual_stack to canonical variant model
body:
## What

OPC's live adapter fetch failed to load `aim-vue-encore` with:

```
adapter not found: discovery failed: Invalid manifest …/aim-vue-encore/manifest.yaml:
Error("dual_stack: missing field `audience_to_stack`", line: 81, column: 3)
```

**Root cause:** the owned **factory-encore** upstream manifest uses the **variant model** (`audience_to_variant` / `variants`, where a variant is a standalone top-level copy with its own `dir` / `auth_driver` / `env_example`), while OAP's Rust `DualStack` parser, its sole consumer, and the mirror schema still carried the pre-factory-encore **stack model** (`audience_to_stack` / `stacks`). serde rejected the manifest on the first missing field.

This is a three-way drift (Rust ⟷ mirror schema ⟷ upstream); the spec-212 lockstep gate did not catch it because the adapter-manifest comparison is section-scoped to `{schema_version, governance}` and `dual_stack` is outside that surface.

## Change

Realign all three OAP-side artifacts to the canonical variant model:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/factory-contracts/src/adapter_manifest.rs` | `DualStack` fields → `audience_to_variant` / `variants`; `DualStackStacks`→`DualStackVariants`, `StackEndpoint`→`VariantEndpoint`; added optional `generator` / `dir` / `auth_driver` / `env_example` |
| `crates/factory-engine/src/manifest_gen.rs` | sole consumer: `ds.stacks.*` → `ds.variants.*`, label `Stack:`→`Variant:` |
| `standards/schemas/factory/adapter-manifest.schema.yaml` | mirror schema `dual_stack` section → variant model |
| `specs/198-factory-governance-envelope/spec.md` | implementation-log entry (198 `refines` the schema path) |
| `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` | regenerated |

## Verification

- `cargo build` + `clippy -D warnings` clean (factory-contracts, factory-engine)
- factory-contracts: 125 tests pass; factory-engine tests pass
- A throwaway test (since removed) ran the exact OPC path — `AdapterRegistry::discover` on the **real cached manifest** — and it now discovers `aim-vue-encore` with the full variant model parsed

## Deferred

The spec-212 lockstep gate's adapter-manifest coverage stays scoped to `{schema_version, governance}`; widening it to cover `dual_stack` so this drift class can't recur is a spec-212 decision, not taken here (noted in the spec 198 log).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: manifest_gen.rs edit is a mechanical .stacks→.variants field rename flowing from the spec-198 adapter-manifest dual_stack realignment; no behavioral change to the extraction/workflow/sandbox/kernel/manifest specs (075/120/162/167/170) that co-own this path. The design change's truthful home is spec 198 (the refined schema), which is amended in this PR.

title: feat(167): .kernel-version stamp in Create flow + retire vendored CI template/generator (WS5 PR 2)
body:
The implementation half of spec 167's npm-kernel self-amendment (PR #341 was the spec-only reframe). Closes WS5 PR 2.

## 1. The born-with stamp, written by the live path

stagecraft's Create flow now writes `.kernel-version` into commit #1 of every produced project — a new sibling helper (`scaffold/kernelVersionStamp.ts`) wired into `perRequestScaffold.ts` as a **step-5 write** (after the L0 pipeline-state seed, before push). It records:

- source SHA; and
- `toolchain_mode: pinned-toolchain` — the kebab-case Rust `ToolchainMode` value (spec 168 **E2** consistency rule; never the unknown `npm-devdependency` variant).

A missing pin is a **hard error**, never a silent skip.

- **Deleted `templates/kernel/tenant-ci.yml.tmpl`** + `render_tenant_workflow` — the npm born-with kernel ships CI from the prebuilt template's `spec-spine.yml` (`npx --no-install spec-spine couple`), not a Rust-rendered workflow that execs loose `tools/spec-spine/` binaries.

- The Rust `emit_kernel` path **stays as the adapter-determined fallback** (OQ-6): it still emits kernel content, the tenant Makefile, `.factory/toolchain.yaml` (spec 168), and `.kernel-version`.

## Spec-graph

- **112** + **168** carry appended narrative `amendment_record` entries (Create-flow stamp; the retirement touched 168's extends targets — its `toolchain.yaml.tmpl` establish + the certificate contract are intact).
- The deletion orphaned forward-looking edges in **draft** specs **203** (`refines` lockfile-parity-gate) and **209** (`extends` enforcing-CI) onto `tenant-ci.yml.tmpl` — repointed to the surviving tenant gate template with a note that their npm-CI premise rewrite is owed when implemented (the `spec-spine.yml` shape lives in the prebuilt template, external to OAP — plan **G3**).

## Verification

- New `kernelVersionStamp` unit suite (6 tests) + the `perRequestScaffold` dual test now assert the stamp; stagecraft typecheck clean (modulo the pre-existing `~encore/*` codegen shims).

title: feat(212): factory schema lockstep — tool + two CI lanes (cross-repo contract gate)
body:
Implements **spec 212** — automates the cross-repo factory contract lockstep that specs 197 AC-8 / 198 verified by hand. OAP-side, unidirectional (factory-encore stays `spec_spine: false`).

## Design correction (self-amend, recorded in spec)

A full file-by-file diff at the pin (`factory-encore@cc1139f`) **falsified spec 212's original FIELD-LEVEL-parity premise** for 3 of 10 files — and spec 197 had already documented why:

- `adapter-manifest.schema.yaml` is **adapter-specialised by design** (Encore-shaped `directory_conventions`, `dual_stack` `variants`, object `scaffold.source`, extra `commands`…). **197 FR-007 explicitly scoped this out.**
- `build-spec.schema.yaml` + `stage-outputs/sitemap.schema.json` carry **additive factory-side evolution** (`workspace_id`, the 24-type page_type catalog).
- **197 AC-8 only verified the narrow 1.1.0 delta** (`provisioning_model` + `implementation_status`), never whole-file parity.

A literal field-level gate would be **red on arrival against its own pin**. So the spec self-amends (FR-001/AC-1/AC-2 + lockstep-set) to a **three-mode compare** that is true at the pin and still falsifiable:

| mode | files | rule |
|---|---|---|
| **exact** | pipeline-state, verification, stage-outputs/{business-rules, entity-model, use-cases, audiences} | any structural diff fails |
| **directional floor** | build-spec, sitemap | OAP fields must persist on factory; **factory additions pass** |
| **section-scoped floor** | adapter-manifest | only `schema_version` + the `governance:` sub-envelope (198 FR-012); adapter sections excluded |

> Resolution direction (OAP-is-the-floor) and the amend-then-build approach were confirmed with the maintainer before implementation.

## What landed

- **Tool** `tools/oap/factory-schema-lockstep/` — three-mode compare + spec-197 FR-005 GoA-concept guard (classification labels / service-catalogue; strips YAML comments so the schema's own rejection-docs aren't flagged). **17 unit+integration tests.** Green at the pin; the Tier-B `governance-envelope.schema.yaml` gap is advisory and never masks a real break (AC-4).
- **PR lane** `ci-factory-schema-lockstep.yml` — sparse-fetch the pinned ref via `FACTORY_ENCORE_RO_TOKEN`, **fail-visible** (never skipped-green, AC-6), runs in `merge_group`, SHA-pinned (158); routed from `ci.yml` on the lockstep surface (177); `secrets: inherit`.
- **Cron lane** `ci-factory-schema-lockstep-cron.yml` — against `factory-encore@main`, opens/**dedups** a tracking issue rather than failing an unrelated PR (FR-004); operational failure still fails.
- **Parity + Makefile** — `ci-factory-schema-lockstep.yml` in `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS` + aligned/divergent fixtures (AC-7); `make factory-schema-lockstep` joins `ci-strict` (strict-only, FR-006); `pinned_ref` in frontmatter (FR-007).

## Verification

- coupling gate **OK** (graph-truthful via `establishes`/`extends`/`co_authority` edges, **no waiver**)
- `ci-parity-check` **OK** (12 enforcing workflows) · featuregraph golden + codebase index regenerated · spec-lint + workflow-pins lint clean · tool green at `cc1139f`

## Notes

- `FACTORY_ENCORE_RO_TOKEN` (read-only contents on `GovAlta-Pronghorn/factory-encore`) has been added to the org action secrets, so both lanes can fetch.
- Spec 212 `implementation: pending → in-progress`.

body:
Manual equivalents of the six open dependabot PRs (#318, #319, #320, #321, #322, #250), authored per the manual-patch-over-dependabot discipline (dependabot PRs are bump-availability signal only).

## What rides

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/provider-registry` | dashmap 5 → 6 (major; usage is plain `DashMap` new/insert — compiles + tests green) |
| `crates/orchestrator` | rusqlite widened to `>=0.39, <0.41` (see below) |
| `product/apps/opc/src-tauri` | rusqlite 0.40.1 + libsqlite3-sys 0.38.1; lock group: ignore 0.4.26, regex 1.12.4, regex-syntax 0.8.11, uuid 1.23.3, which 8.0.3 |

## Why the rusqlite range (and why dependabot's #322 is red)

hiqlite 0.13 (latest published, via axiomregent in the root workspace) pins rusqlite `^0.39`, and libsqlite3-sys's `links = "sqlite3"` forbids two versions in one resolution graph — a flat 0.40 bump cannot resolve at root. The range lets root resolve 0.39 while the isolated opc src-tauri workspace (no hiqlite) takes 0.40.1. Collapse to a flat `"0.40"` once hiqlite accepts rusqlite 0.40.

title: feat(184): session-freshness context survives compaction
body:
## Summary

- Widens the SessionStart session-freshness hook matcher in `.claude/settings.json` from `startup|resume|clear` to `startup|resume|clear|compact`. Compaction summarizes the session context, so the freshness line injected at session start can be summarized away while registry/index state drifts mid-session; SessionStart re-runs on every firing (documented exemption from mid-session stale-replay), so the `compact` matcher re-injects current freshness state into the post-compaction window.
- Records the change as the third dated entry in spec 184's Baseline evolution record with the AC-7 direction judgment: automation coverage broadened; no guard surface changed. Hook command body, permission arrays, and all other hook events are byte-identical.
- Includes the regenerated `.derived/codebase-index/` artifacts (`.claude/settings.json` is a hashed input).

## Testing

- `make pr-prep` clean: coupling gate OK (11 diff paths; the spec 184 edit covers the governed `settings.json` path — no waiver), index regenerated and committed.
- `codebase-indexer check` exits 0 on the committed tree (hashes consistent with the settings edit).
- Local adversarial review (/code-review v2): 16 findings raised, 0 confirmed, 16 refuted — evidence comment follows.
- Matcher semantics (`compact` as a SessionStart source; pipe-delimited disjunction; re-run-on-firing) verified against the official Claude Code hooks reference rather than assumed.

title: fix(112): VCS-free scaffold output — strip embedded .git in the per-request copy
body:
## What

Production project creation (Create New Project, dual variant) failed with the redacted "an internal error occurred"; the underlying error was:

```
Scaffold/push failed: git add -A exited 128:
error: 'internal/' does not have a commit checked out
```

**Root cause**: template-encore's `setup-dual-app.ts` runs `git init` inside each variant directory (`public/`, `internal/`) when invoked as a CLI — which is exactly how `templateCache.ts` materializes prebuilts. The per-request copy filtered only `node_modules`, so the embedded commit-less repos rode into the project tree, and `gitInitAndPush`'s `git add -A` refused the gitlinks. Legacy single profiles only worked by coincidence: their carried `.git` sat at the destination root, where our own `git init` harmlessly reused it.

## Fix (amend-first)

- **Spec 112 §5.3 amended** with the scaffold-output invariant: the tree handed to `gitInitAndPush` is VCS-free; repository initialization belongs to commit #1.
- **`perRequestScaffold.ts`** copy filter strips `.git` at any depth (enforcement of the stated invariant, per the P-1 enforce-don't-compensate principle). `.gitignore` files and the `node_modules` exclusion are unaffected.
- **Regression test** builds a synthetic `_prebuilt-dual` with per-variant + root `.git` dirs and asserts the output is VCS-free with payload intact (pure-filesystem; runs under bare vitest).

A companion template-encore branch gates the generator's `git init` off for machine-driven runs (developer-UX only); this stagecraft filter is the load-bearing defense regardless of generator behavior.

No cache rebuild or re-sync needed after deploy — the filter applies at per-request copy time. The two empty orphan repos from the failed attempts (`june-9-test`, `june-9-test-2`) are recorded as `orphaned` scaffold jobs per the spec 112 operator-reclaim design.

title: feat(198): phase 4 — signing authority, run-grants, certificate countersign (FR-005/FR-014)
body:
## What

Spec 198 phase 4 — the trust-fabric layer on top of the #313 admission gate. Stagecraft becomes the signing authority (the judge owns the seal); OPC stays keyless, categorically (ASI10 m6).

**Platform (stagecraft)**
- Ed25519 signing core (`signing-pure.ts` + secret-bound `signing.ts`), public JWKS at `GET /api/factory/.well-known/jwks.json` with `kid` rotation support.
- **Admission seal (FR-014)**: admitted compositions are signed over their content-addressed constituents; the seal ships in the OPC bundle's new `admission` block.
- **Run-grants (FR-005)**: `factory.run.grant_request` / `grant_renew` duplex envelopes; grants are short-lived audience-bound compact JWS, persisted in `factory_run_grants` (migration 44), renewed at every stage boundary with goal-shift detection, one-way frozen-Build-Spec binding, and the FR-010 four-key composition revocation sweep — **the grant-renewal leg of AC-8**.
- **Emission countersign**: `factory.run.completed` carries the certificate hash + final grant seq; the platform verifies the chain it issued and replies with a targeted `factory.run.certificate_countersign`.

**Engine + OPC desktop**
- `platform_jws` (Rust twin of signing-pure.ts), `intent_capsule` (stable goal id; capsule hash stable for the run's lifetime).
- Certificate **1.3.0 → 1.4.0**: `admittedEnvelopeHash`/`goalId`/`intentCapsuleHash` bound inside hash+signature; `platformCountersign` excluded from both, so sealing never invalidates the offline chain. `verify-certificate` gains `--platform-jwks` / `--jwks-url` / `--require-sealed`; an unsealed certificate verifies as **visibly unsealed** (AC-4).
- Desktop run path is now governed fail-closed (start + resume): admission-seal verification before any stage (ASI04 m1), intent capsule filed, issuance grant before s0, renewal via the new orchestrator `DispatchOptions.pre_step` gate, and — new — the desktop path now **emits the governance certificate** (previously only the headless binary did) and patches the countersign on a live completion.

## Verification

- stagecraft: 17 new `encore test` integration tests (every grant refusal reason, revocation propagation incl. agent-key, countersign chain checks) + 8 signing unit tests; full bare vitest suite green; tsc clean.
- Rust: factory-engine 266 lib tests + suites green; orchestrator 147 (2 new pre_step tests); OPC 341 tests; clippy `-D warnings` clean on all three.
- `make pr-prep` (index + coupling), schema-parity (incl. spec 189 envelope-version parity), cargo-deny: green.
- Runtime end-to-end (first real ADMIT → sealed grant chain → countersigned cert) is gated on the GovAlta-side `chore/envelope-schema-1.0.0-v2` merge + org re-sync; until then admission correctly REFUSES.

## Notes for review

- Recorded deviations + the PD-8/AC-5 verification outcome are in `specs/198-factory-governance-envelope/tasks.md` (PR-A status block).
- Pre-existing, NOT addressed here: `make ci`'s `ci-rust`/`ci-fast-rust` legs reference `crates/Cargo.toml`, deleted by the cut-d cleanup (#176) — broken on main independently of this PR.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: mechanical cross-file touches under other specs' authority — Makefile (one-line verify-certificate flag passthrough), crates/factory-engine/src/{lib.rs (two module registrations), bin/factory_run.rs (DispatchOptions literal field threading)}, product/apps/opc/src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs (module registration), platform/services/stagecraft/web/app/lib/client.ts (generated client refresh), platform/services/stagecraft/vite.config.ts (test-runner exclude made conditional on ENCORE_RUNTIME_LIB so DB suites run under encore test as documented), platform/services/stagecraft/api/projects/opcBundle.test.ts (existing tests thread the new optional admission field)), platform/services/stagecraft/infra.config{,.hetzner}.json (declare the three FACTORY_SIGNING_* secrets — encore build fails closed on undeclared secrets).
