title: fix(183): derive OPC org_id from nested custom.* JWT claims (stop sign-in at every start)
body:
## Problem

After the §3.7/§3.8 persistence work, the Stagecraft session survives an OPC restart — the JWT is restored from the OS keychain on launch. But the user still had to **sign out and sign in again on every cold start**: the boot gate's `has_org` precondition never flipped, so the cockpit never opened.

## Root cause

Rauthy nests the OAP attributes (`oap_org_id`, `oap_user_id`, `oap_org_slug`, …) under a top-level **`custom`** object in the minted JWT (per `api/auth/sessionMint.ts` + the `oap` scope's `attr_include_access` mapping in `scripts/seed-rauthy.mjs`). OPC's Rust read them at the **top level** (`claims.get("oap_org_id")`), so `apply_token` derived an empty `org_id` from every keychain-restored / refreshed token.

Confirmed against the live keychain token: `oap_org_id` is absent at the top level and present under `custom`.

A fresh sign-in masked the defect because `auth_handle_callback` / `auth_select_org` set `org_id` from the HTTP **response body**, never the JWT — only the restore path reads the claim. The duplex connected fine throughout (the server resolves org from the JWT server-side), so this was purely a client-side derivation defect, distinct from the §3.7/§3.8 liveness gaps.

## Fix

- `stagecraft_client.rs` — new `claim_str()` accessor (reads `custom.<key>` first, falls back to top-level for forward-compat); `apply_token` derives `org_id` through it. **This is what opens the boot gate on restart.**
- `auth.rs` — `auth_get_status` and `auth_switch_org` claim reads routed through `claim_str` so a restored session reports its org + identity, not an authenticated-but-empty shell.

## Testing

- New regression tests pin the **real nested wire shape** (`apply_token_derives_org_id_from_nested_custom_claim`, `claim_str_prefers_custom_then_falls_back_to_top_level`) — the prior flat-claim fixture is exactly what let the defect ship.
- `cargo test --lib stagecraft_client` → 11 passed, 0 failed.

## Spec / coupling

`auth.rs` joins spec 183's `refines:` graph under the same org-session-materialisation concern it already observes on `stagecraft_client.rs` (the auth-command half of one discipline), documented in new §3.9. Coupling gate passes with no waiver; featuregraph golden unchanged.

title: refactor(183): round-2 polish for duplex diagnostics (follow-up to #309)
body:
## What

Follow-up to #309. Applies the two round-2 code-review items that were orphaned when #309's round-1 commit merged through the queue while the round-2 fixup was still in flight:

- **hello send** → `try/catch` instead of `.then().catch()`, so a throw from the success-path log can't be misattributed as a send failure (only an actual send failure logs `sync: hello send failed`).
- **null-auth nack `detail`** → generalized to `"authentication unavailable"` (client-facing); the precise cause (`getAuthData()` null in the stream handler) stays in the server `log.warn`.

## Scope / risk

Observability + one string. No change to the duplex contract, auth model, or wire shape. `api/sync/types.ts` is untouched, so the schema-parity gate is unaffected.

## Coupling

Same as #309 — `api/sync/duplex.ts` is co-authored by specs 087/108/111/123/124/183; this is diagnostic polish, not a spec contract change, so it carries a drift waiver.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: follow-up to #309 applying orphaned round-2 review polish to the spec-183 duplex diagnostics (try/catch hello send + generic client-facing nack detail); observability only, no duplex contract or wire-shape change.

title: fix(183): observable duplex handler entry + hello-send (diagnose post-sign-in churn)
body:
## What

Adds server-side observability to the stagecraft duplex handler to root-cause the **spec-183 post-interactive-sign-in duplex churn**, plus a null-safe auth read.

- `sync: duplex handler entered` at the top of the handler — logs `clientId`, `clientKind`, `lastServerCursor`, `hasAuth`, `orgId`, `userId`.
- Reads `getAuthData()` null-safely: a null auth context in the stream handler now surfaces as an explicit logged `stream.close()` instead of a swallowed `auth.orgId` throw.
- `sync: hello sent` / `sync: hello send failed` and a `sync: cursor gap` log around the `ServerHello` + `resync_required` sends (previously `.catch(() => undefined)` — silent on both success and failure).

## Why

Live kubectl tracing showed post-sign-in reconnects reach the `duplex` endpoint (auth completes) but never emit `sync: session registered` and never hit the `!orgId` rejection — the handler body exits before `registry.register` with **no log**, so the desktop never receives `sync.hello` and the socket idles until the edge closes it (the churn). The hello-send path was silent on both success and failure, so the server logs were empty exactly where the answer lives. This instrumentation will confirm whether `getAuthData()` returns null inside the streamInOut handler body on those reconnects.

## Scope / risk

Observability only — no change to the duplex contract, auth model, or wire shape. The null-safe read strictly improves behavior (logged graceful close instead of a swallowed throw). `api/sync/types.ts` is untouched, so the schema-parity gate is unaffected.

## Coupling

`api/sync/duplex.ts` is co-authored by specs 087/108/111/123/124/183. This change is diagnostic logging + a null-safe read; it does not alter the duplex design contract of any co-author, so it carries a drift waiver rather than a gate-satisfying edit to one of those specs.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: diagnostic logging to root-cause the spec-183 post-sign-in duplex churn (handler-entry + hello-send observability; null-safe getAuthData surfaced as a logged close); observability only, no duplex contract or wire-shape change.

title: fix(183): stable hiqlite loopback ports — stop the os error 61 reconnect flood
body:
## Problem

The `:0` self-heal (#305) **converted** the axiomregent reconnect flood, it didn't kill it. `opc.log` is still ~2 lines/sec of:

```
[ERROR hiqlite::client::stream] Could not connect Client API WebSocket to 127.0.0.1:<port>: Connect: Connection refused (os error 61)
```

which evicts the `sync_client` duplex/auth lines a boot/handshake diagnosis depends on (FR-T1 / FR-T2(b)).

## Root cause

`init_hiqlite` resolved a **fresh ephemeral port every launch** via `free_loopback_pair()`. But hiqlite/openraft **freezes the node's raft+api ports in committed membership at first init** and reloads them on every restart; the in-process API client dials that committed `addr_api` forever. So after the first run the bound port and the committed port diverge → the client floods dialing the stale committed port. The old self-heal matched only the literal `127.0.0.1:0`, so a stale *concrete* port was deemed "healthy" and flooded unhealed. A data-dir reset was a one-shot — the next launch re-diverged.

Confirmed three ways: committed raft WAL pins the first-init port; a fresh init binds+commits a matching pair → **0 flood**; an existing store re-floods on the next restart.

## Fix

- **Stable ports.** Persist the resolved `(raft, api)` pair to a data-dir sidecar `.opc-hiqlite-ports.json` and **reuse it every start**, so `NodeConfig.addr_api` always equals committed membership and the client never dials a stale port.
- **Generalised self-heal.** `heal_unstable_membership` replaces the `:0`-only heal: any store that is *initialised but carries no ports sidecar* (every pre-stability store, the `:0` case included) is moved **aside** (numbered sibling, preserved not deleted — regenerable checkpoint/cache per spec 041). A current-binary store (sidecar present) and a pristine dir are untouched.
- Bind-race recovery: a port pair that won't bind drops the suspect sidecar (and moves a committed store aside) so the retry resolves a fresh pair.

## Spec

Spec 183 §3.8(c) amended to document both iterations; the `refines` aspect on `crates/axiomregent/src/db/mod.rs` renamed to `sidecar-hiqlite-stable-ports-and-membership-self-heal`.

## Tests / verification

- 6 unit tests rewritten (`persisted_ports_round_trip`, `read_persisted_ports_rejects_degenerate`, `heal_moves_aside_initialised_dir_without_sidecar`, `heal_leaves_dir_with_sidecar_untouched`, `heal_leaves_pristine_dir_untouched`, `heal_is_a_noop_on_a_fresh_install`).
- `cargo check --lib` + `--tests` clean; coupling gate OK; codebase index regenerated.
- Local `cargo test` / binary build could not link in the dev shell (`ld: library 'clang_rt.osx' not found`, a toolchain path issue unrelated to this change) — CI runs the unit tests.

## Operator note

An existing data dir has no ports sidecar, so the fixed binary moves it aside **once** on first launch (preserved as `data.prestable-corrupt`), then stays stable across every restart after.

title: fix(183+087): stream-identity-scoped duplex session teardown — close the server-side reconnect race that wedged the boot gate (FR-SYNC-011)
body:
## What

Closes the server-side duplex registry reconnect race that wedged the OPC boot gate — the *"Connecting to stagecraft… the project list will arrive once the duplex handshake completes"* hang that never resolved after sign-in.

## Root cause

The stagecraft duplex `registry` keys sessions by `(orgId, clientId)`, and the desktop reuses a stable `client_id` across reconnects (spec 183). Every reconnect collided on the slot:

1. Conn **A** registered, awaiting its inbound loop.
2. Reconnect (e.g. spec 183's sign-in `reconnect_stagecraft_duplex`) → Conn **B**, same `clientId`. `register` closed A's stream and installed B.
3. A's inbound loop ended → A's `finally` ran `registry.unregister(orgId, clientId)`.
4. That `clientId`-only delete removed **B's** entry. Orphaned B's next heartbeat found no session → `heartbeatAlive = false` → loop break → close, **before `sync.hello`**.

So the first connect (no prior session) got `sync.hello` and held; every reconnect died; both sides saw "the other closed" (server logged `Connection reset without closing handshake`). Token/cursor were ruled out — the org resolves from `custom.oap_org_id` and every REST call succeeded with the same token.

## Fix

`registry.unregister(orgId, clientId, stream?)` deletes only when the registered session's stream matches the caller's; the duplex handler's `finally` passes its own `stream`. `register`'s replace-and-close of a superseded session is retained; `sendTo`/`broadcastOrg` prunes pass no stream and are unchanged.

## Spec

- **087** — adds **FR-SYNC-011** (reconnect session-identity teardown) + a design subsection; amendment provenance bumped to 183.
- **183** — server-side cross-reference note; this completes the client-side #303/#305 reconnect fixes.

## Testing

- 2 regression tests in `api/sync/registry.test.ts` (reconnect-race + matching-stream); all 38 `api/sync` tests pass.
- `make pr-prep` clean: spec-code coupling gate OK (6 paths), codebase index regenerated.

## Deploy note

Requires a stagecraft redeploy to take effect (deployed `sha-94543a2` predates this). After deploy + relaunch/sign-in, the Projects list resolves (the reconnect keeps its session, so `sync.hello` lands).

title: fix(180): same-runner baseline for the opc-bench usage_scan gate
body:
## Problem

The `opc-bench / usage scan` gate compares the PR/merge_group head against a `main` baseline **saved on a different runner**. `usage_scan_cold_n200` is a ~6–11 ms *cold filesystem-scan* microbench whose wall-time is dominated by syscall latency, so the `macos-latest` fleet's **±~80% inter-runner I/O variance dwarfs the +25% threshold** — it flags confident-but-spurious regressions.

Evidence from PR #305, which changes **no code on the benched path** (`commands/usage.rs` is byte-identical to `main`):

| Run | Event | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 27053933300 | PR | +44.8% → passed on rerun |
| 27054630563 | merge_group | passed |
| 27055068985 | merge_group | **+75.7% fail** |
| 27055378351 | merge_group | **+84.4% fail** |

Same machine code, measured 6–11.5 ms across runners → the gate was measuring *which runner it landed on*, not a code delta.

## Fix

For `pull_request` / `merge_group`, measure the **base (`main`) commit and the head commit on the same runner** in one job (`--save-baseline` on base, `--baseline` on head) and gate on that same-runner delta. Inter-runner variance cancels.

- Threshold (**+25%**) unchanged.
- Relative-only discipline (**FR-T10**, no absolute budget) unchanged.
- Only the baseline's **provenance** moved: cross-runner Actions cache → same-runner, in-job.
- `push` still records the informational cached `main` baseline (now feeding only the `workflow_dispatch` manual diagnostic); the nightly **N=2000** trend is unchanged.
- Checkout switched to `fetch-depth: 0` so the base commit is available to bench in-job.

## Spec

Amends **spec 180 §5.1 FR-T9** (added a dated callout), exercising FR-T9's own clause that the gate is "amendable via spec amendment if observed false-positive rate from runner noise becomes operationally significant." Not a bypass — the gate stays enforcing at +25%; it's now measuring the right thing.

## Self-test

This PR edits `ci-opc-bench.yml`, so the paths filter runs `opc-bench` on it. `usage.rs` is identical base-vs-head here, so the same-runner comparison should land ~0% — demonstrating the fix.

title: fix(183): recover wedged duplex (reconnect + sign-in budget reset) + self-heal port-0 hiqlite floods
body:
## What

Boot-gate recovery hardening (spec 183 §3.8) — follow-up to the 2026-06-05 duplex/Factory investigation. Two of the three agreed fix-set items; #1 (Factory aim-vue-node substrate-seeding) stays deferred (below).

### #2 — explicit duplex reconnect + sign-in budget reset
- New `reconnect_stagecraft_duplex` command re-spawns the duplex consumer, resetting its per-outage refresh budget + consecutive-failure counter (`run_forever` loop-locals) and forcing an immediate reconnect on the current bearer instead of waiting out the backoff.
- BootGate gains a **Reconnect** button in exactly the org-present-but-no-`sync.hello` stuck branch.
- AuthContext fires it on the authenticated transition, so a session that burned its refresh budget while expired is recoverable by signing in again — previously the budget reset only on a clean connect, so a fresh re-login's upgrade 401s could skip the refresh path and march straight to give-up.

### #3 — hiqlite port-0 membership self-heal
- A pre-fix axiomregent binary committed `127.0.0.1:0` into the single-node raft membership; every restart then floods stderr (`os error 49`) and evicts the duplex/auth lines the boot gate depends on. The concrete-port fix only ever helped a *fresh* init.
- `init_hiqlite` now detects the exact port-0 signature in the raft control-plane files (logs/snapshots — never the SQLite state-machine db, whose user data could false-positive) and moves the poisoned data dir aside (`*.port0-corrupt`, **preserved not deleted**) so the next init gets concrete ports. Healthy concrete-port dirs are left untouched.

## Deferred — #1 Factory `aim-vue-node`
The substrate-seeding steps (un-strip `validation` in `sanitiseManifest`, scoped un-skip in `oapNativeIngest`) are designed in spec 139 §14 / 124 §12 but gated on the mounted `OAP_NATIVE_ADAPTERS_DIR` manifest carrying `schema_version`. The currently-mounted manifest has **no** `schema_version`, so a seeded row would still fail validation — implementing it now would be a no-op. Deferred until the mounted manifest is spec-074-shaped.

## Verification
- axiomregent: `cargo test -p axiomregent --lib db::` → 5/5 pass (heal move-aside, healthy-dir-untouched, exact-port-0 match).
- opc desktop: `cargo check` ✓, `tsc --noEmit` ✓ (0 errors).
- Coupling: spec 183 §2 + new §3.8 + three `refines` edges (settings.rs, bindings.rs → 180; axiomregent db/mod.rs → 073); `validate-graph` clean; coupling gate on the committed diff = OK (9 paths).

title: fix(124+139): clear, attributable errors when factory adapter manifest is not spec-074
body:
## What

Turns the Factory's cryptic, **UI-only** failure —
```
adapter not found: discovery failed: Invalid manifest at …/adapters/aim-vue-node/manifest.yaml:
[YamlParse { source: Error("missing field `schema_version`", line: 1, column: 1) }]
```
— into a **clear, attributable, logged** error at both boundaries.

## Root cause

When an org's factory substrate has no spec-074 `adapter-manifest` row, stagecraft's `projectSubstrateToLegacy` falls back to `buildAdapter`'s **knowledge/orchestration bundle** (keys `entry` / `orchestrator` / `orchestration_source_id`, no `schema_version`). That document was served by `getAdapter`, cached verbatim by the desktop (`AdapterBody.manifest` is an untyped `serde_json::Value`), and only failed much later — deep in `FactoryEngine::new` → `AdapterRegistry::discover` — with a serde message surfaced to the OPC UI and **never written to `opc.log`**. Confirmed server-side: clearing the desktop cache re-downloaded the same bundle (same cache hash).

## Fix — defense-in-depth guards (no projection/substrate change)

- **`factory-platform-client::write_adapter`** — validate the manifest deserialises as `factory_contracts::AdapterManifest` **before** writing the cache; return a clear `CacheIo` error ("stagecraft served a non-spec-074 adapter manifest for '<name>'…") otherwise.
- **`opc factory.rs`** — `log::error!` on `FactoryEngine::new` / `start_pipeline` failures, so engine/discovery faults land in `opc.log` instead of being UI-only.
- **`stagecraft getAdapter`** — refuse to serve a non-spec-074 document as an adapter manifest: `APIError.internal` + `log.error` with the projected keys, instead of silently shipping junk.

## Important — what this does and does NOT do

This makes the failure **clear and diagnosable**. It does **not** yet make the Factory *resolve* `aim-vue-node` for an empty-substrate org. That requires a separate, contract- and deployment-level follow-up (documented in spec 124 §12 / 139 §14):

1. Un-skip `aim-vue-node` in `loadOapNativeAdapterSubstrateRows` (`oapNativeIngest.ts`), **scoped** so upstream-mirrored orchestration/skills aren't duplicated.
2. Stop `sanitiseManifest` (`oapNativeSanitise.ts`) from deleting the `validation` block — the desktop's `AdapterManifest` **requires** it, so without this the seeded row would just fail on `validation` instead of `schema_version`.
3. A verified `OAP_NATIVE_ADAPTERS_DIR` mount carrying the spec-074 `manifest.yaml` (not in the monorepo).

The ingest-skip removal was deliberately **excluded** here because (2)/(3) make it a false fix in isolation, and it risks duplicate substrate rows.

## Testing

- `cargo check` — `factory-platform-client` and the `opc` desktop crate both clean.
- `make pr-prep` — codebase index refreshed; spec-code coupling gate clean (13 paths; specs 124 & 139 amended for the touched files).
- stagecraft `browse.ts` change uses already-imported `APIError.internal` / `log.error` matching existing usage; verified by the stagecraft CI job.

title: fix(183): close duplex consumer startup race that wedged the boot gate
body:
## What

Closes an intermittent startup race in the OPC desktop that left the boot gate stuck on **"Waiting for stagecraft duplex handshake (sync.hello)…"** — recoverable only by fully relaunching the app (sign-out/sign-in did not help).

## Root cause

The duplex reconnect loop (`sync_client.rs::run_forever`) is the boot gate's `sync.hello` source (spec 183 FR-T2(b)). But `lib.rs` spawned the consumer task **before** calling `app.manage(SyncClientState)`, and the task resolved that state with the **panicking** `Manager::state()` accessor. On Tauri's multi-threaded async runtime, a worker could poll the task before the manage ran → panic → and `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` drops the `JoinHandle`, so the panic was **swallowed**. `run_forever` never executed: no connect attempt, no log beyond `sync_client: duplex consumer starting`, and the boot gate waited on `sync.hello` forever. Nothing re-spawns a dead consumer, so only a relaunch (which re-rolled the race) recovered it.

Confirmed from captured stdout: a wedged run showed `duplex consumer starting` with **no** `connecting`/`idle` follow-up; healthy runs showed `connecting → connected → hello received` within ~1s.

## Fix

- **`lib.rs`** — manage `SyncClientState` **before** spawning the consumer; the task now resolves it via the non-panicking `try_state()` with a bounded retry + error log, so a future reordering can never again silently kill the consumer.
- **`sync_client.rs`** — log `run_forever` entry, so a wedged consumer is never silent again ("task died before the loop" vs "loop running but token resolution stalled" are now distinguishable).
- **spec 183 §3.7** — documents the post-approval hardening. No FR-T2 invariant changes (restores assumed loop liveness); FR-T5 give-up/precondition-loss semantics unchanged.

## Testing

- `cargo check --manifest-path product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` — clean.
- `make pr-prep` — codebase index refreshed; spec-code coupling gate clean (both touched files are already owned by spec 183 via `refines:`).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Part of the same duplex-resilience investigation, to land separately:
- Reconnect button on the BootGate + cockpit (re-spawn consumer + force refresh).
- Reset the duplex refresh budget / counters on sign-in (today only resets on a clean connection).
- Surface the real failure reason on the BootGate (401 / refresh-failed / transient-503 / give-up + attempt count).
- `exp`-check before showing org "resolved" (today a decode-without-verify can show org while the token is rejected server-side).
- `init_hiqlite` self-heal of a committed `127.0.0.1:0` raft membership (the sidecar log-flood; harmless to the handshake but blinds diagnostics).
- Factory adapter projection (stagecraft serves a knowledge-bundle instead of a spec-074 adapter manifest → `missing field schema_version`).

title: fix(112): split Open-in-OPC deep link from full bundle to stop per-nav GitHub token mint
body:
## Problem

The deployed `stagecraft-api` pod **OOMKilled** (exit 137) at its 1Gi limit during a bulk knowledge-directory upload. Root cause traced from pod `describe` (OOMKilled) + `--previous` logs + endpoint histogram (137 `requestUpload` / 136 `confirmUpload` / **24 `getProjectOpcBundle`** in ~5 min).

The project layout header (`web/app/routes/app.project.$projectId.tsx`) fetched the full `getProjectOpcBundle` on every loader run, using only `deepLink` + `adapter.name` to render the "Open in OPC" button. That endpoint **mints a GitHub installation token** (`resolveCloneTokenForBundle`, ~0.9–1.7s) and loads the org substrate 3×. Under **React Router v7 single-fetch**, with no `shouldRevalidate`, the layout loader revalidates on every navigation within a project — so each tab hop re-ran the full bundle, minting a token and triple-loading substrate for data the header never reads. During the bulk upload this churn stacked with the spec-115 extraction fan-out and crossed the 1Gi cgroup limit.

## Fix

- **B** — new lightweight `GET /api/projects/:id/opc-deep-link` (`getProjectOpcDeepLink`, `api/projects/opcBundle.ts`) returning only `{ deepLink, adapterName }`. Reuses `buildOpcBundle` (empty collections + null clone token) so the deep-link derivation stays **byte-identical** to the full endpoint, but mints **no** clone token and loads **no** contracts/processes/agents. OPC-the-desktop-client keeps using the full `/opc-bundle` — its §6.3 contract is unchanged.
- **A** — `shouldRevalidate` on the project layout route: the deep link is invariant within a project, so the loader is skipped on plain navigation between child tabs (still revalidates on project change, mutations, and same-URL revalidations).

Net: navigating a project's tabs no longer re-runs the loader; when it does, it no longer mints a GitHub token or triple-loads substrate. The 24× token-mint storm collapses to one cheap call on project entry.

## Spec

Amends **spec 112 §6.3** (web-UI deep-link split) with an in-body callout, and adds a `refines:` edge (`aspect: open-in-opc-handoff`) over the consumer paths so the coupling gate's authority is honest rather than gate-padded.

## Verification (local)

- ✅ spec/code coupling gate (6 paths, exit 0)
- ✅ codebase-index staleness check (regenerated `index.json` committed)
- ✅ spec-lint (fail-on-warn)
- ✅ featuregraph golden (`test_golden_graph` — unchanged)
- ✅ `opcBundle.test.ts` 9/9 (added equivalence + no-token-invariant tests)
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` clean on edited files

## Not in this PR

- Memory bump (1Gi→2Gi) / extraction `maxConcurrency` reduction — held to observe one more bulk upload after this lands (this removes one of three colliding allocations).
- Metrics-server / RSS-trend visibility — deferred to spec 196 (platform-metrics-stack).

title: fix(117): correct desktop SBOM scope + attest every shipped installer (deb/rpm/msi)
body:
## Summary
Fixes three SBOM/attestation defects found in the **unpublished** `opc-v0.4.0` draft release. Two share one root cause (a mis-scoped desktop SBOM scan); Defect A is separate. Every number below was **reproduced on a clean `git archive` export** (syft 1.43.0), the way #292 proved the 0→855 sidecar fix.

| Defect | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **2 — npm under-report** | desktop SBOM scans `product/apps/opc` (below `product/pnpm-lock.yaml`) → **2 npm** (test deps only) | scope `product/` → **792 npm** (784 workspace closure + 8 sibling/test); **cargo unchanged 961** |
| **3 — target/ over-report** | same post-build scan reaches `src-tauri/target/`; MSVC catalogs ~230 purl-less proc-macro DLLs | jq prune drops every `target/`-sourced component; macOS/Linux no-op, Windows 241 → ~0 |
| **A — provenance gap** | attestation globs only dmg/appimage/nsis → `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.msi` **unattested** | subject set extended to all five → every shipped installer gets SLSA provenance + `.intoto.jsonl` |

## Mechanism note (verified, contradicts the obvious fix)
syft's `--exclude` does **not** drop `target/` in syft 1.43.0 — valid `**/target/**` globs are a silent no-op; directory-form patterns error the scan (`must start with one of './', '*/', '**/'`). So the prune is a **deterministic jq filter** (already the workflow's tool for the BOM-Link — no new binary, byte-stable). It drops a component iff its name or *every* syft location is under a `target/` build tree.

## Fail-closed gates (operationalized, not prose — mirrors #292)
- desktop SBOM: `pkg:npm` count > 0 (guards Defect 2 regression)
- desktop SBOM: zero `target/` build-tree components by name or syft location (guards Defect 3 regression)
- sidecar count gate: untouched

## Scope decisions
- **npm closure:** ship the pnpm **workspace** closure (792) — a superset of OPC's production runtime closure (incl. dev tooling + sibling packages), same caveat already accepted for the bundled-sidecar SBOM (§2.1). Never under-reports what ships.
- **`.sha256` checksums:** stay **deliberately updater-scoped** (dmg/nsis/appimage — the set `updater.rs` consumes). `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.msi` get provenance + SBOM but no `.sha256`; documented in RELEASE-VERIFICATION.md so the narrower set reads as intentional.

## Honesty caveats
- The Windows **241** figure is MSVC-PE-specific and **not numerically reproducible on darwin** — syft catalogs 0 components from the real local macOS `target/` (confirmed). The fix is proven *by construction* + fixture, and the gate fails closed if any `target/` component survives.
- The `deb/`/`rpm/`/`msi/` bundle dir names are the Tauri v2 convention; globs are additive (a non-match is harmless), fully confirmable only on a real multi-platform release run.

## Files
- `.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml` — scope, jq prune, gates, subject set, checksum-scope comment
- `specs/117-release-artifact-attestations/spec.md` — §2.2, §3, §4.2, AC-2/AC-4/AC-6, lesson #5
- `docs/RELEASE-VERIFICATION.md` — corrected attestation/SBOM claim + checksum-scope doc
- `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` — regenerated

## Local validation (full #292 suite)
`pr-prep` coupling OK · `codebase-indexer check` 0 · `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` 0 · `workflow-pins` + regression 0 · `release-version-guard-test` 0 · `ci-parity` OK (12 wf) · `actionlint` 0 · extracted prune/gate scripts pass + both negative cases fail-closed.

**Does not touch the draft release.** Spec 117-coupled. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(183+180): boot-gate sign-in/out + version banner + login-gated titlebar nav
body:
## Summary

Three OPC shell affordances + a related boot-gate UX fix, all surfaced while diagnosing a stuck "Preparing OPC" boot gate:

- **Version banner** — the previously-empty titlebar centre now shows `OPC v0.4.0`, resolved at runtime via `getVersion()` from `@tauri-apps/api/app` (single source of truth: `tauri.conf.json`).
- **Boot-gate sign-in / sign-out** — contextual controls in the Stagecraft row: **Sign in** when signed out, **Sign out** whenever a session exists. Sign out clears the keychain session token — the recovery path for the authenticated-but-no-org stuck state (a keychain-restored JWT with no `oap_org_id` claim leaves `org_id` empty, so the gate's `has_org` term never flips and the cockpit never opens).
- **Login-gated titlebar nav** — the right-side cockpit-nav cluster (Projects / Factory / Usage / Settings) is hidden entirely until the boot gate green-lights the cockpit (`navEnabled = bootGateOpen`), closing a latent FR-T3 escape hatch: those icons were clickable during boot.
- **Status-line fix** — the "Waiting for … sync.hello" line now branches on `org_id` (since `org_session_ready == has_org && sync_hello`): it names the real blocker when the org is missing instead of always blaming a handshake that may already have arrived.

## Spec alignment

- Spec: `specs/183-opc-boot-precondition-gate/spec.md` — §3.3 FR-T3, dated sub-clause (2026-06-04): contextual auth controls + titlebar nav suppression + org-vs-handshake status line.
- Spec: `specs/180-opc-shell-codification/spec.md` — §2.2: version banner (shell identity, broad un-bound-shell authority) + spec-183 co-authority on the titlebar surface.

## Change classification

- [x] Enhancement — improvement to existing feature

(Additive affordances on the existing boot gate (183) and desktop shell (180); the Sign out control doubles as the recovery for the diagnosed stuck-boot state.)

## Checklist

- [x] Changes align with the referenced spec (or no spec applies)
- [x] Spec-compiler output unchanged (or spec frontmatter was intentionally modified) — edits are prose-only; no frontmatter relationship/status changes
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or API keys committed

## Consolidated Dependabot bumps

Combines five open Dependabot PRs into one human-authored PR so the `ai-review` / `ci-gate` checks can run (Dependabot PRs run with a restricted token and no secret access) and the codebase index is regenerated for the spec-code coupling gate.

### opc — `product/apps/opc/src-tauri`
- **cargo-minor-patch group, 15 crates** (#296): `tauri` 2.11.1→2.11.2, `tokio` 1.52.2→1.52.3, `serde_json` 1.0.149→1.0.150, `reqwest` 0.13.3→0.13.4, `log` 0.4.29→0.4.32, `chrono` 0.4.44→0.4.45, `cc`, `uuid`, `filetime`, `jsonschema`, `tower-http`, `typenum`, `tauri-build`, `tauri-plugin-global-shortcut`, `tauri-plugin-mcp-bridge`
- **`similar` 2.7.0 → 3.1.1** (#298): semver-major, but the breaking change is only MSRV→1.85 / edition 2024; the toolchain is **1.95.0** and the crate is already edition 2024. `TextDiff::from_lines` / `ChangeTag` call sites unchanged.
- **`sysinfo` 0.34.2 → 0.38.4** (#297): `System::new` / `refresh_cpu_usage` / `global_cpu_usage` call sites unchanged.

### stagecraft — `platform/services/stagecraft`
- **npm-minor-patch group, 6 pkgs** (#295): `@aws-sdk/client-s3` + `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` 3.1061.0→3.1062.0, `react-router` suite 7.16.0→7.17.0.

### deployd-api-rs — `platform/services/deployd-api-rs`
- **`chrono` 0.4.44 → 0.4.45** (#294)

Each bump's `check + clippy + test` already passed CI on its individual Dependabot PR. opc lockfile reconstructed from the tested #296 group lock + surgical `cargo update -p similar -p sysinfo` (not a wholesale refresh); deployd + stagecraft files taken directly from their tested Dependabot branches.

Supersedes #294, #295, #296, #297, #298 (closed in favour of this PR).

**Not included:** #250 (`rusqlite` 0.39→0.40) — hiqlite's latest release (0.13.2) pins `libsqlite3-sys` 0.37 and orchestrator pins `hiqlite ~0.13`, so `rusqlite` 0.40 (`libsqlite3-sys` 0.38) would be a native-link conflict. Left open pending a coordinated hiqlite bump.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: dependency maintenance only — version bumps consolidating Dependabot PRs #294–298. The edited spec-owned files (`product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `platform/services/stagecraft/package.json`) change dependency version strings only; no source code, spec contract, FR, §, or lifecycle field changes, and no governed behavior is altered. body:
Bumps [similar](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/similar) from 2.7.0 to 3.1.1.
Changelog

Sourced from similar's changelog.

3.1.1

  • Fixed DiffOp cursor positions when compacting adjacent inserts/deletes and in Algorithm::Histogram full-replacement output, ensuring operations form contiguous ranges. #95
  • Renamed sample diff input files to a lexicographic caseNN.01.before_* / caseNN.02.after_* scheme.

3.1.0

  • Added capture_diff_slices_by_key and capture_diff_slices_by_key_deadline as convenience helpers for diffing slices by derived keys.
  • Fixed Compact emitting inconsistent DiffOp cursor positions after compaction, which could leave Delete/Insert operations with stale new_index/old_index values.
  • Added explicit lifetime capture (+ use<...>) on iterator-returning APIs to improve compatibility with Rust 2024 lifetime capture behavior. #93

3.0.0

  • Added a Git-style Histogram diff implementation exposed as Algorithm::Histogram, including deadline-aware Myers fallback and comprehensive regression/behavior tests.
  • Raised MSRV to Rust 1.85 and moved the crate to Rust 2024 edition.
  • Added a Hunt-style diff implementation exposed as Algorithm::Hunt.
  • Added configurable inline refinement via InlineChangeOptions and InlineChangeMode, including semantic cleanup and new TextDiff::iter_inline_changes_with_options* methods. #92
  • Added a global disjoint-input fast path in algorithms::diff_deadline to avoid pathological runtimes on large, fully distinct inputs.
  • Improved Algorithm::Myers performance on heavily unbalanced diffs to avoid pathological slowdowns.
  • Added diff_deadline_raw entrypoints in the algorithm modules to bypass shared heuristics and keep minimal intrinsic trait bounds where needed.
  • Added test files in examples/diffs that can be used with the some of the examples as input pairs.
  • Added CachedLookup, a helper for adapting virtual or computed sequences by materializing items on first access and then serving borrowed values through normal indexing. The owned-lookup example demonstrates this approach for issue #33.
  • Fixed ranged indexing in the classic LCS table algorithm.
  • Improved diff compaction to merge adjacent delete hunks across equal runs.
  • Excluded development scripts from published crate contents. #87
  • TextDiff::from_* and TextDiffConfig::diff_* now accept owned inputs (String, Vec<u8>, Cow) in addition to borrowed inputs. This allows returning text diffs from functions without external owner lifetimes. #65
  • TextDiff no longer exposes old_slices / new_slices. Use old_len, new_len, old_slice, new_slice, iter_old_slices, iter_new_slices, old_lookup, and new_lookup instead.
  • TextDiff::iter_changes now panics on invalid out-of-bounds DiffOp

Release notes

Sourced from tower-http's releases.

tower-http-0.6.11

Added

  • set-header: add SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer and SetMultipleResponseHeader for setting multiple response headers at once. Supports overriding, appending, and if_not_present modes. Header values can be fixed or computed dynamically via closures (#672)

    use http::{Response, header::{self, HeaderValue}};
use http_body::Body as _;
use tower_http::set_header::response::SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer;

    let layer = SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer::overriding(vec![
    
(header::X_FRAME_OPTIONS, HeaderValue::from_static("DENY")).into(),
    
(header::CONTENT_LENGTH, |res: &Response<MyBody>| {
    
res.body().size_hint().exact()
    
.map(|size| HeaderValue::from_str(&size.to_string()).unwrap())
    
}).into(),
    
]);

  • set-header: add SetMultipleRequestHeadersLayer and SetMultipleRequestHeaders for setting multiple request headers at once, mirroring the response-side API (#677)

  • classify: add From<i32> and From<NonZeroI32> impls for GrpcCode. Unrecognized status codes map to GrpcCode::Unknown (#506)

title: chore(deps): consolidate Dependabot bumps into one PR (rust + npm + actions)
body:
Consolidates the open Dependabot dependency PRs into one author-owned change, with the code adaptations several of them required (which is why their CI was red). Replaces 8 of the 9 Dependabot PRs; rusqlite is deferred (see below).

## Included

| Ecosystem | Update | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rust | toml `0.8 → 1.1` (spec-compiler) | toml 1.0 changed `str.parse::<Value>()` to parse a single value, not a document — migrated both call sites in `discover_workspace_crate_ids` to `toml::from_str`. Without this the compiler silently fails workspace-member discovery (73 spurious V-021s, exit 1). |
| Rust | octocrab `0.51 → 0.53` + reqwest `0.12 → 0.13` (axiomregent) | reqwest 0.13 feature-gated `RequestBuilder::form()`; added the `form` feature. octocrab needed no code changes. |
| Rust | rand_core `0.6` → **removed** (factory-engine, policy-kernel) | rand_core 0.9+ dropped the `getrandom` feature and `OsRng`. Rather than chase that churn (or adopt the ed25519-dalek `3.0.0-rc.0` pre-release), keygen now seeds a 32-byte buffer from `getrandom::fill` and calls `SigningKey::from_bytes` — **the exact operations `SigningKey::generate` performs internally**, inlined. Same OS entropy, same key, stays on stable ed25519-dalek 2, and `getrandom::fill` lets the signing path fail closed on entropy failure. Closes #252 and #248. |
| Rust | reqwest/serde_json/uuid transitive (deployd-api-rs) | Lockfile-only `cargo update`. |
| npm | 14 stagecraft bumps | react 19.2.7, react-router family 7.16.0, vite 8.0.16, vitest 4.1.8, aws-sdk, tanstack-query, encore.dev. `npm audit --audit-level=high` clean; vitest 534/535 (the 1 fail is a pre-existing network timeout in `ping.test.ts`). |
| Actions | actions/checkout `6.0.2 → 6.0.3` | SHA bump across 27 workflows (`de0fac2e → df4cb1c0`). |
| Config | dependabot.yml path fix | `/apps/desktop/src-tauri → product/apps/opc/src-tauri` — the spec-178 rename left this dead, so the OPC desktop crate wasn't being covered at all. |

## Deferred (not in this PR)

- **rusqlite `0.39 → 0.40`** (#250) — pulls `libsqlite3-sys 0.38`, which collides with `hiqlite 0.13.2`'s transitive `rusqlite 0.39 → libsqlite3-sys 0.37` (only one crate may link native `sqlite3`). No published hiqlite uses rusqlite 0.40 yet; being handled upstream with the hiqlite owner, then bumped in a follow-up.

## Verification

`cargo check --workspace` green; targeted clippy + tests pass for spec-compiler, axiomregent, factory-engine, policy-kernel; deployd-api-rs builds; codebase index regenerated. Full stagecraft typecheck + `encore build docker` left to CI.

Supersedes #287, #254, #251, #288, #289, #283, #252, #248.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: dependency maintenance only — version bumps plus provably-equivalent API adaptations (toml::from_str migration, reqwest `form` feature, getrandom-seeded Ed25519 keygen identical to dalek's `generate`). No spec contract, FR, or lifecycle field changes; the edited spec-owned files adapt to new dependency APIs without altering governed behavior.

title: fix(117): stage workspace lock into sidecar-SBOM scan path; enforce AC-6 count gate
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #291 (axiomregent demotion). The `axiomregent-sbom` job in `release-desktop.yml` shipped a **0-component** sidecar SBOM on every release: it scans `crates/`, but the single workspace lock lands at repo-root `./Cargo.lock`, and syft's `rust-cargo-lock-cataloger` reads only a `Cargo.lock` **inside** the scan path (no ancestor walk). The recipe was lifted from the retired `release-axiomregent.yml` carrying a pre-restructure scan geometry that was never validated green in CI.

## Proof (clean `git archive` export — dodges the cached-`target/` false positive)

| Scan | Components |
|------|-----------:|
| current recipe (`syft dir:crates`, no lock in path) | **0** |
| lock staged into `crates/` | **855** (axiomregent's `octocrab`/`hiqlite`/`fastembed` present) |

## Fix

- **`release-desktop.yml`** — `cp Cargo.lock crates/Cargo.lock` before the scan (transient; ignored by `.gitignore:16`), keeping the scan Rust-scoped. Rejected `path: .` — it would sweep ~12 non-axiomregent lockfiles (pnpm, npm, go, two other Rust workspaces) into the sidecar SBOM.
- **Fail-closed `.components | length > 0` gate** operationalizing AC-6, which was prose-only and enforced nowhere. (CI can't re-prove 0→855 without a release run; this gate is the durable regression guard.)

## Spec 117 amendment (coupling-required; governance corrections)

- §2.1 step 1 — withdraw the "§AC-6 validated to a populated component count" provenance claim (unsupported by the AC-6 record).
- AC-6 lesson #4 — correct lesson #3's workspace-root/`crates/` self-contradiction and its stale "gitignored → no lockfile" cause.
- Known-limitation note: 855 is the whole-workspace Rust closure (superset of axiomregent's link set); `cargo tree -p` narrowing deferred.

## Out of scope (tracked separately)

The **desktop installer SBOM** has the same geometry class on the npm side — `path: product/apps/opc` is below the pnpm workspace root, so `product/pnpm-lock.yaml` (784 pkgs) isn't scanned (repro: 2/786 npm components, the 2 being test-only). Its own PR + repro, not folded in here.

## Local gates (all green)

`make pr-prep` coupling **OK (3 paths)** · index regenerated · `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` clean · `ci-parity` OK · workflow SHA-pin lint OK · version-guard fixture all-pass.

> ⚠️ **Precondition on the 0.4.0 cut** — demote-first-then-cut was chosen specifically to close this sidecar-SBOM gap. Hold the cut until this lands.

title: Demote axiomregent to internal OPC sidecar; retire standalone release (037/117/193/105)
body:
## Summary

Spec-led (CONST-005: specs first, then workflows/config). Demotes **axiomregent** from a standalone released product to an **internal upstream component of OPC**: it is built from OPC's own release commit and bundled as a Tauri sidecar by `release-desktop.yml`. **OPC is the sole release lever.** axiomregent has no independent product version (commit-pinned), no standalone binary/crate/container; anyone wanting a standalone build forks and builds it.

Runtime version-independence re-confirmed: sidecar boot gate is liveness-only (`sidecars.rs`), MCP `serverInfo` version is a static `"0.1.0"` (`router/mod.rs`), and there is no desktop-side version pin.

> **Not a release cut.** No tag is pushed, no release is dispatched, no 0.4.0 cut is bundled here. Operator controls the merge.

## What each spec now says

- **037** — reframed from "standalone shipped product / release matrix" to "internal upstream component built + bundled by the OPC release." The cross-platform **build** matrix is unchanged; only its destination (bundle, not publish). Records the consequence (duplicate-release-object class eliminated) and single-commit provenance.
- **193** — the paired cadence **collapses to a single product (OPC)**. Removes the `axiomregent-v*` tag grammar, the cross-product boundary invariant (`opc.minor == axiomregent.minor`), the axiomregent draft-first gating, and the guard's axiomregent arm. ACs/§2/§3/§4/§5/§5.1/§7 all read OPC-only.
- **117** (load-bearing) — new **§2.1**: the "installer SBOM includes the bundled sidecar's contents" goal is **bound to the desktop flow**. axiomregent's CycloneDX SBOM is generated inside `release-desktop.yml` (the proven generation lifted from the retired workflow) and **referenced** from each installer SBOM via a CycloneDX `externalReferences` BOM-Link, co-attached to the release. **Reference, not merge**, is chosen: matrix-portable `jq`, zero new binary supply-chain surface, sidecar BOM stays independently verifiable. §7 records single-commit provenance (build-ref == bundle-ref) → **no span clause** needed (build-once makes 117 simpler).
- **105** — `make fetch-axiomregent` re-pointed off the standalone release.

## Workflow / config diffs

- **Deleted** `release-axiomregent.yml`. **Kept** `build-axiomregent.yml` (per-commit build/smoke producer) + `ci-axiomregent.yml` (check/clippy/test) as producer/validator — neither publishes a product.
- `release-desktop.yml`: + `Generate workspace Cargo.lock for sidecar SBOM scan`, `Generate axiomregent sidecar SBOM (CycloneDX)`, `Generate installer SBOM bundled-sidecar reference (CycloneDX BOM-Link)`; sidecar SBOM co-attached inside the existing spec-194 draft-guarded upload step.
- `release-version-guard.sh`: axiomregent arm dropped → `opc`-only; `axiomregent` now exits `2`. Fixture test asserts it. `ci-supply-chain.yml` axiomregent guard step removed.
- `Makefile`: `fetch-axiomregent` now `gh run download`s the latest successful `build-axiomregent.yml` artifact (30-day retention) instead of `gh release download`; `make axiomregent` (build-from-source) is the documented offline fallback.
- `rust-toolchain.toml`, `docs/RELEASE-VERIFICATION.md`: stale standalone-release references removed/updated.

**Consequence:** the duplicate-release-object incident class (two release objects on one `axiomregent-v*` tag — e.g. the empty operator-decoy draft) is **structurally eliminated** — there is no second product release object to collide.

## Gates (local)

- spec-code coupling: **clean** (13 paths; 105 amended for the `axiomregent-build` Makefile section)
- spec-lint: **clean** · ci-parity: **OK** · workflow-pins (158): **OK**
- featuregraph golden: **unchanged** · release-version-guard + fixture test: **pass** · YAML parse: **OK**
- codebase index regenerated + staleness check clean

> ⚠️ The sidecar-SBOM wiring in `release-desktop.yml` is structurally complete but **runtime-unvalidated** (no release cut in this PR, per the brief). It will be exercised on the next `opc-v*` cut — consistent with how 117's SBOM-generation lessons were originally discovered.

title: spec(196): post-merge refinement — SC phase-correctness + Grafana auth-as-property
body:
## What

Fast-follow to **#285** (merged at the round-5 state). Carries the round-6 AI-review fixes that couldn't be pushed once #285 entered the merge queue. Spec-only refinements to a **draft** spec (`implementation: pending`) — no implementation impact.

## Changes

- **SC-001 re-phased** — Phase 1 gates the Prometheus-queryable half; end-to-end Grafana rendering is a Phase-2 consequence. (Same per-phase-verifiability class as #285's SC-008 split, now applied after auditing **every** SC — SC-001 was the only remaining offender.)
- **FR-004 / SC-003 — Grafana auth as a *property*** — "every non-OIDC authentication path disabled; OIDC is the sole provider" rather than an enumerated knob-list. Absorbs `auth.anonymous.enabled: false` (the round-6 finding) plus proxy/JWT/API-key/service-account paths; the exhaustive knob enumeration is implementation detail. Closes the knob-by-knob treadmill at the contract level.
- **SC-003** — pointer to the `plan.md` group→role-map Phase-2 precondition (owner's decision).
- **plan.md** — SC-004 path aligned to the full `platform/services/stagecraft/api/**`.

## Provenance

These are the round-6 items from #285's AI-review loop, agreed under the **"no remaining contract-level correctness/security bug"** convergence threshold. Rejected there (and not carried): `depends_on` ordering (deterministic per-tool convention, not corruption). Deferred to tasks.md: per-component resource limits, explicit `collection_interval` chart value, TSDB sizing (covered by FR-010's trigger).

Regenerated `.derived/codebase-index/index.json`; featuregraph golden unchanged (no relationship-edge changes).

title: refactor(180): align OPC release profile to defaults for shared-crate build reuse
body:
## Part A — OPC release-profile alignment (this PR; self-contained)

Aligns `product/apps/opc/src-tauri` `[profile.release]` to cargo defaults so OPC's shared-crate fingerprints match the **root** workspace, unlocking shared-target reuse of the ~555 crates OPC and axiomregent both build.

**Changed:**
- `[profile.release]`: removed `opt-level="z"`, `lto=true`, `codegen-units=1`, `panic="abort"` → now cargo defaults (`3 / false / 16 / unwind`). `strip=true` kept (link-only; does **not** key dependency-rlib reuse).
- Deleted `[profile.bench]` carve-out — its sole purpose was decoupling benches from release's `abort`+LTO; with `release=unwind`, bench inherits the correct strategy. **FR-T8 bench-presence is unchanged.**
- `axiomregent` profile **untouched** (stays `unwind`/default).

**Why (settled operator decision): reuse/CI-speed > binary size.** Tauri v2's lean baseline (~29.7 MB dmg) makes the size knobs not worth their build-time cost (`lto`+`cu=1` serialise codegen and diverge the fingerprint, defeating reuse).

**`panic → unwind` is behavioral, not size:** OPC has no abort dependence (the only `abort`s are `tokio::JoinHandle::abort()`); `unwind` is more resilient — a panicking command unwinds to a `JoinError` at the tokio boundary instead of aborting the app.

### Validation
- `cargo bench --no-run` built the **full OPC closure + `usage_scan` bench** under the inherited `unwind` profile (**4m03s, exit 0**) — empirically confirms the carve-out removal does **not** reintroduce the panic-strategy rlib mismatch (`can't find crate for orchestrator`).
- `make pr-prep` clean: coupling gate OK (3 diff paths), codebase index refreshed + staged.
- Manifest parse OK; spec-lint clean (exit 0, no V-020).
- Full dmg + runtime panic behavior are exercised by `release-desktop` CI (frontend bundling not run locally).

## Spec spine — folded into spec 180 as a completion (not a new spec)
032 stays primary manifest owner; 180 amends the profile rows it authored. §12 now records the rationale the mechanism always lacked: the **libsqlite3-sys `links="sqlite3"` workspace-split isolation**, why the **workspace merge is rejected** (separate cargo graphs ⇒ single `libsqlite3-sys` each ⇒ no `links` collision; a merge re-exposes that + the `rusqlite` feature-union for **zero** extra reuse), the **profile-match + shared-cache + lock-alignment** reuse path (not merging), and a new standing obligation **FR-T11 (sqlite drift-guard)**.

## Deferred (NOT in this PR)
- **Part B** (immediate follow-on): shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`/`sccache` across the two workspaces + lock-alignment of the divergent shared subgraphs (94 packages diverge today; watch `aws-lc-rs`/`openssl`/`h2`), with before/after reuse measurement.
- **FR-T11 impl**: a `tools/lint/` shell check (release-version-guard.sh precedent) wired as a `make ci` sub-target, failing when the OPC and root locks resolve `libsqlite3-sys` to different **majors** (today aligned at 0.37.0 / rusqlite 0.39.0). Spec'd in 180 §12.7; implementation is follow-on.

CONST-005: operator-set design direction recorded honestly via the 180 completion (spec leads; a now-moot mechanism removed). Coupling gate satisfied by the 180 edit.

🚧 Stops at PR-open per merge-queue protocol — operator controls the merge.

title: spec(196): platform metrics stack — Prometheus + Grafana (draft + plan)
body:
## What

Draft **spec + plan** for spec 196 — an operator-facing Prometheus + Grafana metrics stack for the platform control plane. No implementation in this PR (CONST-005: the spec body drives implementation).

## Scope

- **Control-plane oversight only.** Targets are stagecraft (Encore `remote_write`/push) + deployd-api / Flux / ingress-nginx / node-exporter / kube-state-metrics (scrape/pull). **Not** per-project/tenant — that is spec 175 (application layer).
- **Stack:** single `kube-prometheus-stack` Flux `HelmRelease` on Hetzner; Prometheus *server* with `--web.enable-remote-write-receiver` (agent mode can't receive remote_write nor serve queries). Alertmanager disabled + default rules pruned.
- **Grafana auth:** native Rauthy OIDC; the client is **created manually** in the Rauthy admin UI per the documented `[manual]` convention (`platform/infra/hetzner/.env.example`). 196 therefore touches no stagecraft code and does not edit the seeder — the seeder-sectioning path (provisional 197) was investigated and rejected.
- **Azure binding:** declared **deferred-null** (FR-009) with a named reopening trigger; Hetzner implemented.

## Phasing (plan.md)

Single-spec, sequenced: **Phase 1** data plane (independent) → **Phase 2** Grafana + manual OIDC (atomic; SC-003 forbids a local Grafana password). One open decision left for the owner: the Rauthy-group → Grafana-role map.

## Derived artifacts

Regenerated for the new spec: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` (196 claims it via `extends: 034`) and `.derived/codebase-index/index.json`. Spec-code coupling gate passes locally.

title: fix(opc-factory): server-resolve run inputs, fix duplex catalog hydration & session continuity
body:
## Summary

Fixes three issues on the OPC factory ↔ stagecraft seam and removes client-baked structure so the desktop resolves run inputs from platform data.

1. **Projects panel stuck on "Connecting to stagecraft…".** The project-catalog store hydrated *only* from live duplex events, and `project_catalog_sync.rs` cached nothing. The handshake snapshot is delivered once — but the panel mounts only *after* the boot gate opens (which itself waits on the handshake), so its listeners attach too late and Tauri doesn't buffer. (Exposed by the spec-183 boot-gate fix, which let users past the gate for the first time.)
2. **Re-prompting for sign-in despite a valid keychain token.**
3. **Adapter was a free-text field** — should be a server-resolved dropdown; more broadly, factory UI structure should come from the platform.

## Changes by area

### Catalog hydration race (pull-based)
- Rust caches the catalog (`ProjectCatalogCache`) and exposes a `get_project_catalog` command; the handlers write the cache before emitting.
- `subscribeProjectCatalog` now **pulls after attaching listeners**, so a snapshot delivered during the handshake is recovered instead of lost.
- Files: `project_catalog_sync.rs`, `stores/projectCatalogStore.ts`, `lib.rs`.

### Server-resolved factory inputs (specs 076, 124)
- **Adapter** → dropdown from `GET /api/factory/adapters` (`PlatformClient::list_adapters` + `list_factory_adapters` command), replacing the free-text `<Input>`.
- **Process name** → forwarded from `bundle.processes[0].name`; backend resolves from the platform list when absent (no client-baked `"factory"` default).
- **Pipeline DAG stages** → seeded from the process definition (`walk_stage_ids` → `PreparedRun.stage_ids`; `stagesFromProcessDefinition`). `PROCESS_STAGES` is kept only as the display-label source + fallback.
- Net effect: a platform-side rename/addition of adapter/process/stage needs **no desktop rebuild**.

### Session continuity — no spurious re-prompt (spec 183)
- A same-server settings re-save keeps the keychain session and reloads it onto the rebuilt client (a genuine server change still clears + requires re-auth).
- `auth_get_status` silently refreshes an expired token and restores in-memory `org_id` before reporting signed-out.
- The duplex loop emits `session-refreshed`; `AuthContext` re-checks status instead of leaving a stale "Sign in" prompt for a session it just recovered.

## Verification
- `cargo check` clean (factory-platform-client + opc src-tauri).
- Rust tests pass: platform-client (22 lib + 12 integration, incl. new `list_adapters`/`list_processes`), factory (25), project_catalog_sync (9), settings (5).
- Frontend `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- spec-code coupling gate: OK (21 paths); codebase index regenerated.

> Note: Phases that change live runtime behavior (catalog hydration, auth re-prompt, server-derived DAG) are logic/type/test-verified and fallback-guarded, but exercise a running Tauri app + live duplex — worth a manual confirmation in the app.

title: ci(stagecraft): retry base image build on transient registry timeouts
body:
## Problem

The merge-queue run for #281 was ejected by a failure in the
`stagecraft / encore build docker` job — **not** a code error. The
`encore-build` composite action's *Build runtime base image* step pulls
`node:22-slim` (Dockerfile.base `FROM`) from Docker Hub and hit a
transient registry timeout:

```
node:22-slim: failed to resolve source metadata for docker.io/library/node:22-slim:
  ... Head "https://registry-1.docker.io/.../manifests/22-slim": dial tcp 107.23.56.59:443: i/o timeout
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: DeadlineExceeded
```

This is a network flake against Docker Hub, unrelated to the OPC desktop
change in #281.

## Fix

Wrap the runtime base image `docker build` in a bounded retry (3
attempts, linear backoff 10s → 20s) in
`.github/actions/encore-build/action.yml`. A transient Docker Hub /
Debian-mirror timeout no longer ejects a PR from the merge queue. Docker
layer caching makes a retry after a `FROM`-resolution failure cheap; an
exhausted retry still fails the job with `::error::`.

No new action refs (no SHA-pin surface), no Makefile/CI-parity change, no
behavioral change to the produced image.

## Local verification

- `codebase-indexer check` — clean (action file is not a hashed index input)
- `spec-code-coupling-check --base origin/main` — exit 0
- `workflow-pins.sh` (spec 158 SHA-pin lint) — exit 0
- `ci-parity-check` (spec 104) — exit 0
- YAML parses; embedded retry script passes `bash -n`

## Relationship to #281

#281 itself is sound (all PR checks green). Once this merges, re-enqueue
#281 and the merge-queue base-image pull will survive transient timeouts.

title: fix(183): Arc-share StagecraftState so signed-in org_id reaches the boot gate
body:
## What

Fixes the OPC boot gate wedging at **"Waiting for stagecraft duplex handshake (sync.hello)…"** after a fresh sign-in — even though `sync.hello` had already been received — and closes the StagecraftState lifecycle/robustness gaps surfaced across review.

## Root cause (spec 183 FR-T2(a))

`boot_gate_status` reads `org_id` from the live `StagecraftState`, but `StagecraftState` held a **value-type** `StagecraftClient` and `current()` returned a **snapshot clone**. The OAuth callback's `set_org_id`/`set_auth_token` mutated a throwaway clone; the stored client's in-memory `org_id` stayed empty → `has_org = false` → the gate stuck despite `sync.hello`. The keychain was correct, so a relaunch masked it. It also left in-session REST auth running against an empty-token clone.

## Fix

- **Arc-share `StagecraftState`** (`Arc<StagecraftClient>`): boot-gate reader, duplex auth handle, and every REST command share **one** interior-mutable instance, so `set_org_id`/`set_auth_token`/`adopt_token` writes are globally visible. Test `stagecraft_state_shares_one_client_across_current_handles`.
- **URL-change re-spawn** (resolves the spawn-time-binding caveat): `set_stagecraft_base_url` re-spawns the duplex consumer against the new client. `spawn` now **aborts *and awaits*** the prior loop before launching the new one (no two-loop overlap); a cleared URL → `shutdown`. Stable `client_id` preserved via the new `OpcInstanceId` managed state.
- **Lock-poison robustness**: `StagecraftState::{current, replace}` recover a poisoned `RwLock` (log + `into_inner`) **and `clear_poison()`** — so a panicked holder logs once *per poison event*, not on every op, instead of silently disabling Stagecraft. Test `stagecraft_state_recovers_from_poisoned_lock`.
- **Keychain single-source-of-truth**: the URL-change cleanup and `clear_auth` both route through `StagecraftClient::clear_keychain_entries()` over a shared `KEYCHAIN_ENTRIES` const, so the entry list can't drift (a new credential is cleared by both at once).

Spec 183 §3.2 amended (FR-T2(a) in-memory-propagation invariant + spawn-time-binding resolution + lock-poison notes).

## Also in this PR (consolidated per request)

- **spec 188 amendment** — the `oap-index-regen` merge driver emitted a stale-but-clean `index.json` hash during this branch's rebase. Spec 188 User Story 1 AS-2 ("never produces a wrong-but-clean index") is amended to scope that guarantee to the fail-closed path and document the observed best-effort limitation (driver regenerates from the working tree mid-rebase, can't self-detect; CI staleness gate / `make pr-prep` caught it and remain the source of truth; live merge queue makes the path rare). Pointer comment added to `.githooks/merge-derived-index.sh`. Doc-only; precise root-cause needs a reproduction harness (tracked follow-up).

## Mechanical ripple + waiver

`factory.rs`/`factory_platform.rs` changed only as `StagecraftClient → Arc<StagecraftClient>` type propagation; `settings.rs` additionally carries the FR-T2(a) URL-change re-spawn — all spec-183-driven, no factory/settings domain redesign.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: factory.rs, factory_platform.rs, settings.rs — changed only for spec-183 FR-T2(a) reasons. factory.rs/factory_platform.rs are pure Arc<StagecraftClient> type propagation; settings.rs additionally carries the FR-T2(a) URL-change duplex re-spawn (the "switch servers" purpose is unchanged — the re-spawn is the 183 duplex-lifecycle following the new URL). Authoritative record: specs/183 FR-T2(a) (amended 2026-06-02). Scoped to this change only.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy ... -A dead_code -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test` (opc lib) — **153 pass** (incl. both new regression tests); featuregraph golden unaffected
- coupling gate — substantive files satisfied by the 183/188 amendments; the 3 above cleared by the scoped waiver (no new flags from `.githooks/` or spec 188)
- codebase index regenerated; staleness check clean; `.githooks/merge-derived-index.sh` passes `bash -n`

## Also done locally (not a committed change)

- **axiomregent sidecar** rebuilt (`make axiomregent`) — clears the hiqlite `127.0.0.1:0` storm on next launch (the bundled binary is gitignored).

## Status

Ready for review.

title: fix(194): repo-pin the publish-boundary precondition (release-tools.yml)
body:
## Summary

One-line surgical fix to the **spec-194 publish-boundary guard** in
`release-tools.yml`. The `gh release view` draft-state **precondition**
lacked the `--repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` pin that the `gh release upload`
**mutation** four lines down *in the same step* already carries.

```diff
- if state="$(gh release view "$TAG" --json isDraft -q .isDraft)"; then :; else
+ if state="$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json isDraft -q .isDraft)"; then :; else
```

## Root cause (log-verified)

The `publish` job's only checkout uses `path: src` (the SBOM-scan
checkout), so the workspace root has **no `.git`**. With no `--repo`,
`gh` falls back to inferring the repo from a cwd git remote, finds none,
errors `fatal: not a git repository`, and exits non-zero. The guard then
fails **closed** on its `gh-lookup-failed` branch — correctly refusing to
upload, but on a **mislabeled** reason (`"release may be gone or gh failed
to authenticate"`) rather than reading the draft's true `isDraft` state.

Proof it's an oversight, not intent: the `gh release upload` in the same
step already passes `--repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"`. The precondition was
simply not given the same pin. Latent since #277 (spec 194); this run was
the first to reach the guard (prior backfill died earlier at build
checkout). The draft is intact (`isDraft=true`, 16 assets, no tools
attached) — fail-closed preserved integrity.

## What this does NOT change

- **The guard logic.** The exit-code-first / lookup-failed / published /
  draft three-state structure and its error strings are unchanged.
- **The checkout layout.** `path: src` is untouched — it's load-bearing

  surgical fix.

## Governance

- `release-tools.yml` is spec-coupled; **spec 194 owns this guard** and
  already `refines:` the file. Landed as a **graph-truthful spec-194
  self-amendment** (`amended:` + `amendment_record:` + a §3 in-body
  callout), **not** a Spec-Drift-Waiver.
- `make pr-prep` clean: codebase index regenerated, coupling gate
  `OK — 3 diff path(s) checked`.
- No new spec → no featuregraph golden refresh.

## After merge (operator, separate step)

Re-dispatch the full-SHA tools backfill:

```bash
gh workflow run release-tools.yml -f tag=opc-v0.4.0 \
  -f ref=ed00951e4ce8511becbff429d58445a0a50704b6
```

The guard will then read `isDraft=true` and upload the 7 tools assets onto
the draft.

title: fix(193): hoist version guard to a standalone fail-fast front-gate job
body:
## Lane
Pre-build guard fast-fail (cost/correctness). **Safety was already intact** — this restores the missing fail-fast. Diagnosis-first; full findings in `docs/analysis/release-prebuild-guard-fastfail-2026-06-01.md`.

## Diagnosis (premise correction)
The `opc-v0.4.1` mismatch dispatch (run [`26793968624`](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/actions/runs/26793968624)) **did** refuse — but the prompt's premise was half-wrong, and the run log corrects it:

| Premise | Reality (log-verified) |
|---|---|
| guard didn't fire | ❌ it **did** — failing step, emitted `release-version-guard FAILED for opc (reference 0.4.1)` |
| the build ran | ❌ tauri-action **never ran**; all build steps skipped; release jobs died in ~1m |
| post-build refusal | ❌ it was the **pre-build** guard (no SBOM arg); no draft, no version burned |

**Root cause = job-ordering (candidate #1).** The guard is correctly placed *within* the `release` job (before tauri-action) but `release` has `needs: [sidecar, sidecar-linux-arm64]`, so the **sidecar matrix (~16m35s of axiomregent cross-compiles) runs first** and the guard can't execute until it finishes. Guard fired at `02:24:33Z` on a run created `02:07:58Z`. Every mismatched dispatch burns the full sidecar matrix to reject — a real cost problem, not a non-problem. `release-axiomregent.yml` has the identical pattern (guard in `publish`, which `needs: [build, build-linux-arm64]`).

## Fix
Hoist the committed-source check into a standalone `version-guard` job that the entire matrix `needs:`. It reads only committed sources (present in a bare checkout), so it needs no build output. A mismatch now dies in ~30s with **zero build minutes burned, no draft, no tag**.

- `release-desktop.yml`: new `version-guard` job; `sidecar`, `sidecar-linux-arm64`, `release` all `needs: [version-guard]`.
- `release-axiomregent.yml`: new `version-guard` job; `build`, `build-linux-arm64`, `publish` all `needs: [version-guard]`.

**Retained as defense-in-depth (not removed):** the in-job pre-build / pre-publish guards (incl. axiomregent's SBOM-component assertion the front gate can't see) and the post-build SBOM guard (build-time drift).

## Governance
Workflows are claimed by spec 193 via `refines: { aspect: release-version-alignment }`. Landed as a **self-describing spec 193 refinement** (§5.1 + AC-7), not a drift waiver. `make pr-prep` clean (coupling gate OK, index regenerated & committed). No new spec → no golden refresh.

title: spec(195): release-tools dispatch builds from a commit
body:
## P1 fix — release-tools `workflow_dispatch` build ref

**Bug.** `release-tools.yml`'s `resolve-tag` set `REF="refs/tags/$TAG"` on the
`workflow_dispatch` path. A **draft** release has no git tag yet (GitHub creates
the tag only at publish), so `actions/checkout` fails at the nonexistent ref and
the build matrix never runs. The documented backfill
`gh workflow run release-tools.yml -f tag=opc-v0.4.0` is therefore unusable for
exactly the draft releases it exists to complete.

**Observed.** Draft `opc-v0.4.0` (`isDraft:true`, `targetCommitish=ed00951e`,
no git tag) carries **16 desktop-only assets** and **no** tools bundle
(`oap-tools-*.{tar.gz,zip}`, `sbom-tools.cdx.json`, tools `*.intoto.jsonl`). It
was cut via `workflow_dispatch` on *Release Desktop* (`head_branch='main'`), so
the reactive tool chain skipped (gate: `startsWith(head_branch,'opc-v')`), and
the manual backfill would have failed at the tag ref.

**Fix.** Add an optional `ref` `workflow_dispatch` input (commit SHA) and resolve
`REF="${INPUT_REF:-$DISPATCH_SHA}"` (`$DISPATCH_SHA = github.sha`) on the dispatch
path — build from a **commit**, never the tag. Rationale: the tag doesn't exist
on the draft path, and the tools must build from the **same commit as the
desktop binaries** for coherent SLSA provenance (spec 117).

**Unchanged (deliberately):**
- Reactive `workflow_run` branch — still `REF="$UPSTREAM_SHA"`, `TAG="$UPSTREAM_BRANCH"`.
- spec-194 publish-boundary guard (`assert isDraft before gh release upload`) — correct; the draft *is* a draft.

## Resolved build SHA

The desktop draft built from **`ed00951e4ce8511becbff429d58445a0a50704b6`** — the
*Release Desktop* run `26794604178` `head_sha`, equal to the draft's
`targetCommitish` and to current `main` HEAD. Once this PR merges, the dispatch
backfill that completes opc-v0.4.0 is:

```
gh workflow run release-tools.yml -f tag=opc-v0.4.0 -f ref=ed00951e
```

(Backfilling opc-v0.4.0 itself is an operator action **after** merge — out of
scope for this PR, which lands only the workflow fix.)

## Governance

- New spec **195-release-tools-dispatch-build-ref** `refines` the
  `release-tools-dispatch-build-ref` aspect of `.github/workflows/release-tools.yml`
  (distinct from spec 194's `release-publish-boundary` aspect on the same file).
- Coupling gate: **OK — 4 diff paths checked**, satisfied via the `refines`
  claim. **No Spec-Drift-Waiver.**
- `make pr-prep` clean; `spec-lint` clean; `validate-graph` passed; featuregraph
  golden + codebase index regenerated and committed.

## ⚠ Deferred — operator decision (P2, spec 195 §7)

The reactive auto-attach is **non-functional on dispatch-cut releases**
(`head_branch='main'` fails the `'opc-v'` gate). **Not solved here.** Two options
— *do not assume one was picked*:

- **(a) Make `release-tools` dispatch-only.** Drop the `workflow_run` trigger;
  tools become a deliberate pre-publish step. Eliminates the spec-194 §7 TOCTOU
  residual and the silent-skip surprise.
- **(b) Fix the reactive chain to learn the real tag on dispatch cuts.** Needs
  the desktop run to pass its resolved tag/commit through (`workflow_run` exposes
  only `head_branch`/`head_sha`) — non-trivial.

**Interim model until P2 is decided:** tools are attached by a **manual
`release-tools` dispatch** (now buildable from a commit) after the desktop draft
is verified, **before** publish — per the spec-194 §5 runbook.

title: spec(194): publish-boundary guard — automation mutates draft releases only
body:
## What & why

Resolves the deferred item in **spec 193 §7** ("the publish path is controlled").
Spec 193 made release *creation* draft-first and human-gated, but release
*mutation* steps still ran without asserting the target is a draft. This PR adds a
**fail-closed draft assertion** before every `gh release upload` / `gh release delete`
so release automation can only ever mutate a **draft** release. Crossing the publish
boundary — publishing, uploading to an already-published release, or deleting a
published release/tag — now requires a human action *outside* the automation.

## Phase 1 — inventory (report only)

Full table in [`docs/analysis/publish-boundary-hardening-2026-06-01.md`](../blob/194-release-publish-boundary-guard/docs/analysis/publish-boundary-hardening-2026-06-01.md). Every `gh release`/tag/asset/dispatch step across all 28 workflows was enumerated. Findings:

| Step | Class |
|------|-------|
| release-desktop → tauri-action create (`releaseDraft: true`) | ✅ COMPLIANT |
| release-desktop → upload SBOM/attest (`--clobber`) | ⚠️ VIOLATION (race) |
| release-desktop → SHA-256 sidecars (`--clobber`) | ⚠️ VIOLATION (race) |
| release-desktop → guard-failure `gh release delete --cleanup-tag` | ⚠️ VIOLATION (severe — could delete a *published* release+tag) |
| release-axiomregent → `gh release create --draft` | ✅ COMPLIANT (left as-is) |
| **release-tools → `gh release upload --clobber`** | ⚠️ VIOLATION (**primary** — reactive `workflow_run`) |
| ai-changelog → `gh release edit --notes-file` | ✅ COMPLIANT — notes only, legal under immutability (left as-is) |
| ci-supply-chain, ai-pr-review | ✅ out of scope |

**Primary race:** `release-tools` fires on *Release Desktop* completion, spends ~30 min
building CLI tools while the desktop draft already *looks done*, then uploads. If the
operator publishes the draft in that window, the upload lands on an already-published,
already-attested release.

## Phase 2 — remediation (constrain, do not delete)

Per "prefer constraining over deleting": nothing removed. A uniform draft assertion
(`gh release view "$TAG" --json isDraft -q .isDraft` must be `true`) is inlined before
each `gh release upload`/`delete`. The guard-failure delete in release-desktop is
narrowed to draft-only. **Happy path is unchanged** — on a normal run the release is
always a draft, so every assertion passes; the guard bites only on the race, converting
a silent boundary crossing into a loud, safe CI failure.

`release-axiomregent.yml` (create-draft-only) and `ai-changelog.yml` (notes-only) are
verified compliant and untouched, per the lane's explicit instruction.

## Governance

- **Graph-truthful resolution, no waiver.** New spec 194 `refines` the
  `release-publish-boundary` aspect of both workflows (distinct from spec 193's
  `release-version-alignment` aspect) and `extends` 034 for the mechanical golden refresh.
- `make pr-prep` clean: codebase-index refreshed + **coupling gate clean (6 paths)**.
- spec-lint clean (fail-on-warn); workflow-pins SHA-pin lint clean; featuregraph golden
  regenerated (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`) and passing.
- Compliance: OWASP **ASI04** (supply-chain compromise) — published artifact sets and
  their SHA-256/SLSA attestations stay immutable to automation.

## Operator note

🛑 **Do not merge, do not publish.** Operator controls the merge queue. Publishing a
desktop draft should happen only after both *Release Desktop* and *Release Tools* are
green (CLI archives attached); publishing earlier now fails *Release Tools* loudly
instead of mutating the published release.

## Scope decision worth a look

release-tools is the **primary** reactive violation; release-desktop's guards are
defense-in-depth for the same invariant (it's human-tag-triggered, but its long
multi-OS build window + the destructive guard-failure delete make it a real, if
narrower, gap). If you'd prefer to scope this PR to release-tools only, the
release-desktop guards can be dropped — flagging because the lane said "remediate
violations only."

body:
