title: fix(183): harden duplex reconnect (backoff/give-up/keychain) + hiqlite bind retry
body:
Four AI-review hardening follow-ups to #274. None fix a broken behaviour — the boot gate already opens — they remove avoidable edge-case stalls and a TOCTOU race. Landed as one PR.

## Changes

**`sync_client.rs` — reconnect loop (items 1+2)**
- The `consecutive_failures` increment moved into the failure arms. A 401 whose silent refresh succeeds is a *session expiry*, not an unreachable service: it resets the backoff to its floor and retries promptly **without** advancing the give-up counter. Previously a fresh bearer could wait up to `MAX_BACKOFF` (60s) if backoff had grown from earlier transient failures, and a routine token rotation raced the gate toward give-up.
- `MAX_REFRESHES_PER_OUTAGE = 3` bounds a pathological refresh→still-401 hot-loop (e.g. clock skew); past the budget a 401 counts as a genuine failure so the precondition-loss signal stays reachable.

**`sync_client.rs` + `stagecraft_client.rs` — keychain off the executor (item 4)**
- Split the blocking OS keychain read (`read_session_token_from_keychain`, free fn) from the in-memory apply (`adopt_token`). `resolve_token` and the refresh-failed reload now run the read under `spawn_blocking`, so keychain I/O cannot stall the tokio worker driving the loop.

**`crates/axiomregent/src/db/mod.rs` — `init_hiqlite` (item 3)**
- Wrap resolve-ports → `start_node` in a bounded retry (`HIQLITE_BIND_ATTEMPTS = 3`) that re-resolves a fresh loopback pair on a bind failure, closing the TOCTOU window where another process can claim a freed port before hiqlite rebinds. `migrate()` stays outside the retry (a DDL error propagates, not retried).

## Spec amendments (coupling-gate authorities)
- **073** — Phase-1 step 3 sub-bullet: bind retry.
- **110** — reconnect-loop hardening + keychain read/apply split.
- **183 §3.2** — FR-T2(b) follow-up hardening note.

## Validation
- `cargo check` both manifests — clean, no new warnings.
- `cargo test` `sync_client` (32) + `stagecraft_client` (7) + axiomregent `db` (new `free_loopback_pair` distinctness test) — all pass.
- `make pr-prep` — **coupling gate clean (7 diff paths)**; regenerated `index.json` staged.

## Noted, deliberately out of scope
`StagecraftClient::refresh_jwt` still does a synchronous keychain read/write inside an `async fn`. Impact is smaller (it already awaits a network call), so it was left alone to avoid scope-creep — flagged here per the handoff rather than folded in.

title: fix(183): refresh duplex JWT + resolve hiqlite loopback ports
body:
## Summary

Fixes the OPC boot precondition gate (spec 183) hanging on **"Waiting for stagecraft duplex handshake (sync.hello)…"**, plus silences an unrelated hiqlite log flood surfaced in the same logs.

### 🔴 Blocker — duplex JWT never refreshed
The duplex consumer baked the launch-time JWT into its reconnect loop and retried the **same expired token forever** (`401 → 60s backoff → 401`). The Encore gateway rejects an expired bearer with HTTP 401 *before* the WebSocket upgrade, so `sync.hello` never arrived and the org-session precondition never flipped.

- **`sync_client.rs`** — resolve the bearer at connect time from the shared OS keychain (not a launch snapshot); classify a 401 on the upgrade distinctly (`ConnectError::Unauthorized`) and drive a silent Rauthy refresh (`StagecraftClient::refresh_jwt`) before retrying; idle on a short poll when no session exists yet.
- **`lib.rs`** — spawn the consumer whenever a Stagecraft base URL is configured (dropped the launch-time-token requirement), so cold-start and expired-token both self-recover.
- **`stagecraft_client.rs`** — expose `refresh_jwt` as `pub(crate)` so the loop reuses the exact refresh path the REST calls already use.

### 🟡 Noise — hiqlite dialing `127.0.0.1:0`
`axiomregent/src/db/mod.rs` advertised `127.0.0.1:0` for the single-node Raft/API addresses, leaving port 0 in Raft membership; the in-process client's background WS stream then dialed an unconnectable address and flooded stderr with `EADDRNOTAVAIL` (os error 49) once/sec. Now resolves concrete free loopback ports (bind `:0` → read `local_addr()` → release → advertise) — the same pattern the probe port uses. **Log-noise only**; the single-node data path runs in-process regardless. deployd-api's hiqlite was verified separately as correct and is untouched.

## Spec amendments (coupling-gate authorities)
- **073** — hiqlite loopback port resolution (Phase 1 §3).
- **110** — duplex consumer auth lifecycle (§10).
- **183** — boot-gate token liveness (§3.2).

## Validation
- `cargo check` both crates, no new warnings.
- Tests: axiomregent full suite, `sync_client` (32), `stagecraft_client` (7) — all pass.
- `make pr-prep` — coupling gate clean, codebase index regenerated.

## Verify at runtime
Self-heals on rebuild + relaunch: expired access token → 401 → refresh → fresh bearer → `sync.hello` → gate opens, no user action, provided the Rauthy *refresh* token is still valid.

> Note (out of scope): if the refresh token is *also* expired the loop can't self-heal and re-auth is needed, but the gate shows no sign-in affordance — a separate UX gap worth a follow-up.

title: spec(103): /init recompiles spec registry before lifecycle read (FR-06)
body:
## Why

`/init` reported stale spec lifecycle counts this session: it showed **192 specs — 183 approved, 5 draft, 4 superseded**, listing 165/175/187/188 as `draft` and omitting 192 entirely. The specs' own frontmatter said otherwise (all `approved`).

**Root cause:** `.derived/spec-registry/registry.json` is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:310`) — a per-clone local build artifact, never committed. The local copy was a month-old cache (written May 31) read *before* the Jun 1 lifecycle-close commits (#269/#270) edited the spec frontmatter. The `/init` protocol runs a staleness *gate* for the codebase index (`codebase-indexer check`) but had **no equivalent freshness step for the spec registry**, so it read the stale cache verbatim.

On-disk frontmatter (ground truth) is **193 specs — 188 approved, 1 draft (143), 4 superseded**. After `spec-compiler compile`, the governed read agrees.

## What changed

- **`AGENTS.md § New Sessions`** — `/init` now runs `spec-compiler compile` *before* the `registry-consumer` reads, plus a **Registry freshness** note explaining why this differs from the codebase-index staleness check.
- **`specs/103-init-protocol-governed-reads/spec.md`** — adds **FR-06 (Registry Freshness Before Lifecycle Read)** + a §6 clarification + self-amendment record. Spec 103 holds coupling authority over `AGENTS.md` (via `refines`), so this edit is required to keep the coupling gate green.
- **`README.md`** — corrects a stale inline lifecycle comment (`186 approved, 3 draft, 4 superseded` → `188 / 1 / 4`). No spec claims coupling authority over `README.md`.
- **`.derived/codebase-index/index.json`** — regenerated (`specs/*/spec.md` is a hashed index input).

## Design note: recompile, not check

FR-03 *surfaces* codebase-index staleness and continues, because that artifact is **committed** (there's a committed hash to compare). FR-06 *eliminates* registry staleness by recompiling, because the registry is **gitignored** — there is no committed truth to diverge from, only source (`spec.md`) and a derived cache. The recompile is deterministic (Principle IV), idempotent, and is the same `spec-compiler compile` that produces the canonical registry (Principle II) — read-side hygiene, not a new authoring channel.

## Local gates

- `make pr-prep` → coupling gate **OK (4 diff paths checked)**, index refreshed.
- `spec-lint` → clean (exit 0).
- `spec-compiler compile` → registry now reports 188/1/4, matching frontmatter.

## `implementation: in-progress` (not `complete`) — deliberate

Asserting `complete` at PR time would be hopeful-state. It flips in a small follow-up after the **first green nightly** confirms AC-5/7/9 on Linux — the verification gate working, not friction.

## AC-8 staged — precise-cause finding (spec §6 AC-9)

183 AC-8 starts "from a fully-signed-in cockpit". Reaching that headlessly isn't possible today: OPC sign-in is a full GitHub OAuth/PKCE flow against Rauthy (`commands/auth.rs`, no dev bypass) and `org_session_ready` needs a materialised `org_id`. AC-8 is migrated as a `describe.skip` with a recorded reason (FR-T6 manual-only — **not** a flake skip); follow-up **`[[opc-e2e-auth-state-seeding]]`** un-skips it. Also recorded: **FR-T5(b)** refined (per-PR desktop matrix is macOS-only, which tauri-driver can't drive → nightly runs the WebDriver-capable Linux subset).

## Governance

title: chore(175): lifecycle closure — stagecraft project dashboard approved/complete
body:
## Lifecycle-closure PR — second merge-queue canary

Closes out spec 175 (`stagecraft-project-dashboard-observability`). Implementation landed earlier via #219/#221; this is the lifecycle flip.

### Scope (3 files)
- **`specs/175-…/spec.md`**: `status: draft → approved`, `implementation: pending → complete`. Adds an additive `extends: 034` edge on `features_graph.json` — 175's lifecycle state is snapshotted in the golden, so the flip shifts the golden fingerprint; the edge declares that *true* relationship (convention precedent: 165/167/168/169/183/188). No `amends:` record, no body change.
- **`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json`**: regenerated — delta is exactly the `status`/`implementation` flip + fingerprint.
- **`.derived/codebase-index/index.json`**: regenerated (contentHash).

title: spec(165): complete the OPC decomposition pipeline (caching, LLM synth, certificate, promotion, checkpoint, UI) + spec(192) embedding cache
body:
## What

Completes **spec 165** (OPC decomposition pipeline) to **all ten FRs and all six SCs**, taking `implementation:` from `in-progress` → `complete`. The deterministic backbone (stages 1–6 + Tauri commands) landed in PR #205; this is the follow-up that fills in the remaining contracted behaviour. Authored as a sequence of TDD, per-phase commits.

Also authors and implements **spec 192** (decomposition embedding cache), the spec-first realisation of spec 165 landing-1's deferred F-006.

## Delivered

| Area | Spec | What |
|------|------|------|
| Stage caching | 165 FR-007 / SC-004 | `PipelineRunner` reuses stages 1–5 (`Cached`) when tree+knowledge signatures match a prior run; only stage 6 re-runs |
| LLM synthesiser | 165 §2.1 | `Synthesiser` trait; `DeterministicSynthesiser` (default, CI-safe) + feature-gated `ProviderSynthesiser` (provider-registry; falls back to deterministic if model output misses the emission contract) |
| Governance certificate | 165 FR-009 / SC-006 | Reuses factory-engine's `GovernanceCertificate`; verifies via the same `make verify-certificate`. Binds stage hashes + synthesiser identity + prompt-template hash (§2.3) + staged-spec hashes |
| Promotion | 165 FR-008 / SC-005 | `promote_spec` writes into `<project>/specs/`, recompiles the registry, runs the coupling gate; `decomposition_promote` Tauri command |
| Branch-of-thought | 165 §2.2 | `CheckpointSink` trait + `FsCheckpointSink` DAG-ledger (default); runs over the same evidence share an anchor, distinct trajectories |
| React panel | 165 FR-001 | `DecompositionSurface` + panel shim + `decomposition` tab + TS api wrappers |
| Embedding cache | **192** | Content-addressed on-disk cache; the `embeddings` clustering path never re-embeds unchanged content across runs |

## Notable fixes surfaced en route

The promotion compile revealed the backbone's emitted specs **never actually compiled** (spec-lint had tolerated it):
- `summary: >` YAML block scalar lost its continuation indentation → serde_yaml reject. Now a single-line quoted summary.
- provenance emitted a bare `source:` hash; the grammar (V-028) requires `ref: xray-fingerprint://<sha256>` **and** spec-lint (W-161) requires `derived_at:`. Now emits both.
- clustering now excludes `.opc`/build dirs so stage 6 never emits a "spec" describing the pipeline's own scratch output.

## Engineering decisions (preserve spec intent; not spec edits)

- **Checkpoint backend:** spec-095's `CheckpointStore` is async + hiqlite-backed and lives in the axiomregent sidecar process (not linkable in-process). The filesystem DAG-ledger delivers the §2.2 capability without pulling hiqlite into the pipeline; an axiomregent-backed sink is a drop-in behind the same trait. Mirrors landing-1's "xray over axiomregent for stage 3" decision.
- **LLM path is feature-gated** (`llm-synthesis`, off by default) — CI never hits the network. The deferred prompt-template *library* and model-selection *UX* remain out of scope (spec 165 §5).

## Verification (local)

- `opc-decomposition-pipeline`: all tests pass on default, `embeddings`, and `llm-synthesis` features; clippy clean on all three.
- Workspace: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --workspace --exclude axiomregent` green (axiomregent's `fastembed`→ONNX-runtime native link is a pre-existing local env issue, unchanged by this PR).
- Frontend: 176 vitest pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean; `src-tauri` cargo check clean.
- Governance: spec-lint 0 errors; coupling gate exit 0 (resolved via proper `establishes`/`extends`/`refines` — **no Spec-Drift-Waiver needed**); codebase-index staleness check clean; featuregraph golden regenerated; registry compile all-validations-pass.

title: spec(180): OPC shell codification — Phase 2 (Tier 1 invariants + Tier 2 bench gate)
body:
Implements **Phase 2** of spec `180-opc-shell-codification` (the spec doc / Phase 1 already merged). Enforces the §3 Tier 1 structural invariants on the bug-adjacent OPC tab/IPC seam and inaugurates the §5 Tier 2 bench gate, then flips the spec to `approved`/`complete`.

## What lands (by FR)

**Tier 1 — tab-list reconciliation (§3.1, FR-T1/T2/T3)**
- **FR-T1**: removed `<AnimatePresence mode="wait">` wrapping the mapped panel list in `TabContent.tsx` — `mode="wait"` gated reconciliation of every panel behind a sibling's exit animation (the originating perf defect). The list now reconciles directly.
- **FR-T2**: per-tab components memoized via `React.memo` with a `tab.id` + `isActive` (+ `updatedAt`) comparator — binds on both `TabContent`'s `TabPanel` and `TabManager`'s `TabItem` (§3.3). Comparators live in the pure, unit-testable `tabPanelMemo.ts`.
- **FR-T3**: a single-panel update preserves sibling object identity (already true of `updateTab`; now locked by a behavioural test).

**Tier 1 — filesystem-scanning IPC handlers (§3.2, FR-T4..T7)** on `commands/usage.rs`:
- **FR-T4** `pub async fn` + `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` — the `~/.claude` scan no longer starves the Tauri runtime.
- **FR-T5** process-lifetime, path-keyed, mtime-fresh `UsageCache` — an unchanged-mtime hit isn't re-read.
- **FR-T6** single read per file: `parse_file_full` yields both the records and the earliest timestamp, removing the former two-pass read (`get_earliest_timestamp` + `parse_jsonl_file`).
- **FR-T7** the cache is registered as Tauri managed state in `lib.rs`. Dedup semantics preserved exactly.

**Tier 2 — bench gate (§5, FR-T8..T10)**
- **FR-T8** `benches/usage_scan.rs` (criterion) exercises the scan over a synthetic N-file corpus.
- **FR-T9** new reusable `ci-opc-bench.yml` (macОС): PR gate at N=200 vs a cached `main` baseline (fail >25% relative regression), baseline saved on merge-to-main, nightly N=2000 report. Composes into `ci-gate` (spec 177).
- **FR-T10** strictly relative delta — no absolute latency threshold.

## Notes for review
- **Inaugural bench run**: there is no `main` baseline yet, so the bench gate on *this* PR measures-only and passes (`--baseline-lenient`); the first baseline is saved when this merges to `main`.
- **`ci-opc-bench.yml` is parity-exempt** (not in `ci-parity-check`'s `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS`): the gate is CI-stateful (baseline in the Actions cache) and can't be mirrored by a local `make` recipe — same shape as `cd-index-staleness-report.yml`.
- **`[profile.bench] panic = "unwind"`** is load-bearing (the inline comment explains why) — Cargo's "ignored for bench profile" note is about the bench binary, not its deps; removing it reintroduces a `can't find crate` build failure.
- **Graph-truthful coupling**: Phase 2's authority is declared, not waived — `establishes` the `benches/` tree + `ci-opc-bench.yml`; `extends` 177 (ci.yml), 032 (Cargo.toml bench deps), 034 (featuregraph golden), each matching existing precedent (188/190/191).
- Folds in current `origin/main` (#267's `ci-gate` AI-review edit was combined with the `opc-bench` wiring in `ci.yml`).

## Local verification
- Frontend: `tsc` clean; vitest **179 pass** (11 new tab-reconciliation cases).
- Rust (ci-desktop parity): `cargo check`, `clippy -A dead_code -D warnings`, `test --lib` (**151**), `test --doc` — all clean.
- Bench: builds + runs; gate mechanic verified end-to-end (save-baseline → baseline-lenient → `change/estimates.json` → jq mean; +2.7% passes, a simulated 30% trips the gate).
- Gates: coupling **clean** (14 paths), spec-lint clean (V-020 silent on 180 — AC-2), `codebase-indexer check` fresh, workflow-pins + ci-parity clean, `by-authority` resolves 180 over every claimed path (AC-4).

Closes the Phase 2 work for spec 180.

title: ci(177): fold AI review into ci-gate — failed review now blocks merge
body:
## What

Now that **#265** made the AI review actually run, this makes it a real gate. `ai-pr-review.yml` becomes a **reusable** (`workflow_call`) workflow dispatched from `ci.yml` as the PR-only `ai-review` job and added to the terminal **`ci-gate` `needs:`** — so a failed or absent review **blocks merge** (green `ci-gate` ⇒ actually reviewed). No branch-protection edit needed; `ci-gate` is already the required check.

## Mechanism

- **`ai-pr-review.yml`**: `pull_request` trigger → `workflow_call` (+ `workflow_dispatch`), conforming to spec 177 FR-002 (no standalone `pull_request`/`push` trigger). Eliminates a double-run.
- **`ci.yml`**: new `ai-review` job — `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (it needs PR context, like `spec-code-coupling`; skipped = success on `push`/`merge_group`), job-level `pull-requests: write` (overrides ci.yml's `read` default for this job only, so the called workflow can post its comment), `secrets: inherit` (passes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`). Added to `ci-gate.needs`.

This PR is the live test: `ci.yml`'s head version runs the folded `ai-review` job on *this* PR, exercising the reusable-workflow dispatch + permissions/secrets path. If the mechanism is wrong, **this PR's** `ci-gate` goes red (main is unaffected).

## Graph-truthful amendments

- **Spec 177** (owns `ci.yml`): self-amendment recording the fold; `ai-pr-review.yml` added as a trigger-consolidation reference; FR-005 note; **`amends: 104`** (the coupling authority for the 104 edit — mirrors how #264's spec 188 declared `amends`).
- **Spec 104** (parity contract): its prose that said *"ai-pr-review.yml — no validation gates"* and *"AI-assist workflow is not enforcing"* is now **false**, so it's corrected. `ai-pr-review.yml` is now the first **ENFORCING-but-parity-EXEMPT** gate.

## ⚠️ Design note for your blessing at merge

This introduces the **first gate that blocks merge but has no `make ci-strict` mirror** — an AI review calls a hosted model and has no deterministic local equivalent. That's a deliberate evolution of spec 104's parity model: **enforcing ⇏ mirrored**, as a documented single-instance exception. The parity *tool* needs no change (it iterates `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS`, which `ai-pr-review.yml` is correctly absent from, and never reads `ci-gate.needs`). If you'd rather AI review stay advisory-not-blocking, this is the PR to say so.

## Validation

Coupling clean (5 paths); spec-lint clean; featuregraph golden unchanged; registry + index regenerated (carries the `177 amends 104` edge); workflow YAML validated; `ai-pr-review.yml` triggers are `workflow_call`/`workflow_dispatch` only.

title: Codebase index (broad cache) is stale on main
body:
The broad committed `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` on `main` no longer matches a fresh recompute of its inputs.

This is **non-blocking**. Per spec 188 Phase 3, the broad index is a *best-effort regenerable cache*: no PR gates on it, and the direct-push heal was retired as incompatible with branch protection. The cost is SC-06 (an agent reading a stale index gets stale structural context).

**To clear:** run `make registry` locally and open a refresh PR (it merges via the queue like any other change). This issue auto-closes when `main` is fresh again.

The narrow `claudeConfigHash` guarantee (spec 184 / FR-009) is unaffected — `ci-config-hash` enforces it at PR time, independent of this cache.

title: ci(085): fix AI PR review auth — CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN + drop failure-swallow
body:
## Why

The **AI PR Review has been green-but-dead on every PR sampled back to #220** (220, 230, 240, 247, 250, 253, 255, 256, 257–264 all show "Review generation failed"). Two compounding faults:

1. **Auth.** `ai-pr-review.yml` set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from an empty/unset secret. An empty API key wins by precedence over the subscription-backed `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so the headless `claude` CLI never authenticated.
2. **Rail.** `claude … || echo "Review generation failed"` swallowed the failure → step exits 0 → job green. "Green" never meant "reviewed" — the exact rule-without-a-rail this platform exists to prevent.

## Fix

- **Auth:** the `Run AI Review` step now passes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}` and **removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` entirely** so it can't win by precedence.
- **Rail:** dropped the `|| echo` swallow. `claude`'s real exit code + stderr now surface in the runner log; on failure the step fails and the `Post review comment` step (implicit `success()` in its `if`) is skipped — a red check with a visible cause, never a misleading "passed" comment.

## Verification

This PR is the live test: a same-repo PR runs the **head** version of the workflow with secrets available, so the AI review on *this PR* should now post a real review under the OAuth token (or fail visibly with the real stderr).

## Deliberately NOT in this PR

Promoting the review into the **required `ci-gate`** (a failed review blocks merge) is the next step — gated on first confirming here that a review genuinely runs under the OAuth token. Hardening before that would just turn every PR red.

## Scope notes

- Coupling gate passes — `ai-pr-review.yml`'s `# Spec: 085` header is an *allowlist* mapping (spec 118), not a Layer-2 authority edge, so no spec amendment is required.
- `ai-pr-review.yml` is parity-exempt AI-assist (spec 104), and the edit doesn't touch the Claude config slice, so `ci-config-hash` is unaffected.

title: spec(188): Phase 4a — re-home claudeConfigHash to config-hash.json (index schema 3.0.0)
body:
## What

Spec 188 **Phase 4a** — re-home the narrow Claude shared-config slice hash out of the broad codebase index into its own tracked file, dissolving the cache/contract tension Phase 3 surfaced.

- `build.claudeConfigHash` (lived inside `index.json`, schema 2.3.0) → `.derived/codebase-index/config-hash.json` (new schema `config-hash.schema.json` 1.0.0).
- Broad index schema **2.3.0 → 3.0.0** (BREAKING: required field removed under `additionalProperties:false`).
- `check-config` reads the re-homed file; `compile` writes **and self-validates** it (FR-09 parity).
- **Behavior is bit-for-bit unchanged** — same two files, same hash (`bcb796fe…` preserved exactly), same PR-time blocking `ci-config-hash` gate. Only the storage location moved, so the broad `index.json` now carries nothing governed/gated.

## Scope decision — Goal 1 only (Phase 4 split)

Spec 188's designed Phase 4 bundled **two** steps. This PR lands **4a** (re-home) and **defers 4b** (`​.gitignore` the broad `index.json`):

- 4a alone fully dissolves the tension — once the gated value leaves the cache, the cache governs nothing.
- 4b is separable, **reverses spec 101 SC-06** (present-on-clone), and pulls in a wider blast radius (`/init` read path + `AGENTS.md`/spec 103, README "Try it", Makefile consumers). It's held as its own decision on SC-06's merits.
- The broad index stays a committed best-effort cache; `cd-index-staleness-report.yml` remains its visibility mechanism.

## Graph-truthfulness (the load-bearing bit)

Specs 101 and 188 already contained forward-references claiming Phase 4 *"restores the broad-freshness invariant structurally by making the index a pure build artifact (`.gitignore`d)."* That is only true of the **deferred 4b**. Those notes are **corrected** here (101 SC-05 + §2.5; 188 SC-004 + phase table + Phase 4 narrative): 4a does **not** restore the invariant (the index stays committed and may lag).

Coupling graph edges added so the diff is graph-true:
- `188 extends 101 → types.rs` (the `BuildInfo`/`ConfigHash` struct edit — Phase 3 touched `types.rs` untraced; corrected now).
- `188 extends 127 → tests/cli.rs` (the index major-bump trips the coupling gate's own version guard, so its fixture bumps `2.0.0→3.0.0`).
- `188 establishes config-hash.schema.json` and `tests/spec188_check_config.rs` (the latter created by Phase 3 but never declared).

## Validation

- `codebase-indexer` + `spec-code-coupling-check` + enricher test suites pass.
- featuregraph golden **unchanged** (amendment/relationship fields aren't scanner-captured; status/implementation/depends_on/title untouched).
- `check-config` exit 0; coupling gate clean (21 paths); `cargo check/clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; `spec-lint` clean.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

The OAP enricher does **not** validate its output against `codebase-index-oap.schema.json`, whose `build` is `additionalProperties:false` yet never listed `claudeConfigHash` — a latent mismatch that only never fired because nothing validates. This PR removes the field (so the passthrough is cleaner), but wiring enricher output validation (or marking that schema advisory) is worth a separate change.

title: spec(188): retire direct-push heal → report-only staleness job (broad index = best-effort cache)
body:
Follow-up to #262, prompted by enabling the GitHub merge queue.

## Why
The merge queue requires **PR-required + signed-commits** branch protection on `main`. The `cd-index-heal.yml` direct-push heal (shipped in #262) cannot satisfy that — a bot push has no PR and an unsigned commit — and the only way to keep it would be a **bypass actor with unreviewed `main` write**, which is an attack surface and an ideological self-own on a governance platform. So the heal is **retired, not bypassed**.

Phase 3 already demoted the broad index to a cache; caches don't belong under signed-commit branch protection. The load-bearing narrow `claudeConfigHash` guarantee is untouched.

## What changed
- **Delete `cd-index-heal.yml`; add `cd-index-staleness-report.yml`** — runs `codebase-indexer check` on `main` and *reports* broad drift (a `::warning::` annotation + a single auto-managed tracking issue), **never pushes, never fails the run**. Recovers the SC-06 (agent-orientation) visibility of a stale cache without a push.
- **Spec 188** — FR-007 (heal retired; broad index = best-effort regenerable cache), FR-009 (back door now closed **by construction** — no healer writes, so config drift can't be silently absorbed), SC-004 (best-effort, not byte-fresh-on-main), and a new **Phase 4** design: re-home `claudeConfigHash` to its own tracked file and `.gitignore` the broad index, *dissolving* the cache/contract split that created this whole tension.
- **Specs 101 / 177 / 184** — propagate the mechanism change (heal → report-only + best-effort cache).
- Fix now-stale `cd-index-heal.yml` comments in `ci.yml`, `ci-config-hash.yml`, `spec-conformance.yml`, `ci-parity-check`.

## Unaffected
The narrow `ci-config-hash` / `check-config` guarantee (spec 184 / FR-009) is unchanged — config-touching PRs still regenerate `index.json` and carry the fresh slice into their squash, enforced at PR time + in the queue.

## Verification (local)
spec-code-coupling (11 paths) ✓ · ci-parity (12 workflows) ✓ · spec-lint --fail-on-warn ✓ · validate-graph ✓ · codebase-indexer check + check-config ✓.

title: spec(188): Phases 3 & 2 — narrow config-hash gate + post-merge index heal + merge queue + dup-id lint
body:
Implements spec **188** Phases 3 and 2, in the spec-mandated order (Phase 3 → Phase 2 per FR-006). Resolves the §spec-184 tension via **re-homing (path 1)**: broad index freshness moves post-merge while spec 184's PR-time blocking guarantee is preserved on a narrow, merge-queue-safe surface.

## Phase 3 — narrow config-hash gate + post-merge heal (commit 1)
- **Indexer**: `build.claudeConfigHash` sub-hash over **only** `.claude/settings.json` + `.mcp.json`; new `codebase-indexer check-config`; index schema `2.2.0 → 2.3.0` (additive). The slice is independent of the broad `contentHash`, so the narrow gate stays valid in a merge queue regardless of unrelated input churn (FR-006).
- **`ci-config-hash.yml`** replaces `ci-codebase-index.yml` in the constitutional always-on set (runs on `pull_request` **and** `merge_group`).
- **`cd-index-heal.yml`** post-merge heal regenerates+commits `index.json` on `main`, but **fails loud on a config-slice delta first** (back-door corollary, FR-009) rather than silently absorbing config drift.
- Makefile `ci-config-hash` target + `ci-strict` prereq; `ci-parity-check` `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS` swap (188 `extends` 104, per the spec 191 precedent).
- Amends specs **101 / 177 / 184**.

## Phase 2 — merge queue + duplicate-id lint (commit 2)
- **`merge_group:`** trigger on `ci.yml`; the full routed suite runs against the speculative merged tree. **Inert until** a repo admin enables the queue (ops step, below).
- **V-032** spec-compiler lint (error severity) catches the spec-186 duplicate-numeric-id-prefix collision class that previously compiled silently.

## Verification (local, both commits)
spec-code-coupling ✓ · ci-parity ✓ · spec-lint --fail-on-warn ✓ · validate-graph ✓ · `check` + `check-config` ✓ · featuregraph golden ✓ · indexer + spec-compiler (incl. V-032) + parity tests ✓.

## Remaining ops step (NOT code — do after this lands on main)
Per FR-006, enabling the merge queue is deliberately deferred: a repo admin **enables the GitHub merge queue and requires `ci-gate` on `merge_group`** in branch protection, only after Phase 3 is on `main`. The `merge_group:` trigger is inert until then. Note: `cd-index-heal.yml` pushes to `main` under a bot identity — branch protection must permit that push.

title: spec(191): wire ci-schema-parity as an enforcing CI job (bun)
body:
## Summary

Closes the loop on spec 189: the Rust↔TS schema-parity gate (`make ci-schema-parity`) was restored and extended with envelope-version parity, but it ran **only in the local `make` loop** — no CI workflow enforced it pre-merge (a gate that can't catch its own breakage, which is how it stayed dark for so long). This wires it as an **enforcing** reusable workflow dispatched from the spec-177 orchestrator.

This is the second of the two follow-ups split out of the boot-gate work (the first, #259, fixed the desktop paths-filter).

## What lands

**1. `ci-schema-parity.yml` (new enforcing workflow)**
Mirrors the Makefile `ci-schema-parity` recipe verbatim:
- `cargo test … crates/factory-contracts … writes_*_fingerprint_file` — emit Rust fingerprints
- `bun run tools/oap/schema-parity-check/index.mjs` — envelope-version parity (spec 189) + knowledge compare + reserved provenance/stakeholder

Runtime is **bun**, via SHA-pinned `oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e… # v2.2.0` (spec 158). bun's fast startup + native `.ts` suit a per-PR gate, and keeping the `bun run` command identical to the Makefile means spec 104's run-mirror holds with zero Makefile churn. Crucially, the only TS the walker imports (`api/knowledge/extractionOutput.ts`) is **dependency-free**, so there's no `npm install` step (which would also have broken the run-mirror).

**2. `ci.yml` routing (spec 177)**
A `schema_parity` paths-filter scoped to what the walker compares, a routed job, and an entry in the `ci-gate` aggregator:
```yaml
schema_parity:
  - 'crates/factory-contracts/**'
  - 'platform/services/stagecraft/api/knowledge/**'
  - 'platform/services/stagecraft/api/governance/**'
  - 'platform/services/stagecraft/api/sync/**'
  - 'product/apps/opc/src-tauri/src/commands/sync_client.rs'
  - 'tools/oap/schema-parity-check/**'
  - '.github/workflows/ci-schema-parity.yml'
```
The `sync/**` + `sync_client.rs` entries are what make the envelope drift this whole lineage started with (#257 → #258 → #259) catchable at PR time going forward.

**3. Parity classification (spec 104)**
`ci-schema-parity.yml` added to `ci-parity-check`'s `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS` (`make ci-strict` already mirrors it), plus the two empty fixture stubs the parity integration tests require (they read every enforcing workflow from the fixture trees).

## Why bun, not node
The walker imports `.ts` at runtime, so it needs a TS-capable runtime (`pnpm`/`npm` are package managers, not runtimes). `node --experimental-strip-types` would work, but bun was chosen deliberately: ~4–12 ms startup vs node's ~60–120 ms for a script a gate runs on many PRs, native `.ts`, and Makefile-identical command (spec 104). See spec 191 §3.

## Verification
- `ci-parity-check` — **OK, 12 enforcing workflows mirrored**; `cargo test` **3/3 pass** (incl. enforcing/coverage disjointness)
- `workflow-pins` (spec 158) — **pass** on the new workflow
- `make ci-schema-parity` — **green** (envelope-version OK v=2, knowledge OK, provenance/stakeholder reserved)
- spec-code coupling gate — **OK, 8 paths**
- registry compiles; `spec-lint` exit 0; codebase index fresh; featuregraph golden refreshed

title: spec(190): fix ci.yml desktop paths-filter stranded by the #178 rename
body:
## Summary

A one-line routing fix that restores a **silently-dark CI gate**. The spec-177 orchestrator (`ci.yml`) routes the desktop PR gate (check + clippy + test) behind a `dorny/paths-filter` glob that still names `product/apps/desktop/**` — the directory **spec 178 renamed to `product/apps/opc/`**. So a PR that changes only the desktop app does **not** match the `desktop` filter, the job is skipped, and the aggregator treats skipped as success — the gate is absent without anyone noticing.

It fired at all only via the filter's other glob, `crates/**`. That's exactly how the regression surfaced in this very chain of PRs:

- **#257** changed `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/**` (no `crates/`) → `desktop` **skipped** → a `clippy::collapsible_match` violation merged uncaught.
- **#258** changed `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/**` → `desktop` **ran** (via `crates/**`) → caught the lint #257 introduced.

A gate that skips on PRs touching its *own* code but runs on PRs touching *other* areas is worse than no gate — it reads green-by-coverage while the guarded code goes unchecked.

## Fix

```diff
 desktop:
-  - 'product/apps/desktop/**'
+  - 'product/apps/opc/**'
   - 'crates/**'
   - 'product/packages/**'
   - '.github/workflows/ci-desktop.yml'
```

`ci-desktop.yml`'s body already operates on `product/apps/opc/**`; only the router glob lagged. This is the **only** stranded `product/apps/desktop` reference in `.github/workflows/` (the other tracked hits are spec 178's title in the featuregraph golden and two cosmetic doc/comment strings in the `opc` tree — neither affects routing).

## Verification
- `ci-parity-check` (spec 104) — **OK** (this changes a `filters:` glob, not a `run:` block, so the Makefile↔CI run-mirror is untouched)
- spec-code coupling gate — **OK, 4 paths** (`ci.yml` via 190 `refines` 177; golden via `extends` 034; spec established; index)
- registry compiles; `spec-lint` exit 0; codebase index fresh; featuregraph golden refreshed

## Scope
Just the desktop routing glob. Wiring `make ci-schema-parity` as its own CI job is a separate, larger follow-up (introduces a TS-capable runtime to CI) — tracked next.

## Test plan
After merge, the next desktop-only PR (changes confined to `product/apps/opc/**`) should route `desktop == true` and run the gate, rather than skipping it.

title: spec(189): restore schema-parity gate + add envelope-version parity tripwire
body:
## Summary

The named follow-up to spec 183 (PR #257): the protocol-wide duplex envelope version had **no automated cross-language parity check**, which is why it drifted silently (desktop pinned to v1 while spec 119 moved the server to v2) until spec 183's boot gate surfaced it. This adds that tripwire — and, in the process, restores the schema-parity gate it extends, which turned out to have been **silently non-functional** for a while.

## Part 1 — restore the schema-parity walker (§3.0)

`tools/oap/schema-parity-check/index.mjs` had two stale path assumptions, each from a repo-wide move the walker wasn't updated for. Either one made it `exit 2` ("fingerprint not found") before comparing anything:

1. **`REPO_ROOT` climbed `..,..`** (two levels) but the tool now sits three deep at `tools/oap/schema-parity-check/` since commit #176 ("cut-d cleanup: spec-spine crate split"). It resolved every path under `tools/`. → climb `..,..,..`.
2. **It read fingerprints from `build/schema-parity/`**, but the Rust emitters (`crates/factory-contracts`) write to `.derived/schema-parity/` after the `build/`→`.derived/` migration. → read `.derived/`.

Added a **loud `REPO_ROOT` guard**: it asserts `crates/factory-contracts` + `platform/services/stagecraft` exist under the resolved root and `exit 2`s with a clear "REPO_ROOT does not resolve to the repo root" message otherwise — so a future relocation fails loudly instead of silently re-darkening the gate (the exact failure mode here).

With both fixed, the gate runs **green end-to-end**: `knowledge` parity passes (no accumulated drift), provenance/stakeholder stay in their spec-121/122 reserved mode.

## Part 2 — envelope-version scalar parity (§3.1–3.3)

- `envelope-version.mjs` — dependency-free pure helpers that read `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` from the desktop Rust (`sync_client.rs`) and server TS (`types.ts`) with anchored patterns and compare them. Source-read (not import) keeps it stable under Encore's TS parser, consistent with spec 125's design. Throws (loud) on a missing or duplicated constant so a rename can't silently pass.
- Wired into the walker as the **first, import-independent** check.
- `envelope-version.test.mjs` — 8 cases: equal/unequal, type-alias-vs-const, comment-vs-const, `u8`/`u16`, absent, duplicate.

## Why a scalar check rather than the fingerprint pattern

The per-contract checks emit a Rust fingerprint via `cargo test` in `factory-contracts`. The envelope version is a scalar that lives in the **desktop** crate — reusing that pattern would compile the large Tauri crate in the parity job just to read one integer, and widen Makefile co-authority. A source-read comparison needs no build step, no import, and no new Makefile/CI step — it runs inside the existing `bun run …/index.mjs`.

## Verification
- `node tools/oap/schema-parity-check/envelope-version.test.mjs` — **8 passed**
- `make ci-schema-parity` — **exit 0**: `envelope-version OK (v=2)`, `knowledge OK`, provenance/stakeholder reserved
- root guard fires `exit 2` on a wrong root
- spec registry compiles (189 valid); `spec-lint` exit 0; codebase index fresh; featuregraph golden refreshed
- spec-code coupling gate vs `origin/main` — **OK, 6 paths**

## Test plan for reviewers
`make ci-schema-parity` → green. To see the tripwire bite: set the desktop `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to a value ≠ the server's and re-run → `exit 1` naming both files and versions.


---

Spec-Drift-Waiver: clippy-only fix (collapsible_match → match guard) to product/apps/opc/src-tauri/src/sidecars.rs — a #257 leftover surfaced by #258's now-running desktop clippy job (which skipped on #257). Pure lint refactor, no behaviour and no spec-183 contract change, so spec 183 is not edited.

title: fix(opc): unblock boot gate — sidecar data-dir + envelope v2 parity (spec 183)
body:
## Summary

Two independent **spec 183** boot-gate preconditions could never go green in a Finder-launched release build (OPC 0.3.4), so the cockpit was permanently stuck on **"Preparing OPC"** — Sidecar *not ready* and Stagecraft *not ready*. This fixes both and amends spec 183 to record the preconditions its gate implicitly depends on.

## Root causes

### 1. Sidecar `axiomregent` exits `code 1` (FR-T1)
`spawn_axiomregent` inherited OPC's working directory, which is `/` for a Finder-launched `.app`. axiomregent's default hiqlite store is `<cwd>/.axiomregent/data` (`crates/axiomregent/src/config/mod.rs`), so under `/` it was unwritable, `init_hiqlite` returned `Err`, and the process exited **1 before binding its probe port** — so FR-T1(b)'s TCP liveness probe could never succeed. The cause was invisible because the spawn loop scanned stderr only for the `OPC_AXIOMREGENT_PORT=` line and **discarded everything else**, collapsing the failure to an opaque `terminated code 1`.

**Fix:** pin `AXIOMREGENT_DATA_DIR` to the app-data dir + a writable cwd on the spawned child, and log the sidecar's stderr.

### 2. Stagecraft duplex never completes the handshake (FR-T2(b))
The desktop's `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` was `1`, but the server moved to **v2 in spec 119** (collapsing the session key from `workspaceId` to `orgId`). `is_server_envelope`'s strict-equality guard rejected every server frame — including `sync.hello` — so the gate-flip (`mark_sync_hello_received`) never fired, even on a fully authenticated, connected socket. The log signature was:

```
sync_client: rejected envelope with unknown kind or bad schema: kind=sync.hello v=2
```

The desktop already carried the v2 **struct shapes** (`ServerMeta.org_cursor` / `org_id`) — only the version constant lagged. This was silent before spec 183; the boot gate turned the latent skew into a hard block.

**Fix:** bump `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` `1 → 2`; align the version-pinned tests (raw-JSON fixtures, accept-loops, outbound-frame asserts) to the constant; invert `rejects_wrong_schema_version` to reject the retired v1.

## Spec changes (spec 183)
- **§2** — note that the sidecar launcher pins a writable data/working dir + surfaces stderr, and that `sync_client.rs`'s `ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` must equal the server's.
- **§3.1 FR-T1 launch environment (binding)** — the gate observes liveness; it can't manufacture it, so the launch environment (writable data dir + surfaced stderr) is part of the contract.
- **§3.2 FR-T2(b) envelope-version parity (binding)** — `sync.hello` receipt presupposes the desktop *accepts* the frame; version parity with the deployed server is a precondition of the gate-flip.

## Verification
- `cargo check --lib --tests` (opc) — exit 0, no warnings
- **35 unit tests pass** (`sync_client`, `sidecars`), incl. `dispatch_sync_hello_envelope_flips_observer_flag` (the v=2 gate-flip path)
- spec-code coupling gate vs `origin/main` — **OK, 4 paths**
- codebase index regenerated; spec registry undrifted

## Known gap (follow-up)
There is **no automated cross-language parity check** on the protocol-wide envelope version (unlike the per-kind mirror constants, which fail at Rust build time). That's why this drifted silently from spec 119 until the gate exposed it. Wiring it into the schema-parity walker (spec 125) is a sensible follow-up.

## Test plan for reviewers
`make dev` on this branch → boot gate should clear both Sidecar and Stagecraft preconditions against `stagecraft.ing` and render the cockpit.

title: spec(188): one-command merge-driver enabler for multi-clone setup
body:
Follow-up to #255 (merged). The `oap-index-regen` merge driver from #255 needs a per-clone `git config` registration (it can't be committed, since it lives in `.git/config`). With multiple clones on one machine, two copy-paste commands per clone is friction.

## What
- Adds **`.githooks/enable-merge-driver.sh`** — idempotent, resolves repo root, registers the driver, and prints the verified `path → driver` chain. One command per clone.
- Spec 188 **FR-003** now requires the enabler; `establishes` it.
- `CLAUDE.md` documents running it once per clone (worktrees inherit it).

Stays consistent with the project's opt-in posture (FR-003 + the pre-commit hook precedent) — this makes enabling easy, it does not turn the driver on by default.

## Usage
```bash
./.githooks/enable-merge-driver.sh   # run once in each clone
```

## Verification (local, base = merged main)
- `codebase-indexer check` ✓ · `spec-lint` ✓ · featuregraph golden ✓ · `spec-code-coupling` OK (5 paths) ✓
- enabler runs idempotently; no duplicate spec ids in the corpus ✓

## Not included
Merge-queue / post-merge-heal (spec 188 Phases 2–3) remain designed-only, gated on the spec-184 tension.

title: spec(188): derived-index merge driver + fix duplicate spec id 186
body:
## What & why

Two coupled changes that came out of investigating multi-agent PR/merge friction.

### 1. Spec 188 — derived-index merge serialization (Phase 1 implemented)

The friction reduces to **one** serialization point: the single committed derived artifact `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` carries a global content hash, and `ci-codebase-index` requires it byte-fresh on every PR — so each merge to `main` forces every other open PR to rebase + regenerate it. (The coupling gate is *already* ephemeral — `ci-spec-code-coupling.yml` recompiles the index — so it was never part of the problem.)

**Phase 1 (this PR):** an opt-in `oap-index-regen` git merge driver (`.githooks/merge-derived-index.sh` + `.gitattributes`) that auto-regenerates the index from the merged tree on conflict, dropping per-rebase toil to zero. Fails closed if the indexer isn't built; CI's `codebase-indexer check` stays the source of truth. Registration is opt-in per clone (documented in `CLAUDE.md`); worktrees inherit it, so it covers agent worktrees.

**Phases 2 (GitHub merge queue) & 3 (post-merge index heal): designed, NOT implemented.** Phase 3 is explicitly gated on the **spec-184 PR-time-blocking tension** — spec 184 (one week old) made `.claude/settings.json` / `.mcp.json` edits block at PR time, and Phase 3 would move that enforcement post-merge. The spec records the trade and two non-destructive resolutions; nothing in spec 184's contract is inverted here.

### 2. Fix duplicate spec id 186

Surfaced while authoring 188: PRs #245 and #246 both allocated id 186 (the spec-compiler keys on directory slug, so it never hard-failed — a silent logical divergence no per-PR gate caught).

- **Keeps** `186-sandbox-k8s-backend` — approved, code landed (`crates/sandbox-k8s`, 12 files), sibling of `185-sandbox-local-container-backend`.
- **Renumbers** the draft `186-opc-e2e-test-harness` → **187** (zero code references; lowest blast radius).
- New spec takes **188**.

This collision is now cited in spec 188 as concrete evidence for the Phase 2 merge queue.

## Verification (local)

- `spec-compiler compile` ✓ · `codebase-indexer check` ✓ · `spec-lint` ✓
- featuregraph golden (regenerated, clean compare) ✓
- `spec-code-coupling` — OK, 7 paths ✓
- No duplicate numeric spec ids remain ✓
- Merge driver exercised directly: happy path clears conflict markers (exit 0), fail-closed leaves the conflict (exit 1).

## Not included
Merge-queue (`merge_group:`) wiring and the post-merge heal job — they are designed in spec 188 Phases 2–3 and will land in their own changes, Phase 2 after Phase 3, Phase 3 after the spec-184 tension is decided.

Updates the requirements on [rusqlite](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from rusqlite's releases.

0.39.0

What's Changed

  • Fix constraints on VTab Aux data #1778, #1771
  • Fix docs.rs generation #1779
  • Fix a small typo in rollback_hook docstring #1780
  • Fix some warnings from Intellij #1781
  • Minimal doc for features #1783
  • Clear hooks only for owning connections #1785, #1784
  • Fix link to SQLite C Interface, Prepare Flags #1787
  • Comment functions which are not usable from a loadable extension #1789
  • Factorize code #1792
  • Update getrandom to 0.4 #1798
  • Update Cargo.toml #1800
  • Fix appveyor #1807
  • Add support to unix timestamp for chrono, jiff and time #1808, #1803
  • fix(trace): check that the sql string pointer is not NULL #1805
  • Bump bundled SQLite version to 3.51.3 #1818
  • Use TryFrom for Value #1819, #1817
  • Make possible to pass your own pointers #1626, #1602

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/compare/v0.38.0...v0.39.0

Changelog

Sourced from rusqlite's changelog.

For version 0.15.0 and above, see Releases page.

Version 0.14.0 (2018-08-17)

  • BREAKING CHANGE: ToSql implementation for time::Timespec uses RFC 3339 (%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ). Previous format was %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S:%f %Z.
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Remove potentially conflicting impl of ToSqlOutput (#313).
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Replace column index/count type (i32) with usize.
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Replace parameter index/count type (i32) with usize.
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Replace row changes/count type (i32) with usize.
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Scalar functions must be Sendable and 'static.
  • Bugfix: Commit failure unhandled, database left in unusable state (#366).
  • Bugfix: free_boxed_hook does not work for fn.
  • Update the bundled SQLite version to 3.24.0 (#326).
  • Add DropBehavior::Panic to enforce intentional commit or rollback.
  • Implement sqlite3_update_hook (#260, #328), sqlite3_commit_hook and sqlite3_rollback_hook.
  • Add support to unlock notification behind unlock_notify feature (#294, #331).
  • Make Statement::column_index case-insensitive (#330).
  • Add comment to justify &mut Connection in Transaction.
  • Fix tyvar_behind_raw_pointer warnings.
  • Fix handful of clippy warnings.
  • Fix Connection::open documentation (#332)
  • Add binding to sqlite3_get_autocommit and sqlite3_stmt_busy.
  • Add binding to sqlite3_busy_timeout and sqlite3_busy_handler.
  • Add binding to sqlite3_expanded_sql.
  • Use rerun-if-env-changed in libsqlite3-sys (#329).
  • Return an InvalidQuery error when SQL is not read only.

Version 0.13.0 (2017-11-13)

  • Added ToSqlConversionFailure case to Error enum.
  • Now depends on chrono 0.4, bitflags 1.0, and (optionally) cc 1.0 / bindgen 0.31.
  • The ToSql/FromSql implementations for time::Timespec now include and expect fractional seconds and timezone in the serialized string.
  • The RowIndex type used in Row::get is now publicly exported.
  • New sqlcipher feature allows linking against SQLCipher instead of SQLite.
  • Doc link in README now point to docs.rs.

Version 0.12.0 (2017-05-29)

  • Defines HAVE_USLEEP when building with a bundled SQLite (#263).
  • Updates dependencies to their latest versions, particularly serde to 1.0.
  • Adds support for vcpkg on Windows.
  • Adds ToSql impls for str and [u8].

Version 0.11.0 (2017-04-06)

  • Avoid publicly exporting SQLite constants multiple times from libsqlite3-sys.
  • Adds FromSql and ToSql impls for isize. Documents why usize and u64 are not included.

## Summary

Establishes the test infrastructure that retires the nightly/manual deferral pattern from spec 183 §6 (boot-precondition-gate AC-7/8/9). Status: `draft` / `implementation: pending` — this PR lands the spec only, not the implementation.

### What the harness binds (FR-T1..FR-T7)

| FR | Invariant | Why |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Drives a *built* OPC binary (not mocked Tauri) | Only a real build exercises App.tsx's conditional render boundary |
| T2 | Mock-stagecraft duplex server with 4 modes (healthy / network-unreachable / handshake-rejects / mid-session-drop) | AC-7-class "substrate-unavailable" cases must be deterministic |
| T3 | Platform-portable process-tree introspection | AC-9-class "no orphan sidecar" assertions need uniform `pgrep`-equivalent |
| T4 | Time-bounded UI-state assertions via `wait_for_subtree` | AC-8-class kill→unmount race windows |
| T5 | Nightly CI integration (NOT per-PR) | Preserves spec 134's ~5min fast-CI budget |
| T6 | No flake-amnesty (no skip-flaky flag) | Spec 116/127 precedent: gates that can be silenced erode invariants |
| T7 | Co-authority on per-AC fixtures | Harness shape must survive consumer-spec drift |

### Establishes-deferred pattern

The harness paths (`product/apps/opc/tests-e2e/`, `.github/workflows/opc-e2e-nightly.yml`) are mandated by §2 but **NOT** declared in `establishes:` because they don't exist on disk yet — spec 154 §3.5 hard-errors on missing-directory units at compile time. Matches spec 180's benches/ precedent: a follow-up frontmatter amendment lands `establishes:` alongside the directory creation at implementation time.

### Acceptance scope (per-PR vs. post-impl)

- **Per-PR (this PR):** AC-1..AC-4 — frontmatter shape, spec-lint, pr-prep, by-authority post-establishes (footnoted for the deferred path).
- **Post-implementation:** AC-5..AC-9 — gate the harness's `implementation: complete` flip, not this spec's `status: approved` flip.

### Why a separate PR from #244

Different concern. #244 closed spec 183's per-PR ACs and flipped lifecycle. This spec is a `kind: capability` draft that documents how spec 183 (and future deferred-AC specs) get their end-to-end coverage. Bundling would have muddied #244's reviewable surface.

- `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` regenerates with new feature nodes touching authority specs (034, 154, 156, 161, 167, 168, 169, 183). This is the documented featuregraph-golden-on-spec-add pattern — none of those authority specs need behavioural changes; the golden bump is the artifact of adding spec 186 to the corpus.
- `deny.toml` gains four `RUSTSEC` ignore entries for kube-client 0.95 unmaintained transitives (`backoff`, `derivative`, `instant`, `rustls-pemfile`) — all maintenance-status, no CVE, no unsound. This mirrors the existing Tauri / hiqlite ignore pattern under spec 116 and matches the spec 127 FR-005 dep-refresh-waiver precedent for transitive-only adjustments. Spec 116 itself does not need to change; the new ignores follow the existing rules verbatim. Kube 3.x drops all four, filed as a follow-up under spec 186.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p sandbox-k8s` — 69 unit tests pass (admission, pod_spec, network_policy, runtime_class, descriptor, hashing, lifecycle terminal-phase harvest) + 4 integration scaffolds
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --manifest-path Cargo.toml -- -D warnings` — clean (mirrors CI's `.github/actions/rust-ci`)

landed via PR #207 and §6's done-when ("the ASI05 gap closes the
moment the contract is enforced") is satisfied.

  and tested.
- **FR-009 preserved end-to-end** — the backend is the first one
  that can *accept* work; the contract's fail-closed posture still
  fires on `Unavailable` (no socket reachable) or `AdmissionRejected`
  (egress allowlist / SandboxRuntime tier / non-empty input artifacts
  / image not resolvable).

### Six bisect-safe commits

| # | Phase | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spec draft + crate scaffolding (universally Unavailable) | 3 |
| 2 | Runtime detection — DOCKER_HOST / Podman / Docker probe | 9 |

## Summary

Closes three of the six follow-ups still listed as outstanding on spec 143 and files dispositions for the remaining three. The spec was at `implementation: in-progress` since 2026-05-07 with FU-001 through FU-024 already closed; this PR retires the remaining FU surfaces that fit a single closure PR.

### Closed in this PR

- **FU-017 — knowledge object detail-page extractor rendering.** Both legs of the three-leg done-when: quick-win (text with real newlines + raw-JSON `<details>` toggle) → typed `ExtractionView<Kind>` component covering deterministic-text / deterministic-pdf-embedded / deterministic-docx (plus a generic fallback for agent kinds). Per-kind metadata (lines/bytes/mime; pageCount; wordCount + mammothMessages count), collapsible outline tree, 5k-char text-collapse toggle, and raw-JSON toggle.
- **FU-018 — knowledge object detail-page two-column layout.** `md:grid-cols-[minmax(280px,360px)_1fr]` with sticky metadata sidebar. Outer container widened `max-w-3xl` → `max-w-7xl`.

Finding 3 (the audit step itself) is this closure entry — walks every M2M JWT validator on the platform (m2mAuth.ts, rauthy.ts, deployd-api-rs/auth.rs, plus the three consumers) and confirms every issuer derives from the OIDC discovery doc and every Rauthy-side validator accepts both RS256 and EdDSA. No latent validators surfaced. L-008 invariant satisfied platform-wide.

### Deferred with rationale notes in spec §12

- **FU-003** — Sibling spec creation (amends spec 115/087/124 with K8s CronJob templates). Crosses spec 143's authority boundary; needs its own owner-spec PR.
- **FU-008** — `setup.sh` secret-sync granularity. Stub explicitly says "Decision needed: which shape (a or b, or hybrid)." Open design question.

title: fix(opc): session/workspace bugs + spec 183 boot precondition gate
body:
## Summary

12 commits addressing eight user-reported OPC issues, two of which converged into a single load-bearing architectural piece — **spec 183 (OPC boot precondition gate)** — which is drafted and fully implemented in this PR (Stages A/B/C). The constitutional claim from spec 183 is **structurally enforced from `8fa7aa9a` forward**: OPC cannot transition out of its boot state until both the bundled axiomregent sidecar is alive AND a materialised org session is verified by stagecraft's `sync.hello` acknowledgment; and any precondition loss mid-session restores the shell to boot.

## Issues addressed

| Issue | Disposition | Commit(s) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. CLAUDE.md edit → "No Claude file ID specified" | Fixed | `23ec5f09` |
| 2. Workspace Projects stuck "Connecting to stagecraft…" | Band-aid then **architectural** | `23ec5f09` then `ec4752f8` (`project.catalog.snapshot.complete` envelope; spec 112 §8a) |
| 3a. Factory "no active organization (sign-in incomplete)" | Stopgap + constitutional fix | `f9bdad30` (sign-in CTA in PipelineSelector) — **retired by spec 183 FR-T2**, see Stage D notes |
| 3b. URL doesn't stick in factory picker | Deferred — separate component-state bug, not downstream of 3a per review | — |
| 5. Tools → CLAUDE.md always empty | Fixed | `c33c2f2e` (root-aware via `findClaudeMdFiles`) |
| 6. Bundled axiomregent probe port not announced | Stopgap + constitutional fix | `993de5ae` (auto-poll) — **retired by spec 183 FR-T1**, see Stage D notes |
| 10. Agents menu empty despite `.claude/agents/*.md` | Empty-state hint only (partial) | `c33c2f2e` |
| 12. Settings → Commands empty despite `.claude/commands/*.md` | Scope-discovery hint only (partial) | `c33c2f2e` |

**Not in this PR** — separate branches off main per agreed sequencing:
- Issue 4 (Tools-bar → composer popup)
- Issues 7/8/9 substantive fix (Semantic Search / Call Graph / Checkpoint MCP routing) — needs the `opc-mcp-stdio-router` spec drafted fresh, simplified by spec 183's hard sidecar-availability guarantee
- Issue 10 full (filesystem agent discovery from `.claude/agents/*.md`)
- Issue 13 (Settings consolidation of Agents + MCP Servers)
- Stage D strip pass (retire `f9bdad30` + `993de5ae` now that spec 183 enforces what they were patching)

## Spec work (the load-bearing piece)

**Spec 183 — `OPC boot precondition gate`** (`specs/183-opc-boot-precondition-gate/spec.md`)

The shell occupies a single observational *boot* state until two preconditions both green-light:

- **FR-T1** — sidecar liveness: `OPC_AXIOMREGENT_PORT=<n>` parsed from stderr AND a TCP-connect to `127.0.0.1:<n>` succeeds within bounded timeout. (Probe port is a diagnostic-only TCP listener in `axiomregent/src/main.rs`; MCP framing flows over stdio. TCP-connect establishment is the entire green-light contract — there is no `/health` endpoint to call.)
- **FR-T2** — org session materialised: `StagecraftState.org_id` populated AND `sync.hello` envelope received from stagecraft over the duplex stream. `sync.hello` proves the server accepted the handshake for the claimed `(clientId, orgId)` and rides the same channel every cockpit feature uses.
- **FR-T3** — observational boot state, App-level component branch (`<BootGate>` vs `<Cockpit>` conditional render in `App.tsx`), explicitly NOT a route — only an outer conditional can structurally enforce "the rest of the route tree is not observable from within boot."
- **FR-T4** — bounded explicit retry: user-initiated, no silent reconnect loop. The boot screen's periodic re-read of `boot_gate_status` is observation, not retry (long-form rationale in `BootGate.tsx`).
- **FR-T5** — precondition loss mid-session restores to boot:
  - (a) sidecar `CommandEvent::Terminated` — observed in `spawn_axiomregent`'s receiver loop
  - (b) duplex reconnect exhaustion — `DUPLEX_GIVE_UP_FAILURES = 5` consecutive failures in `run_forever`, emits + resets `sync_hello_received`
  - (c) `auth_logout` cleared org session
- **FR-T6** — Quit tears down spawned sidecars before exit. `quit_opc` takes the retained `CommandChild`, calls `kill()`, then `app.exit(0)`.

**Non-goals (binding):** no offline mode, no sidecar-optional mode, no "skip for now" bypass, no per-feature degraded paths, no silent boot retry. A change that contradicts any amends the corresponding invariant rather than landing as a flag.

**Spec 112 amendment** — §7 + §8a document the new `project.catalog.snapshot.complete` envelope as a backward-compatible Phase 8a extension.

**Spec 180** — small §8 future-work pointer addition `[[opc-boot-precondition-gate]]` only; no body or invariant changes.

## Implementation stages

| Stage | Commits | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| A | `fd0092e3` | Rust observability scaffolding: `boot_gate_status`, `check_axiomregent_alive`, `sync_hello_received` on `SyncClientInner` |
| B | `8fa7aa9a` | `<BootGate>` component + `App.tsx` conditional render + `quit_opc` Tauri command |
| C1 | `b325c9c3` | Sidecar `CommandChild` retention + `Terminated` observer + Quit teardown wiring |
| C2 | `9554fba3` | Duplex give-up signal + `reset_sync_hello_received` + org-id-cleared observer (FR-T5(b)+(c)) |
| C3 | `16ea30c1` | `App.tsx` `boot-gate-precondition-lost` listener + polling-vs-retry rationale in `BootGate.tsx` |

## What's deliberately not in this PR

Per agreed sequencing, AC tests are open against intentional non-implementation:

- **AC-5** (FR-T1 port-but-no-listener fixture test) — Rust unit test, deferred
- **AC-6** (FR-T2 `sync.hello` observability test) — Rust unit test, deferred
- **AC-7** (cockpit MUST NOT appear with sidecar+no-stagecraft) — e2e; **structurally satisfied** by `App.tsx`'s `bootGateOpen` branch gating on `sidecar_alive && org_session_ready`
- **AC-8** (cockpit unmounts on sidecar kill within ~2s) — e2e; **structurally satisfied** by FR-T5(a) emit + `App.tsx` listener
- **AC-9** (Quit leaves no axiomregent process) — e2e; **structurally satisfied** by `quit_opc`'s `kill()` + `app.exit(0)` order

The structural satisfaction is the contract; the e2e harness is the proof. Reading the commit count as "spec 183 done" overshoots — Stage D strip + AC harness are still real work items.

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: This PR is a coherent unit of spec-183-scoped work plus a handful of user-reported bug fixes whose authority claims sit under spec 180's broad OPC shell authority (commits `23ec5f09`, `f9bdad30`, `c33c2f2e`, `993de5ae`) and spec 112's protocol contract (`ec4752f8`). The spec amendments land first (`3ed0c737`, `4ae25026`, plus spec 112 §8a in `ec4752f8`); the implementation refines code paths under each spec's `refines:` edges (App.tsx, sidecars.rs, sync_client.rs, stagecraft_client.rs, AuthContext.tsx). No documented invariant in any upstream authority spec is contradicted — the stopgap commits `f9bdad30` and `993de5ae` are intentional graceful-degradation safety nets explicitly named in spec 183 §3.2 and §3.4 rationale, and Stage D of the spec 183 implementation (a follow-up branch) will retire them under FR-T1 / FR-T2's harder guarantees.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make pr-prep` against `origin/main` passes the coupling gate (waiver above) and codebase index check
- [ ] Manual: launch OPC with stagecraft unreachable → BootGate renders, cockpit does NOT mount (AC-7)
- [ ] Manual: launch OPC, sign in, reach cockpit → kill axiomregent externally → cockpit unmounts, BootGate re-mounts within ~2s (AC-8)
- [ ] Manual: launch OPC, sign in, reach cockpit → click Quit from boot → confirm no `axiomregent` process via `pgrep axiomregent` (AC-9)
- [ ] Manual: factory pipeline tab still works for a signed-in user with an org that has projects (regression check for `f9bdad30` retained behaviour)
- [ ] Manual: opening the Workspace Projects panel against an org with zero projects shows the empty state (not the spinner) within 1s of `sync.hello` (regression check for the `ec4752f8` envelope)
- [ ] Cargo tests pass: `cargo test --manifest-path product/apps/opc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib commands::project_catalog_sync commands::sync_client`

title: chore(claude): tighten settings.json permissions + wire staleness hooks
body:
## Summary

PR 3 (final operational PR) of the Claude-directory-modernization rollout. Tightens `.claude/settings.json` permissions from wildcards to explicit narrow patterns + a load-bearing deny list. Wires PostToolUse + Stop hooks for codebase-indexer staleness gating.

Lands under spec 184's draft authority (spec 184 in PR #233). Spec 184's "Retroactive authority over existing reality" section explicitly takes the post-PR-3 settings.json content as the baseline — meaning this PR's diff defines what spec 184 governs going forward.

## Permissions

Replaced `Bash(*:*)` + `Bash(**)` wildcards with ~75 explicit patterns enumerated from the actual command surface in Makefile + cargo/git/gh/npm subcommands + tool binary paths + standard shell utilities. Tool-path globs use explicit-chain form (`./tools/spec-spine/*/target/release/*`) to remove single-vs-any-segment ambiguity in Claude Code's permission glob semantics.

## Deny list

Load-bearing safety net per spec 184's framing:
- Tree destruction (`rm -rf *`, `sudo *`)
- Git destruction (`--force *`, `--force-with-lease *`, `--mirror *`, `--delete *`, `reset --hard *`, `clean -f*`, `branch -D *`, `worktree remove --force*`)
- Remote-branch delete via colon-form (narrow patterns: `origin :*`, `upstream :*`, `* :HEAD*`, `* :refs/*` — preserves legitimate `local:remote` refspec pushes)
- Publication/release (`cargo publish*`, `npm publish*`, `gh release create/delete/upload/edit *`, `gh repo delete/archive *`)

## Hooks

**PostToolUse** on Edit|Write: runs the codebase-indexer staleness check only when the touched path is in the indexer's hashed input set. Implementation:
- jq install guard with explicit `[hook] jq missing` signal
- POSIX `case` matching against absolute paths (every relative-rooted pattern prefixed with `*/`)
- 12 glob classes verified empirically against 16 representative paths (12 expected matches + 4 negatives all behave correctly)

**Stop** hook: runs the same check at conversation end, emits `[codebase-index] stale - run: make index` on staleness.

## Known gaps preserved

Per spec 184's "Known gaps in the baseline" section, the following remain at their pre-PR wildcards as the accepted current safety posture; tightening is governed by follow-up specs:

- File-tool wildcards: `Read(**)`, `Edit(**)`, `Write(**)`, `MultiEdit(**)`
- MCP catch-all: `mcp__*`
- Subagent catch-all: `Agent(*)`

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Fresh-session permission-prompt test: invoke `./tools/spec-spine/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer check` and verify no permission prompt fires (matches `Bash(./tools/spec-spine/*/target/release/*)`)
- [ ] PostToolUse hook fires correctly: edit `specs/<some>/spec.md`, observe `[codebase-index]` advisory output
- [ ] PostToolUse hook does NOT fire on README.md edits (negative test)
- [ ] Stop hook surfaces staleness when applicable

## Sequencing

This is the third (final operational) PR. Depends on:
- PR #232 — agent memory + path-scoped rules (merge-independent)
- PR #233 — spec 184 draft (recommended to land first, but technically settings.json edits aren't blocked since spec 184 is `status: draft` and takes effect at promote-to-approved)

If PR 4 (deletion of `.claude/commands/`) lands later per spec 182's deprecation plan, no further settings.json changes are needed.

## Summary

PR 2 of the four-PR Claude-directory-modernization rollout. Lands two **draft** specs plus the files they `establishes:`, satisfying the codebase-indexer's I-007/I-008 gates ("established paths must exist on disk").

Two independent draft specs on one branch for landing efficiency. If approval timelines diverge, the branch can be split into two PRs on request — neither spec implements anything load-bearing in this PR (just file scaffolding).

## Spec 182 — claude-skills-migration

Migrates `.claude/commands/` to `.claude/skills/`. **AGENTS.md preserved unchanged** as the cross-agent protocol body (per the AAIF / Linux Foundation AGENTS.md standard read by Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Copilot). `skills/init/SKILL.md` is a thin Claude-Code-specific dispatcher that reads AGENTS.md.

Spec details:
- AC-9 uses a structured-manifest equivalence check (not byte-identical transcript), with deterministic extraction rules to prevent spurious divergence
- AC-3 includes concrete falsifiable negative checks for the init dispatcher (line count < 30, no protocol-body phrases, must reference AGENTS.md)
- Two-PR migration plan: PR 2 (this) lands skills; deprecation PR later deletes `.claude/commands/`

## Spec 184 — claude-shared-config-governance

Brings `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.json` into the indexer's hashed input set so quiet edits trip the staleness gate. Closes the self-governance gap where the PostToolUse hook glob in settings.json guards other hashed inputs but isn't itself governed.

Spec details:
- Explicit "Retroactive authority over existing reality" section — current contents become baseline at promote-to-approved
- AC-7 honest about scope: "self-governance loop made VISIBLE, NOT closed" (hashing reveals edits in diff; reviewer must judge whether they narrow or broaden)
- "Known gaps in the baseline" enumerates accepted safety-posture choices (`Read(**)` / `Edit(**)` / `Write(**)` wildcards, `mcp__*` catch-all, `Agent(*)` unbounded) deferred to follow-up specs
- "Follow-up tooling" names permission-smoke-test (with execution-surface caveat) and structural hook-glob lint

## What this PR contains

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `specs/182-claude-skills-migration/spec.md` | Spec 182 draft |
| `specs/184-claude-shared-config-governance/spec.md` | Spec 184 draft |
| `.claude/skills/<10 dirs>/SKILL.md` | 10 skill files. 9 are byte-for-byte copies of `commands/<n>.md`; `init/SKILL.md` is the thin dispatcher (24 lines) |
| `specs/182-claude-skills-migration/baseline-init.txt` | Placeholder per AC-9; actual capture happens at promote-to-approved |
| `.mcp.json` | Wires `axiomregent` as team-shared MCP server. Build prereq: `make axiomregent` |
| `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` | Regenerated for the new spec files |

## Deferred to later PRs

- **PR 3** — `.claude/settings.json` hardening (lands under spec 184 authority)
- **Implementation PR** — Spec 101 + 071 amendments + indexer source change to hash `.claude/skills/`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`
- **Deprecation PR** — delete `.claude/commands/` after transition window

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green: `ci-fast-spec-coupling`, `ci-fast-tools`, `ci-rust`
- [ ] `codebase-indexer check` exits 0; no I-007 (directory missing) or I-008 (file missing) diagnostics
- [ ] Spec-lint passes on both new spec files
- [ ] `/init` in a fresh Claude Code session resolves to `skills/init/SKILL.md` (skill > command precedence), dispatcher reads AGENTS.md correctly
- [ ] Manual verify: each of the 9 non-init skills (`/setup`, `/commit`, `/code-review`, etc.) produces the same prompt as their legacy `commands/<n>.md` counterpart

---

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` regeneration is a mechanical consequence of adding two new draft specs (182, 184) to the spec corpus. The golden's authority specs (034-featuregraph-registry-scanner-fix, 154-logical-unit-ownership-grammar, 156-references-edge-provenance-grammar, 161-knowledge-requirements-provenance-emission, 167-born-with-spec-spine-kernel, 168-per-project-governance-certificate, 169-tool-schema-strictness) govern featuregraph's *behavior* and *contract*, not the golden's *content* for any given spec corpus. The golden file is a fixture that re-derives deterministically from the registry; its diff here is an output-side regeneration via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p featuregraph test_golden_graph`. No behavioral change to featuregraph, no authority-spec edits required.

title: spec(180): OPC shell codification
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 codification of the OPC desktop shell per the `/tmp/handoffs/opc-spine-seam-fix-2026-05-23/` handoff. Closes the spec/code authority seam Phase 0 surfaced (whole subsystem trees of the OPC desktop returned empty from `registry-consumer by-authority`).

**Posture (per user's `phase-0-resolutions.md`):** broad authority via `establishes:` on the enumerated un-bound subsystem roots; narrow Tier 1 invariants only on the bug-adjacent surface (tab-list reconciliation + filesystem-scanning IPC handlers); Tier 2 bench-presence + relative-regression gate (inaugural, not extensional); Tier 3 absolute latency budgets explicitly excluded.

## Tier-by-tier contract

### Tier 1 — Structural invariants (FR-T1..T7)

- **FR-T1.** Tab-list rendering must not wrap mapped panel children in `<AnimatePresence mode="wait">`; exit animation must be local to the closing panel.
- **FR-T2.** Per-tab list children must be `React.memo`'d with comparator on at minimum `tab.id` and the active marker.
- **FR-T3.** `TabContext.tsx` / `useTabState.ts` must not trigger remount of unaffected sibling panels on per-panel state change.
- **FR-T4.** Filesystem-scanning Tauri handlers under `src-tauri/src/commands/` must be `pub async fn` with blocking work via `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- **FR-T5.** Handlers aggregating from many filesystem inputs must consult a process-lifetime cache keyed by file path with mtime as freshness marker.
- **FR-T6.** No redundant read-passes over the same file per invocation.
- **FR-T7.** Cache registered as Tauri managed state at app init (transitive from FR-T5).

### Tier 2 — Bench-presence + relative regression (FR-T8..T10)

- Criterion benches under `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/benches/` for every filesystem-scanning handler.
- CI-gated at >25% relative regression vs `main` baseline (amendable via spec amendment).
- N=200 per-PR, N=2000 nightly.
- Wired as a `workflow_call:` reusable workflow dispatched from spec 177's `ci.yml`, not as a new top-level workflow.
- Operational ownership: OPC subsystem maintainer (§6).

### Tier 3 — Absolute latency budgets explicitly excluded (§4)

## Composition

- `refines:` 172 on three tab-system files (aspect: `tab-list-reconciliation-discipline`; `refines_specs: ["172-opc-live-agent-session-introspection"]` for bidirectional discoverability via `registry-consumer show-relationships`).
- `references:` 165 (parallel-claim; explicit non-displacement note).
- No `co_authority:` declarations (future-work pointer `[[opc-tab-system-co-authority]]`).
- No manifest `oap.spec` displacement: spec 032 stays product-consolidation owner; spec 180 is governance overlay (§10).

## Mechanical amendment

- `amends: ["034-featuregraph-registry-scanner-fix"]` declared per spec 178's encoded discipline. Receipt note added to spec 034's "Amendments received" section. Fixture refresh (featuregraph golden + codebase-index) carries inside this PR per spec 177's atomicity contract.

## Substrate finding surfaced (tracked as future-work pointer)

- `[[registry-consumer-unit-grammar-authority]]` — `authority_for_path` doesn't consume the spec 154 unit grammar. **PRs #227 + #228** (stacked) close this gap; after those merge, AC-4's "registry holds the claim" disclaimer in this spec tightens via a trivial follow-up commit to "by-authority resolves substantively."

## Test plan

- [x] `make pr-prep` clean (4 diff paths, coupling gate OK).
- [x] `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` exits 0 (no V-020 firing; no warning-tier regressions).
- [x] `featuregraph-golden` regenerated to include spec 180's row.
- [x] `registry-consumer show 180-opc-shell-codification --json` returns expected establishes / refines / references graph.
