title: spec(154): resolver honors committed .gitignore in §3.7 walk
body:
## Summary

- Amend spec 154 §3.7 to add a `.gitignore`-honoring clause on top of the baseline exclusion floor. The resolver now uses `ignore::WalkBuilder` configured with `git_ignore(true).git_exclude(false).git_global(false)`, so the walk is driven by committed-tree state only. Per-clone (`.git/info/exclude`) and per-user (`core.excludesFile`) sources are deliberately NOT honored — keeping resolution deterministic across machines.
- Fix the `.gitignore` `Cargo.lock` negation that went stale in PR #224 (`apps/desktop → product/apps/opc` rename) so the (tracked) opc lockfile isn't dropped from `kind: crate` location lists.

## Why

`.derived/codebase-index/index.json` was being regenerated on every fresh `make setup`, surfacing as a spurious 122-line diff in `git status`. Root cause: the prior `walkdir`-based resolver indexed every file on disk regardless of `.gitignore`, so the committed `index.json` captured whatever cruft happened to be sitting in the committer's working tree — macOS `.DS_Store` files, fetched `axiomregent-*` sidecar binary, Tauri-generated `gen/schemas/*.json`. A new clone (or any machine without that cruft) regenerated a smaller index, producing the diff.

§3.7 was a closed contract that listed only six baseline globs. Adding `.gitignore` honoring is an amendment to that contract — surfaced and resolved per CONST-005 before touching the resolver. The §3.7 amendment is the spec spine refinement; this PR carries both the spec edit and the matching code change in one commit.

## Verification

- `cargo test --release` on codebase-indexer: 22 resolver tests, schema-conformance, spec156-provenance all pass
- `cargo test --release` on spec-code-coupling-check: 9 pass / 1 ignored
- `codebase-indexer check`: exit 0 (idempotent — second `compile` produces no further diff)
- `spec-code-coupling-check --base origin/main`: OK, 0 paths
- `spec-lint` (full corpus): exit 0
- `spec-compiler compile`: exit 0
- Re-run `codebase-indexer compile` on this branch: drops only 14 truly-gitignored entries (`.DS_Store` ×7, `axiomregent-aarch64-apple-darwin`, `gen/schemas/*.json` ×4, `CODEBASE-INDEX.md`, platform's `.env.example`). Zero false drops. Cargo.lock for `product/apps/opc/src-tauri/` correctly preserved after the negation fix.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green across rust / tools / desktop / spec-coupling / supply-chain / schema-parity
- [ ] Reviewer confirms §3.7 amendment language matches intent (committed `.gitignore` only; per-clone and per-user sources excluded by configuration)
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the spec edit was made in-place rather than as a separate amender spec (the §3.7 contract authorizes additions "by spec amendment to this section" — interpreted as the section edit itself)
- [ ] `make setup` from a fresh clone leaves `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` clean in `git status`

## Notes

- `platform/.gitignore` excludes `.env.example` via `.env*` with no negation. The file dropped from the index. Not touched here — that file is subtree-imported from `stagecraft-ing/platform` per `platform/CLAUDE.md`. If you want it indexed, the fix belongs upstream.
- The symbol/module index walks (`resolver/symbol_index.rs`, `resolver/module_index.rs`) still use `walkdir`. They scan `.rs` files inside already-resolved crate dirs, so the leakage surface is much smaller. Flagged as a possible follow-up — not done here since it'd expand §3.7's scope to non-resolver walks.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Mechanical cleanup adjacent to §3.7 amendment.
Makefile: reorder fetch-axiomregent before codebase-indexer compile
so the binary is present when the resolver walks (setup-ordering
bug fix, no contract change). tools/shared/spec-types/src/lib.rs:
RESOLVER_EXCLUSIONS docstring pointer update to amended §3.7 text.

title: spec(177): collapse PR-gate workflow fleet behind single ci-gate
body:
## Summary

- New orchestrator `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the single PR-time entry point. Routes via `dorny/paths-filter@v4.0.1` (SHA-pinned per spec 158) and aggregates results in a `ci-gate` job.
- 14 underlying workflows (`ci-*.yml` + `spec-conformance.yml`) converted to `on: workflow_call:`. `workflow_dispatch:` preserved everywhere; `schedule:` retained on `ci-supply-chain.yml` so the Monday advisory-db refresh fires independent of PR activity.
- Constitutional carve-out per spec 177 §2.2 — `spec-conformance`, `ci-spec-code-coupling`, `ci-supply-chain`, `ci-codebase-index` run unconditionally on PRs regardless of paths.
- `ci-spec-code-coupling` is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` because spec 127 reads PR base/head SHAs (mirrors its pre-spec-177 PR-only trigger).

## Why

Before this PR, OAP's merge contract was distributed across 14 separate workflow files plus the branch-protection page in the GitHub UI. `needs:` is intra-workflow only, so no single job could aggregate the fleet, and path-filter skips read as "pass" — the actually-required set varied per PR with no declared source of truth. This PR makes the merge contract a single hashable file under the same review discipline as every other authority-bearing artifact in the tree.

Spec: [`specs/177-ci-orchestrator-pr-gate/spec.md`](specs/177-ci-orchestrator-pr-gate/spec.md).

## Operator action required before this can be required

Branch protection on `main`:

- Remove the 14 individual `ci-*` required checks.
- Add `ci / ci-gate` as the sole required check.

Until that change is made, this PR's checks are advisory — the new `ci / ci-gate` will run and (hopefully) go green, but old required-check names will be missing because the underlying workflows no longer self-trigger on PRs. That is the expected transitional state.

## Test plan

- [ ] `ci / ci-gate` is green on this PR.
- [ ] `ci / changes` (paths-filter) emits the expected booleans for this PR's diff (parity = true; specs = featuregraph = true).
- [ ] `ci / spec-conformance`, `ci / spec-code-coupling`, `ci / supply-chain`, `ci / codebase-index` all run unconditionally.
- [ ] `ci / featuregraph-golden` runs (paths-filter hits `specs/**` for the new spec dir).
- [ ] `ci / parity` runs (paths-filter hits `.github/workflows/**`).
- [ ] Update branch protection per §7 (manual; tracked above).
- [ ] After merge: open a tiny no-op PR to a single subsystem and confirm only the relevant routed workflows + the four constitutional ones fire, the rest skip, and `ci-gate` is green.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: featuregraph golden — spec 177 added to registry; per memory note feedback_featuregraph_golden_regen the golden bumps on every spec add.

title: spec(176): amends-aware section satisfaction parity
body:
## Summary

- Closes the implementation gap between spec 133 §4's satisfaction
  contract and the section-scoped branch of `check_coupling_section_aware`
  in `tools/spec-spine/spec-code-coupling-check/src/lib.rs`. The whole-file
  branch honours `OwnerSet { implements, amends, amendmentRecord }`
  composition via `any_owner_in_diff`; the section branch consulted only
  the bare `section_spec_ids` set and ignored the amender / amendment-
  record edges. Spec 133 §4's pseudocode computes `A` uniformly across
  both branches — the spec always covered this; the runtime diverged.

- New helper `legitimate_owners_for_section(section_spec_ids, index)`
  lives in the `authority-derivation` region (spec 133's anchor) and
  mirrors `legitimate_owners` keyed on the section authority set
  instead of the path's whole-file claim index. `check_coupling_section_aware`
  routes through it. FR-005 strict-expansion preserved by construction:
  the helper fires only inside the branch that already located
  `section_spec_ids` for `(path, section)`.

- Specs 133 and 152 receive `amended:` / `amendment_record:` frontmatter
  pointing to spec 176 plus body callouts per the spec 119 amender
  convention. Spec 176 ships as `kind: amendment, shape: bug-fix`,
  amends [133, 152].

## Decision

Bug-fix-only, not a new contract. Spec 133 §4's prose is explicit that
the satisfaction predicate ranges over whichever authority set the
gate computed; the amender clause sits below the section/whole-file
branch and applies uniformly. Spec 152 inherits via `extends:` and
shares the substrate gap. Reading (A) — "implementation diverged" —
was preferred over (B) — "deferred mechanism" — because §4's pseudo-
code is unambiguous and spec 152 §5 cites §4 as the consumer of its
section mechanism without re-specifying satisfaction.

Note: `invariant-freeze` is a *constraint kind* under `constrains:`
(spec 130), not a top-level spec kind. The right (kind, shape) pair
per spec 147's table is `amendment / bug-fix`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --release --manifest-path tools/spec-spine/spec-code-coupling-check/Cargo.toml` — 71 lib + 8 CLI + 9 section-aware verification tests pass, including three new tests:
  - `section_aware_amender_clears_section` (AC-1)
  - `section_aware_amendment_record_clears_section` (AC-2)
  - `section_aware_owner_set_strict_expansion_when_no_amenders` (AC-5 / FR-005)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `spec-compiler compile` clean; spec 176 registered with correct relationship graph
- [x] `spec-lint` clean
- [x] `make pr-prep` clean
- [x] Codebase index regenerated and committed
- [x] `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`

Spec-Drift-Waiver: corpus-snapshot bump. crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json is regenerated mechanically on every spec add (it is a SHA-256-fingerprinted snapshot of the registry), so any new-spec PR shifts it without touching the prior claimants. Spec 176 is the authority for *this* bump (the new feature entry it adds); the legacy implements: list on the golden (034/154/156/161/167/168/169) reflects earlier mechanical bumps each declared one-off. Same pattern used by spec adds 170-175. Architectural fix (treat the golden as empty-authority-by-rule via spec 152 §3.2) deferred — out of scope for this PR.

## Summary

- Adds the Live Sessions panel to OPC (spec 172, ASI10 mitigation) — every connected Claude session and active orchestrator workflow is visible in real time, with a force-disconnect control for runaway agents.
- Force-disconnect runs the spec §2.2 five-step semantics: cancel in-flight tool calls, kill the session process, create a forensic checkpoint (spec 095), append a `force_disconnect` audit event under `scope="audit"` to the orchestrator's scoped event store (spec 102 audit-chain substrate), and emit a Tauri event for the TS NotificationOrchestrator (spec 057).
- Threshold-based status badge (idle / active / warning / critical) driven by a configurable `LiveSessionThresholds` profile (`~/.local/share/opc/spec-172-thresholds.json`) with conservative defaults.

## Phases shipped (one commit each)

1. `process::activity` — sliding-window tool-call / token tracker on every `ProcessHandle`, with `record_session_tool_call` / `session_activity_snapshot` keyed by Claude session id.
2. Orchestrator consumer surface: `SqliteWorkflowStore::list_active_workflows` (status filter + steps-table enrichment) + optional live-state fields on `WorkflowStateSummary`. The panel reads workflow state through this typed API (FR-008, spec 103).
3. `force_disconnect_session` Tauri command — five ordered steps; returns `ForceDisconnectResult` with per-step success + warnings.
4. `LiveSessionsSurface` / `LiveSessionsPanel`, new tab type, `useTabState.createLiveSessionsTab`, `TabContent` case, `ProjectToolbar` entry. Polls every 2s + listens for the `live-sessions:force-disconnected` Tauri event.
5. Spec frontmatter: status draft→approved, implementation pending→complete, relationship graph (`establishes` + additive `extends` for spec 032 and spec 052), §5.1 implementation note clarifying how FR-007 is satisfied via the orchestrator's scoped event store. Codebase index regenerated; coupling gate clean against `origin/main`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p opc_lib --lib process::activity` — 6 tests for the sliding-window tracker

- Each action carries a **gate-impact preview** (coupling / lint / invariant-freeze / supply-chain / codification) and a **critical-action marker** (kernel / invariant / production-deploy) stubbing future M-of-N dual-auth (FR-003, FR-007).
- Plans that include a factory run carry a **predicted governance certificate stage list**; post-execution the actual certificate is diffed against the prediction and any discrepancy gates the next plan (FR-006, SC-004).
- Rendering is **hash-deterministic** for the same plan input (FR-008, SC-005) via a canonical-JSON + FNV-1a-64 plan hash; the narrative is excluded from the hash by design.

### What landed

|---|---|
| `planTypes.ts` | `AgentPlan` / `PlanAction` / `StructuralDiff` / `GateImpact` / `CertificatePrediction` types + deterministic hash + approval-traversal helpers |
| `planAnalysis.ts` | Pure helpers: kernel/invariant/prod-deploy path classifiers, `inferGateImpact`, `inferCriticalMarker`, `enrichPlan`, `summarizeGateImpact` |
| `PlanStructuralDiff.tsx` | Added / removed / modified specs view |
| `PlanActionGraph.tsx` | Action rows with traversal checkbox + collapsed YAML view |
| `GateImpactSummary.tsx` | Rolled-up worst-level + per-level + M-of-N counts |
| `PlanCertificatePrediction.tsx` | Predicted-vs-actual stage diff (`diffCertificate`) |
| `PlanReviewDialog.tsx` | Primary §2.1 action surface, traversal gate, plan-hash display |
| `FactoryPipelineContext.tsx` (extends spec 076) | `proposedPlan` / `certificateActual` state + listeners |
| `FactoryPipelinePanel.tsx` (extends spec 076) | Renders the dialog when a plan is pending |

### Gates / lifecycle

- `spec-code-coupling-check` (local, against origin/main): **OK** — 18 paths.
- `make pr-prep`: clean, codebase index regenerated and committed.
- Desktop test suite: **171 passing** (54 new tests across 6 files for spec 171).
- Featuregraph golden refreshed (lifecycle flip + new file rows).
- Spec lifecycle flipped to `status: approved`, `implementation: complete`. `establishes:` declared on 7 new files; `extends:` on the two spec-076-owned files touched.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: featuregraph golden `features_graph.json` violations-section entries added for the 7 new `product/apps/desktop/src/components/factory/{Plan*,planAnalysis,planTypes,GateImpactSummary}{,test}.{ts,tsx}` files mirror the existing pre-PR pattern for specs 076/122/138/etc. — the featuregraph scanner regex expects the legacy `// Spec: spec/...` (singular) header while the entire codebase writes `// Spec: specs/...` (plural). The lifecycle-row change for spec 171 itself is in the same diff; the section-authority gate flags the unrelated draft specs (161/167/168/169) whose neighbouring rows shifted purely from rendering order. Resolving the scanner regex is out of scope for this PR.

title: spec(168): per-project governance certificate emission and tenant-side verifier
body:
## Summary

Closes spec 168 — per-project governance certificate emission and tenant-side verifier.

Spec 102's `governance-certificate.json` discipline (binding requirements hash, frozen Build Spec hash, per-stage artifact hashes, and a self-authenticating SHA-256) applies today only to OAP's own factory runs. Spec 168 extends it to tenant projects: every factory pipeline a born-with tenant runs now emits the same independently-verifiable certificate, with a Rauthy-style signer identity bound into the canonical content. The kernel emission (spec 167) ships the emitter + verifier identity pin so the tenant inherits the discipline rather than re-implementing it.

Six phased commits — each green on its own:

- 2525aeca — typed relationship fields on spec 168 (extends 102 + 167).
- d9341863 — `Signer` struct + `build_tenant()` fallible builder path that halts when no signer is attached (FR-007). Bumps CERTIFICATE_VERSION to 1.3.0. Six new lib tests.
- e5c54bd3 — stage-shape flexibility: `generate_certificate_with_stage_ids` + `OAP_STAGE_IDS` constant. Tenant pipelines pass their own stage list; empty slice triggers filesystem discovery (§2.4). Three new tests.
- 9066a3fb — `build-certificate` CLI gains `--tenant-mode`, `--signer-subject`, `--signer-identity-provider`, `--signer-session-id`, `--stage-ids`. Six integration tests through the published binaries (FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-006, FR-007, FR-009).
- 8506a11b — kernel emission writes `.factory/toolchain.yaml` and records `certificate_toolchain` in `.kernel-version` (FR-001, FR-008). Eight new tests.
- 3a0baf03 — `spec_168_sc_001_through_005_end_to_end` integration test walking the closure narrative: born-with kernel → tenant pipeline → cert emission → clean verify → tamper-and-fail → no-signer halt. Spec flipped to `status: approved, implementation: complete`.

## Surface changes (public)

- `factory_engine::Signer` + `SignerError` — identity attribution with non-empty subject enforced by constructor (FR-007 anonymous-signing prohibition).
- `factory_engine::CertificateBuilder::signer(_)` + `build_tenant() -> Result<_, CertificateBuildError>` — tenant emission entry point.
- `factory_engine::generate_certificate_with_stage_ids(...)` + `OAP_STAGE_IDS` constant.
- `factory_engine::kernel_emission::CertificateToolchainRef` + `TenantToolchainContext` + `render_tenant_toolchain` — the kernel-side surface that records and emits the toolchain pin.
- `build-certificate` CLI: five new flags (`--tenant-mode`, `--signer-subject`, `--signer-identity-provider`, `--signer-session-id`, `--stage-ids`). Existing OAP-side invocation unchanged.
- `.kernel-version` schema: new optional `certificate_toolchain` field; pre-spec-168 fixtures round-trip unchanged.
- New file `.factory/toolchain.yaml` in every newly-emitted kernel.

## Backward compatibility

- OAP-side `factory_run.rs` and the existing `build-certificate` flow are untouched. `generate_certificate()` continues to default to OAP_STAGE_IDS; the new variant is additive.
- `GovernanceCertificate.signer` is `Option<Signer>` with `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, so pre-1.3.0 certificates serialise byte-identically (same `certificateHash`).
- `KernelVersion.certificate_toolchain` is also optional in serde, so legacy `.kernel-version` files round-trip without manual migration.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p factory-engine` (238 lib + 7 tenant_emission_integration + existing suites — all green)
- [x] `make pr-prep` clean (codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean across 11 diff paths)
- [x] spec-compiler + spec-lint clean against full corpus
- [x] Coupling gate green against `origin/main`
- [ ] CI workflows on this PR pass

title: spec(170): signed inter-stage manifests in factory-engine (ASI07)
body:
## Summary

Implements [spec 170](specs/170-signed-inter-stage-manifests/spec.md) — every factory-engine inter-stage hand-off is now identified by an Ed25519-signed manifest anchored to a per-run root key. Composes into the governance certificate (spec 102) so the auditor's `verify-certificate` validates both the run-level cert and the per-stage manifest chain offline.

- New `crates/factory-engine/src/inter_stage_manifest.rs`: `InterStageManifest`, `RunKeyChain`, `StageHandoffSigner` runtime session, deterministic ephemeral derivation, post-hoc `generate_chain_from_run_dir` walker for the s0–s5 sequential + dynamic s6* fan-out shape.
- Certificate composition: `CERTIFICATE_VERSION` bumped to `1.3.0`; new optional `interStageChain` field; verifier replays every manifest against the embedded chain. `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` preserves byte-identity for runs that omit the chain.
- `factory-run::emit_certificate` builds the chain from the artifact directory and binds it into the cert on every run termination (success or halt).
- Spec frontmatter flipped to `approved` / `complete`; new §7 \"Implementation map\" routes FR/SC to code; `establishes:` / `extends:` declared per the relationship-graph model (spec 130 / 152).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p factory-engine` — 241 lib + 36 integration tests pass.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p factory-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `make pr-prep` — codebase index refreshed, spec-code coupling gate green (9 diff paths checked).
- [x] SC-001..SC-005 exercised end-to-end through `crates/factory-engine/tests/spec_170_certificate_chain.rs`, including a binary-level `verify-certificate` CLI check (happy + tamper paths) for SC-004.
- [x] Round-trip: spec lint clean; cert hash invariance test guards the field introduction.

## Out of scope (per spec §5)

- mTLS at the network layer.
- Cross-run key-rotation policy.
- HSM key custody.
- Per-handoff signing wired through the orchestrator's stage-completion hook (the post-hoc chain emission from the artifact directory satisfies FR-007 today; per-receive-time validation is exposed through `StageHandoffSigner::verify_handoff` for future orchestrator integration).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` to reflect spec 170's lifecycle flip (`status: draft → approved`, `implementation: pending → complete`) and added relationship fields. title: spec(162) + feat(sandbox): backend-agnostic execution contract + fail-closed trait
body:
## Summary

Reframes spec 162 from "Dockerised execution substrate" (K8s-shaped) to
"Sandbox execution contract" (backend-agnostic) and lands the contract
code with three load-bearing shape constraints:

1. **No backend types in the trait surface.** `SandboxClient` knows
   nothing about K8s, Podman, or OCI. Inputs are `SandboxRequest`
   (command, input artifacts, egress allowlist, TTL, resource ceilings,
   minimum isolation tier); outputs are `SandboxExecution` (output
   artifacts, resource peak, isolation tier, opaque
   `runtime_descriptor`, deadline-hit flag).
2. **`NullSandboxClient` is universally fail-closed.** Every
   `execute()` returns `SandboxError::Unavailable`. FR-009 is a
   *contract* invariant, not a backend choice — a factory-engine
   without an operational backend MUST refuse to exercise
   adapter-emitted code rather than fall back to host execution.
3. **Cert stage shape normalises `isolation_tier` to 1/2/3** (numeric)
   and stores `runtime_descriptor` as opaque base64. The verifier
   reasons about isolation strength without parsing backend-specific
   fields.

## Background — why reframe before landing

The original spec 162 expressed §2 entirely in K8s-pod terms
(`PodSecurity` admission, `runtimeClassName`, `activeDeadlineSeconds`).
Two surfaces face the same ASI05 threat — OPC-driven local exercise
(developer laptop) and cluster-driven exercise (CI / control plane).
ASI05's prescription is substrate-agnostic ("e.g. hardened containers
with rigid network policies and low time-to-live thresholds"); the
contract is what closes the gap, not a specific backend. Pre-baking
K8s assumptions into the trait surface would force a re-do the
moment a local-container backend lands. Splitting the contract
(this PR) from the backends (separate companion specs, filed as
follow-up drafts) lets the contract spec freeze under the
`factory-engine` invariant-freeze while backends evolve
independently.

## What's in / what's deferred

**In this PR (spec 162 contract landing):**

- Spec reframe (`162-dockerised-execution-substrate` →
  `162-sandbox-execution-contract`) with full backend-agnostic §2 /
  §3 / §4 / §5 / §6 / §7. Slug rename, dir rename, frontmatter
  shape, reframe-history amendment record in §8.
- `crates/factory-contracts/src/sandbox.rs` (NEW) —
  backend-agnostic types: `SandboxRequest`, `SandboxExecution`,
  `IsolationTier`, `ResourceCeilings`, `EgressAllowlistEntry`,
  `InputArtifact`, `OutputArtifact`, `ResourcePeak`. Plus
  `SandboxRequest::validate()` enforcing FR-002 (hostname-only
  allowlist), FR-003 (300 s default, 900 s hard ceiling), FR-004
  (resource ceilings required), and the Tier-3-not-as-minimum rule.
- `crates/factory-engine/src/sandbox/mod.rs` (NEW) — async
  `SandboxClient` trait, `SandboxError` taxonomy, `BackendDescriptor`,
  `NullSandboxClient` (fail-closed default), and the
  `factory_engine::sandbox::exercise()` dispatcher that honours
  FR-001 (every exercise dispatches through `execute`) and FR-009
  (any unsuccessful path halts; no host fallback).
- `crates/factory-engine/src/governance_certificate.rs` extended —
  optional `StageRecord.sandbox_execution: SandboxExecutionRecord`
  (FR-008 binding). `CERTIFICATE_VERSION` bumped 1.1.0 → 1.2.0.
  Legacy fixtures (Option::None) are byte-identical to pre-1.2.0
  canonical form — `legacy_stage_record_hash_invariant_under_field_introduction`
  guards the `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` attribute.
- `FactoryError::SandboxRefusal { category, diagnostic }` —
  pipeline halt error for FR-009.
- Spec 074 amendment record + in-body callout (this spec adds the
  sandbox module to the `factory-contracts` crate that 074
  establishes).
- Spec 170 textual cross-ref updated to the new slug.
- 22 net new unit tests covering: request validation, isolation
  tier numerics, serde round-trips for both contract types and cert
  record, NullSandboxClient fail-closed behaviour, exercise()
  halt behaviour across all error categories (Unavailable,
  AdmissionRejected, RequestValidation), and cert hash binding to
  command + tier (SC-004).

**Deferred to companion specs (separate PRs):**

- **Local-container sandbox backend** — rootless Podman default
  (AGPL-friendly), Docker via `bollard` as alternative. Hits the
  common developer path (OPC laptop runs) first. Validates the
  trait abstraction against a real backend before kube-rs complexity
  layers in. Tests run in CI directly, no cluster-gated skips.
- **K8s sandbox backend** — kube-rs + PodSecurity admission
  policies under `platform/k8s/policies/sandbox/` + per-stage pod
  spec templates + RuntimeClass selection (gVisor / Firecracker /
  standard runc). Hits the CI / control-plane path. Integration
  tests behind `--features k8s-cluster-tests`.
- **Operational FR-001 wiring** — re-routing existing factory-engine
  exercise call sites (`checks::run_command`,
  `verify_harness::run_factory_gate_check`, stage runners) through
  `factory_engine::sandbox::exercise()`. No operational benefit
  until a real backend can satisfy the calls; lands with the
  local-container backend PR.

## Compliance posture

The ASI05 gap closes structurally with this PR — `NullSandboxClient`
is fail-closed by default, so factory-engine cannot exercise
adapter-emitted code on the host without an operational backend
overriding the default. ASI10 (Rogue Agents) is co-mitigated:
without backend code that grants execution privileges, no codegen
agent can spin up parasite processes.

## Spec lifecycle

Spec 162: `status: draft` (design refined and ratified by this PR's
review; flip to `approved` can happen on merge or in a follow-up).
`implementation: pending` → `implementation: in-progress` (contract
landed; backends are operational delivery, tracked separately).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace --manifest-path Cargo.toml --lib` — all
  workspace lib tests pass (47 cargo + 199 factory-engine + 14

title: spec(165): OPC decomposition pipeline — deterministic backbone (stages 1-6 + Tauri)
body:
## Summary

Lands the **deterministic backbone** of spec 165's OPC decomposition
pipeline. The pipeline takes a project tree (+ optional knowledge
bundle) and produces draft specs satisfying the spec 161 emission
contract, the spec 147 kind grammar, and the spec 154 logical-unit
grammar. Phase by phase across 11 commits, every phase builds and
tests green; the spec frontmatter is flipped from `implementation:
pending` → `in-progress` (intentionally not `complete` — follow-up
PRs land LLM synthesis, promotion, certificate emission, and the
React UI per spec 165 §5 and the plan).

Spec 165 was scoped per the user's choice of "deterministic backbone"
in plan-time scope confirmation (see `specs/165/plan.md`).

### What lands

- New crate `crates/opc-decomposition-pipeline`:
  - Stage 1: `artifact_extract::extract_deterministic` over a knowledge
    bundle directory; per-file `ExtractionOutput` JSON; degraded path
    on missing bundle (FR-010).
  - Stage 2: `xray::scan_target` + `xray::fingerprint::generate_fingerprint`
    over the project tree; persisted as `index.json` + `fingerprint.json`.
  - Stage 3: semantic clustering. Default: directory-grouping; the
    `embeddings` feature swaps in fastembed-backed union-find on
    cosine similarity ≥ 0.85. Both produce the same `Cluster` shape.
  - Stage 4: `xray::analysis::call_graph::analyze_directory`; persisted
    graph + summary.
  - Stage 5: git lineage via `git log --follow` per logical unit;
    degraded to `unknown` on missing `.git` (FR-010).
  - Stage 6: deterministic baseline synthesiser. Emits one
    `spec.md` per cluster under `s6-synthesis/specs/<slug>/spec.md`
    with `role: decomposition-origin` + `provenance: { kind:
    code-fingerprint, ... }` (FR-004), `kind: capability` (FR-005),
    `establishes: [{ unit: { kind: file, path: ... } }, ...]` (FR-006),
    `origin: retroactive: true`.
  - Persistence under `<project>/.opc/decomposition/<run-id>/` with
    content-addressed `run.json` manifest.
  - `list_runs` / `load_run` helpers for the Tauri layer.
- Tauri commands in `product/apps/desktop/src-tauri`:
  `decomposition_run`, `decomposition_list_runs`, `decomposition_get_run`.
- Tests:
  - 11 unit tests across stage modules (degraded paths, happy paths).
  - `tests/end_to_end.rs` — full pipeline against a fixture project;
    asserts SC-001 / SC-003 / FR-010 degraded markers / manifest
    persistence + listing.
  - `tests/spec_lint_compliance.rs` — emitted draft specs pass
    `open_agentic_spec_lint::lint_repo` with zero error-tier
    diagnostics (SC-002).

### Explicitly deferred (follow-up specs/PRs)

Tracked in `specs/165/tasks.md` as F-001..F-006:

- **F-001** Real LLM-backed `Synthesiser` impl. The spec §5 defers
  model selection to platform config; this PR ships a deterministic
  baseline that satisfies the emission contract.
- **F-002** Promotion flow: write staged spec.md files into
  `<project>/specs/`, invoke project's spec-compiler, run coupling
  gate (FR-008, SC-005).
- **F-003** Governance certificate at promotion (spec 102, FR-009,
  SC-006).
- **F-004** React panel: "Decompose project" action button, staging
  browser, promotion UI. The spec 163 Requirements view (the
  rendering consumer) is itself draft.
- **F-005** Checkpoint integration (spec 095): branch-of-thought
  decomposition trials.
- **F-006** Persistent embedding cache (the originally-named
  axiomregent substrate) for cross-run reuse.

### Substrate decision (documented in plan.md)

Spec §2.1 names `crates/axiomregent` (via its `search` module) as
the stage-3 substrate. In practice, axiomregent's semantic search
and xray's `analysis-embeddings` both wrap fastembed; the vector-
matching primitive is identical. axiomregent layers persistent
hiqlite indexing on top, which this pipeline does not need. This
PR uses `xray/analysis-embeddings` for stage 3 (avoiding the
~25 transitive dep tree of hiqlite + reqwest + octocrab). FR-010
explicitly defines the xray-only fallback as the degraded path; the
backbone treats it as the primary. A future spec can introduce the
axiomregent persistent-index implementation behind the same
clustering trait. This is an engineering choice, not a spec edit.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json`
is a derived file owned by specs 034/154/156/161. This PR's only
edit to it is the fingerprint plus spec 160's status flip
(draft/pending → approved/complete) inherited from PR #203's merge
into main; no spec 165 entry appears in the diff. Regeneration is
mechanical refresh, not authority claim.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p opc-decomposition-pipeline` — 14 tests green
  (11 unit + 2 end-to-end + 1 spec-lint compliance)
- [x] `cargo build --manifest-path product/apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
  — Tauri build green with new commands registered
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `make pr-prep` — codebase index refreshed, coupling gate
  clean (origin/main baseline)
- [x] `spec-lint --repo .` — zero diagnostics; `--fail-on-warn`
  also exits 0
- [ ] GitHub Actions: full CI parity, including spec-compiler,
  spec-lint, coupling gate, featuregraph golden, build/test of all
  Rust crates, Tauri desktop build, npm workspace.

title: spec(161): W-161 lint rule reserves `role: decomposition-origin`
body:
## Summary

- Implement spec 161's currently-implementable surface: a new spec-lint rule **W-161** that reserves `role: decomposition-origin` on `references:` entries for entries that (a) use the `provenance:` arm of the spec 156 grammar and (b) carry a non-empty `provenance.derived_at:` ISO-8601 timestamp (FR-006, FR-007, SC-003, SC-004).
- Add the `error` severity tier to spec-lint — V-026-equivalent, fails the binary unconditionally so a CI invocation that forgets `--fail-on-warn` cannot silently accept a reserved-role violation (spec 161 §2.3 / SC-004).
- Flip spec 161 `implementation: pending` → `in-progress`. FR-001–005 still bind when the producer (spec 165 OPC decomposition pipeline) and consumer (spec 163 stagecraft Requirements view) implementations land.

W-161 fires zero times across the current corpus — no production spec carries the reserved role yet. The first emitter will be spec 165's decomposition pipeline.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --release -p open_agentic_spec_lint` — 25/25 pass (8 new W-161 unit tests + 2 binary-level tests for error-tier exit semantics)
- [x] `cargo test --release -p open_agentic_spec_types` — 19/19 pass
- [x] `make pr-prep` — codebase index refreshed, spec-code coupling gate clean
- [x] `spec-lint` over corpus — zero W-161 hits (no false positives on hand-authored specs, SC-003)
- [x] `registry-consumer show 161-...` — frontmatter compiles, `extends:` edges emit
- [ ] GitHub Actions: full CI parity (fast-ci, spec-code coupling, supply-chain, schema-parity, etc.)

## Notes for reviewers

- **Severity tier semantics.** SC-004 calls for "V-026-equivalent severity" but FR-006 says "spec-lint rule". Resolved by adding `error` as a new tier alongside the existing `warning`/`info` — keeps the rule on spec-lint's surface (per FR-006) while preserving the hard-fail semantics (per SC-004). Documented in the `Warning` doc comment.
- **derived_at validation.** The ISO-8601 check is a cheap `YYYY-MM-DD[Thh:mm:ss…]` prefix match — enough to reject `"yesterday"` or `"05/22/2026"` without pulling in a date-parsing crate. Strict RFC-3339 validation can layer on later if needed.
- **No spec text changes.** The spec body already specifies all four W-161 conditions; this PR just builds what spec 161 already documents.

title: spec(154): logical-unit ownership grammar — Segments 4–6
body:
## Summary

Closes spec 154 (logical-unit ownership grammar). Carries four commits — Segments 4, 5, the Segment 6 handoff, and the Segment 6 landing. Spec 154 flips from `implementation: pending → complete` with a §12 closure note recording all six segments.

The headline mechanic is the **logical-unit grammar**: relationship-graph fields (`establishes:`, `extends:`, `refines:`, …) carry typed `unit: { kind: crate|symbol|module|section|directory|file, … }` values instead of bare file paths. The coupling gate consumes the resolved graph, so refactor-invariance becomes a structural property of ownership rather than a path-hygiene exercise.

### What landed across segments 4–6

- **Segment 4** (`bfa6e060`): `tools/spec-spine/spec-code-coupling-check` consumes the resolved-unit API surface introduced by Segment 3.
- **Segment 5** (`beb1e3e6`): 142 spec.md files migrated from bare-string / `paths: [list]` shapes into spec 154 §5 typed-unit shapes. One-shot migrator at `tools/oap/spec-unit-migrate/` retained as a historical artifact.
- **Segment 6 handoff** (`8d79cfe2`): planning artifact for the final segment.
- **Segment 6 landing** (`91169ec7`):
  - **4' refinement** (the structural repair surfaced mid-segment): `references:` is now genuinely non-owning, including existence-exemption. Both spec-compiler and codebase-indexer route existence-validation off the wrapping field, not the unit's surface syntax. Spec 154 §4 amended with an "existence is also non-owning" paragraph.
  - **Orphan resolution**: 80 I-101 / I-108 orphans cleared across ~30 specs using a four-way disposition matrix (planned / historical / deferred / delete / fix-path).
  - **Legacy parser excision**: bare-string `establishes:` and `extends.paths:` / `co_authority.paths+section:` arms removed from `tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/src/lib.rs`. L-005 promoted `info → error`. I-108 retired (`MissingFile` always emits the blocking I-008 regardless of authoring shape). V-020 widened to count `references:`, `superseded_by:`, `composition.requires:`, `selects:` as relationship-satisfying.

body:
## Summary

Replaces five open dependabot PRs with hand-authored equivalents per the manual-patch-over-dependabot discipline. Fixes the breakages that left three of them red so this consolidated PR has a path to green.

## What landed (5 commits, 1 chore tail)

| Replaces | Commit | What |
|---|---|---|
| #179 | `fc56863d` | cargo-minor-patch in `/platform/services/deployd-api-rs` (tokio 1.52.3, hiqlite 0.13.2, tower-http 0.6.11, jsonwebtoken 10.4.0) |
| #177 | `8aaca703` | octocrab 0.50 → 0.51 in `/crates/axiomregent` |
| #178 | `ad131661` | jsonschema 0.33 → 0.46 in `/tools/spec-spine/{spec-compiler,codebase-indexer}` |
| #180 | `d1b201d5` | npm-minor-patch group (15 packages) in `/platform/services/stagecraft` + ENCORE_VERSION 1.56.7 → 1.57.5 in ci-/cd-stagecraft + regenerated client.ts |
| #130 | `7e6143d2` | @types/node 22 → 25 in `/platform/services/stagecraft` + JsonWebKey → webcrypto.JsonWebKey at two callsites |
| — | `d0ea24db` | refresh `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` content hash |

## Fixes for what dependabot left red

**#180 / #130 — `encore build docker: FAILURE`**
Workflows pin `ENCORE_VERSION: '1.56.7'`; the CLI refuses a runtime newer than itself. Dependabot's PR bumped `encore.dev` to 1.57.5 but never touched the workflow env, so CLI 1.56.7 + runtime 1.57.5 hit `installed 'encore.dev' package version (1.57.5) newer than 'encore' release`. Bumped both `ci-stagecraft.yml` and `cd-stagecraft.yml` to 1.57.5 in lock-step with the runtime.

**#180 — stale generated client**
`web/app/lib/client.ts` is checked-in output of `encore gen client`. With the CLI bumped to 1.57.5, the regenerated client adds an `environments` ServiceClient and several agent-binding interfaces that the 1.56.7 generator was emitting stale. Landed alongside the runtime bump.

**#130 — `typecheck + test: FAILURE`**
`@types/node` 25 reshuffled WebCrypto exports: `JsonWebKey` is no longer re-exported from `node:crypto`. Two callsites in `api/auth/{m2mAuth,rauthy}.ts` used the old shorthand cast — retargeted at `webcrypto.JsonWebKey`.

**All 5 — `coupling-check: FAILURE`**
Standard for dep refreshes per spec 127 §2 / FR-005. Waiver is below.

## Deviations from dependabot

- **`@types/node` taken to 25.9.1** (current latest), not dependabot's 25.7.0 — same major, two minor newer.

## Verification

- `cargo check` clean across `deployd-api-rs`, `crates/` workspace, `spec-compiler`, `codebase-indexer`.
- `cargo test -p axiomregent -p open_agentic_spec_compiler -p open_agentic_codebase_indexer` — all green; tests for deployd compile.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in stagecraft — clean.
- `npm test` in stagecraft — 48/48 files, 457/457 tests.
- `npm audit --audit-level=high` in stagecraft — exit 0 (4 moderate, all below threshold).
- `encore build docker` reaches the docker-daemon stage locally with CLI 1.57.5 + runtime 1.57.5 (build proper requires CI's docker; the parser-fail mode that broke dependabot's PR is gone).
- `codebase-indexer check` — clean (committed refreshed index).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: 5 dependabot dep-refresh PRs (#177, #178, #179, #180, #130) consolidated; manifests/lockfiles/codegen output changed without spec design changes

Per spec 127 §2 and FR-005, dep-refresh PRs use the explicit waiver path rather than mass-amending owner specs whose design has not changed (CONST-005 / `.claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md`). The waiver echoes as `::warning::` in CI for reviewer visibility.

## Closes

- Supersedes #130, #177, #178, #179, #180.

## Test plan

title: spec(158): workflow-ref SHA-pinning lint (amends 116)
body:
## Summary

The Megalodon campaign (2026-05-18, 5,718 malicious commits to 5,561 repositories in a six-hour window) used compromised PATs to plant exfiltrating workflow files into target repos. The targeted variant (`Optimize-Build`) sat dormant behind `workflow_dispatch` for selective activation; the mass variant (`SysDiag`) fired automatically on `push` and `pull_request_target`. Both relied on the attacker introducing a workflow file or replacing an existing one — a class of compromise that SHA-pinning of `uses:` refs partially defends against, but only when SHA-pinning is *enforced*, not merely asserted.

At the time spec 116 (`supply-chain-policy-gates`) closed on 2026-05-02, every external Action ref in this repo was SHA-pinned to a 40-hex commit. That posture was correct, but it was discipline — maintained by hand, verifiable only by review. No gate would have refused a regression. This PR closes that convention-vs-contract gap. It is the fourth falsifier in the [four-falsifiers framework](docs/launch-notes/spec-158-workflow-ref-pinning.md) being assembled for the pre-launch hardening sprint:

| Falsifier | Mechanism | This PR |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| 1 — required signed commits | branch protection | hardening step 1 |
| 2 — required status checks (`workflow-pins`, `coupling-check`, etc.) | branch protection | hardening step 3 |
| 3 — `allowed_actions: selected` allow-list | repo Actions settings | hardening step 4 |
| **4 — `uses:` refs SHA-pinned, enforced by lint** | **CI + pre-commit, no allow-list** | **this PR** |

## Three commits, in this order — the order is the argument

1. **`fix(githooks): correct stale INDEXER path post Cut D reorg`** ([6888fa00](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/commit/6888fa00))
   The opt-in pre-commit hook referenced a stale binary path from before the Cut D crate reorg, leaving Stage 1 silently broken for any adopter. One-line correction. Shipped first as a separable concern because the PR's thesis is "the pre-commit hook is the lower boundary of the supply-chain contract" — shipping a hook whose Stage 1 is broken contradicts that thesis on the same file.

2. **`feat(supply-chain): workflow-ref SHA-pin lint`** ([c59fa5fc](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/commit/c59fa5fc))
   The contribution. `tools/lint/workflow-pins.sh` (line-oriented, fail-closed on dynamic refs), regression tests with fixtures that act as the lint's own spec, a `workflow-pins` job in `ci-supply-chain.yml`, and a Stage 2 gate in `.githooks/pre-commit` — same script, two consumers. Methodology note documents the zero-scan regression the first draft would have shipped (a lint that returns exit 0 across zero lines is the precise failure mode this spec exists to refuse) and the count-the-lines check that caught it.

3. **`spec(158): workflow-ref SHA-pinning lint (amends 116)`** ([54ba6a3f](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/commit/54ba6a3f))
   The contract that authorises the contribution. Five FRs: SHA-pin enforcement, one-script-two-consumers, no allow-list (dynamic refs refused on soundness grounds — same argument as Rust refusing to compile where the borrow checker cannot prove non-aliasing), no embedded `uses:` examples in workflow YAML, and trust-transitivity as the positive shape of escape valves. Spec 116 amended in-place per the constitutional amendment convention (`amended:` + `amendment_record:` + in-body callout).

4. **`docs(launch-notes): capture Block 5 (CI evidence) + auto-trigger gap`** ([18fbc695](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/commit/18fbc695))
   Platform-side evidence to match the local-side falsifiers. See gap note below.

## Evidence

The full evidence bundle is at **[`docs/launch-notes/spec-158-workflow-ref-pinning.md`](docs/launch-notes/spec-158-workflow-ref-pinning.md)** — five reproducible terminal/CI blocks plus a methodology note. Not recapitulated here; the file is the citation.

CI run: [`26277186106`](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/actions/runs/26277186106) — all four `ci-supply-chain` jobs green, including the new `workflow-pins / SHA-pin enforcement` job. That rendered name is the literal string to bind in `required_status_checks` post-merge.

## Auto-trigger gap (worth investigating before required_status_checks binding)

Opening this PR produced zero `pull_request:`-triggered workflow runs at the head SHA, in both draft and ready states. `gh api repos/.../actions/runs?head_sha=...` returned an empty list across multiple polling intervals. CI evidence was captured via `workflow_dispatch` fallback. Root cause not yet diagnosed — see the launch-notes "process observation" section for hypotheses. The required_status_checks binding step of the hardening sprint should not run until the auto-trigger path is reliable, because a gate that exists but doesn't fire is indistinguishable from no gate — and that's the exact failure shape this PR's lint exists to prevent at a different layer.

## See also

- #194 — pre-existing `spec-compiler` silent exit-1 with no diagnostic. Scoped separately; reproduces on pristine `main`; orthogonal to this PR and does not block `make pr-prep`.

## After merge

Land [hardening step 3](docs/launch-notes/spec-158-workflow-ref-pinning.md#what-the-bundle-authorises) — bind `workflow-pins / SHA-pin enforcement` (and the other `ci-supply-chain` jobs as a family) into `required_status_checks.contexts` on `main` — once the auto-trigger gap above is resolved. That step is the difference between "the contract is enforceable" and "the contract is enforced."

## Test plan

- [x] `./tools/lint/workflow-pins.sh` exits 0 against the tree (126 `uses:` refs across 22 workflow files + 4 composite actions)
- [x] `./tools/lint/workflow-pins-test.sh` — all 4 assertions PASS (passing fixture, failing fixture, bash 4+ gate present, tree-wide scan)
- [x] `./.githooks/pre-commit` — both stages exit 0 on clean tree (Stage 1: codebase-index staleness; Stage 2: workflow-pins)
- [x] `make pr-prep` — coupling gate clean across 10 diff paths
- [x] `shellcheck` clean on `workflow-pins.sh`, `workflow-pins-test.sh`, `.githooks/pre-commit`
- [x] CI run `26277186106` — `workflow-pins / SHA-pin enforcement` green; full `ci-supply-chain` workflow green
- [ ] After auto-trigger gap resolved: `pull_request:`-event `workflow-pins` job renders green on a subsequent push without `workflow_dispatch` fallback

---

**Updated 2026-05-22 (round 2)** — rebased onto current main; added spec 159 (V-004 carve-out for `tools/*/tests/fixtures/**`) which fixes the `spec-compiler` and `featuregraph / golden graph` CI failures. The failures were not the #194 silent-exit bug; they were V-004 firing on this PR's own lint fixtures (`tools/lint/tests/fixtures/{passing,failing}/action.yml`). Spec 159 amends spec 000 by extending V-004's explicitly-policy-extensible scan-path boundary, without touching V-004's frozen anchor. Featuregraph golden regenerated to absorb specs 158 + 159.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: featuregraph golden fixture-bump for specs 158 + 159 corpus addition; analogous to PR #191 which used the same waiver path for specs 156, 157.

title: spec-compiler: silent exit 1 from `compile` with no diagnostic output
body:
## Observed

`./tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/target/release/spec-compiler compile` exits with code 1, emitting no output to either stdout or stderr.

```
$ ./tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/target/release/spec-compiler compile 1>/tmp/sc.stdout 2>/tmp/sc.stderr
$ echo "rc: $?"
rc: 1
$ wc -c /tmp/sc.stdout /tmp/sc.stderr
0 /tmp/sc.stdout
0 /tmp/sc.stderr
```

No log file appears to be written. `RUST_LOG=debug` produces the same result. `script(1)` (which captures the controlling TTY) also captures nothing.

## Reproducer

```bash
git checkout f0114bc5    # pristine HEAD as of 2026-05-22 (main, no working-tree changes)
make -B tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/target/release/spec-compiler   # fresh build via Makefile per the per-crate target-dir convention
./tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/target/release/spec-compiler compile
echo "rc: $?"   # → rc: 1
```

The Makefile target `make spec-compile` produces the same failure (`make: *** [spec-compile] Error 1`) without propagating any diagnostic.

## Scope (what this is NOT)

- **Not a `make pr-prep` failure.** `make pr-prep` runs the codebase-indexer and the spec-code coupling check, neither of which invoke `spec-compile`. `pr-prep` continues to exit 0 cleanly on the same tree.
- **Not a `make ci` blocker.** Spec conformance CI runs `spec-compile` separately in GitHub Actions; if that surface is currently green, the silent-fail is local-only — possibly an environment-dependent panic that the CI runner's stderr capture does surface.
- **Not caused by recent work.** Reproduces against pristine `f0114bc5` (last commit on `origin/main` as of 2026-05-22), independent of any in-flight branch.

## Why this matters

Silent failures are the precise failure mode the spec spine exists to refuse. A compiler that exits non-zero with no diagnostic is indistinguishable from "compile failed for an opaque reason" — which is the same epistemic shape as the zero-scan lint regression documented in `docs/launch-notes/spec-158-workflow-ref-pinning.md`. The contract for `spec-compile` should be: exit 0 on success, exit non-zero with a `path:line:reason` diagnostic on failure. Silent exit non-zero violates the contract.

## Suggested next steps

1. Reproduce locally and capture any panic backtrace (`RUST_BACKTRACE=full`).
2. Confirm whether the current CI workflow `spec-conformance.yml` job for `spec-compile` is currently green against `main` — if green, scope the bug as local-only / shell-or-environment-dependent.
3. If reproducible in CI, the path forward is to ensure the compiler emits a diagnostic to stderr on every non-zero exit path before further investigation.

## Surfacing context

Surfaced during work on PR `158-workflow-ref-sha-pinning-lint`, which is unrelated to the spec compiler. `make pr-prep` (the load-bearing pre-commit gate) passed cleanly throughout that work, confirming this issue is scope-orthogonal. Tracked here so the silent-fail isn't conflated with that PR's correctness.

title: ci(featuregraph): dedicated workflow for golden test on spec-only PRs
body:
## Summary

Implements **Option B** from [issue #192](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/issues/192) — the path-filter follow-up surfaced when PR #190 paid the cleanup cost for #186–#189's accumulated featuregraph-golden drift.

Adds `.github/workflows/ci-featuregraph-golden.yml`: a narrow, single-purpose workflow that runs only `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden.rs::test_golden_graph`, triggered on the test's actual input surface:

```yaml
paths:
  - 'specs/**'
  - 'tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/**'
  - 'crates/featuregraph/**'
```

The broader `ci-crates.yml` keeps running the same test as part of `cargo test --workspace`. This workflow is **redundant** on Cargo-touching PRs (both fire) and **authoritative** on spec-only PRs (the gap that let #185 → #189 drift silently).

Spec 135's fast-CI principle is preserved: spec-only PRs now pay ~1–2 min for a focused job instead of either skipping the gate entirely (status quo) or paying ~5 min for the full workspace job (Option A).

## What the workflow does

```yaml
jobs:
  golden:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - rust toolchain (1.95.0, dtolnay/rust-toolchain pinned)
      - Swatinem/rust-cache (shared-key: featuregraph-golden)
      - cargo build --release spec-compiler        # produce the registry fixture
      - ./spec-compiler compile                    # emit .derived/spec-registry/registry.json
      - cargo test --test golden -- test_golden_graph
```

No `cargo check` / `cargo clippy` against the whole crate (those would just duplicate `ci-crates` work). Direct invocation; the composite `.github/actions/rust-ci` action isn't used here because it does too much.

## Design choices documented in the workflow header

- **NOT added to `ci-parity-check::ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS`.** The workflow is coverage-of-existing-gate, not a new enforcement axis. `make ci-strict` already mirrors the golden test via `cargo test --workspace` in `ci-rust`; adding this would falsely claim a new mirror obligation.
- **Redundancy with `ci-crates` on Cargo/crates-touching PRs is intentional.** Trying to exclude featuregraph from the workspace test set in `ci-crates.yml` adds config complexity for no real benefit — both run, both pass, no harm.
- **No `make` target added.** The workflow's purpose is a CI-only trigger gap-fix; replicating it locally would just rerun what `cargo test --workspace` already covers.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML syntax valid (`python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` exit 0)
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path crates/featuregraph/Cargo.toml --test golden -- test_golden_graph` → exit 0 locally
- [x] `make pr-prep` → coupling-check OK on 2 diff paths (workflow file + index.json regen); codebase-index refreshed clean
- [x] `ci-parity-check` → `OK — Makefile mirrors 11 enforcing workflow(s); fresh-clone preconditions satisfied` (new workflow correctly NOT counted in enforcement set)
- [ ] CI on push: the new workflow fires on this PR (it touches `.github/workflows/ci-featuregraph-golden.yml`, plus the path filter includes `crates/featuregraph/**` via the description but not the workflow file itself — the new workflow will self-trigger via the `workflow_dispatch` push to its own file)
- [ ] CI on push: the existing `ci-crates` workflow does NOT fire (no Cargo / crates touch in this diff) — confirms the gap-fix actually targets the right surface
- [ ] CI on push: `ci-codebase-index` fires (it path-filters on `.github/workflows/*.yml` via codebase-indexer inputs, indirectly) and passes

## Acceptance against issue #192

- [x] Single-purpose workflow with narrow trigger (`specs/**` + producer/consumer code paths)
- [x] Spec-only PRs going forward will run the golden test
- [x] Drift is structurally prevented from re-accumulating
- [x] Coverage, not new enforcement (Makefile mirror unchanged via existing `ci-crates` ↔ `ci-rust` mapping)

## Closes

- #192 — ci: ci-crates path filter misses 'specs/**' — golden-graph drift accrued silently #185 → #189

## Second commit — ci-parity-check formalisation

Added in a second commit on this branch (60a5ac75): a sibling `COVERAGE_WORKFLOWS` const next to `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS` in `tools/oap/ci-parity-check/src/lib.rs`, plus a disjointness unit test. Makes the "coverage, not enforcement" classification durable at the parity-check tool level rather than only in the new workflow's header comment.

Strictly additive — no enforcement-logic change. The 11-workflow mirror obligation reported by ci-parity-check is unchanged (`OK — Makefile mirrors 11 enforcing workflow(s)` before and after).

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: additive sibling-const + doc-comment + unit-test in `tools/oap/ci-parity-check/src/lib.rs` documenting the coverage-vs-enforcement distinction. Specs 104 (`makefile-ci-parity-contract`), 134 (`fast-local-ci-mode`), and 135 (`fast-ci-as-default`) own the touched file and have no contract change to record — `ENFORCING_WORKFLOWS` membership, the `make ci-strict` mirror obligation, and the parity-check behaviour are all unchanged. The new `COVERAGE_WORKFLOWS` const is parallel documentation, not a redefinition of any enforcement axis. Amending three spec.md files just to note "added a sibling const" would be receipt-loading the relationship graph for what is functionally a comment.

title: ci: ci-crates path filter misses 'specs/**' — golden-graph drift accrued silently #185 → #189
body:
## Summary

`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden.rs::test_golden_graph` consumes the compiled spec registry as input (via `.derived/spec-registry/registry.json`, regenerated by `spec-compiler` at the top of the CI job). Its actual input surface is therefore `specs/**`. But the workflow that runs it (`.github/workflows/ci-crates.yml`) has a path filter that does **not** include `specs/**` — so PRs that only add or edit spec markdown skip the workspace job entirely, including this test.

Result: between **PR #185** (last golden bump) and **PR #189**, four spec PRs landed (#185, #186, #187, #188, #189) without `test_golden_graph` firing once. PR #190 — `chore(crypto): drop rand dep` — was the first PR in a workflow path that did trigger `ci-crates.yml` (it touched `Cargo.lock` and `Cargo.toml`), and it surfaced the accumulated drift as a test failure on something it had nothing to do with.

PR #191 cleaned the drift retroactively. This issue is for the structural fix that prevents the next round.

## The path filter today

[`.github/workflows/ci-crates.yml:19-33`](.github/workflows/ci-crates.yml#L19-L33):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'Cargo.toml'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
      - 'crates/**'
      - 'tools/spec-spine/**'
      - 'tools/oap/**'
      - 'tools/shared/**'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'Cargo.toml'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
      - 'crates/**'
      - 'tools/spec-spine/**'
      - 'tools/oap/**'
      - 'tools/shared/**'
```

`specs/**` is not in the filter, even though the workflow's first two steps explicitly compile the spec registry as a test fixture (`Compile spec-compiler` → `Emit spec registry`), and `crates/featuregraph` tests against that fixture.

## What broke in practice

- **#185** (spec 155) — last golden bump
- **#186** (spec 154 Segment 3 handoff docs) — spec-only, didn't trigger `ci-crates`. Golden drift accumulated.
- **#187** (codebase-indexer Segment 3 code) — touched `tools/spec-spine/**`, triggered `ci-crates`. But Segment 3's logical-unit resolver doesn't change features in the graph, so the golden didn't visibly drift on this PR.
- **#188** (spec 156) — spec-only. Drift now masks two missing feature entries (156, plus 157 once it landed).
- **#189** (spec 157) — spec-only. Drift now masks both 156 and 157.
- **#190** (rand removal) — touched `Cargo.lock` + Rust source in `crates/**`. Triggered `ci-crates`. Failed on `test_golden_graph` for completely unrelated reasons.

Two systemic costs:
1. **Provenance integrity gap** — `main`'s featuregraph fixture was misrepresenting OAP's spec inventory for 4 PRs between #185 and #191. For a project whose pitch is hash-verifiable traceability, having `features_graph.json` claim the corpus was 155 specs when it was actually 157 is exactly the class of structural lie the spec-spine discipline exists to prevent.
2. **Wrong-PR cost** — drift surfaces on whichever PR happens to touch Cargo or crates next. That PR's author bears the cost of investigating and fixing debt they didn't introduce. For #190 specifically: 1 extra round-trip (open #191, merge, rebase #190, force-push, re-CI) for a fixture issue that should have been caught at #186.

## Proposed fixes

### Option A — Add `specs/**` to `ci-crates.yml` path filter (broad)

Single-line edit. Every spec edit triggers the full Cargo workspace job (~5 min warm). Easy to land; high cost per spec edit; catches every drift class going forward (not just featuregraph).

### Option B — Split the golden test into a dedicated workflow with a narrower trigger (targeted)

Move `test_golden_graph` into its own workflow (`.github/workflows/ci-featuregraph-golden.yml` or similar) with a tight path filter:

```yaml
paths:
  - 'specs/**'
  - 'crates/featuregraph/**'
  - 'tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/**'
```

The workflow still has to compile `spec-compiler` to regenerate the registry fixture, but the rest of the `ci-crates` workspace job stays gated to Cargo/crates touches. Cost on a spec-only PR drops from ~5 min to ~1-2 min (just the featuregraph test path).

### Option C — Both, with `ci-crates` carrying a fast featuregraph-only mode

Keep the broad path on the existing workflow but add an early-exit fast path that runs only the featuregraph golden when only `specs/**` changed. More config complexity, but every PR pays the minimal cost.

## Recommendation

**Option B.** Single-purpose workflow, single-purpose trigger. The pattern `spec-corpus-as-input → derived fixture → golden test` is what got us here; isolating it makes the dependency structural and audit-able. The fast-CI principle (spec 135) favours narrow, named workflows over generic catch-alls.

## Out of scope for this issue

- Whether to make `test_golden_graph` part of `make pr-prep` (pre-push gate). Considered, but `pr-prep`'s contract today is staleness + coupling, and the golden test compiles the whole featuregraph crate which is slower than `pr-prep` should be. Better solved at the CI level here.
- Other golden tests with similar shape. Surveyed: `crates/axiomregent/tests/mcp_contract.rs` is the only other golden, but its input is a tools list, not the spec registry. No equivalent drift risk.

## Related

- PRs that accrued the drift: #186, #187, #188, #189
- PR that surfaced it: #190
- PR that fixed it: #191
- Memory entries (auto-memory, not in repo): `feedback_pr_prep_after_last_commit`, `feedback_dep_refresh_waiver`, `feedback_indexer_test_suite` (the analogous case for `codebase-indexer check` vs `cargo test --test exit_codes`).

title: chore(featuregraph): regenerate golden for specs 156, 157
body:
## Summary

- Regenerates `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` to include feature entries for **spec 156** (`references-edge-provenance-grammar`) and **spec 157** (`opc-session-model`), plus the updated `graph_fingerprint`.
- **Accrued debt — not introduced by this PR.** The golden file last updated at `2eda5720` (spec 155 PR #185). Specs 156 (PR #188) and 157 (PR #189) landed without touching it; this PR is the cleanup.

## Why this surfaced now

The `crates workspace` CI workflow that runs `test_golden_graph` is path-gated. Neither #188 nor #189 touched a path that triggered it, so the drift accumulated silently. The first PR in a workflow path that *does* run the test (PR #190 — `chore(crypto): drop rand dep`, which touches `Cargo.lock` and forces the crates workspace job) is where the failure showed up. PR #190 is paused on the same branch waiting for this golden bump to land + rebase.

## Diff scope

Exactly 33 lines changed in one file:

- One new feature entry for `156-references-edge-provenance-grammar` (status `approved`, implementation `pending`, depends_on `[154]`)
- One new feature entry for `157-opc-session-model` (status `approved`, implementation `complete`, depends_on `[045]`)
- `graph_fingerprint` updated: `cf787761...` → `5fe1246d...` (the trailing change tracks the feature-set hash, not a content edit of existing entries)

No code change. No spec change. No fingerprint computation logic change. Pure fixture bump.

## Regen recipe

```bash
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test --manifest-path crates/featuregraph/Cargo.toml --test golden
```

## Test plan

- [x] Regen via the recipe above; diff verified to be exactly the two new feature entries + fingerprint update
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path crates/featuregraph/Cargo.toml --test golden` (no UPDATE_GOLDEN) → exit 0
- [ ] CI: `crates workspace` job runs `test_golden_graph` and passes
- [ ] CI: spec-code-coupling gate is unaffected (this is a test-fixture change, not a spec-claimed-path change)

## Follow-up (separate issue, not blocking this PR)

The CI workflow's path-filter that let this drift accumulate from #185 → #189 (4 PRs without the test firing on a touched-corpus change) is the real signal worth fixing. Filing as a separate concern after this lands. The structural fix is to make `test_golden_graph` fire on any change under `specs/**` since that's its actual input surface, not only on changes under `crates/featuregraph/**`.

Once this lands, PR #190 rebases on top to clear its CI.

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: fixture regeneration for accrued spec-corpus drift — the touched file (`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json`) is owned by spec 034 (`featuregraph-registry-scanner-fix`), but no contract under that spec has changed. The fixture is a test golden that captures the current spec inventory; bringing it back in sync with the inventory after specs 156 and 157 landed in #188 / #189 is a hygiene operation, not a refinement of spec 034. Amending spec 034's spec.md to record this regeneration would be receipt-loading the relationship graph for a fixture that's structurally derived from the registry, not authored.

title: chore(crypto): drop rand dep, use rand_core::OsRng directly
body:
## Summary

- Drops the `rand = "0.8"` direct dep from `crates/policy-kernel` and `crates/factory-engine`. Both crates use `rand` only for an `OsRng` handle passed to ed25519-dalek's `SigningKey::generate`; that handle is reachable from `rand_core` directly (which is already in our tree via ed25519-dalek's `rand_core` feature) by enabling rand_core's `getrandom` feature.
- Closes #126 (rand 0.8 → 0.10 in policy-kernel) and #127 (rand 0.8 → 0.10 in factory-engine) by removing the affected dep entirely rather than upgrading it.
- Hand-authored refactor — not a dependabot merge. (See repo discipline: dependabot PRs are bump-availability signal, never click-merged.)

## Why now, not "wait on ed25519-dalek"

- **ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 is still pinned to `rand_core 0.6.4`.** PR #160 to bump it has sat open since the rand 0.7→0.8 era; PR #167 floated *removing* `rand` from ed25519-dalek's public API entirely rather than chasing rand_core versions. Path A ("wait") = "wait indefinitely, with upstream possibly resolving by removing the dep surface altogether."
- **rand 0.10 (Feb 2026) churned the very type we use.** `OsRng` was replaced with `SysRng` (re-exported from `getrandom`); `RngCore` renamed to `Rng`; old `Rng` renamed to `RngExt`; `from_os_rng`/`try_from_os_rng` removed. Trait-and-type identity churn around `OsRng`'s name. Cleanest move: stop being a passenger on that train for code that only needs an OS CSPRNG handle.
- **The existing `Cargo.toml` comment** (`# rand_core 0.6 matches ed25519-dalek 2's expected RNG interface`) becomes literally true at the dep declaration after this change — rand_core is what we depend on, not a parallel tree downstream of rand.

## Diff shape

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml` | `- rand = "0.8"` / `+ rand_core = { version = "0.6", features = ["getrandom"] }` + updated comment |
| `crates/policy-kernel/src/proof_chain.rs:262` | `rand::rngs::OsRng` → `rand_core::OsRng` |
| `crates/factory-engine/Cargo.toml` | same |
| `crates/factory-engine/src/governance_certificate.rs:412` | same |
| `Cargo.lock` | `rand` removed from direct deps of both crates; `rand_core` retained |
| `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` | regenerated (Cargo.toml is an indexer input) |

4 lines of effective code change, 6 files in the diff including index + Cargo.lock churn.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --manifest-path crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml` → exit 0
- [x] `cargo check --manifest-path crates/factory-engine/Cargo.toml` → exit 0
- [x] `cargo test --lib --manifest-path crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml` → **59 passed**; includes `proof_chain::tests::sc009_hundred_record_chain_verifies` which exercises the OsRng path
- [x] `cargo test --lib --manifest-path crates/factory-engine/Cargo.toml` → **185 passed**; includes governance-certificate generation paths
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` (both crates) → clean
- [x] `cargo tree`: `rand` removed from direct dep of both crates; `rand_core 0.6.4` retained
- [x] `make pr-prep`: coupling gate fires on 4 paths (expected — waiver covers); codebase-index refreshed
- [ ] CI: cargo workspace check + clippy across all targets
- [ ] CI: spec-code-coupling gate accepts the `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` annotation

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: dep-removal refactor — identical `OsRng`, identical `SigningKey::generate`, identical crypto behavior. Authority specs governing the touched files (036, 047, 063, 068, 075, 102) have no contract change to record. Amending six spec.md files just to swap `rand::rngs::OsRng` for `rand_core::OsRng` in narrative text would be receipt-loading the relationship graph for a no-op.

## Future direction

If ed25519-dalek #167 ever lands (`SigningKey::generate` taking `[u8; 32]` of entropy instead of an `RngCore` impl), even the `rand_core` direct dep can disappear: `getrandom::fill(&mut seed)` and pass the bytes. Path B's footprint is a strictly shrinking commitment.

## Closes

- #126 — chore(deps): update rand requirement from 0.8 to 0.10 in /crates/policy-kernel
- #127 — chore(deps): update rand requirement from 0.8 to 0.10 in /crates/factory-engine

title: spec(157): OPC session model — multi-session-per-project-path
body:
## Summary

- Lands spec **157-opc-session-model**, a closure spec (`implementation: complete`) that formalises the OPC desktop session discipline already shipped: OPC reads Claude Code's own filesystem-backed JSONL session history under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/<uuid>.jsonl` via four Tauri commands in `claude.rs`. No code changes ride on this PR.
- Symbol-level spec authority over `claude::list_projects`, `claude::get_project_sessions`, `claude::decode_project_path`, and `claude::get_project_path_from_sessions`. Coexists with spec 045's pre-existing file-level wrapping extension on `claude.rs` under spec 154 §6's authority function.
- Four load-bearing claims: filesystem layout, many-sessions-per-project (inverse of AIDE-HARNESS's one-UUID-per-project), JSONL-content-normative-for-identity, non-disambiguating-by-design (inherited from Claude Code).

## Test plan

- [x] `spec-compiler compile` → exit 0; spec 157 visible in registry with `depends_on: ["045"]`, four `establishes:` symbol units, three `references:` entries (`implementation-witness` on sessionStore.ts, `analogous-pattern` on spec 099, `complementary-mechanism` on spec 095).
- [x] `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` → exit 0; no L-005 fires (frontmatter uses unit form throughout, no legacy bare-string paths).
- [x] `codebase-indexer check` → exit 0.
- [x] `make pr-prep` after the last commit → `spec-code-coupling-check: OK — 2 diff path(s) checked. codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean.`
- [x] Spec §7 acceptance: four named symbols exist; closure spec; no code changes required.
- [ ] CI on push: spec-compiler, spec-lint, codebase-indexer staleness, spec-code-coupling gate.
- [ ] CI on push: cross-platform builds (axiomregent, desktop) — should be unaffected since this is a docs-only change to `specs/` + `.derived/`.

## Notes

- **Q-extra absorbed.** §3.3 makes the JSONL-content-over-encoded-directory-name resolution order *normative*, not just defensive. This is the load-bearing detail that distinguishes "OPC reads Claude Code's session model" from "OPC defines its own session model on top." `get_project_path_from_sessions` is authoritative; `decode_project_path` is a lookup-index fallback.
- **Non-disambiguating framing.** §4 states affirmatively that the layout is non-disambiguating across developers *by design* (inherited from Claude Code), not apologetically marked out-of-scope. Per-developer disambiguation is a separable concern; a future spec authoring it extends this surface.
- **Spec 052 not cited.** The original handoff for spec 156 incorrectly named spec 052 (orchestrator workflow state) as spec 157's predecessor. Per design-pass closure, spec 052 has zero touch on `product/apps/desktop/` and is not in the relationship graph. The correction is captured in this PR's commit body, not in the spec corpus — the spec spine doesn't carry receipts.
- **Forward pointer to stagecraft-side ingestion.** §3.4 and §6 explicitly mark the stagecraft-side session-stream ingestion (INTENT §4.2's third claim about "disambiguable session streams at the stagecraft level") as out of scope and deferred to a later spec. The deferral is structural, not lost.

title: feat(codebase-indexer): spec 154 Segment 3 — logical-unit resolver
body:
## Summary

- Adds the codebase-indexer **logical-unit resolver** per spec 154 §6 step 1 — six per-kind dispatchers (`crate`/`symbol`/`module`/`section`/`directory`/`file`), four anchor parsers (Makefile, workflow YAML, region marker, GFM heading), and tree-sitter-rust symbol + module indices. Resolved units surface through a new `resolvedUnits` field on `traceMapping` (schema **2.0.0 → 2.1.0**, strictly additive).
- Closes **Tier 2 Segment 3** of the spec 154 ownership-grammar rollout. Segments 4 (gate refactor consuming `ResolvedUnit`), 5 (corpus migration), and 6 (legacy excision + explicit-only flip) remain.
- **Stop #3 fired and was resolved as A-with-refinement.** The bare-vs-explicit discriminator lives in `UnitEntry.was_explicit` (indexer-internal). Bare-string `MissingFile` → `I-108` (warning, non-blocking, captured for the Segment 5 worklist); explicit `MissingFile` → `I-008` (blocking, mirroring the spec-compiler's V-023). Segment 6's flip is a one-line `diagnostic_code` change in lockstep with V-021..V-024.

## Implementation notes

- **Vendored grammar.** `tree-sitter-rust = { path = \"../../vendor/grammars/tree-sitter-rust\" }` (the grammar at `tools/vendor/grammars/tree-sitter-rust` is the standard Cargo package the upstream maintains). Mirrors xray's pattern at `crates/xray/Cargo.toml:37` but without the feature gate — the resolver is non-optional.
- **Symbol index MVP.** Top-level items + nested `mod foo { ... }` only. `impl<T>` methods, `pub use` re-exports, `cfg`-gated items, and macro-synthesized items are halt-and-surface decision points per the Segment 3 calibration. The corpus today has zero `symbol:` or `module:` units, so none of the four classes are exercised yet — see `memory/project_spec_154_segment_3_symbol_index_mvp.md`.
- **Determinism contract** enforced at the `resolve()` boundary (sort + dedup before return) and at the per-spec batch boundary (sort by `source_field`, `kind`, canonical unit key). Verified byte-identical across runs by `compile_is_byte_deterministic_against_worktree` integration test.
- **Performance.** `compile()` warm = ~0.7s wall-clock on M1 Pro against the full corpus (10s budget per design §7; 14x headroom).
- **Spec 154 frontmatter** extended with `extends: 101-codebase-index-mvp` for the Segment 3 paths so the spec/code coupling gate (spec 127) recognises authored ownership.
- **Handoff doc deleted** per its own lifecycle. Three downstream-capture items migrated to auto-memory:
  - `project_spec_154_segment_5_l005_worklist` — worklist is now L-005 ∪ I-108 ∪ I-101.
  - `project_spec_154_segment_6_explicit_only_flip` — added the resolver-side I-108→I-008 lift step.
  - `project_spec_154_segment_3_symbol_index_mvp` (new) — documents the four stop-#1 halt points.

## Corpus state post-Segment-3

| code  | severity | count | what it means |
|---    |---       |---    |---            |
| I-008 | error    | 0     | explicit `{kind: file, path: X}` whose `X` is absent (blocking). None today. |
| I-108 | warning  | 49    | bare-string `MissingFile` (44 already known via I-101 + 5 net-new from `references:`). Captured for Segment 5. |
| I-101 | warning  | 44    | legacy traceability layer; unchanged. |

650 `ResolvedUnit` entries emitted across 152 mapped specs. Schema validation passes.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path tools/spec-spine/codebase-indexer/Cargo.toml` — 55+ tests pass (28 inline lib + 21 integration + others).
- [ ] `make registry` exits 0 and emits an `index.json` with `\"schemaVersion\": \"2.1.0\"`.
- [ ] `./tools/spec-spine/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer check` exits 0.
- [ ] `make pr-prep` exits 0 and the coupling gate reports OK.
- [ ] `cargo bench --bench resolver -- --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 1` runs all four bench cases.

---

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `tools/spec-spine/spec-code-coupling-check/src/lib.rs` test fixture initialisers gained `resolved_units: Vec::new()` as a type-system-required mechanical follow-on to the additive `TraceMapping.resolved_units` field added by this PR. No behavior change to the coupling gate, the amend protocol (spec 133), or the section-authority machinery (spec 152); the change is strictly the new struct field threaded through the 9 test-side literals so the lib-test build compiles. Owner specs 127 / 133 / 152 are not touched.

title: docs(spec-154): Segment 3 implementation handoff
body:
## Summary

Operational handoff doc for the next session picking up **Tier 2 Segment 3** (codebase-indexer logical-unit resolver). Working-doc lifetime — gets deleted in the Segment-3 closure PR.

Separate from the governance PR (#185) by design. The handoff is ephemeral working state, not permanent governance content; keeping it in its own PR avoids coupling the review surface for spec-155 amendment text (which outlives the segment) to the review surface for "where the next session picks up" (which doesn't).

## What's inside

- **Ground truth pointers** — the four-commit chain (#176, #183, b941bf60, fda92edc), spec 154 + 155, the Segment 3 design doc.
- **Scope boundary** — Segment 3 only; Segments 4–6 explicitly out of scope.

- **Four stop conditions specific to Segment 3** — surface rather than improvise on tree-sitter surprises, perf regressions past 10s warm-compile, unit-set mismatches vs. prior path lists, or determinism violations.
- **Operating-principles reminder** — one segment / one PR / one concern, amend FIRST then implement, SOLID over rushing, surface don't improvise.

## Coordination with PR #185
