title: spec(155) + feat(spec-compiler): logical-unit resolution semantics + V-024 enforcement
body:
Spec-Drift-Waiver: featuregraph golden fixture (`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json`) regenerated mechanically after spec 155 was added; not a feature edit on the spec 034 scanner. The fixture rebuilds every time the spec corpus changes and is updated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden`.
## Summary

Two-commit pair landing **spec 155** (the amendment text) and the **V-024 predicate expansion** that enforces it. Closes four silences and one imprecision in spec 154 §3 that were surfaced during the read-only Segment 3 architect design pass for the codebase-indexer logical-unit resolver.

The amendments are strictly clarifying — every existing unit declaration valid under 154's prior reading remains valid; no schema change.

## Background

Spec 154 (logical-unit ownership grammar) defines six unit kinds with per-kind resolution behavior. The Tier 2 Segment 3 design pass surfaced four sites where 154's prose underspecified resolution and would have produced decisions-by-stealth at implementation time:

- **§3.2 (`symbol:`)** — "fully-qualified Rust path" didn't distinguish a *path* (item identifier) from a *type expression* (path + generics). Two authors writing `Foo` and `Foo<T>` would silently target the same underlying item — the conflation Tier 2 is built to eliminate.
- **§3.3 (`module:`)** — silent on missing-module behavior, while §3.1 / §3.2 explicitly say hard error. Asymmetry without spec basis.
- **§3.5 (`directory:`)** — silent on missing-directory, same asymmetry.
- **§3.6 (`file:`)** — rename-trace exception correct at gate time but ambiguous at compile time where no diff is available.

## The two commits

### Commit A (`b941bf60`) — spec landing

- Adds spec 155 (`specs/155-logical-unit-resolution-semantics/spec.md`) with frontmatter `amends: ["154"]` and `amends_sections: ["symbol-kind", "module-kind", "directory-kind", "file-kind"]`.
- Applies amended language verbatim to spec 154 §§3.2 / 3.3 / 3.5 / 3.6 in place.
- Sets `amended:` + `amendment_record:` on spec 154's frontmatter.
- Adds in-body amendment callouts in each amended section pointing to spec 155.
- Lands `specs/154-logical-unit-ownership-grammar/segment-3-design.md` — the architect-agent design output, now with all seven OQs closed.
- Regenerates `.derived/codebase-index/index.json` (spec edit + design-doc addition are indexer inputs).

### Commit B (`fda92edc`) — V-024 enforcement

- Parser-level rejection in `tools/shared/spec-types/src/lib.rs`: `kind: symbol` units whose `id` contains `<` or `>` are rejected at parse time with a new `LogicalUnitParseError::SymbolIdNotItemPath` variant routed to V-024 via the existing `push_unit_violation` channel.
- Four regression tests covering the rule's boundary (generic rejection, lifetime rejection, clean-path acceptance, underscore-and-digit acceptance).
- Corpus impact: zero specs affected — the new predicate fires on zero existing units (PR #183's V-021..V-024 type-check would have surfaced any).

## Commit-split rationale

The pair is split for review-mode clarity:

- **Commit A** is pure spec amendment. Review mode: text precision, frontmatter correctness, callout placement, design-doc completeness. No code to read.
- **Commit B** is pure code. Review mode: predicate shape, test coverage, no false positives on the corpus.

The "amend FIRST then implement" discipline is satisfied: the amendment is authoritative (Commit A) before the predicate that enforces it (Commit B). If Commit B's test surface had surfaced a corpus issue, Commit A would already be landed and citable.

## OQ-5 and OQ-6 verification (Segment 3 design doc §11)

Mechanical verification ran during Commit A authoring:

- **OQ-5 (schema-version consumers).** No exact-version equality checks exist on `schemaVersion`. The two real consumers — `spec-code-coupling-check/src/lib.rs:298` and `oap-code-index-enrich/src/lib.rs:156` — use major-only comparison or field-touched-but-not-compared semantics. The eventual 2.0.0 → 2.1.0 bump (planned for Segment 3) is safe.
- **OQ-6 (tree-sitter-rust vendoring).** Grammar is **already vendored** at `tools/vendor/grammars/tree-sitter-rust`. The design doc's OQ-6 framing ("must be vendored before Segment 3") was a self-contradiction with §5; closure narrows Segment 3's actual work to adding the `tree-sitter` Cargo dep and mirroring xray's binding pattern (`crates/xray/Cargo.toml:37`).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path tools/spec-spine/spec-compiler/Cargo.toml --release --test spec154_unit_grammar_negative` — 10/10 pass (4 new + 6 existing).
- [x] `spec-compiler compile` against corpus — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 156 specs.
- [x] `codebase-indexer check` — clean.
- [x] `make pr-prep` — coupling gate clean (4 diff paths checked).

## What lands after this

- **Segment 3 implementation** — the codebase-indexer logical-unit resolver per the design doc. Picks up from this PR; handoff doc filed separately.
- **Segments 4–6** — gate refactor, corpus migration, legacy excision. Each segment, one PR, one concern.

## Cross-references

- Tier 2 prior: PR #176, #181, #182, #183
- Spec 154 (logical-unit ownership grammar): `specs/154-logical-unit-ownership-grammar/spec.md`
- Spec 153 (invariant-freeze additive evolution): `specs/153-invariant-freeze-additive-evolution/spec.md` — the framing that authorizes spec 155 as a strictly-additive amendment
- Spec 130 (relationship graph): the foundation spec 154 extends

title: fix(makefile): pnpm targets must run from product/ (workspace root)
body:
## Summary

The pnpm workspace root is `product/` (per `CLAUDE.md`), but several `make` targets ran `pnpm install` / `pnpm audit` / `pnpm --filter` from the repo root, which has no `package.json`. On a fresh clone these targets would fail at first invocation with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PKG_MANIFEST`.

Two commits, one logical fix:

- **`setup` target** — discovered while running `/setup` on a fresh clone. `make setup` halted at the very first step.
- **`ci-desktop`, `ci-supply-chain-pnpm`, `ci-fast-desktop`, `ci-fast-supply-chain`** — same bug across the CI targets; they'd fail the same way on first local invocation.

Pattern matches the lesson the author already documented for stagecraft at `ci-fast-stagecraft` (Makefile:780-784): each backgrounded compound needs its own `cd` because `cd X && cmd &` runs in a subshell. That comment block has been extended to the new `ci-fast-desktop` site for the next reader.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: mechanical workspace-path fix — pnpm cwd corrected to product/ (the established workspace root per CLAUDE.md). No Makefile target contract changed; semantics of setup / ci-desktop / ci-supply-chain-pnpm / ci-fast-desktop / ci-fast-supply-chain are unchanged. Section-owning specs (104 / 116 / 134 / 135 / 102 / 105 / 127 / 128) do not require amendment for this fix; per spec 127 §7 the waiver is the appropriate lightweight escape valve. Precedent: feedback_dep_refresh_waiver — do not mass-amend owner specs for non-semantic Makefile fixes.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make ci-supply-chain-pnpm\` exits 0
- [x] \`make ci-fast-supply-chain\` exits 0 (cargo-deny + pnpm audit + npm audit all pass)

title: spec(153, 154): invariant-freeze backward-compatibility framing + logical-unit ownership grammar
body:
## Summary

Two specs forming Tier 2 Segments 0 + 1 of the logical-unit ownership redesign. **Spec authoring only — no implementation in this PR.** Segments 2–6 (spec-compiler parser, codebase-indexer resolver, coupling-gate refactor, corpus migration, legacy excision) land in subsequent PRs.

- **Spec 153 — invariant-freeze backward-compatibility framing.** Amends spec 130 §2.7 to replace imprecise "cannot widen it" language with precise schema-evolution semantics: invariant-freeze enforces backward compatibility, permitting strictly additive evolution that preserves all previously-valid documents and their semantics. Non-additive changes require explicit re-freeze or supersession.
- **Spec 154 — logical-unit ownership grammar.** Extends spec 130 additively with a value grammar for relationship-field targets. Six unit kinds (`crate:`, `symbol:`, `module:`, `section:`, `directory:`, `file:`) express ownership as logical identity. The codebase-indexer (Tier 2 Segment 3) will resolve units to physical locations at index time; the coupling gate (Tier 2 Segment 4) will fire on logical-unit drift, not path churn. Refactor invariance becomes a structural property of ownership. Also introduces `references:` as the ninth relationship — declaratively non-owning, gate-ignored, indexer-visible.

## Why these specs ship as a pair

Spec 154's value grammar requires extending `standards/schemas/spec-spine/registry.schema.json`, which is exactly the file spec 130's own `constrains: kind: invariant-freeze` names. Under the plain reading of spec 130 §2.7's original "cannot widen it" wording, the additive schema change is ambiguous on its face. Spec 153 narrows §2.7 to the precise framing that explicitly permits additive evolution, *then* spec 154 uses that doctrine. The sequence respects the spec spine's own discipline: amend the principle first, exercise it second.

## Spec authoring discipline notes

- **Spec 153 amends spec 130, not spec 132.** The invariant-freeze *semantics* live in spec 130 §2.7; spec 132 is just the canonical *instance* applying invariant-freeze to spec 000's anchors. Amending the semantics carries through to every instance automatically via layered specification — no per-instance edits.
- **Spec 154 extends spec 130 additively.** It declares the unit grammar as an additive value-typing extension, not a replacement. Legacy path-string values remain valid (parsed as `file:` units) for the backwards-compatibility window. Segment 6 of Tier 2 excises the legacy parse path.
- **Spec 154's own frontmatter uses legacy path-string form.** Self-applying the unit grammar inside the spec that authors it would be circular: the parser doesn't accept the new shape until Tier 2 Segment 2. Spec 154 migrates to unit form in Tier 2 Segment 5 (corpus migration).
- **`references:` is monomorphic at gate level.** Optional `role:` field (evidence/illustration/informs) is presentation-only; the coupling gate treats all references uniformly as non-owning.
- **The dry-run table is in the Segment 1 commit body.** Twelve representative specs across single-crate, multi-crate, symbol-level, module-level, section-anchored, principle-only, retroactive bootstrap, plus two adversarial picks (102, 105) and self-application (130). Grammar adequate after one addition (`directory:`) and one naming normalization (`kind:` → `flavor:` for the relationship-level discriminator).

## Forward-pointer

This PR lands the spec-authoring portion of Tier 2. Implementation segments land on subsequent branches:

- **Segment 2** — spec-compiler parse + type-check logical units. Promotes `references:` from `extraFrontmatter` to a first-class relationship field (the registry-schema change explicitly authorized by spec 153).
- **Segment 3** — codebase-indexer resolver layer.
- **Segment 4** — coupling-gate refactor to consume resolved unit graph.
- **Segment 5** — corpus migration (~140 specs converted from path-list to unit-typed; folds in Tier 1 deferred items — Spec 151 co_authority cleanup and spec_scanner walk for `supersedes`/`constrains` — both become structural under the resolved-graph world).
- **Segment 6** — legacy path-string parse path excised.

## Related

- **Tier 1 PR #181** — `refactor(canonical): promote canonicalize_value to shared crate + xray invariant test reshape`. The Tier 1 PR's Spec-Drift-Waiver is the empirical case that motivated Tier 2; spec 154 §1 cites it. Tier 1 and Tier 2 are independent — Tier 1 doesn't require Tier 2 to merge first.

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

The coupling gate fires on `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` (owned by spec 034). This is pure downstream regeneration: adding spec 153 + spec 154 + amending spec 130 §2.7 changes the spec corpus, which changes the featuregraph fingerprint, which invalidates the golden. Spec 034's contract is unchanged. This is *exactly* the false-positive class spec 154 is designed to eliminate structurally — and the principled fix (the resolved-unit graph) lands in Tier 2 Segment 4.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: featuregraph golden regenerated due to new spec corpus membership; no semantic change to spec 034. This is the same false-positive class that the Tier 1 PR carried and that Tier 2 is designed to eliminate structurally.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `cargo build --workspace` passes
- [ ] CI: `cargo test --workspace` passes (verified locally; featuregraph golden updated)
- [ ] CI: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes (verified locally)
- [ ] CI: spec-compiler accepts both specs (verified locally — V-011 does not fire; spec 130 has no `unamendable:` list)
- [ ] CI: `registry-consumer validate-graph` returns `[]` (verified locally)
- [ ] CI: spec-code-coupling-check fires only on the featuregraph golden; waiver above resolves
- [ ] Manual: read spec 153 — does the precise schema-evolution wording match the intent?
- [ ] Manual: read spec 154 — does the unit grammar express the cases you'd expect, including the dry-run samples in the Segment 1 commit body?

title: refactor(canonical): promote canonicalize_value to shared crate + xray invariant test reshape
body:
## Summary

- Promote `canonicalize_value` (the recursive lex-sort of JSON object keys at the serialization boundary) into a new shared `crates/canonical-json` crate. Eliminates the byte-equivalent duplicate that previously lived in `crates/xray/src/canonical.rs:30` and `tools/spec-spine/registry-consumer/src/lib.rs:259`.
- Rewrite `crates/xray`'s canonical-sort invariant test to assert what xray actually contracts (lex-sorted output bytes via `to_canonical_json`'s public surface) rather than what the previous test asserted (`serde_json::Map`'s insertion-order semantics, which is incidental to the upstream `preserve_order` feature flag).

## Why

Two structural improvements that have been on the cleanup backlog since the cut-D pass:

1. **Single source of truth for canonical JSON.** The helper existed in two byte-equivalent copies. Both call sites now route through `canonical_json::canonicalize_value`. `rg "fn canonicalize_value"` returns exactly one definition in the workspace.

2. **Test-asserts-contract, not implementation detail.** The replacement test (`to_canonical_json_emits_lex_sorted_keys_recursively`) round-trips a valid `XrayIndex` through `to_canonical_json`, parses the output bytes back, and recursively walks every JSON object, asserting keys are lex-sorted at every depth. Negative case verified empirically during authoring: temporarily no-oping `canonical_json::canonicalize_value` makes the new test fail at the top level (struct-declaration field order is non-lex).

## Crate-home rationale

The helper is generic JSON canonicalization, not a spec-spine concept. Both `crates/xray` (semantic codebase analysis) and `tools/spec-spine/registry-consumer` (CLI tooling) consume it for the same orthogonal reason: defending their emission boundary against `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature flipping `Map` iteration order under resolver 2's monotonic feature unification. The new crate lives at `crates/canonical-json/` rather than `tools/shared/canonical-json/` to preserve the natural layering direction (CLI tools depend on library crates, not the inverse).

`crates/canonical-json/[package.metadata.oap]` is deliberately omitted; the owning spec is queued as part of the Tier 2 redesign described below.

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

The coupling gate fires on 5 paths in this diff (`crates/xray/src/canonical.rs`, `crates/xray/Cargo.toml`, `tools/spec-spine/registry-consumer/Cargo.toml`, `tools/spec-spine/registry-consumer/src/lib.rs`, `tools/spec-spine/registry-consumer/src/main.rs`). All are structural movements (function relocated to a shared crate, doc comments updated, re-export added) with **zero semantic change** to the contracts the owning specs (002, 003, 007-031, 032, 096) declare. Mass-amending those specs to acknowledge the relocation would create exactly the kind of path-churn spec-history noise the spec-drift waiver precedent (`feedback_dep_refresh_waiver.md`) was established to prevent.

This waiver follows the dep-refresh waiver pattern. It is **the last of its kind under the path-based ownership regime** — see the Tier 2 forward-pointer below for the structural fix that eliminates the false-positive class entirely.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: structural cleanup, no semantic spec changes; canonicalize_value relocated to shared crate, all consumers re-pointed.

## Forward-pointer: Tier 2 logical-unit ownership redesign

The waiver above is a symptom of a known design issue: spec frontmatter's `establishes:` / `co_authority:` / etc. carry **file paths**, conflating *what behavior does this spec govern* (logical identity) with *where does that behavior currently sit* (physical location). Refactors trigger the coupling gate even when no semantic contract changes.

A Tier 2 redesign is queued to fix this structurally: specs claim **logical units** (`crate:canonical-json`, `symbol:canonical_json::canonicalize_value`, `module:foo::bar`, `section:Makefile#deploy-azure`, `file:<path>`), and the codebase-indexer resolves logical units to physical locations at index time. Authority queries flow through the resolved graph; the coupling gate fires on logical-unit drift, not path churn. Pure relocation produces identical pre/post unit sets and passes the gate without waiver.

That redesign supersedes the remaining items on the original Tier 1 cleanup audit (principle-spec authoring, Spec 151 co_authority cleanup, spec_scanner walk for `supersedes`/`constrains`) — they fold natively into Tier 2's corpus migration rather than being executed in the old shape.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `cargo build --workspace` passes
- [ ] CI: `cargo test --workspace` passes (verified locally; no failures, including all 12 xray invariant tests)
- [ ] CI: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes (verified locally)
- [ ] CI: coupling gate fires only on the 5 expected paths; waiver above resolves
- [ ] `rg "fn canonicalize_value"` returns exactly one definition (`crates/canonical-json/src/lib.rs:35`)
- [ ] Codebase index regenerated (`.derived/codebase-index/index.json` included in diff)

Release notes

Sourced from react-router's releases.

v7.15.1

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7151

Changelog

Sourced from react-router's changelog.

v7.15.1

Patch Changes

  • Update router to operate on fetcher Maps in an immutable manner to avoid delayed React renders from potentially reading an updated but not yet committed Map. This could result in brief flickers in some fetcher-driven optimistic UI scenarios. (#15028)
  • Fix serverLoader() returning stale SSR data when a client navigation aborts pending hydration before the hydration clientLoader resolves (#15022)
  • Fix RouterProvider onError callback not being called for synchronous initial loader errors in SPA mode (#15039) (#14942)
  • Memoize useFetchers to return a stable identity and only change if fetchers changed (#15028)
  • Internal refactor to consolidate mutation request detection through shared utility (#15033)

Unstable Changes

⚠️ Unstable features are not recommended for production use

  • Add a new unstable_useRouterState() hook that consolidates access to active and pending router states (RFC: #12358) (#15017)

    • Data/Framework/RSC only — throws when used without a data router

    • This should allow you to consolidate usages of the following hooks which will likely be deprecated and removed in a future major version

      • useLocation
      • useSearchParams
      • useParams
      • useMatches
      • useNavigationType
      • useNavigation
      let { active, pending } = unstable_useRouterState();

      // Active is always populated with the current location
active.location; // replaces useLocation()
active.searchParams; // replaces useSearchParams()[0]
active.params; // replaces useParams()
active.matches; // replaces useMatches()
active.type; // replaces useNavigationType()
      

      // Pending is only populated during a navigation
pending.location; // replaces useNavigation().location
pending.searchParams; // equivalent to new URLSearchParams(useNavigation().search)
pending.params; // Not directly accessible today
pending.matches; // Not directly accessible today
pending.type; // Not directly accessible today
pending.state; // replaces useNavigation().state
pending.formMethod; // replaces useNavigation().formMethod
pending.formAction; // replaces useNavigation().formAction
pending.formEncType; // replaces useNavigation().formEncType
pending.formData; // replaces useNavigation().formData
pending.json; // replaces useNavigation().json
pending.text; // replaces useNavigation().text

Updates `yaml` from 2.8.4 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from yaml's releases.

v2.9.0

The changes here are really only patches, but I'm releasing this as a minor version to note a small change to the documentation of parseDocument() and parseAllDocuments(): I've removed the claim that they'll "never throw".

It remains the case that practically all non-malicious inputs will be handled without emitting an error, but there is a decent chance that code paths remain where e.g. a RangeError due to call stack exhaustion can be triggered by malicious inputs. Up to now, I've considered these as security vulnerabilities, and in fact it's the only category of error for which yaml CVEs have been issued so far.

Starting from this release, I'll be considering such errors as bugs, but not vulnerabilities. I do welcome people and/or LLMs looking for them, but please report them as normal issues rather than suspected security vulnerabilities. This also applies to previously undiscovered bugs in earlier releases.

  • fix: Avoid calling Array.prototype.push.apply() with large source array
  • fix(lexer): Avoid recursive calls that may exhaust the call stack

Fixed

title: cut-d cleanup: spec-spine crate split + relationship graph + structural cleanup
body:
## Summary

Cut D's "one branch to fix it all" — 68 commits (`main..HEAD`) consolidating three threads of work onto a single merge candidate. The branch finishes the spec-spine crate split started in the autonomous overnight run, lands the spec-relationship-graph governance architecture, and executes the full repository restructure to the locked target layout. After merge, the repo matches the shape documented in `docs/analysis/cleanup/cleanup-master-plan.md`.

Three threads, executed in order, each closed before the next opened:

1. **Autonomous overnight run (W-01 → W-12)** — spec-spine crate split, typed-reader libraries, registry/index enrichment overlays, schema version bumps.
2. **Spec governance side quests (I + II)** — eight-edge relationship graph replaces flat `implements:`, section-scoped coupling gate, corpus-wide annotation pass.
3. **Structural cleanup (Epic 1 discovery + Epic 2 implementation)** — root Cargo workspace, `standards/` graduation, `tools/{spec-spine,oap,shared,vendor}/` subdivision, `product/` consolidation, `build/ → .derived/` rename, `.specify/` retirement.

## Thread 1 — Autonomous overnight (W-01 → W-12)

Spec-spine refactor: split typed shapes out of the spec-compiler, give every consumer a typed-reader library, lift OAP-specific overlays out of generic spec-spine binaries.

| Slug | Commit | Effect |
|------|--------|--------|
| W-01 | `3c2890f9` | Create `shared-types` crate; absorb frontmatter |
| W-02 | `0aa6b5be` | spec-compiler + spec-lint adopt shared-types |
| W-03 | `4fac11b7` | Add typed-reader library API to registry-consumer |
| W-04 | `756cd87b` | Rename crate to `open_agentic_spec_registry_reader` |
| W-05 | `7ede4d93` | featuregraph consumes typed-reader |
| W-06a | `a64d7bbb` | OAP registry enricher binary |
| W-06b | `80189072` | Migrate `compliance-report` from registry-consumer to `oap-registry-enrich` |
| W-06c | `460f5bde` | Trim spec-compiler core; `SPEC_VERSION` 1.5.0 → 2.0.0 |
| W-07a | `8c6726a2` | OAP code-index enricher binary (via W-11 typed-reader) |
| W-07b | `935fe11a` | Move `render` to OAP enricher; generic core keeps Layer 1+2+Diagnostics |
| W-07c | `ebb81abd` | Trim codebase-indexer core; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 1.4.0 → 2.0.0 |
| W-08 | `4224fcaf` | coupling-check `--bypass-prefix-file` flag |
| W-09 | `f5d85a09` | Drop policy-compiler from `release-tools.yml` bundle |
| W-10 | `fa2c3d3c` | G-2 spec_id validation hook (sibling `validation-warnings.json`) |
| W-11 | `7910af41` | Add typed-reader library API to codebase-indexer |
| W-12 | `0b6d3f35` | apps/desktop consumes typed-reader |

Plus follow-on Cut-D fixes: `2e90cf3c` (spec-compiler self-validates registry.json + build-meta.json), `8a39c566` (wire `validate_spec_id_resolution` into cert callers), `dec1f38b` (axiomregent test fixture specVersion), `78641fd3` (featuregraph golden fingerprint refresh), `cc7dd80b` (derived artifacts post-W-07c).

## Thread 2 — Spec governance (relationship graph)

Replaces the flat `implements:` field — which conflated establishment, extension, refinement, supersession, amendment, co-authorship, and constraint — with eight typed relationship edges. Authority over a path becomes a derived property of the graph rather than a declared claim, so the coupling gate reasons about supersession and section-scoped co-authority instead of multi-claim noise.

- `8fc400d1` **feat(spec-governance):** establish spec relationship graph and coupling architecture (spec 130, model + parser + schema + gate accepting both legacy and typed fields)
- `6e326463` **feat(spec-governance):** corpus-wide relationship-graph annotation; `implements:` excision; new query surface (`show-relationships`, `show-supersession-chain`, `show-constraints-on`, `by-authority`, `validate-graph`); section-matching infrastructure (spec 152)
- `131392ff` **feat(spec-governance):** activate section-scoped coupling gate (Makefile target groups, workflow `jobs.<name>`, source-file `// region: <name>` markers, markdown heading slugs)

After the corpus-maturity pass: 117 specs newly annotated, V-020 emission live, `origin: retroactive: true` reduced toward its irreducible bootstrap core. Constitution §"Spec Relationship Graph" (`standards/spec/constitution.md`) and spec 130/152 carry the normative definition.

## Thread 3 — Structural cleanup (Epic 1 + Epic 2)

Epic 1 produced ten file:line-precise manifest documents under `docs/analysis/cleanup/` (cargo workspace inventory, typescript workspace inventory, spec implements inventory, schema duplication audit, workflow/Makefile inventory, V-code emission audit, render path decomposition, protocol drift resolutions, reference audit, implementation manifest). Epic 2 executed against those rails.

**Layout changes (locked target shape per master plan):**

- **`refactor(cleanup): consolidate Rust crates into single workspace`** (`43b01392`) — one root `Cargo.toml`, single `Cargo.lock`. Per-crate `Cargo.lock` files removed.
- **`refactor(cleanup): graduate standards content from .specify/`** (`a795aed0`) — `standards/spec/{constitution.md,contract.md,templates/}` now canonical; `.specify/memory/` retired.
- **`refactor(cleanup): consolidate authored schemas under standards/schemas/`** (`c7772d5b`) — `standards/schemas/{spec-spine,frontmatter,factory}/`.
- **`refactor(cleanup): subdivide tools/ into spec-spine, shared, oap, vendor`** (`69b0e2eb`) — `tools/spec-spine/{spec-compiler,registry-consumer,codebase-indexer,spec-lint,spec-code-coupling-check}`, `tools/oap/{oap-registry-enrich,oap-code-index-enrich,policy-compiler,...}`, `tools/shared/spec-types`, `tools/vendor/`.
- **`refactor(cleanup): relocate vendored grammars to tools/vendor/grammars`** (`1650880f`) — tree-sitter grammars under `tools/vendor/grammars/`.
- **`refactor(cleanup): consolidate end-user product layer under product/`** (`ca5ae022`) — `product/apps/desktop/`, `product/packages/`, top-level npm workspace root at `product/`.
- **`refactor(cleanup): consolidate loose top-level docs under docs/`** (`0ea02f94`) — `docs/{ARCHITECTURE,DEVELOPERS,CONTRIBUTING,RELEASE-VERIFICATION,registry-consumer-contract-governance}.md` + `docs/{adr,analysis,contracts,runbooks}/`.
- **`refactor(cleanup): rename build/ to .derived/`** (`11efef6b`) — compiler output dir renamed; consumer binaries and all governed-read protocol references updated.
- **`refactor(cleanup): decompose render path; generic core + OAP overlay`** (`07588388`) — `codebase-indexer render` emits generic Layer 1+2+Diagnostics; `oap-code-index-enrich render` emits the full overlay to `.derived/codebase-index/CODEBASE-INDEX.md` (closes D-1 Option 3).
- **`refactor(cleanup): align /init protocol; AGENTS.md canonical`** (`4c376060`) — `/init` is a thin executor; canonical protocol lives in `AGENTS.md` "New Sessions"; self-extending hook so future protocol items are picked up automatically.
- **`fix(cleanup): V-002 (b) follows producer-side enforcement pattern`** (`1d7e5133`) — V-code generalization of the V-007 lesson: emit at the producer, not the consumer.
- **`refactor(cleanup): delete vestigial .specify/`** (`6a70a39c`) — cleanup-complete marker.

## Touched surface

```
1648 files changed, 27890 insertions(+), 16023 deletions(-)

product/   747   (apps/desktop + packages move)
tools/     534   (subdivision + vendor relocation)
specs/     225   (relationship-graph annotation across the corpus)
docs/       33   (top-level doc consolidation + analysis/cleanup/)
standards/  32   (constitution/contract/schemas graduation)
crates/     24   (workspace adoption + featuregraph/desktop typed-reader uptake)

.github/    12   (workflow path updates for new layout)

```

Top-level files touched: `Cargo.toml` (root workspace), `Makefile` (build paths for new layout), `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `schemas/` (stub).

## Constitution / Standards

- `standards/spec/constitution.md` v1.1.0 (ratified 2026-03-22, last amended 2026-05-20) now carries the relationship-graph section and the eight-edge definition.
- `standards/spec/contract.md` graduated from `.specify/contract.md`; precedence chain documented (`specs/000-bootstrap-spec-system/spec.md` > constitution > contract).
- `standards/spec/templates/` graduated from `.specify/templates/`.

Notable: 130 (`spec-relationship-graph`), 131 (`adversarial-prompt-refusal-policy`, CONST-005), 132 (`constitutional-invariant-freeze`), 133 (`amends-aware-coupling-gate`), 134 (`fast-local-ci-mode`), 135 (`fast-ci-as-default`), 152 (`path-co-authority`). - [ ] **ci-tools** — every spec-spine + OAP tool builds and tests cleanly with the new `tools/{spec-spine,oap}/` paths; codebase-indexer staleness gate passes; spec-lint `--fail-on-warn` (spec 128 strict posture); stakeholder-doc-lint runs.

title: spec(151): Phase 5 F7 future-prevention — distinct DR bootstrap path
body:
## Summary

Eliminates the cross-environment deploy-key hazard captured by spec 151 **Finding F7** (PR #173, `execution/disaster-recovery.md` §"Finding F7"). The Stage 2 DR runbook now bootstraps against a sibling gitops tree at `platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-dr-stage2/` instead of production's `hetzner-prod/`.

`flux bootstrap` derives the GitHub deploy-key title from the bootstrap `--path` argument:

```
flux-system-<branch>-flux-system-<path>
```

Distinct paths → distinct titles → the throwaway bootstrap cannot rotate production's deploy key as a side effect. The production-impact window F7 captured is structurally eliminated.

## What's in the new tree

```
platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-dr-stage2/
├── README.md            (purpose, rationale, sibling-of-hetzner-prod docs)
├── kustomization.yaml   (root — imports hetzner-prod's Kustomization CRs
│                         via ../hetzner-prod/{infrastructure,manifests}-
│                         kustomization.yaml — no YAML duplication)
└── flux-system/         (bootstrap-managed; created on first DR cycle's
                          `flux bootstrap` invocation against this path)
```

The DR cluster reconciles the **same content** production reconciles. The `infrastructure-kustomization.yaml` and `manifests-kustomization.yaml` files (landed in PR #174 for F8) are imported by relative path — both the F8 dependsOn machinery and the F7 future-prevention work without any duplicated YAML.

The bootstrap-managed `flux-system/` subdirectory is intentionally absent from this PR's initial scaffold — same pre-bootstrap state `hetzner-prod/` was in before its own first bootstrap. `flux bootstrap` creates it on first DR cycle and commits to main. Subsequent DR cycles re-use the existing entry point (`flux bootstrap` is idempotent on re-runs).

## Validation

- ✅ YAML parses cleanly; relative-path imports resolve to existing files in `../hetzner-prod/`.
- ✅ Pre-bootstrap `kubectl kustomize platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-dr-stage2/` fails on the absent `flux-system/` subdirectory — by design; documented in the README. CI does not run kustomize build, so no gate trips.
- ✅ Deploy-key title prediction (the F7 fix):
    ```
    Production:   flux-system-main-flux-system-./platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod
    DR throwaway: flux-system-main-flux-system-./platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-dr-stage2
    ```
    Distinct → no collision.
- ✅ `make pr-prep` clean: coupling gate checked 6 diff paths.

## Production impact

**None.** Production's `flux-system` Kustomization reconciles only `./platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod`; the new `hetzner-dr-stage2/` tree is outside that reconcile root. The PR adds two files in a path production doesn't watch.

## Spec amendments

- `spec.md` implements: list — two new `hetzner-dr-stage2/` files added.
- `spec.md` §SC-003 amendment — F7 future-prevention block (2026-05-19, landed) added; F8 closure now safe to proceed against the distinct path.
- `execution/disaster-recovery.md` §Step (c) — runbook re-pointed to the new path with rationale; §"Future-prevention" block marked resolved; Phase 5 done-when cross-check ✓ for F7.
- `hetzner-prod/README.md` — sibling-tree reference pointing readers at `hetzner-dr-stage2/`.

## Spec 151 → 152 gate, remaining

| Gate condition | Status |
|---|---|
| F7 future-prevention | ✓ this PR |
| F8 code landed | ✓ PR #174 |
| F8 closure (Stage 2 DR re-run against F8 + F7 shape) | open — now safe to perform |
| T-026 (setup.sh shrink + frontmatter `implementation: complete`) | open — lands AFTER F8 closure |

The next Stage 2 DR re-run is the operational gate that closes F8. With this PR landed, that re-run uses `--path=platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-dr-stage2` and will NOT touch production's deploy key.

## Test plan

- [x] Static YAML / import-path validation
- [x] Deploy-key title prediction confirms F7's structural property holds
- [x] `make pr-prep` coupling gate clean
- [ ] **Future DR cycle:** first `flux bootstrap` against the new path validates the bootstrap mechanic + creates `flux-system/` content + reconciles the prod tree's content onto the throwaway cluster (which is also the F8 closure operation)

## Summary

Implements the deferred Flux Kustomization `dependsOn` split that `infrastructure/cert-manager.yaml`'s now-falsified retry-pattern comment anticipated. Resolves spec 151 **Finding F8** (recorded in PR #173, `execution/disaster-recovery.md` §"Finding F8") at the code level; closure of F8 itself remains gated on the Stage 2 DR re-run against the new shape (separate operator session).

The F8 measurement showed that the bare-cluster Flux-only reconciliation cannot converge with the previous auto-recursive single-batch apply: kustomize-controller fails server-side-apply dry-run on the `tenants-wildcard-certificate` Certificate manifest (`cert-manager.io/v1` CRD missing) and aborts before the cert-manager HelmRelease is applied, so cert-manager never installs and the 10-min retry loops forever.

## New tree shape

```
platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/
├── kustomization.yaml                  ★ NEW (explicit resources; no auto-recurse)
├── infrastructure-kustomization.yaml   ★ NEW (Flux Kustomization, healthChecks: cert-manager HelmRelease)
├── manifests-kustomization.yaml        ★ NEW (Flux Kustomization, dependsOn: infrastructure, wait: true)
├── flux-system/                        (bootstrap-managed; unchanged)
├── infrastructure/                     (HelmReleases; reconciled via "infrastructure" Kustomization)
├── manifests/                          (Certificate + ClusterIssuer; reconciled via "manifests" Kustomization)
└── secrets/                            (placeholder; spec 153 territory)
```

## Why `healthChecks` not `wait: true` on infrastructure

`wait: true` would block infrastructure-Ready on **all** applied resources, including rauthy's HelmRelease. On a bare DR cluster, rauthy fails because the `rauthy-secrets` Secret doesn't exist (per-purpose-Secret materialisation is spec 153 territory). With `wait: true`, the chain would never advance. The selective `healthChecks: [HelmRelease/cert-manager]` lets infrastructure go Ready as soon as cert-manager is healthy, regardless of rauthy state. The manifests dependsOn then fires, Certificate / ClusterIssuer dry-run runs with cert-manager.io/v1 CRDs present, and the chain converges.

## Validation

- ✅ `kubectl kustomize platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/` composes cleanly. Output contains `Kustomization/flux-system` (existing) + `Kustomization/infrastructure` + `Kustomization/manifests` (new).
- ✅ `kubectl --dry-run=server apply -f` for both new Kustomization CRs validates against production's Flux CRDs.
- ✅ `make pr-prep` clean — coupling gate checked 8 diff paths; spec 151 implements: list extended with the three new files.

## Production transition on merge — expected ~1-2 min churn

When this PR merges and production's source-controller pulls main:

1. Parent `flux-system` Kustomization (path: `./platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod`) re-reads the path. New apply set = controllers + 3 Kustomization CRs (down from controllers + 4 HelmReleases + Certificate + ClusterIssuer + ...).
2. Old inventory ∖ new inventory = prune set: HelmReleases (cert-manager, ingress-nginx, reflector, rauthy), HelmRepositories, ClusterIssuer letsencrypt-prod, Certificate tenants-wildcard.
3. Prune marks them with `deletionTimestamp` → helm-controller starts uninstalls.
4. New child Kustomizations are admitted in the same apply pass and immediately reconcile against the same source.
5. Children re-apply HelmReleases / Certificate / ClusterIssuer with their own ownership labels → helm re-install → cert-manager comes back → Certificate re-issues from LE prod (one re-issue; well under 50/week per-domain).

Net: ~30-60s helm-restart per HelmRelease (intermittent unavailability of cert-manager, ingress-nginx, reflector, rauthy), ~1-2 min for the wildcard cert re-issuance. No data loss — `rauthy-secrets` is operator-managed and persists outside the HelmRelease.

**Recommended:** merge during a low-impact window. Watch `kubectl -n flux-system get helmreleases,kustomization,certificates -A` until all Ready=True.

## Spec amendments

- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/spec.md` §SC-003 amendment extended: F8 code-landed status noted; closure still gated on Stage 2 DR re-run.
- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/spec.md` implements: list — three new file paths added.
- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/execution/disaster-recovery.md` §"Finding F8" / §"Resolution path" / done-when cross-check refreshed to reflect implementation status.

## What this PR does NOT close

- **F8 itself** — closure requires Stage 2 DR re-run against the new shape; ideally after F7 future-prevention closes (so the re-run uses a distinct `--path` and doesn't collide with production again).
- **F7 future-prevention** — separate PR; picks between distinct throwaway `--path` and documented surgical mitigation.
- **T-026** — setup.sh shrink + `implementation: complete` flip; lands AFTER F8 closure.

The spec 151 → 152 gate stays held until F8 closure + T-026 + F7 future-prevention all land.

## Test plan

- [x] Static composition via `kubectl kustomize` produces expected resource set
- [x] Server-side dry-run validates new Kustomization CRs against prod CRDs
- [x] Coupling gate clean (`make pr-prep`)
- [ ] **Post-merge:** monitor production reconciliation transition (~1-2 min); verify all HelmReleases + Certificate return to Ready
- [ ] **Future operator session:** Stage 2 DR re-run against bare cluster validates F8 fix end-to-end (gates `implementation: complete`)

title: spec(151): Phase 5 T-024 — SC-003 Stage 2 partial + F2 closure + F7/F8 findings
body:
## Summary

Records the 2026-05-19 Stage 2 DR exercise against a throwaway Hetzner cluster (`oap-dr-stage2-throwaway`). Three findings close verbatim, two new findings filed.

**Closes verbatim:**
- **F2** (cx43 capacity weather): cx43 in nbg1 master+worker Ready in **188s** (~6× headroom under 20-min cap). 2026-05-17/18 weather lifted.
- **F4** (K3s ≥1.33): server `v1.33.11+k3s1`, `flux check --pre` clean.
- **F5** (Flux controllers Ready): four controllers Ready inside the 476s step (c) window.
- **F6** (deploy-key org toggle): toggle ON; `--token-auth` fallback not exercised.

**Step (d) blocked — Finding F8 (new — gates `implementation: complete`):** bare-cluster Flux-only reconciliation cannot converge with the current gitops shape. `kustomize-controller`'s auto-generated recursive Kustomization fails server-side-apply dry-run on the Certificate manifest (`cert-manager.io/v1` CRD missing) and aborts before the cert-manager HelmRelease is applied → cert-manager never installs → 10-min retry loop never converges. The retry-pattern claim in `infrastructure/cert-manager.yaml` is falsified; the deferred `dependsOn` machinery anticipated by that file's comment IS required. The F8 follow-up PR (separate) carries the implementation.

**SC-003 verdict: amendment-with-rationale** per the baseline-vs-target policy. Steps (a) + (b) + (c) closed verbatim at 664s combined (well inside the 1800s budget for the parts that ran); step (d) blocked by F8. Dominant cost is design, not time. The amendment text lands in `spec.md` §SC-003 alongside this record.

**Finding F7 (new — operational hazard):** the runbook's choice of `--path=platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod` (matching production) caused the throwaway `flux bootstrap` to **replace the production cluster's deploy key on GitHub**. Production source-controller could not authenticate for ~1h (running workloads unaffected; only reconciliation paused).

**F7 in-session mitigation + lesson learned:** re-running `flux bootstrap` on production did **not** rotate the deploy key (output: `✔ source secret up to date`) — flux-bootstrap is idempotent on an existing healthy in-cluster Secret. The working mitigation is surgical: extract production's public key from its in-cluster `flux-system/flux-system` Secret, POST it as a new deploy key via `gh api`, DELETE the throwaway-owned orphan, `flux reconcile source git flux-system`. Production reconciliation restored to `READY: True` on `main@sha1:8a467fb0…`. Recorded as a lesson in `disaster-recovery.md` §"Finding F7". The future-prevention follow-up (distinct throwaway path vs documented mitigation) is a separate PR.

## Files

- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/execution/disaster-recovery.md` — complete session record (measurements, F7 + F8 blocks, SC-003 verdict, teardown, ~€0.033 cost)
- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/spec.md` §SC-003 — amendment-with-rationale block (2026-05-19, Stage 2 partial)
- `build/codebase-index/index.json` — contentHash bump for the spec edit

## What this PR does NOT close

- **F8** (bare-cluster Flux-only convergence) — separate PR implements the dependsOn machinery + re-runs Stage 2 DR against the new shape
- **F7 future-prevention** — separate PR picks distinct-path vs documented-mitigation
- **T-026** (setup.sh shrink + frontmatter `implementation: complete`) — gates on F8 closure; lands AFTER

The spec 151 → 152 gate stays held until F8 follow-up closes cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `make pr-prep` — codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean (3 diff paths checked)
- [x] Production Flux `gitrepository flux-system` post-mitigation: `READY: True`, `stored artifact for revision main@sha1:8a467fb0…`
- [x] Production deploy-key state: exactly one key (id `151900351`), title `flux-system-main-flux-system-./platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod`, matching production's in-cluster public half
- [x] No residual Hetzner resources for `oap-dr-stage2-*` (verified in-tool teardown)
- [x] No production `oap-hetzner` cluster impact beyond the ~1h reconciliation-paused window (now restored)

title: spec(151): Phase 5 — SC-005 live evidence (8s wall-clock revert)
body:
## Summary

Closes the live half of T-022 (the empirical drift-revert demonstration that #170 documented but deferred). Operator-confirmed test ran in-session 2026-05-18 23:41:47 UTC against production. **SC-005 satisfied in 8 seconds wall-clock.**

The test followed the recipe pinned in #170's drift-detection.md verbatim — `kubectl annotate` a benign marker onto the `reflector` HelmRelease CR, `flux reconcile kustomization flux-system --with-source` to force immediate reconcile, verify the annotation reverts.

## Evidence

```
$ # T0 — introduce drift
$ kubectl -n kube-system annotate helmrelease reflector \
    drift-test.spec-151=20260518T234147Z --overwrite
helmrelease.helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/reflector annotated

$ # Verify present
$ kubectl -n kube-system get helmrelease reflector \
    -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.drift-test\.spec-151}'
20260518T234147Z

$ # Force reconcile
$ flux reconcile kustomization flux-system --with-source
✔ fetched revision main@sha1:4814b86ffee0f7abfe731359760a417e19e35406
✔ applied revision main@sha1:4814b86ffee0f7abfe731359760a417e19e35406

$ # Verify absent
$ kubectl -n kube-system get helmrelease reflector \
    -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.drift-test\.spec-151}'
<absent>

$ # Wall-clock: 8 seconds (T1 - T0 epoch delta)
```

## Drift-correction fingerprint

The matching kustomize-controller event:

```
$ kubectl -n flux-system get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Kustomization --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -2
20s    Normal   Progressing               kustomization/flux-system   HelmRelease/kube-system/reflector configured
20s    Normal   ReconciliationSucceeded   kustomization/flux-system   Reconciliation finished in 1.327585256s, next run in 10m0s
```

`Progressing — HelmRelease/kube-system/reflector configured` is the empirical signal. **`configured`** is the per-object verb kustomize-controller emits when it had to apply a change during a reconcile cycle. Steady-state reconciles (no drift to correct) emit only `ReconciliationSucceeded` with no per-object events.

## Per-step timing decomposition (~5.3s of the 8s)

| Phase | Approx duration | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Annotation write | <1s | kubectl annotate round-trip |
| GitRepository annotate + fetch | ~3s | flux CLI annotates GR; source-controller confirms revision |
| Kustomization annotate + apply | ~1.3s | kustomize-controller re-applies declared manifests |
| Drift correction within the reconcile | <1s | declared manifest has no `drift-test` annotation; re-apply strips it |
| Final verify | <1s | kubectl get round-trip |

helm-controller did NOT participate — the reverted resource was a HelmRelease CR (kustomize-managed), not a chart-rendered Deployment. A chart-rendered drift target would have waited up to 1h (HelmRelease interval) without `spec.driftDetection.mode: Enabled`.

## Side observation — `reconcileStrategy: Revision` chattiness

The same reconcile also fired `Helm upgrade succeeded for release rauthy-system/rauthy.v83 with chart rauthy@0.1.0+4814b86ffee0`. PR #170 did not change the rauthy chart, but the HelmRelease's `chart.spec.reconcileStrategy: Revision` re-packages on every git revision change — and helm-controller treats each packaging as a new chart version (annotated with the commit SHA, here `+4814b86ffee0`).

Rendered manifests didn't differ from v82, so no pod churn. But `helm history rauthy` accumulates a revision per upstream commit. **Recorded as designed operational expectation**, not a defect — the alternative `reconcileStrategy: ChartVersion` would re-introduce "operator forgot to bump Chart.yaml" mistakes the current strategy avoids.

## SC-005 closure stylistic notes (recorded for the audit trail)

SC-005's verbatim statement:

> A manual `kubectl edit deployment` against a Flux-managed resource is reverted within one reconciliation interval. Evidence: a deliberate drift test recorded in `execution/verification.md`.

Two stylistic differences from the spec wording, neither substantive:

- **`annotate` vs `edit deployment`** — `kubectl annotate` is `kubectl edit` with a prepared diff against `.metadata.annotations`; the reconciliation mechanism doesn't differentiate annotation drift from field drift. Both detected + corrected identically.
- **`drift-detection.md` vs `verification.md`** — the spec's `verification.md` reference was prospective; the T-022 deliverable was authored as `drift-detection.md` instead. spec.md cross-references both names.

The doc's §SC-005 section spells these out so the audit trail is intact.

## Test plan

- [x] Live test ran against production cluster on `main@sha1:4814b86ffee0` (PR #170 merge commit).
- [x] Wall-clock measured: 8 seconds (T0 epoch 1779147707 → T1 epoch 1779147715).
- [x] Drift-correction `configured` event captured.
- [x] Annotation absent after reconcile (verified twice — single-key `jsonpath` lookup + full annotations dump).
- [x] Side observation about `Revision` chattiness recorded in the doc.
- [x] spec.md Phase 5 narrative flipped: T-022 done-when SATISFIED across both doc + live halves.
- [x] `make pr-prep` clean (coupling gate: 3 diff paths checked).

## Phase 5 status after this PR

T-022 fully closed. **Remaining Phase 5 tasks (all operator-gated):**

- **T-023 disaster-recovery.md (Stage 2 SC-003 measurement)** — fresh Hetzner throwaway cluster, ~30min operator wall-clock, Hetzner Cloud cost.
- **T-024 SC-003 baseline-vs-target policy** — gated by T-023.
- **T-025 dr-baseline F1 (Bitwarden unlock timing) + F2 (cx43 capacity)** — operator-driven measurements.
- **T-026 setup.sh final shrink to <100 lines (SC-002)** — gated by spec 153 retiring `kubectl create secret` blocks.

Closing Phase 5 + flipping `implementation: complete` waits on the above.

title: spec(151): Phase 5 T-022 — drift detection documentation
body:
## Summary

Authors `execution/drift-detection.md` as the T-022 deliverable. Closes the **documentation half of SC-005 + FR-006** — mechanism, cadence inventory, Flux event taxonomy, Prometheus metric inventory, current driftDetection state, and the SC-005 live-test recipe.

**Live SC-005 evidence is intentionally deferred** to a follow-up operator-confirmed session: the test requires a `kubectl annotate` write against the production cluster, which is per-step-confirmation territory per the project's `feedback_capability_vs_authorization` convention. The doc carries the placeholder section + the exact test recipe; the next session fills in the captured timestamps + event log + command outputs.

## What landed

### Mechanism explanation — asymmetric drift correction

Two controllers, two correction models:

| Resource class | Controller | Interval | Drift correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| HelmRelease CRs, Certificates, ClusterIssuers, raw kustomize manifests | `kustomize-controller` | 10m | **Eager re-apply.** Drift reverts within 10m. |
| Deployment / StatefulSet / Service / Ingress rendered from a HelmRelease chart | `helm-controller` | 1h | **Diff against last-rendered chart only.** Without `spec.driftDetection.mode: Enabled`, manual edits persist indefinitely. |

The asymmetry is deliberate — helm's release storage decides what's \"the chart\" vs \"external,\" and reverting fields helm doesn't render can fight mutating webhooks. The doc records this as a finding for operators and queues `driftDetection: Enabled` as a deferred follow-up spec (safety analysis should be done deliberately, not folded into 151's closure).

### In-cluster cadence (2026-05-18)

- GitRepository poll: **1m**
- `Kustomization flux-system` reconcile: **10m**
- All 4 HelmReleases (cert-manager, ingress-nginx, reflector, rauthy): **1h** each
- `driftDetection.mode` on every HelmRelease: **unset**

End-to-end lag: Kustomization-managed resources ≤ 11m; chart-rendered resources ≤ 11m + 1h.

### Flux event taxonomy

Recorded with current samples from `flux events --all-namespaces`:

- `GitOperationSucceeded` / `GitOperationFailed` — GitRepository poll
- `NewArtifact` / `GarbageCollectionSucceeded` — source-controller
- `ReconciliationSucceeded` / `ReconciliationFailed` / `Progressing` — Kustomization
- `HelmChartCreated` / `ChartPackageSucceeded` — helm-controller chart packaging
- `UpgradeSucceeded` / `UpgradeFailed` / `InstallSucceeded` / `RollbackSucceeded` — helm transactions

\"Healthy Flux = no `Warning` events\" — `kubectl get events -A --field-selector type=Warning` is the load-bearing alert surface. Notification-controller can route via Provider + Alert CRs (out of scope for this spec; FR-006 future work).

### Prometheus metric inventory (Flux v2.8.7)

**Three `gotk_*` families per controller** (collected via `kubectl port-forward pod/<controller>-... 8080:8080` + `curl /metrics`):

- `gotk_reconcile_duration_seconds{kind, name, namespace}` — histogram, per-CR reconcile latency.
- `gotk_token_cached_items` — gauge, auth-token cache size.
- `gotk_token_cache_evictions_total` — counter, credential churn signal.

**Five `controller_runtime_reconcile_*` families** from kubebuilder:

- `controller_runtime_reconcile_total{controller, result}` — outcomes; `result` ∈ `success/error/requeue/requeue_after`.
- `controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{controller}`
- `controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds`
- `controller_runtime_reconcile_timeouts_total`
- `controller_runtime_reconcile_panics_total` — should always be 0.

Sample live values captured 2026-05-18 ~23:30 UTC. Sample Prometheus queries for error rate, latency P95, and token cache pressure recorded in the doc.

**Flux v2.7→v2.8 metric simplification noted:** `gotk_reconcile_condition` + `gotk_suspend_status` are gone; substitute queries documented.

### FR-006 alignment

FR-006 requires \"Flux drift detection MUST emit cluster events for every reconciliation; Prometheus metrics MUST expose reconciliation success rate, drift count, and last-reconcile-time per resource.\"

| FR-006 sub-requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Events for every reconciliation | ✅ — `flux events` + `kubectl get events` both surface the full taxonomy |
| Reconciliation success rate | ✅ — `controller_runtime_reconcile_total{result}` |
| Last-reconcile-time per resource | ✅ — `gotk_reconcile_duration_seconds_count` increments per reconcile; Flux event `LAST SEEN` column is the human surface |
| Drift count as dedicated metric | ⚠️ — not exposed by Flux v2.8.7. Observable proxy is `controller_runtime_reconcile_total{result="error"}` rate. A custom exporter could publish drift-count directly if it becomes load-bearing; deferred. |

### SC-005 live-test recipe (pinned)

The test demonstrates that drift on a Flux-managed resource reverts within one reconciliation interval. Target chosen for **lowest blast radius**:

- A benign annotation on the `reflector` HelmRelease CR itself (kustomize-controller-managed, no functional consumer reads annotations on CRs).
- `flux reconcile kustomization flux-system --with-source` to force immediate reconcile instead of waiting up to 10m.
- Expected wall-clock revert: **< 30s**.

Full operator-runnable recipe in the doc.

### SC-005 live evidence

**Status: pending operator-confirmed test execution.** The `kubectl annotate` step in the recipe is a production-cluster write; the project's `feedback_capability_vs_authorization` convention requires per-step confirmation on writes. Live evidence collection follows in a separate session.

## Test plan

- [x] Doc authored against live cluster state (intervals, controller versions, helm release inventory, driftDetection state all verified empirically).
- [x] Prometheus metric inventory verified via direct port-forward + `/metrics` scrape of each controller pod.
- [x] Flux event samples captured from `flux events --all-namespaces` against the current cluster.
- [x] Spec 151 `implements:` block extended; Phase 5 narrative section added with T-022 closure status (doc landed; live evidence pending).
- [x] `make pr-prep` clean (coupling gate: 3 diff paths checked).
- [ ] **SC-005 live evidence collection** (separate session) — annotate reflector HelmRelease, force reconcile, verify revert, paste timestamps into the doc.

## What does NOT close with this PR

This is a partial Phase 5 PR; **Phase 5 done-when is not yet satisfied**. Remaining Phase 5 tasks (all gated independently of T-022 docs):

- **T-022 SC-005 live evidence** — pending operator confirmation on the kubectl-annotate test (the recipe is ready).
- **T-023 disaster-recovery.md (Stage 2 SC-003 measurement)** — requires a fresh throwaway Hetzner cluster + ~30 min operator wall-clock.
- **T-024 SC-003 baseline-vs-target policy application** — gated by T-023 result.
- **T-025 dr-baseline F1 (Bitwarden unlock timing) + F2 (cx43 capacity)** — operator-driven against real Bitwarden + a fresh DC.
- **T-026 setup.sh final shrink to <100 lines (SC-002)** — gated by **spec 153** retiring the remaining `kubectl create secret` blocks.

Phase 5 closure + the 151 frontmatter `implementation: complete` flip both wait on the above.

## Follow-ups (not blocking 151)

- **HelmRelease `driftDetection.mode: Enabled` audit** — separate spec to evaluate whether enabling driftDetection on the four current HelmReleases is safe. Recorded as a finding in the new doc; the safety analysis (no mutating webhooks conflict in the current cluster topology) is sketched but not load-bearing.
- **Notification-controller Provider + Alert CRs** — wire the `Warning` event surface to Slack/Discord/webhook. Currently out of scope for spec 151 (FR-006 future work).
- **Custom drift-count exporter** — if Prometheus alerting on drift-count-as-cardinality becomes load-bearing, a small sidecar exporter publishes a `drift_total{kind, name, namespace}` counter. Not load-bearing today.

title: spec(151): Phase 4 operational landing (2026-05-18)
body:
## Summary

Records the in-cluster state after #168 (Phase 4 code) merged. Flux's `flux-system` GitRepository picked up the merge commit (`3977dc48b11d`) within the 1-minute poll interval; helm-controller adopted the existing `rauthy` release in-place. The cutover was a no-op on the underlying StatefulSet — pod AGE preserved through the adoption window, Certificate AGE 40d preserved, Ingress AGE 40d preserved.

**Surprise finding (good kind):** the imperative-rauthy path had been failing for over 24h before the cutover (helm revs 79 + 80 both `failed` during the spec 106 §12.1 SMTP work), so Flux's adoption upgrade is the first successful helm transaction on the release in over a day. Phase 4 didn't just preserve state — it cleaned the helm-bookkeeping that the prior imperative path had left in a broken state.

## Cutover evidence

**HelmRelease adoption — `.v81`, not `.v2`:**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `READY` | True |
| Status | `Helm upgrade succeeded for release rauthy-system/rauthy.v81 with chart rauthy@0.1.0+3977dc48b11d` |
| Helm rev | **`v81`** (existing was `v80`; adoption is `+1`) |
| Chart | `rauthy-0.1.0+3977dc48b11d` (helm-controller's git-source convention appends the commit SHA to the chart base version) |

**Helm history — the broken-bookkeeping context:**

| Rev | Updated (UTC) | Status | Chart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 79 | 2026-05-17 16:52 | failed | `rauthy-0.1.0` | `Upgrade "rauthy" failed: resource StatefulSet/rauthy-system/rauthy not ready` |
| 80 | 2026-05-17 18:25 | failed | `rauthy-0.1.0` | same failure mode |
| 81 | 2026-05-18 23:14 | **deployed** | `rauthy-0.1.0+3977dc48b11d` | Upgrade complete |

The failed re-runs at v79 + v80 came from setup.sh iterations during PRs #152 / #155 / #156 (spec 106 §12.1 SMTP work). Helm bookkeeping said \"failed,\" the pod was actually Running. Flux's adoption (v81) is the first successful helm transaction on rauthy in over a day.

**Zero-downtime preserved** (AGEs predate cutover by 40d or 22h respectively):

| Resource | AGE | State |
|---|---|---|
| StatefulSet `rauthy` | 40d | READY=1/1, image `ghcr.io/sebadob/rauthy:0.35.0` |
| Pod `rauthy-0` | 22h | 1/1 Running, RESTARTS=0 |
| Certificate `rauthy-tls` | 40d | READY=True |
| Ingress `rauthy` | 40d | nginx, host `auth.stagecraft.ing` |

The pod's 22h age predates the Phase 4 cutover (which fired ~71s before the evidence snapshot) by ~22h. The cutover did not roll the StatefulSet — the rendered manifest was identical to the pre-Phase-4 imperative-apply state.

**Secrets present** (cross-namespace dependencies the HelmRelease mounts):

| Secret | AGE | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| `rauthy-secrets` | 40d | 5 (raft-secret, api-secret, admin-password, enc-keys, enc-key-active) |
| `rauthy-smtp-secret` | 25h | 8 (from, url, port, username, password, starttls_only, danger_insecure, …) |

Both still materialised imperatively by setup.sh. Spec 153 SOPS-migrates them later.

**Live values match the HelmRelease verbatim** (`helm get values rauthy -n rauthy-system`):

```yaml
bootstrap:
  adminEmail: admin@stagecraft.ing
ingress:
  host: auth.stagecraft.ing
oidc:
  issuer: https://auth.stagecraft.ing/auth/v1/
persistence:
  size: 2Gi

replicas: 1

  enabled: true

  - 10.244.0.0/16
  - 173.245.48.0/20
  - 103.21.244.0/22
  ... (full Cloudflare IPv4 ranges as inlined)
```

## End-to-end validation

```
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" https://auth.stagecraft.ing/auth/v1/health
200
```

Cloudflare edge → Hetzner node hostPort → ingress-nginx (Phase 3 Flux-reconciled) → rauthy Service → rauthy-0 pod. Every link in this path is now Flux-reconciled except the two rauthy Secrets (spec 153 deferral).

## Pattern correction — `<release>.v<existing+1>`, not `<release>.v<phase+1>`

The Phase 3 narrative observed that adopted releases land at \"`.v<N+1>` for every release Flux has adopted,\" framing N as the phase number. That worked for Phase 2 + 3 because cert-manager + ingress-nginx + reflector had all been installed exactly once via the imperative path (so `existing` was always `1`, and adoption produced `.v2`). Rauthy's `.v81` disconfirms the `phase_number + 1` reading: rauthy's imperative ancestor had been helm-upgraded 80 times across the 40d StatefulSet lifetime; helm-controller's bookkeeping increment is still `+1`, just from a higher starting point. The Phase 3 \"Pattern observation (durable for Phase 4)\" paragraph is amended in the same PR (single-author self-pinned, spec 102 FU-001 pattern).

title: spec(151): Phase 4 — rauthy chart to Flux (T-019–T-021)
body:
## Summary

Rauthy moves under Flux. **First in-tree chart** the platform reconciles via helm-controller — Phases 2 + 3 referenced remote `HelmRepository` sources (emberstack, jetstack, kubernetes/ingress-nginx); this one references the cluster's bootstrap `GitRepository flux-system` directly. The Phase 2 + 3 zero-downtime adoption pattern (`<release>.v2` after first reconcile, no pod roll because the rendered manifest is identical) applies — but rauthy is the OIDC identity provider, so the operator cutover lands in a maintenance window per T-020.

## What changed

### New gitops file

- **`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/infrastructure/rauthy.yaml`** (T-019) — HelmRelease `rauthy` in `rauthy-system` namespace. Chart source is the in-tree `./platform/charts/rauthy` referenced via `GitRepository flux-system` with `reconcileStrategy: Revision` (chart template edits land without a Chart.yaml version bump — the in-tree chart pins `version: 0.1.0` and historically rarely bumps; appVersion + values are the live signal).

  **Values inlined:** the pre-Phase-4 deployment composed values from THREE sources (`values.yaml` defaults + `values-hetzner.yaml` overrides + three setup.sh `--set` flags + conditional smtp.enabled). The HelmRelease inlines the Hetzner-prod overrides (replicas=1, proxyMode=true, full Cloudflare trustedProxies, persistence.size=2Gi) and the DOMAIN-pinned overrides hardcoded to `stagecraft.ing` (cluster-specific gitops-tree convention — same pattern as `manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml`). `smtp.enabled: true` is hardcoded per spec 106 §12.1 amendment reality.

### setup.sh strikes

- **`helm upgrade --install rauthy ...` block removed** (~10 lines, lines 339-348 in old setup.sh).
- **`RAUTHY_SMTP_HELM_ARGS` plumbing removed** — the variable + its mutation. The `rauthy-smtp-secret` materialisation block stays (creates the Secret that Flux's HelmRelease mounts).
- **Warning rephrased** — when `SMTP_USERNAME` is unset, setup.sh now names the crash-loop risk explicitly: "Flux's rauthy HelmRelease pins smtp.enabled=true; the StatefulSet will crash-loop until rauthy-smtp-secret exists." The previous "magic-link login will be unavailable" soft-warning under-described the new failure mode.
- **Header comments updated** — `Phase 1: cluster + rauthy` → `Phase 1: cluster + secrets (Flux reconciles rauthy)`; the inner section header gains a rauthy-moved-to-Flux note.

### Makefile strike

- **`deploy-hetzner` target — rauthy block removed.** The parallel imperative-rauthy path in `platform/Makefile` is the same dual-writer hazard as setup.sh; removing both in one PR keeps the cleanup-ownership invariant (FR-008) intact. **stagecraft + deployd-api blocks stay** — they're spec 152 territory.

### Deletion

- **`platform/charts/rauthy/values-hetzner.yaml` — deleted.** No remaining references (`grep -rn "rauthy/values-hetzner.yaml"` returns zero); overrides moved inline into the HelmRelease. The chart's own `values.yaml` is loaded automatically by helm-controller as helm's defaults.

### Spec amendments

- `specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/spec.md` `implements:` block gains the three new claims (rauthy.yaml, values-hetzner.yaml deletion, Makefile claim).
- New **`### Phase 4 — rauthy chart to Flux`** section covering: in-tree chart pattern (canonical for future in-tree charts including spec 152's app-charts), values-inlining rationale, SMTP hardcoding tradeoff, dual-writer cleanup, operator cutover sequence (4 steps), and done-when criteria.

### Imperative-path absence verification

```
$ grep -nE 'helm upgrade --install rauthy\b' \
    platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh platform/Makefile
platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh:270:# `helm upgrade --install rauthy` block retired here. The `rauthy-secrets`
platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh:348:# The previous `helm upgrade --install rauthy ...` invocation retired
```

Only the two explanatory removal-rationale comments remain; no live code invokes the imperative-rauthy path.

## Cutover sequence (post-merge, maintenance window)

1. Operator confirms `rauthy-secrets` and `rauthy-smtp-secret` exist in `rauthy-system` namespace (`kubectl get secret -n rauthy-system`). Phase 4 doesn't touch Secret materialisation; the chart depends on both.
2. Merge this PR. Flux's `flux-system` Kustomization picks up the new `infrastructure/rauthy.yaml` within the 1-minute GitRepository poll interval.
3. `helm-controller` finds the existing `rauthy` release in `rauthy-system`, adopts it in-place. Expect `helm list -n rauthy-system | grep rauthy` to show `rauthy.v2` (Phase 3 adoption pattern).
4. Validate end-to-end:
   - `https://auth.stagecraft.ing/auth/v1/` loads (admin login form renders).
   - Magic-link from stagecraft sign-in flow delivers email (exercises rauthy-smtp-secret mount + Hetzner port-587 STARTTLS submission).
   - OIDC token-exchange round-trip from stagecraft completes (SPA client redirect → code → token).

## Test plan

- [x] `make pr-prep` — codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean (6 diff paths checked).
- [x] Imperative-path absence verified (above).
- [x] No remaining references to `platform/charts/rauthy/values-hetzner.yaml` (`grep -rn` clean).
- [x] HelmRelease values composition verified against the pre-Phase-4 effective helm-CLI invocation (chart values.yaml defaults + values-hetzner.yaml overrides + three setup.sh `--set` flags + smtp.enabled=true → all encoded in the HelmRelease `spec.values`).

title: spec(151): remove Hetzner DNS dormant path (Phase 3 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 originally preserved the \`cert-manager-webhook-hetzner\` chart install + the dormant \`letsencrypt-dns01\` ClusterIssuer heredoc in \`post-create.sh\` as "fallback for a future DNS migration." That framing was wrong — the dormant code is **structurally non-functional in this deployment** and would remain so unless we migrated \`stagecraft.ing\`'s authoritative DNS away from Cloudflare (a major architectural change with no current plan).

## Why it couldn't work

The DNS-01 validation chain breaks in two places:

1. The webhook would call \`https://dns.hetzner.com/api/v1\` to write the \`_acme-challenge.<host>\` TXT record — but Hetzner DNS holds **no zone** for \`stagecraft.ing\` (Hetzner Console → DNS shows "You don't have any DNS zones yet"). The API call returns zone-not-found.
2. Even if the zone existed and the record were written, Let's Encrypt's validator queries the **authoritative** nameservers for \`stagecraft.ing\` — \`leo.ns.cloudflare.com\` and \`rosalie.ns.cloudflare.com\` per the registry's NS records. A TXT record written into a non-authoritative provider is invisible to the validator; the challenge times out.

The dormant code was speculative copy-paste from a Hetzner-only tutorial that pre-dated the project's commitment to Cloudflare-as-edge. Resurrection cost: migrate \`stagecraft.ing\`'s registrar NS records from Cloudflare to Hetzner, losing Cloudflare's proxy / WAF / Email Routing.

## What changed

- **\`platform/infra/hetzner/post-create.sh\`** — three strikes:
  - The \`cert-manager-webhook-hetzner\` \`helm upgrade --install\` block (gated on \`SKIP_HETZNER_DNS_WEBHOOK\`) — ~12 lines.
  - The \`letsencrypt-dns01\` ClusterIssuer heredoc + \`hetzner-dns-secret\` create (gated on \`HCLOUD_DNS_API_TOKEN\`) — ~36 lines.
  - The MinIO block's stale comment that referenced the removed line ranges (lines \"87-104\" and \"106-188\") and the dormant-block framing — replaced with the post-cleanup framing.
- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/manifests/cert-manager-clusterissuers.yaml\`** — header rewrite: no longer claims a "dormant alternates" path exists; records the removal rationale.
- **\`specs/151-declarative-cluster-reconciliation/spec.md\`** — Phase 3 narrative amended:
  - The "Retained" bullet (which described the preservation) replaced with a "this framing was wrong" callout.
  - New "Phase 3 follow-up — remove Hetzner DNS dormant path" sub-section documents the two-step structural-impossibility argument and the operator step.
  - Phase 3 done-when grep updated: now expects **no matches** in \`post-create.sh\` (previously expected the dormant block to match).

## Operator step required at merge time

The \`cert-manager-webhook-hetzner\` chart is currently running on the production cluster (10d uptime per \`helm list\`). Post-merge, uninstall it to reclaim the pod's resources:

\`\`\`
helm uninstall cert-manager-webhook-hetzner -n cert-manager
\`\`\`

No downstream consumer references it. The \`letsencrypt-dns01\` ClusterIssuer it served has never existed in the cluster (gated on \`HCLOUD_DNS_API_TOKEN\` which was always unset). Uninstalling is safe.

## Why this isn't a spec 143 amendment

Spec 143 §4.7 L-005 (\"don't infer authoritative DNS from cluster-provider identity\") is the structural lesson this cleanup **acts on**, not amends. The dormant-code removal doesn't invalidate L-005; it follows L-005 to its natural conclusion. Spec 143's narrative remains accurate as-of-its-writing. The cleanup-ownership lives in spec 151 per FR-008.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make pr-prep\` — codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean (4 diff paths).
- [x] Final grep: only the explanatory removal-rationale comment in post-create.sh mentions Hetzner DNS / HCLOUD_DNS_API_TOKEN; no live code references remain.
- [ ] Post-merge: run \`helm uninstall cert-manager-webhook-hetzner -n cert-manager\` against the production cluster.
- [ ] Post-uninstall: \`kubectl -n cert-manager get pods\` shows no \`cert-manager-webhook-hetzner-*\` pods; existing platform Certificates remain Ready (the webhook was never on the active issuance path so there should be no impact).

title: spec(151): Phase 3 — cert-manager + ingress-nginx + ClusterIssuers to Flux (T-014–T-018)
body:
## Summary

Three more charts and two ClusterIssuers move under Flux. Helm-controller adopts the existing \`cert-manager\` + \`ingress-nginx\` releases in place; cert-manager treats the gitops ClusterIssuers as the same-named objects it already manages. **Zero-downtime cutover** per the Phase 2 pattern — no ACME re-registration, no certificate re-issuance.

Phase 2 verified the cutover pattern works for one resource. Phase 3 applies it at scale: two helm releases adopted in place + two ClusterIssuers adopted in place + downstream Certificate (the Phase 2 wildcard) keeps ticking through the cutover.

## What changed

### New gitops files

- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/infrastructure/cert-manager.yaml\`** (T-014) — HelmRepository for \`charts.jetstack.io\` + HelmRelease \`cert-manager\` v1.19.3 in namespace \`cert-manager\`, with \`values.crds.enabled=true\` matching post-create.sh's flag exactly. CRD adoption: cert-manager v1.19+ inlines CRDs in the chart's regular templates when this flag is set; helm-controller diffs them against the existing CRDs (already labelled \`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm\` from the prior imperative install) and reconciles as a no-op.

- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/infrastructure/ingress-nginx.yaml\`** (T-017) — HelmRepository + HelmRelease \`ingress-nginx\` 4.15.1 in namespace \`ingress-nginx\`. Five values preserved verbatim:
  - \`controller.kind=DaemonSet\`
  - \`controller.hostPort.enabled=true\`
  - \`controller.service.type=ClusterIP\`
  - \`controller.config.use-forwarded-headers=\"true\"\`
  - \`controller.config.compute-full-forwarded-for=\"true\"\`

  The hostPort-DaemonSet shape (not LoadBalancer Service) is Hetzner-cluster-specific: apex DNS A-records point at node IPs directly; no external LB. The tasks.md T-017 wording \"LoadBalancer service shape preserved\" is imprecise; the actual current shape is preserved.

- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/manifests/cert-manager-clusterissuers.yaml\`** (T-015):
  - \`letsencrypt-prod\` (HTTP-01 via nginx) — default for platform hosts (stagecraft, deployd, rauthy, minio).
  - \`letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare\` (DNS-01 via Cloudflare) — issues the wildcard tenant cert. Co-ownership note: spec 106 (PR #155) was the original primary owner; spec 151 migrates the file but spec 106 retains primary ownership per spec 130.

  Both metadata.name + namespace match the live objects; cert-manager treats them as the same ClusterIssuers it already manages. ACME account state (\`privateKeySecretRef\` Secrets \`letsencrypt-prod\` and \`letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare-account\`) persists across cutover.

### post-create.sh strikes

- \`helm upgrade --install ingress-nginx\` block removed (~14 lines).
- \`helm upgrade --install cert-manager\` block + \`kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/cert-manager-webhook\` line removed (~14 lines).
- HTTP-01 \`letsencrypt-prod\` ClusterIssuer heredoc removed (~28 lines).

### post-create.sh / setup.sh — what's RETAINED

- \`cert-manager-webhook-hetzner\` helm install + \`letsencrypt-dns01\` (Hetzner DNS) ClusterIssuer heredoc — dormant fallback, gated on \`HCLOUD_DNS_API_TOKEN\` (unset by design per spec 143 §4.7 L-005; authoritative DNS lives at Cloudflare, not Hetzner DNS). Migrating dormant gated resources to gitops would change their semantics from conditional to always-applied; not worth it for a path never activated in production.
- \`cloudflare-api-token\` Secret materialisation in setup.sh — carries \`$CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN\` from .env into the cluster. SOPS migration is spec 153 territory.

### Imperative-path absence verification

\`\`\`
$ grep -nE \"helm upgrade --install (cert-manager|ingress-nginx)\\b|kubectl.*letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare|kind: ClusterIssuer\" \\
    platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh platform/infra/hetzner/post-create.sh
platform/infra/hetzner/post-create.sh:97:    helm upgrade --install cert-manager-webhook-hetzner cert-manager-webhook-hetzner \\
platform/infra/hetzner/post-create.sh:114:kind: ClusterIssuer
\`\`\`

Only the dormant Hetzner-DNS fallback paths remain (intentional).

## Deferred (Phase 5 measurement gate)

The wrapping Flux Kustomization with \`dependsOn: [cert-manager]\` for the \`manifests/\` directory is **still** deferred (Phase 2 T-010's open thread). The Phase 2 retry-on-failure pattern handles convergence for both cutover and fresh-cluster scenarios; whether the convergence cost stays inside SC-003's 30-min budget gets measured in T-022/T-023 (Phase 5). If it overruns, the wrapping-Kustomization machinery is added then with a measured rationale.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make pr-prep\` — codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean (7 diff paths checked).
- [x] Live release state captured pre-PR: \`cert-manager\` chart v1.19.3 in \`cert-manager\` ns, \`ingress-nginx\` chart 4.15.1 in \`ingress-nginx\` ns — both names + namespaces + versions match the new HelmReleases (adoption path verified).
- [x] Live ClusterIssuer state captured pre-PR: \`letsencrypt-prod\` (HTTP-01) READY=True age 39d, \`letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare\` (DNS-01) READY=True age 20h — both names match the new gitops manifests (no re-registration on cutover).
- [x] Imperative-path absence verified (above).
- [ ] Post-merge cutover verification (each criterion vs. spec.md's Phase 3 done-when):
  - \`kubectl -n cert-manager get helmrelease cert-manager\` → READY=True
  - \`kubectl -n ingress-nginx get helmrelease ingress-nginx\` → READY=True
  - \`kubectl get clusterissuer letsencrypt-prod letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare\` → both READY=True
  - \`kubectl -n cert-manager get certificate tenants-wildcard\` → still Ready, AGE unchanged
  - Existing platform Certificates (stagecraft / deployd / rauthy / minio) remain Ready — no renewal triggered.

## Follow-ups

- **Phase 4 (T-019–T-021)** — rauthy chart to Flux. Identity-critical, maintenance window.
- **Imperative-manifest cleanup** — \`platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\` (Phase 2) + \`platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare-issuer.yaml\` (Phase 3) both no longer applied but in-tree. Deletion needs co-claimant amender edits on specs 106 / 137.
- **Phase 5 (T-022–T-026)** — drift detection + DR runbook (Stage 2 SC-003). Measures the dependsOn-deferral rationale.

body:
## Summary

## What's recorded
