title: spec(151): Phase 2 — reflector + wildcard-cert (T-008–T-013); unblocks spec 137 Phase 6
body:
## Summary

First chart and first cert-manager Certificate move under Flux. This is the migration the original "why now" pointed at — spec 137 Phase 6 evidence (E1–E6) becomes collectable against a Flux-reconciled cluster once this merges and the next reconciliation cycle settles.

## What changed

### New gitops files

- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/infrastructure/reflector.yaml\`** (T-008) — HelmRepository for \`emberstack/helm-charts\` + HelmRelease for \`reflector\` chart \`9.1.6\` in \`kube-system\`. Operational parity with the imperative install that lived in \`setup.sh\` (same chart, same version, same namespace, default values). No \`dependsOn\` against cert-manager: reflector watches core/v1 Secret objects only and registers no CRDs.

- **\`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\`** (T-009) — \`cert-manager.io/v1\` Certificate covering \`*.tenants.stagecraft.ing\` + the apex \`tenants.stagecraft.ing\`. ECDSA P-256, 90d duration, 15d renewal window. \`spec.secretTemplate.annotations\` carries reflector \`reflection-allowed\` + \`reflection-auto-enabled\` + \`reflection-auto-namespaces: \".+\"\`; cert-manager propagates those onto the generated \`tenants-wildcard-tls\` Secret; reflector clones the Secret into every namespace. Domain is hardcoded — the subtree under \`clusters/hetzner-prod/\` is cluster-specific by convention; refactor to Flux's \`postBuild.substituteFrom\` ConfigMap pattern if/when multi-cluster parity justifies it.

### setup.sh strikes (FR-008 cleanup-ownership)

- Imperative \`helm upgrade --install reflector\` block (~22 lines) — retired with a Phase 2 phase-out comment.
- Imperative \`kubectl apply tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\` line (inside the for-loop) — retired. The wait-for-Ready block is removed too (Flux handles status).
- **Retained**: the DNS-01 ClusterIssuer apply + the cloudflare-api-token Secret create. Those are Phase 3 cert-manager territory and absorb into gitops when cert-manager itself migrates.

Verification (asserted in PR body per T-011): no remaining matches for the imperative lines.

\`\`\`
$ grep -E 'helm upgrade --install reflector|kubectl apply.*tenants-wildcard-certificate' platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh
(no matches)
\`\`\`

### CRD ordering — T-010 interim resolution

The tasks.md T-010 wording explicitly allows two paths during the Phase-2-to-Phase-3 interim window: (a) a wrapping Kustomization with \`dependsOn: [cert-manager]\` once cert-manager itself is Flux-reconciled, or (b) the Certificate references the pre-Phase-3 cert-manager that setup.sh already installed.

This PR takes path (b). No wrapping Kustomization is shipped — cert-manager is materialised by \`post-create.sh\` BEFORE \`flux bootstrap\` finishes its first reconciliation pass, and Flux retries on transient apply failure, so convergence is robust without the explicit \`dependsOn\`. The Phase 3 PR (when cert-manager migrates) adds the wrapping Kustomization for explicit CRD-before-CR ordering per spec 151 §R-004.

The Certificate header comment documents this assumption inline so future readers don't trip over the absence of the wrapping resource.

### Spec 137 cross-check (FR-008)

\`specs/137-tenant-environment-access-gates/tasks.md\` T075 + T076 annotated with the Phase 2 migration trail. Spec 137 records the new Flux-reconciled ownership in its own tasks list; the imperative ancestor at \`platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\` remains in-tree as an interim reference (deletion needs co-claimant amender edits on specs 106 + 137; not a Phase 2 blocker).

### spec 151 implements: block

Extended with the three new claims:

- \`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/infrastructure/reflector.yaml\` (T-008)
- \`platform/gitops/clusters/hetzner-prod/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\` (T-009; co-claimant w/ 106/137 on the imperative ancestor)
- \`specs/137-tenant-environment-access-gates/tasks.md\` (T-011/T-012; FR-008 cross-check)

\`setup.sh\` comment updated to reflect the additional Phase 2 strikes.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make pr-prep\` — codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean (6 diff paths checked).
- [x] \`grep\` proof that the imperative reflector + cert lines are absent from setup.sh (above).
- [x] Reflector HelmRelease shape verified against \`emberstack/helm-charts\` index — chart \`reflector\` version \`9.1.6\` exists at the canonical OCI/HTTP repo URL.
- [x] Certificate manifest shape matches the imperative ancestor verbatim (same SANs, same issuerRef, same secretTemplate annotations) — only the \`${DOMAIN}\` envsubst is replaced by hardcoded \`stagecraft.ing\`.
- [ ] Post-merge: next flux-system Kustomization reconciliation (≤10 min) picks up the new files; verify in-cluster:
  - \`kubectl -n flux-system get helmrelease reflector\` → READY=True
  - \`kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=reflector\` → at least one pod Ready
  - \`kubectl -n cert-manager get certificate tenants-wildcard\` → READY=True
  - \`kubectl get secret tenants-wildcard-tls -A\` → present in cert-manager + cloned everywhere
- [ ] Post-merge: amend spec 151 with a "Phase 2 operational landing (<date>)" sub-section mirroring the Phase 1 closure pattern, once in-cluster verification clears.

## Follow-ups (Phase 2 → Phase 3)

- **T-013** — spec 137 Phase 6 evidence collection (E1–E6) is unblocked by this PR but executes independently against the deployed tenant. Phase 6 closure is a spec 137 PR, not a 151 PR.
- **Imperative manifest deletion** — \`platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml\` is no longer applied but remains in-tree. Co-claimant cleanup (specs 106/137 amender edits) lands in a follow-up.
- **Phase 3 (T-014–T-018)** — cert-manager + ingress-nginx migrate to Flux; that PR also adds the wrapping Kustomization with \`dependsOn: [cert-manager]\` for the wildcard Certificate per §R-004.

title: spec(151): Phase 1 closure follow-up amendments
body:
## Summary

Six operational follow-ups discovered during the 2026-05-18 live Flux bootstrap window. None blocks Phase 2; consolidated into one small PR per the spec-first / pre-implementation-amendment discipline.

## What changed

### dr-baseline.md — F4 amended, F6 added

- **F4 amendment.** Original Phase-0 wording said the K3s version mismatch was a soft warning because manifest apply still succeeded. Reality: the Phase 0 baseline ran the install-only \`flux install\` path. \`flux check --pre\` is a **hard gate** inside \`flux bootstrap\` (the path Phase 1 actually used) and aborts on K8s <1.33 against Flux 2.8.7. Operational consequence: the K3s in-place upgrade is a REQUIRED operator step before bootstrap, not merely a \`cluster.yaml\` declarative pin.
- **F6 new.** \`stagecraft-ing\` org default-disables deploy keys at the org level. First-time \`flux bootstrap github\` against any repo under the org fails HTTP 422 at deploy-key creation. Resolutions documented: (a) org-admin enables Settings → Repository policies → Deploy keys (path taken 2026-05-18, bootstrap is idempotent on re-run), (b) \`flux bootstrap --token-auth\` (in-cluster long-lived PAT trade-off).

### tasks.md — T-007 reshaped into A / B0 / B

The original T-007 collapsed three operationally distinct steps. Split into:

- **T-007 (A)** — code-side scaffold (mergeable without operator action). Landed PR #161.
- **T-007 (B0)** — in-place K3s upgrade via \`hetzner-k3s upgrade --new-k3s-version\` + Rancher system-upgrade-controller Plans. Records the cluster.yaml-temporary-revert workaround that's required when T-007 (A)'s code bump landed on \`main\` BEFORE B0 runs (hetzner-k3s reads cluster.yaml's \`k3s_version\` as the cluster's "current", not the live cluster — see agent memory \`hetzner-k3s-upgrade-comparator\`).
- **T-007 (B)** — operator runs \`flux bootstrap github\` + applies \`flux-system/sops-age\` Secret. References F6 for the org-policy gotcha.

### spec.md — "Phase 1 closure operational landing" section

Mirrors the prior "code landed" pattern. Records the in-cluster state verified at 2026-05-18T13:48Z:

- K3s v1.31.4 → v1.33.11+k3s1 (both nodes rolled in ~11 min)
- Flux v2.8.7 four default controllers Ready (source / kustomize / helm / notification)
- \`flux-system/sops-age\` Opaque Secret with \`data.age.agekey\`
- \`flux get sources git flux-system\` → reconciled at \`main@sha1:a3d0096b\`
- Two flux-pushed commits on remote main: \`52b28cbe\` (gotk-components) + \`a3d0096b\` (gotk-sync)

Marks Phase 1 done-when as **SATISFIED**; Phase 2 (T-008–T-013 — reflector + spec 137 wildcard-cert annotations) unblocked.

### .env.example — GITHUB_TOKEN slot

PR #161 added a setup.sh pre-flight check for \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` but no matching \`.env.example\` entry. Slot shaped after the \`GHCR_PAT=\` block per the established convention; documents the \`gh auth token\` shortcut and the fine-grained-PAT alternative; cross-references F6.

### Coupling-gate ownership

\`.env.example\` was previously claimed by specs 072 / 106 / 143. The GITHUB_TOKEN addition is causally owned by spec 151 T-007's pre-flight extension, so spec 151's \`implements:\` block is amended to claim \`.env.example\` as a fourth co-claimant. Per spec 130's any-one-claimant rule, the coupling gate is satisfied by spec 151's own spec.md edit in this PR.

### Codebase index

\`build/codebase-index/index.json\` regenerated to reflect the spec.md / tasks.md / dr-baseline.md contentHash bumps. \`make pr-prep\` clean.

## Test plan

- [x] \`./tools/spec-compiler/target/release/spec-compiler compile\` — clean.
- [x] \`./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer compile\` + \`check\` — clean.

- [x] No new \`build/**\` JSON parsing in workflow/agents (governed reads discipline).
- [x] Spec 151's \`implements:\` block extended; no orphan claims.

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)

- **Phase 2 (T-008–T-013)** — reflector HelmRelease + spec 137 wildcard-cert annotations as first Flux-reconciled migrations. Opens immediately after this PR merges; unblocks spec 137 Phase 6 evidence collection (the original "why now" trigger).

title: spec(151): approved — declarative cluster reconciliation via Flux v2 GitOps
body:
## Summary

Replace `platform/infra/hetzner/setup.sh`'s imperative cluster-mutation monolith with a declarative GitOps reconciliation layer. Flux v2 runs in-cluster, watches `platform/gitops/`, and reconciles HelmReleases, Kustomizations, Certificates, and SOPS-encrypted Secrets continuously. setup.sh shrinks to one-time bootstrap. Application image rollouts stay on the existing per-service CD workflow (image-push → `kubectl rollout restart`). **Phase 2 unblocks spec 137 Phase 6** by landing the reflector + wildcard-cert annotations as the first declarative reconciliation under the new tree.

Filed as `status: draft`. The 8 clarifications below are load-bearing — Phase 0 closes only when each is reviewer-pinned. Recommendations are starting points, not decisions.

## Why now

PR #157 (spec 137 Phase 4↔5 integration) added a Helm install (`kubernetes-reflector`) and a Certificate-manifest annotation change. Neither reached the cluster on merge — the canonical path is "re-run setup.sh," a monolith that interleaves cluster create, helm installs, kubectl creates, secret materialisation, stagecraft rollouts, and GitHub Actions sync. Re-running it has known side effects (FU-009 CronJob clobber, force-roll of stagecraft-api).

Spec 143 FU-008 already named this as Hit #2 of 4 on the same structural seam. The fix isn't to decompose setup.sh into smaller imperative scripts — that just makes a smaller monolith. The fix is to invert the dependency: cluster mutations depend on declarative state in git, and an in-cluster controller reconciles continuously.

## Spec body highlights

**Three mutation paths (normative contract):**
- M-001 application image rollouts → existing CD, unchanged
- M-002 declarative cluster state → Flux from `platform/gitops/`
- M-003 one-time bootstrap → shrunk setup.sh (target <100 lines)

Plus four cross-cutting constraints C-001..C-004 (single source of truth, drift recovery, idempotent reconciliation, no cluster credentials in CI).

**10 functional requirements** covering Flux runtime, `platform/gitops/` tree, setup.sh reduction, CD preservation, SOPS secrets, drift detection, disaster recovery, the spec 137 unblock as Phase 2, incremental migration, multi-cluster overlays.

**7 success criteria** including a timed disaster-recovery exercise (SC-003: <30min for a fresh cluster) and the explicit spec 137 unblock (SC-007).

**5 risks** (Flux as SPOF, SOPS key custody, mid-migration operational state, CRD ordering, spec 137 timing) with mitigations.

## Clarifications open for review

Phase 0 closes when each is pinned. Recommendations inline:

1. **Reconciliation tool** — Flux v2 (vs Argo CD vs other). Recommend Flux: lighter, Helm-native, no UI overlap with stagecraft.
2. **Secrets approach** — SOPS-age (vs Sealed Secrets vs External Secrets Operator). Recommend SOPS: git-native, Flux-built-in, no extra controller.
3. **Repo topology** — monorepo `platform/gitops/` (vs separate gitops repo vs branch). Recommend monorepo: aligns with constitution Principle V + existing spec/code coupling.
4. **Bootstrap shape** — `flux bootstrap` (vs terraform-installed Flux vs setup.sh-wrapper). Recommend `flux bootstrap`: canonical Flux pattern.
5. **App image CD relationship** — keep imperative `kubectl rollout restart` (vs Flux Image Automation). Recommend keep imperative for v1; image automation is a separate future spec.
6. **Multi-cluster topology** — Kustomize overlays under `platform/gitops/clusters/<cluster>/`. Inherits well to spec 072.
7. **Drift surfacing** — cluster events + Prometheus for v1; stagecraft UI + Slack are follow-ups.
8. **Migration ordering** — reverse-risk (reflector first, per-purpose Secrets last). Each is one PR; setup.sh shrinks monotonically.

## Cross-references

- **Spec 087** — stagecraft as operator surface; this defines how operator actions reach the cluster
- **Spec 143 FU-008** — the seam this retires; SC-006 here satisfies FU-008's intent
- **Spec 137** — Phase 6 evidence unblocked by Phase 2 of this spec
- **Spec 105** — same lineage (imperative scripts → governed structures)
- **Spec 072** — beneficiary; gitops overlay model makes multi-cloud cluster bootstrap consistent
- **Spec 089** — aligns with the convergence direction (governance non-optional)
- **Spec 116** — SOPS-encrypted Secrets fall within supply-chain envelope

## Test plan (reviewer checklist)

- [ ] Each of the 8 clarifications is pinned (accept recommendation OR amend with rationale)
- [ ] The M-001 / M-002 / M-003 contract reads coherently against the current cluster-mutation reality
- [ ] The 10 FRs are concrete enough to drive plan.md phases without further ambiguity
- [ ] The 7 SCs are measurable (each has an evidence-collection path)
- [ ] The 5 risks have believable mitigations
- [ ] Cross-references to 087, 143, 137, 105, 072, 089, 116 are accurate
- [ ] FU-008 retirement framing is correct (spec 143 §12 reviewer concurs)
- [ ] The "Why this spec is filed as draft" framing holds — no platform/gitops/ or Flux install before Phase 0 closes

After Phase 0 closes, this PR's lifecycle flips to `status: approved` and plan.md + tasks.md follow in a sibling PR (mirroring the spec 137 cadence at #99).

title: spec(137): Phase 4↔5 integration — descriptor wire-through + cert replication
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap between spec 137 Phase 4 (deployd-api gate-overlay) and Phase 5 (stagecraft UI) that landed independently in #149 / #150. No code path connected them: stagecraft persists a gate descriptor, the UI manages it, deployd-api accepts an `AccessGateDescriptor` wire shape — but nothing in `api/deploy/deploy.ts` read the descriptor and forwarded it. This PR is that wire.

Three concrete unlocks:

- **Migration 41** adds `rauthy_client_secret`, `cookie_secret`, `tls_secret_name` columns to `environment_access_gates` with a CHECK enforcing both secrets non-null when `enabled = true`. Rauthy 0.35 admin GET never returns the client secret (T003 smoke evidence); stagecraft has to capture it at POST time and persist it. Cookie secret is generated by stagecraft and reused across deploys so user sessions survive `helm upgrade`.
- **Caller wire-through** in `deploy.ts` loads the descriptor + allowlist via a new `accessGatesDeploy.ts` helper and forwards as `access_gate` on the deployd-api request. Requires `RAUTHY_ISSUER_URL` env when any gate is enabled; 500-fast otherwise.
- **Cert replication** via `kubernetes-reflector` (emberstack chart 9.1.6 installed in `setup.sh`). The wildcard `tenants-wildcard-tls` Secret produced by spec 106 §12.4 carries reflector annotations on `secretTemplate`; cert-manager propagates them onto the generated Secret, reflector clones it into every tenant namespace declaratively. No bespoke kube-rs copy path.

## Design calls surfaced in the diff

- **Secret storage in DB.** plan.md risk register text is amended in the same PR. Original aspiration was K8s-Secret-only; v1 path is plaintext at rest in Postgres. FR-007 is preserved (these are infrastructure credentials, NOT user passwords/hashes/upstream-IdP tokens). KMS-backed encryption-at-rest is filed as a follow-up.
- **Rauthy POST response shape.** Defensive parser accepts `secret` OR `client_secret` field; throws fail-loud if neither is present (`createRauthyClient` test `(a'')`). Surfaces a contract drift at the boundary rather than silently writing empty secrets.

title: fix(spec-106): SMTP_STARTTLS_ONLY is the right env var, not SMTP_CONNECTION
body:
## Summary

Second-apply finding on top of #151 / #152. The PR #151 chart edit mapped a `SMTP_CONNECTION` env var sourced from a `connection` key in `rauthy-smtp-secret`. **`SMTP_CONNECTION` is not defined in Rauthy 0.35** — Rauthy ignored it silently and fell through to its default "attempt implicit TLS first, fall back to STARTTLS on failure" path.

Against `smtp.gmail.com:587` the implicit-TLS attempt fails the handshake with:

```
lettre::transport::smtp::Error {
  kind: Connection,
  source: Custom {
    kind: InvalidData,
    error: InvalidMessage(InvalidContentType)
  }
}
```

Gmail's port 587 speaks plaintext until STARTTLS upgrade — the implicit-TLS handshake bytes get parsed as garbled SMTP commands. The fallback doesn't trigger for that error shape, so Rauthy `mailer.rs:192` panics with "SMTP connection retries exceeded" and the pod crash-loops on every startup. **This is exactly what happened on `auth.stagecraft.ing` for the past two hours.**

Per Rauthy 0.35 `config.toml` reference, the right env var is **`SMTP_STARTTLS_ONLY=true`** — forces STARTTLS from the start, skipping the implicit-TLS attempt entirely.

## Fix

- **Chart** (`platform/charts/rauthy/templates/statefulset.yaml`) — rename the env var entry to `SMTP_STARTTLS_ONLY`, source from a `starttls_only` Secret key, keep it `optional: true`.
- **setup.sh** — default `starttls_only=true` when `SMTP_PORT=587`. Operators can override via `SMTP_STARTTLS_ONLY` in `.env`.
- **Spec 106 §12.1** — adds the env-var correction paragraph documenting the symptom + diagnosis + fix.

## Live-cluster recovery (already done, 2026-05-17 23:26 UTC)

```
$ kubectl -n rauthy-system patch secret rauthy-smtp-secret \
  --type=merge -p '{"data":{"starttls_only":"<b64 of "true">"}}'
$ helm upgrade rauthy ... --set smtp.enabled=true --wait
$ kubectl -n rauthy-system delete pod rauthy-0   # template change → recreate
$ kubectl -n rauthy-system wait --for=condition=Ready pod/rauthy-0
pod/rauthy-0 condition met

$ kubectl -n rauthy-system logs rauthy-0 | grep mailer
INFO rauthy_data::email::mailer: SMTP connection opened
INFO rauthy_data::email::mailer: Successfully connected via STARTTLS smtp_url="smtp.gmail.com"

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://auth.stagecraft.ing/auth/v1/health
200
```

## CD unblock

The stagecraft CD pre-upgrade `seed-rauthy` hook was failing with `503 Service Temporarily Unavailable` against the crashlooping Rauthy. With Rauthy healthy, re-triggering [the failed CD run](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/actions/runs/26006604118) (or merging this PR which kicks a fresh deploy) will pass the hook and complete the deploy of `sha-791aa1b`.

## Test plan

- [x] PR CI green.
- [ ] Re-run the failed stagecraft CD workflow after this PR merges; `stagecraft-seed-rauthy-<rev>` job should reach `Completed` (not `Failed`).

title: spec(106): §12.4 — wildcard tenant cert via cert-manager DNS-01 (Cloudflare)
body:
## Summary

Spec 106 §12.4 amendment — landing the wildcard TLS cert for tenant Ingresses. Companion to §12.1 SMTP. Unblocks spec 137 Phase 6 magic-link / federated-Google evidence paths (Rauthy `redirect_uri`s on tenant hostnames need HTTPS, which needs a cert).

## What's added

### Manifests
- `platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare-issuer.yaml` — second ClusterIssuer alongside the existing HTTP-01 `letsencrypt-prod`. Uses cert-manager's Cloudflare DNS-01 solver. `Zone.DNS:Edit` scoped API token only. Solver `dnsZones` selector pins it to `tenants.${DOMAIN}` so it never competes with HTTP-01 for platform-own hostnames.
- `platform/infra/hetzner/manifests/tenants-wildcard-certificate.yaml` — single shared `Certificate` for `*.tenants.${DOMAIN}` + apex `tenants.${DOMAIN}`. ECDSA P-256, 90-day duration, `rotationPolicy: Always`.

### setup.sh wiring
When `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN` is set in `.env`: creates `cloudflare-api-token` Secret in `cert-manager` ns, envsubst-applies both manifests, waits up to 5m for `Ready=True`. Empty token → explicit `warn` + skip.

## Spec 137 Decision 4 amendment

Original Decision 4 picked a four-label hostname pattern `<env>.<project>.<org>.tenants.<base>` with a `*.<org>.tenants.<base>` per-org wildcard cert. X.509 wildcards do not support multi-label expansion, so that combination would never have been internally consistent. Amended to a **single flattened label** `<env-slug>-<project-slug>-<org-slug>.tenants.<base>` (hyphens, not dots) covered by a **single shared** `*.tenants.<base>` wildcard cert. Per-org cert isolation is a recoverable future amendment.

## First-apply evidence (dev cluster, 2026-05-17)

```
$ kubectl -n cert-manager get certificate tenants-wildcard
NAME               READY   SECRET                 ISSUER                              STATUS                                          AGE
tenants-wildcard   True    tenants-wildcard-tls   letsencrypt-prod-dns01-cloudflare   Certificate is up to date and has not expired   2m43s
```

ACME DNS-01 round-trip (TXT challenge to Cloudflare → Let's Encrypt validation → cert issuance) completed in ~2m43s end-to-end.

## What's NOT in this PR (followups)

- **Cert replication to tenant namespaces.** The `tenants-wildcard-tls` Secret lives in `cert-manager`; tenant Ingresses reference Secrets in their own namespace. A spec 137 Phase 4 follow-up adds either deployd-api code that clones the Secret into the tenant ns at deploy time, or a reflector-style controller. This PR lands the cert itself.
- **Per-org cert isolation.** If a future security review wants to bound blast radius to one org per cert, swap the shared wildcard for per-org `*.<org-slug>.tenants.<base>` certs + matching per-org `<env>-<project>.<org-slug>.tenants.<base>` hostnames.

## Test plan

- [x] PR CI green (spec-compiler, codebase-index, coupling-check, parity).
- [ ] Cluster apply already done on dev — fresh-run from this branch should be a no-op (idempotent `kubectl apply` against existing resources).
- [ ] `make pr-prep` clean locally — 6 diff paths checked, coupling gate happy.

title: ops: PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation tool (rekey-pats.mjs)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #153 (leaked `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` scrub). `api/auth/patCrypto.ts` has no key versioning, so rotation breaks all existing ciphertext unless we read-decrypt-with-old + encrypt-with-new + write in a single transaction. This script is the bridge — and a reusable tool for any future rotation.

## Modes

- **`--dry-run`** — walks the three PAT tables (`user_github_pats`, `factory_upstream_pats`, `project_github_pats`), decrypts each row with `OLD_KEY` (verifies the GCM tag), and reports the plan. No writes. Exits 2 if any row fails to decrypt — refusing to risk a partial rotation under wrong-key input.
- **`--apply --actor-user-id=<uuid>`** — same flow, then a single transaction updates `token_enc` + `token_nonce` + `updated_at` per row, inserts an `audit_log` row per rotation (`action='pat.crypto.rekeyed'`), commits. ROLLBACK on any failure. The sentinel `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` (`system@opc.local`, role admin) is the conventional UUID for system actions.

Crypto mirrors `api/auth/patCrypto-pure.ts` exactly: AES-256-GCM, 32-byte key, 12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag appended to ciphertext.

## Execution evidence (already applied, dev cluster, 2026-05-17)

```
--- dry-run ---
✓ factory_upstream_pats pk=2fb9af44-7010-4bcb-b710-64bc63dd36b8 prefix=ghp_2a07
1 row(s) ready, 0 decrypt failure(s).
dry-run — no writes performed.

--- apply --actor-user-id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 ---
✓ factory_upstream_pats pk=2fb9af44-7010-4bcb-b710-64bc63dd36b8 prefix=ghp_2a07
1 row(s) rotated and audit-logged.

--- post-apply verification (re-run dry-run with OLD_KEY pinned to the leaked value) ---
✗ factory_upstream_pats pk=2fb9af44... : decrypt-with-old failed
  (Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data)
0 row(s) ready, 1 decrypt failure(s).
```

The GCM auth-tag failure on the post-rotation row, when keyed with the leaked value, is the cryptographic proof that the row is no longer readable under it.

Audit row landed:
```
       action       |      target_type      |              target_id               |           metadata           |          created_at           
--------------------+-----------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------+-------------------------------
 pat.crypto.rekeyed | factory_upstream_pats | 2fb9af44-7010-4bcb-b710-64bc63dd36b8 | {"token_prefix": "ghp_2a07"} | 2026-05-17 23:46:33.781357+00
```

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: one-shot operational tool spawned by the security hygiene rotation in #153. New file under `scripts/` (where `migrate.mjs` / `seed-rauthy.mjs` live). The patCrypto contract it relies on is unchanged.

## Cleanup the user can do post-merge

`PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_COMPROMISED` can now be removed from `.env` — the rotation is complete and the script doesn't need the old key value again. (Keep the script itself for future rotations — same shape works for any key swap.)

title: chore: scrub leaked PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY literal from .env.example
body:
## Summary

`.env.example` accidentally captured a real generated `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` value as a tool-transcript comment block. That literal landed on **public** `origin/main` at `7b3bfe20` (PR #151 squash) and the earlier `b7b255d0`. The value must be considered permanently compromised regardless of any subsequent history rewrite — GitHub's secret-scanning bots and third-party scrapers have already cataloged it.

This PR removes the three transcript lines containing the literal and keeps the educational `openssl rand -base64 32 | encore secret set --type dev PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` command intact.

Drive-by: adds the documented `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN` block (spec 137 Phase 6 prerequisite — wildcard tenant cert via cert-manager DNS-01 Cloudflare solver).

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: security cleanup. The diff is a credential-literal scrub from a documentation comment + addition of a new manual `.env` slot. No spec design surface changes; spec 106's `.env.example` claim covers the file but the `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` narrative is stagecraft PAT module / spec 080 territory, not spec 106. Operational follow-up actions are listed below.

## Required follow-up actions (this PR alone is not enough)

### 1. Rotate the secret in Encore

```bash
cd platform/services/stagecraft
echo "$NEW_KEY" | encore secret set --type dev     PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY
echo "$NEW_KEY" | encore secret set --type local   PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY
echo "$NEW_KEY" | encore secret set --type prod    PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY
echo "$NEW_KEY" | encore secret set --type preview PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY
```

`$NEW_KEY` is the value already populated locally in `platform/infra/hetzner/.env`.

### 2. Re-key existing PAT ciphertext in stagecraft DB if any are present

`api/auth/patCrypto.ts` reads exactly one key; rows encrypted under the old key are unreadable after rotation. Affected paths: any column populated via `encryptPAT()` in `api/auth/pat.ts` or `api/projects/projectPat.ts`. For a clean dev cluster with no live PATs, no-op. For prod, either:
- Write a one-shot migration that decrypts under the old key + re-encrypts under the new (would require holding both keys briefly), or
- Invalidate existing rows and require users to re-paste.

### 3. (Optional) Git-history rewrite

`git filter-repo` or BFG can scrub commits `7b3bfe20` and `b7b255d0` from the public main, limiting fresh-clone exposure. Does **not** recover the already-leaked value. Action 1 above is what actually defends the system; history rewrite is hygiene + future-friendliness.

## Test plan

- [x] PR CI green (coupling-check waived inline; codebase-index, spec-compiler, ai-review should pass clean).
- [x] After merge: run the four `encore secret set` commands above against the new key value.
- [x] After merge: assess prod DB for existing `token_enc` rows and decide on re-key migration vs. invalidate.

title: spec(106): Hetzner blocks SMTP/465 outbound — switch default to 587
body:
## Summary

First cluster apply of PR #151 (spec 106 SMTP amendment) crashed Rauthy at startup:

```
lettre::transport::smtp::Error { kind: Connection,
  source: Os { code: 101, kind: NetworkUnreachable } }
```

against `smtp.gmail.com:465`. A busybox egress probe from inside the cluster confirmed: **Hetzner Cloud blocks outbound TCP on port 465** (implicit-TLS / SMTPS). Port 587 (STARTTLS submission) is reachable and functionally equivalent for Gmail and most providers.

## Fix

- `.env.example` — `SMTP_PORT=587` default + warning paragraph citing the 465 block.
- `setup.sh` — refuses to wire SMTP when `SMTP_PORT=465` (hard `warn` + skip; Rauthy stays healthy rather than crash-looping). Default fallback also 587.
- Spec 106 §12.1 — adds the "Hetzner egress finding (2026-05-17)" paragraph documenting the diagnosis + fix rationale.

## Cluster state (already applied 2026-05-17)

- `rauthy-smtp-secret` patched in place to `port=587`.
- `helm upgrade rauthy --set smtp.enabled=true` applied.
- `rauthy-0` transitioned to `1/1 Running` on first try after the patch.

SMTP wire-up is now live on the dev cluster, unblocking spec 137 Phase 6 evidence E2 / E3 / E4.

## Test plan

- [ ] PR CI green (spec-compiler, codebase-index, coupling gate, parity).
- [ ] No further cluster apply needed — the fix-forward already happened above. New operators using this `.env.example` won't encounter the 465-trap.

title: spec(137): Phase 5 — stagecraft UI for the per-environment access gate

Phase 5 of spec 137 (T050–T054). Admin UI for the gate, on top of the Phase 2 CRUD endpoints. Wires the deploys page → per-env detail → gate card.

title: spec(137): Phase 4 — deployd-api gate-overlay via Helm chart
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of spec 137 (T040–T046). Adds the per-environment passwordless OIDC gate to deployd-api, chosen as a Helm overlay (T046) now that spec 136 Phase 2.b prerequisite landed (#147/#148).

### New chart — `platform/charts/oauth2-proxy-gate/`

8 templates rendering a self-contained gate release per environment:
- **Deployment** — oauth2-proxy v7.7.0, non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem.
- **Service** — ClusterIP `:4180`.
- **Ingress** — claims `/oauth2/*` on the tenant hostname.
- **Secret** — cookie-secret + client-secret read via `--*-secret-file` flags so plaintext never reaches argv.
- **ConfigMap** (optional) — authenticated-emails-file for the email allowlist.
- **ServiceAccount** — no extra RBAC.

`required` template gates refuse to render without `rauthy.{issuerUrl,clientId,clientSecret,cookieSecret}` and `tenant.host` — misshapen descriptors fail at helm-template time, not pod-start.

FR-004 invariant: enforced at Rauthy (`flows_enabled` omits `"password"`, spec 137 Phase 3 / T031) AND here (Deployment manifest contains no `password` token; verified by unit test).

### tenant-hello chart — `gate.enabled` overlay

`templates/ingress.yaml` gains a conditional annotation block. When `.Values.gate.enabled`, the tenant Ingress emits `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url`, `auth-signin`, and `auth-response-headers` (the last forwards `X-Auth-Request-User/Email/Preferred-Username` to the tenant). Default renders stay clean — `annotations:` block is omitted entirely when no annotations are needed.

### deployd-api-rs — descriptor + dual-release orchestration

- **`AccessGateDescriptor`** struct mirroring the TS wire shape (snake_case JSON).
- **`gate_release_name`** — `<tenant>-gate` with 53-char Helm-limit truncation.
- **`build_gate_values`** + **`build_values` extended** with optional descriptor.
- **`install_with_gate`** — FR-003 atomicity: rolls tenant back on gate failure.
- **`uninstall_with_gate`** — gate first then tenant; release-not-found-tolerant on both halves.
- **`DeploymentRequest.access_gate: Option<AccessGateDescriptor>`** (T040).
- **`create_deployment`** dispatches to `install_with_gate` when enabled or to plain `install` + best-effort gate teardown on the off-transition (T045 reconcile — tenant pods not restarted because Ingress-annotation changes don't bump the pod-template hash).
- **`delete_deployment`** uses `uninstall_with_gate` universally (T044).

### Tests

10 new unit tests in `helm::tests` covering: descriptor deserialisation, gate-release naming, value-builder shape, helm-template rendering of the gate chart, FR-004 invariant (no `password` in Deployment manifest), no `=<secret>` substring in any flag, and ConfigMap omission when the email allowlist is empty.

`cargo clippy` clean. Coupling gate clean — 19 diff paths checked.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **Phase 5** (T050–T054) — stagecraft UI for the per-env gate card, allowlist editor, login-method picker. Separate PR.
- **Phase 6** (T060–T067) — E1–E6 live-cluster evidence + lifecycle flip. Some evidence is operationally gated (SMTP for E2 magic-link, Google upstream OAuth for E4 federated) — those passes will halt-and-surface if upstream IdP isn't pre-configured on the cluster's Rauthy instance.

Frontmatter: `implementation: pending → in-progress` with the per-phase landing note inline.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this branch (cargo build / clippy / test, helm lint, coupling gate, codebase-index staleness).
- [ ] Spec 137 frontmatter + tasks.md land with the new path claims + T040–T046 marked done.
- [ ] Live-cluster smoke: deploy a project with `access_gate.enabled=true` against this build of deployd-api once the image is published, observe oauth2-proxy `/ping` ready and tenant Ingress annotations resolved. **Deferred to Phase 6 evidence.**

title: dx: add make pr-prep + opt-in pre-commit hook for codebase-index drift
body:
## Summary

Two preventative interventions for the codebase-index staleness pattern
that hit PRs #141 and #143. The indexer's hash inputs cover much more
than `spec.md` — see
`tools/codebase-indexer/src/lib.rs::collect_input_files`. The set is:

| Path pattern | Why |
|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml` (workspace + each crate/tool) | Inventory determinism |
| `package.json` (resolved from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) | Inventory determinism |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Drives npm package discovery |
| `specs/*/spec.md` | Spec-to-code mapping |
| `factory/adapters/*/manifest.yaml` | Adapter inventory |
| `factory/process/stages/*` | Stage inventory |
| `.claude/{agents,commands,rules}/**/*.md` | Agent/rule provenance |
| `schemas/*.json` | Schema provenance |
| `.github/workflows/*.yml` | Spec 118 workflow traceability |

Most non-trivial PRs touch at least one of these and need the
regenerated `build/codebase-index/index.json` in the same diff.

## What landed

**1. `make pr-prep`** (`Makefile`, `CLAUDE.md`) — single command that
chains `make index` and `make ci-fast-spec-coupling`. Discoverable via
`make help`; runs both the index regen and the coupling-gate verdict
locally before `git commit`. The fix prints when the index drifts:

```
==> pr-prep: codebase-index refreshed, coupling gate clean.

  ⚠  build/codebase-index/index.json drifted — stage it:
       git add build/codebase-index/index.json
```

**2. `.githooks/pre-commit`** — opt-in strict gate. Off by default;
enable per-clone with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Refuses
commits when the index is stale and prints the exact `make pr-prep`
fix line. Bypass available with `git commit --no-verify` for
emergencies. Both run the existing read-only `codebase-indexer check`
binary — no working-tree mutations, no auto-commits.

`CLAUDE.md` §"Build Commands" picks up a new sub-section explaining
the indexer's input set and pointing at both interventions.

## Spec drift

`Makefile` is claimed by 8 specs (102, 104, 105, 116, 127, 128, 134, 135).
None of those specs' contracts or invariants change — this is a new
target plus help-text entry, additive only. Same waiver pattern as
PR #142 / #143 / #144.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Makefile additive new target (pr-prep) + help-text entry — no existing target semantics changed; no spec invariant affected; documented contributor flow only.

## Test plan

- [x] `make pr-prep` runs locally: `make index` succeeds (no-op when
      inputs already current), `make ci-fast-spec-coupling` runs the
      gate against `origin/main` and reports verdict. Exits non-zero
      on this PR with a Makefile-claimant message — that's the gate
      working correctly, satisfied by this PR's `Spec-Drift-Waiver:`.
- [x] `.githooks/pre-commit` rejects commits when the index is stale
      (smoke-tested locally by enabling the hook and making a no-spec
      edit).
- [ ] PR CI green (existing checks).

title: ci(deployd-api): parameterize helm install with TARGETARCH
body:
## Summary

Second of two preventative follow-ups to PR #141 / #142. Drops the hard-coded
`linux-amd64` from the deployd-api Dockerfile's helm install layer and routes
the URL + extraction path through BuildKit's automatic `TARGETARCH`. The
Dockerfile is now arm64-ready without any further edits when a downstream
platform target needs it.

## What changed

`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Dockerfile`:

- Declares `ARG TARGETARCH` in the runtime stage so BuildKit's
  cross-build value enters scope.
- `helm-${HELM_VERSION}-linux-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz` and
  `/tmp/linux-${TARGETARCH}/` replace the literal `amd64` references.

Helm release-asset naming aligns 1:1 with `TARGETARCH` values BuildKit emits
(`amd64`, `arm64`), so no mapping layer is needed.

## Behaviour today vs. tomorrow

- **Today** (CD does not pass `--platform`): BuildKit defaults `TARGETARCH`
  to the host arch — `linux/amd64` on `ubuntu-latest`. The image produced
  is byte-identical to today's amd64-only image.
- **Tomorrow** (CD adds `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64`): the same
  Dockerfile produces both arches. No further Dockerfile edit needed.

## Spec drift

`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Dockerfile` is claimed by spec 073
(axiomregent-unification, package owner) and spec 136 (Phase 2.b Helm
bridge). The TARGETARCH parameterization removes a latent assumption from
the helm install layer but does not change any spec invariant or contract
clause. Same waiver pattern as PR #142 and PR #143.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: build-system parameterization (TARGETARCH) — removes a literal-arch assumption; no spec invariant change; produces the same amd64 image when --platform is unset.

## Test plan

- [ ] PR CI green (existing checks).
- [ ] If PR #143 has merged before this PR's CI runs, the new
      `docker-build` job exercises this Dockerfile change with
      `TARGETARCH=amd64` (host arch) and proves the parameterization
      compiles. If PR #143 hasn't merged yet, the validation lands on
      next push or merge-into-main.
- [ ] On merge, `cd-deployd-api-rs` Docker build still succeeds (no
      multi-arch yet — `--platform` is still unset by the CD workflow).

title: fix(spec-136): unbreak deployd-api Dockerfile helm install
body:
## Summary

Hotfix for [PR #141](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/pull/141)
— the post-merge `cd-deployd-api-rs` run
([25944630938](https://github.com/stagecraft-ing/open-agentic-platform/actions/runs/25944630938))
failed at the helm install layer with:

```
dpkg : Depends: tar (>= 1.28-1) but it is not going to be installed
E: Error, pkgProblemResolver::Resolve generated breaks, this may be
   caused by held packages.
```

## Root cause

`debian:bookworm-slim` ships `tar` as a dpkg-essential dependency. Listing
it in `apt-get install` confuses the resolver, and the subsequent
`apt-get purge -y curl tar` would have broken `dpkg` itself.

## Fix

Stream the helm tarball with `curl | tar xz` instead of installing+purging
the `tar` package. Only `curl` participates in the apt transaction.

## Spec drift

The Dockerfile is claimed by spec 073 (axiomregent-unification, package-level
owner) and spec 136 (Phase 2.b Helm bridge). Neither spec's invariants,
contract clauses, or narrative are affected by this fix — it is a debian
package-resolution regression introduced by the PR #141 Dockerfile edit and
caught only post-merge because `cd-deployd-api-rs` does not run on PRs.
The corrective change is local to the apt transaction layer, not to any
spec-bound behaviour. Same pattern as the dep-refresh waiver precedent
(per spec 127 §FR-005).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: build-system-only Dockerfile apt-resolver patch — no spec invariant changes; the dpkg/tar regression was a PR-time blind spot because cd-deployd-api-rs does not run on pull_request.

A separate follow-up will land the preventative gate so this class of
failure is caught at PR time (`docker build` step in `ci-deployd-api-rs.yml`).

## Test plan

- [ ] PR CI green (Rust untouched).
- [ ] On merge, `cd-deployd-api-rs` Docker build completes past the helm
      install layer and pushes `ghcr.io/.../deployd-api:sha-<sha>` +
      `:latest`.
- [ ] Hetzner deploy step rolls deployd-api to the new image.

Local Docker validation skipped — the dev machine's macOS Docker daemon
isn't running. The fix targets a specific apt-resolver behaviour and is
minimal.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs, not this one)

- Add a `docker build` step to `ci-deployd-api-rs.yml` so future Dockerfile
  changes are validated at PR time, not main-merge time.
- Multi-arch image: current Dockerfile hardcodes `linux-amd64` for helm.
  Switch to `${TARGETARCH}` substitution when arm64 deployd-api images are
  needed (Hetzner is amd64-only today).

title: spec(136): Phase 2.b — deployd-api Helm migration via embedded charts
body:
## Summary

Closes the Phase 2.b gate on spec 136. `deployd-api-rs` no longer hand-rolls
Kubernetes objects via kube-rs — it shells `helm upgrade --install` against
charts embedded into the binary at compile time, with stagecraft's
`chartSelector` (Phase 2) as the upstream resolver. The image is
self-contained: no chart registry pull at runtime, no out-of-band ConfigMap.

This unblocks the spec 137 Phase 4 work that was waiting on a Helm-driven
deployd-api (per the project memory note linking 136 → 137).

## What changed

- **`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/src/helm.rs`** (NEW) — `HelmRunner`
  shelling `helm` v3 (`upgrade --install --wait --output json`,
  `uninstall --wait`, `template` as a test seam), embedded `tenant-hello`
  chart bytes via `include_str!`, pure `build_values()` for the values
  mapping, error taxonomy.
- **`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/src/k8s.rs`** — shrunk to
  `probe_cluster()` only. Local dev without a kubeconfig still
  short-circuits to `ROLLED_OUT` (record-only), preserving the previous UX.
- **`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/src/routes.rs`** — `DeploymentRequest`
  accepts optional `chart` + `chart_version` (defaults: `tenant-hello`,
  `0.1.0`). `create_deployment` / `delete_deployment` drive Helm inside
  `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- **`platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Dockerfile`** — bundles helm v3.16.4;
  builder stage broadened to the `platform/` context.
- **`.github/workflows/cd-deployd-api-rs.yml`** — Docker build context bumped
  to `platform`, explicit `file:` directive added.
- **`.github/workflows/ci-deployd-api-rs.yml`** — `azure/setup-helm` step so
  the `helm template` tests assert in CI instead of no-op'ing.
- **`platform/services/stagecraft/CLAUDE.md`** — new "Chart selection and
  deploy wire contract (spec 136)" section.
- **`specs/136-tenant-hello-demo-service/spec.md`** + **`tasks.md`** —
  T021/T022 ticked, decisions captured (shell vs Rust Helm lib, embed
  vs registry, context broadening), `implements:` list extended to the
  files this PR touches.

## Scope discipline (CONST-005)

- Phase 3 (negative-path C-clause violations) and Phase 4 (lifecycle flip)
  still require a live cluster. Both stay **out** of this PR.
- spec 136 frontmatter stays `implementation: in-progress` — SC-002 has
  not been evidenced yet.

## Test plan

      `platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Cargo.toml` — 19 unit tests green
      locally (including `helm template` rendering positive + ingress

## Summary

Lands spec 137 Phases 0–3 (passwordless OIDC tenant access gates via Rauthy) plus a session-prep housekeeping commit closing the spec 145 merge-wave drift.

**Phase 4 (deployd-api K8s renderer) is intentionally NOT in this PR** — it depends on spec 136 Phase 2.b (Helm migration) landing first, per the [Option B decision recorded in spec.md](specs/137-tenant-environment-access-gates/spec.md#open-question--dual-renderer-for-phase-4-filed-2026-05-15).

## What ships

### Spec-closure housekeeping (1 commit)
- **144** hiqlite default-features: status `draft → approved` + tasks ticked (impl landed 2026-05-10 at 5476596c; only housekeeping outstanding).
- **146** deployd-api memory hardening: status `draft → approved + closed` under the implicit-close-loop framing (chart wave deployed via PR #124).
- **147** spec-kind grammar: implementation `pending → in-progress` (Phase 1 already landed across compiler/lint/indexer/amendment records; subsequent phases pending).
- **143** §13 ledger: FU-022 closed by back-ref to 146 closure.

Registry: draft `5 → 2` / approved `139 → 142`.

### Spec 137 Phases 0–3 (6 commits)

**Phase 0** — clarifications resolved. Five decisions locked from spec analysis (oauth2-proxy topology, schema shape, hostname stability, user mapping, Auth Providers UX); decision 3 (Rauthy admin contract) closed via empirical T003 smoke against the live Rauthy 0.35 instance from inside the cluster.

T003 smoke results (`specs/137-tenant-environment-access-gates/execution/rauthy-admin-smoke.{md,json}`):
- (a) Volume: PASS — 10 clients, 2–3ms steady-state
- (b) Delete: PASS — DELETE 200, post-delete GET 404
- (c) Flow toggle: PASS via PUT — **Rauthy 0.35 has NO `password_login_enabled` field; password disable is `flows_enabled` minus `\"password\"`. No PATCH endpoint.**
- (d) Provider binding: deferred — no upstream providers configured at smoke time

**Pre-implementation spec amendment** per the `feedback_pre_implementation_spec_amendments` discipline: spec.md §Access-gate contract + FR-004 + Success Criteria amended to replace the non-existent `password_login_enabled: false` scalar with the actual `flows_enabled` array mechanism. Load-bearing intent (platform never sees passwords) preserved verbatim; only the mechanism corrected.

**Phase 1** — schema migration 40 (`environment_access_gates` + `environment_access_gate_allowlist_emails` tables). Three CHECK constraints (`enabled_requires_ref`, `federated_provider_values`, `federated_pair_consistent`). `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `environments(id)`. Case-insensitive uniqueness via `lower(value)` index (no citext — FIPS-mode Postgres). Both migrations validated against live Postgres in a BEGIN…ROLLBACK txn; up + down round-tripped clean.

**Phase 2** — Stagecraft API CRUD. Four endpoints under `/api/environments/:environmentId/access-gate{,/allowlist,/allowlist/:entryId}`. Audit-log emission on every mutation (`tenant.gate.descriptor.{enabled,disabled}` / `tenant.gate.allowlist.{added,removed}`). FR-007 defense-in-depth password-field rejection as a pure helper.

**Phase 3** — Rauthy admin client provisioning. Typed wrapper for the four admin verbs + idempotent provision/deprovision. `putAccessGate` rewired to auto-provision on enable / auto-deprovision on disable; callers no longer pass `rauthyClientRef`. `addAllowlistEntry` wired to `provisionRauthyUser` for magic-link email entries (FR-008 propagation hook).

**FR-004 invariant** (no password authentication on gate clients) enforced via `assertNoPasswordFlow` guard inside both create + PUT paths — a hand-built payload cannot bypass it.

## Out of scope (this PR)

- **Phase 4** — deployd-api K8s renderer. Deferred to post-spec-136-Phase-2.b (Option B / Helm overlay path).
- **Phase 5** — Stagecraft UI for managing gates per environment.
- **Phase 6** — lifecycle flip (`implementation: pending → complete`).

## Verification

- **26 vitest tests passing** (Phase 2: 12 pure-helper tests; Phase 3: 14 pure-helper + stub-fetch tests).
- **TypeScript clean** (`npx tsc --noEmit` on stagecraft).
- **Coupling gate** OK (20 diff paths on the last regen).
- **Migration validated** against live Hetzner Postgres in a rollback transaction; tables created + indexed + dropped cleanly.
- **Rauthy admin smoke** validated end-to-end against live Rauthy 0.35 from inside the cluster (10-client create + roundtrip-PUT + idempotent DELETE + cleanup).

title: spec(147): kind grammar amendment — Phase 1 landing
body:
## Summary

Lands spec 147 (spec-kind grammar) Phase 1: grammar additions + schema bumps + tooling support, all at warning severity per the C3 decision. The amendment promotes `kind` to a validated 16-value enum, introduces `shape` + `category` universal dimensions, declares per-kind structural contracts for capability/registry/profile, serializes `implements:` to registry output (closing a silent-consumption gap), and adds the `primary:` per-claim flag that resolves spec 130 OQ-1 as a corpus-wide invariant.

Spec 147 is the third amendment to spec 000 (after specs 119, 132) and the first amendment to spec 128. Both amended specs gain `amended:` / `amendment_record:` frontmatter and additive body content; no frozen-anchor content is modified.

Phase 1 is grammar landing only. V-013/V-014/V-015/V-017 promotion to error severity is explicitly deferred to a separate follow-on amendment after a critical mass of new-kind specs exercises the contract.

## Multi-target amendment surface (spec 133 gate double-duty)

This PR is the first real exercise of spec 133's amends-aware coupling gate against a multi-target amendment. Each amended spec is independently traced:

| Spec amended | File(s) edited | How the coupling gate clears |
|---|---|---|
| spec 000 | `specs/000-bootstrap-spec-system/spec.md` (scalar `amendment_record:` overwrite + summary narration) and `specs/000-bootstrap-spec-system/contracts/registry.schema.json` (1.5.0 field declarations) | spec 147's `amends: ["000", "128"]` forward link + 147's `spec.md` in the diff |
| spec 000 contract | `specs/000-bootstrap-spec-system/contracts/registry.schema.json` | spec 132 owns this path via `implements:` — its 000-cascade amendment_record back-link now points to 147, so editing 147 clears the gate for spec 132's claim. Also spec 001 implements the spec-compiler; its edit is in the diff via spec 147's amendment |
| spec 128 | `specs/128-spec-lint-default-fail-on-warn/spec.md` (frontmatter + new §7 body section) | spec 147's `amends: ["000", "128"]` forward link |
| spec-compiler | `tools/spec-compiler/src/lib.rs`, `tools/spec-compiler/tests/code_aliases.rs` | spec 001 implements `tools/spec-compiler`; its edit is in the diff (147's amendment is the impetus) |
| spec-lint | `tools/spec-lint/src/lib.rs`, `tools/spec-lint/src/main.rs` | spec 006 implements spec-lint; 128 amends 006 — both surface in the amend chain |
| codebase-indexer | `tools/codebase-indexer/src/{spec_scanner,types,xref}.rs`, `schemas/codebase-index.schema.json` | spec 101 implements `tools/codebase-indexer`; 147 amends the schema field set |
| spec-code-coupling-check fixtures | `tools/spec-code-coupling-check/src/lib.rs` (4 test fixtures gain `primary: None`) | spec 127 (amended by 130, 133) owns this path; the test fixture change is a downstream type cascade from the codebase-indexer schema 1.4.0 bump |

If the coupling gate fires on any of these in CI, that's a bug in the gate (likely spec 130/133 not yet handling multi-target amends) and should be diagnosed before merge. Per Bart's flag: the PR is doing double duty — verification of spec 147 AND regression test for spec 133 against multi-target amenders.

## Commits

1. `spec(147)`: author the spec (governance, draft)
2. `spec(000,128)`: record the amendment in amended-spec frontmatter
3. `spec(147,001)`: spec-compiler KNOWN_KEYS extension, VALID_KINDS, SHAPE_TABLE reservation, V-012..V-019 at warning severity, registry schema 1.5.0, conformance test refreshed (the "land 1-3 atomically" ask)
4. `spec(147,006,128)`: spec-lint severity tier infrastructure + W-130 (info), W-131 (warning), W-132 (info corpus phase) per spec 128 §7
5. `spec(147,101,133)`: codebase-indexer `primary: Option<bool>` flag + schema 1.4.0; spec-code-coupling-check test fixture cascade
6. `chore(index)`: derived-artifact refresh — `build/codebase-index/index.json` + featuregraph golden

## What this PR does NOT do

Per spec 147 §Out of scope and the C3 decision:
- Does not promote V-013..V-017 to error severity (deferred to a separate follow-on amendment after open-ended new-kind authoring exercises the contract).
- Does not close spec 130 OQ-1 (the `primary:` mechanism is the proving ground; closure ships as a separate follow-on after soak time).
- Does not reclassify specs 119 and 132 to `kind: amendment` (historical record stands).
- Does not backfill `kind:` on the 28 unkinded specs (that's Phase 2, separately revertible).
- Does not author the three new-kind proving-ground specs (capability/registry/profile) — that's Phase 3.
- Does not rewire W-002/W-003 from prose scans to frontmatter checks — that's Phase 4.
- Does not switch featuregraph's `implements:` consumption path from codebase-index to registry.json (substantive enough for a Phase 1.5 follow-up).

## Self-eligibility

Spec 147 classifies itself per the grammar it introduces: `kind: amendment, shape: mechanism-add`. Per the (kind, shape) table this amendment establishes, this is the precise self-description. Four commitments hold (per spec 147 §Constitutional positioning):

1. Optionality — new universal fields are OPTIONAL; V-002 NOT TOUCHED.
2. V-code allocation — V-012..V-019 used, V-006..V-010 NOT POPULATED.
3. extraFrontmatter cap preserved — markdown-truth-boundary NOT TOUCHED.
4. Spec 128's fail-on-warn posture preserved at the warning tier (empty-W-set audit posture is warning-tier-only; info tier is additive).

`amends_sections: []` — V-011 does not fire at compile time. No frozen anchor of spec 000 is modified.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make ci` passes on CI (zero warning-tier W-codes against the 148-spec corpus per spec 128's empty-W-set posture)
- [ ] Schema gate accepts registry.json 1.5.0 + codebase-index.json 1.4.0
- [ ] Spec 133's amends-aware coupling gate clears each amender→amended pair listed in the "Multi-target amendment surface" table
- [ ] `spec-compiler` emits V-012..V-019 at warning severity only (no errors)
- [ ] `spec-lint --fail-on-warn` exits 0 (info-tier W-130/W-132 emit but do not gate)
- [ ] `codebase-indexer check` confirms index is fresh against the post-Phase-1 corpus
- [ ] Featuregraph golden test passes against the regenerated fingerprint

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)

- Phase 1.5: switch featuregraph to consume `implements:` from registry.json instead of joining via codebase-index.
- Phase 2: backfill `kind:` on the 28 unkinded specs; promote V-012 to error.
- Phase 3: author capability/registry/profile proving-ground specs.
- Phase 4: rewire W-002/W-003 prose scans to frontmatter checks; promote V-018/V-019 to error.
- Separate amendment: close spec 130 OQ-1 once `primary:` has soaked.
- Separate amendment: promote V-013/V-014/V-015/V-017 to error after open-ended new-kind authoring.

---

## Update — coupling-gate cascade resolved (2026-05-14)

First CI run surfaced 11 coupling-gate firings against the original `amends: ["000", "128"]`. The gate is correctly enforcing FR-005 strict-expansion: amend back-links only resolve for `specs/<id>/spec.md` paths, never for code paths. For code paths claimed via `implements:`, the diff must contain at least one claimant's spec.md.

Resolved via honest amends expansion (commit 28d6af2): spec 147's `amends:` now reads `["000", "128", "001", "006", "101", "132", "133"]`. Each new amendee gained `amended:` + `amendment_record:` frontmatter and a one-line summary callout per spec 119 convention. Rationale per amendee in the commit message.

The "Multi-target amendment surface" table above is now superseded by the expanded list. Each amendee covers a distinct path-claim cluster:

| Amendee | Surface cleared |
|---|---|
| 001 | `tools/spec-compiler/**` (V-012..V-019 added) |
| 006 | `tools/spec-lint/**` (severity tiers + W-130/131/132) |
| 101 | `tools/codebase-indexer/**`, `schemas/codebase-index.schema.json` (primary flag, schema 1.4.0) |
| 132 | `specs/000-bootstrap-spec-system/contracts/registry.schema.json` (1.4.0 → 1.5.0) |
| 133 | `tools/spec-code-coupling-check/src/lib.rs` (test fixture cascade from index schema bump) |

## Spec-Drift-Waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` is a derived test artifact regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`. The featuregraph source is unchanged by this PR; the golden fingerprint shifted only because spec 147 itself is a new record in the corpus. The five implements-claimants of the golden file (034, 039, 091, 093, 096) have no semantic surface modified by spec 147 — amending any of them would be spurious. Pure derived-artifact refresh.

title: chore(deps): bump date-fns from 3.6.0 to 4.1.0
body:
Bumps [date-fns](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns) from 3.6.0 to 4.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from date-fns's releases.

v4.1.0

This release adds time zone support to format functions (that I somehow missed when working on the feature) and fixes a few bugs.

Make sure also upgrade TZDate to v1.0.2 as it includes a bunch of critical bug fixes.

Fixed

  • Fixed internal constructFrom throwing an exception on null arguments. While null isn't allowed, the functions should rather return Invalid Date or NaN in such cases. See #3885.

Added

  • Added missing time zone support to format, formatISO, formatISO9075, formatRelative and formatRFC3339. See #3886.

v4.0.0

I have great news! First, ten years after its release, date-fns finally gets first-class time zone support.

Another great news is that there aren't many breaking changes in this release. All of them are type-related and will affect only those explicitly using internal date-fns types. Release notes

Sourced from tailwindcss's releases.

v4.3.0

Added

  • Add @container-size utility (#18901)
  • Add scrollbar-{auto,thin,none} utilities for scrollbar-width, and scrollbar-thumb-* / scrollbar-track-* color utilities for scrollbar-color (#19981, #20019)
  • Add scrollbar-gutter-* utilities (#20018)
  • Add zoom-* utilities (#20020)
  • Add tab-* utilities (#20022)
  • Allow using @variant with stacked variants (e.g. @variant hover:focus { … }) (#19996)
  • Allow using @variant with compound variants (e.g. @variant hover, focus { … }) (#19996)
  • Support --default(…) in --value(…) and --modifier(…) for functional @utility definitions (#19989)

Fixed

  • Ensure @plugin resolves package JavaScript entries instead of browser CSS entries when using @tailwindcss/vite (#19949)
  • Fix relative @import and @plugin paths resolving from the wrong directory when using @tailwindcss/vite (#19965)
  • Ensure CSS files containing @variant are processed by @tailwindcss/vite (#19966)
  • Resolve imports relative to base when result.opts.from is not provided when using @tailwindcss/postcss (#19980)
  • Canonicalization: preserve significant _ whitespace in arbitrary values (#19986)
  • Canonicalization: add parentheses when removing whitespace from arbitrary values would hurt readability (e.g. w-[calc(100%---spacing(60))] → w-[calc(100%-(--spacing(60)))]) (#19986)
  • Canonicalization: preserve the original unit in arbitrary values instead of normalizing to base units (e.g. -mt-[20in] → mt-[-20in], not mt-[-1920px]) (#19988)
  • Canonicalization: migrate arbitrary :has() variants from [&:has(…)] to has-[…] (#19991)
  • Upgrade: don’t migrate inline style attributes (e.g. style="flex-grow: 1" → style="flex-grow: 1", not style="grow: 1") (#19918)
  • Allow multiple @utility definitions with the same name but different value types (#19777)
  • Export missing PluginWithConfig type from tailwindcss/plugin to fix errors when inferring plugin config types (#19707)
  • Ensure start and end legacy utilities without values do not generate CSS (#20003)
  • Ensure --value(…) is required in functional @utility definitions (#20005)
  • Canonicalization: preserve required whitespace around operators in negated arbitrary values (e.g. -left-[(var(--a)+var(--b))]) (#20011)

Updates `yaml` from 2.8.4 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from yaml's releases.

v2.9.0

The changes here are really only patches, but I'm releasing this as a minor version to note a small change to the documentation of parseDocument() and parseAllDocuments(): I've removed the claim that they'll "never throw".

It remains the case that practically all non-malicious inputs will be handled without emitting an error, but there is a decent chance that code paths remain where e.g. a RangeError due to call stack exhaustion can be triggered by malicious inputs. Up to now, I've considered these as security vulnerabilities, and in fact it's the only category of error for which yaml CVEs have been issued so far.

Starting from this release, I'll be considering such errors as bugs, but not vulnerabilities. I do welcome people and/or LLMs looking for them, but please report them as normal issues rather than suspected security vulnerabilities. This also applies to previously undiscovered bugs in earlier releases.

  • fix: Avoid calling Array.prototype.push.apply() with large source array
  • fix(lexer): Avoid recursive calls that may exhaust the call stack

title: chore(deps): update rand requirement from 0.8 to 0.10 in /crates/factory-engine
body:
Updates the requirements on [rand](https://github.com/rust-random/rand) to permit the latest version.
Changelog

Sourced from rand's changelog.

[0.10.1] — 2026-02-11

This release includes a fix for a soundness bug; see #1763.

Changes

  • Document panic behavior of make_rng and add #[track_caller] (#1761)
  • Deprecate feature log (#1763)

#1761: rust-random/rand#1761 #1763: rust-random/rand#1763

[0.10.0] - 2026-02-08

Changes

  • The dependency on rand_chacha has been replaced with a dependency on chacha20. This changes the implementation behind StdRng, but the output remains the same. There may be some API breakage when using the ChaCha-types directly as these are now the ones in chacha20 instead of rand_chacha (#1642).
  • Rename fns IndexedRandom::choose_multiple -> sample, choose_multiple_array -> sample_array, choose_multiple_weighted -> sample_weighted, struct SliceChooseIter -> IndexedSamples and fns IteratorRandom::choose_multiple -> sample, choose_multiple_fill -> sample_fill (#1632)
  • Use Edition 2024 and MSRV 1.85 (#1653)
  • Let Fill be implemented for element types, not sliceable types (#1652)
  • Fix OsError::raw_os_error on UEFI targets by returning Option<usize> (#1665)
  • Replace fn TryRngCore::read_adapter(..) -> RngReadAdapter with simpler struct RngReader (#1669)
  • Remove fns SeedableRng::from_os_rng, try_from_os_rng (#1674)
  • Remove Clone support for StdRng, ReseedingRng (#1677)
  • Use postcard instead of bincode to test the serde feature (#1693)
  • Avoid excessive allocation in IteratorRandom::sample when amount is much larger than iterator size (#1695)
  • Rename os_rng -> sys_rng, OsRng -> SysRng, OsError -> SysError (#1697)
  • Rename Rng -> RngExt as upstream rand_core has renamed RngCore -> Rng (#1717)

Additions

  • Add fns IndexedRandom::choose_iter, choose_weighted_iter (#1632)
  • Pub export Xoshiro128PlusPlus, Xoshiro256PlusPlus prngs (#1649)
  • Pub export ChaCha8Rng, ChaCha12Rng, ChaCha20Rng behind chacha feature (#1659)
  • Fn rand::make_rng() -> R where R: SeedableRng (#1734)

Removals

  • Removed ReseedingRng (#1722)
  • Removed unused feature "nightly" (#1732)
  • Removed feature small_rng (#1732)
