title: feat(spec-145): deployd-api durability chain — PVC + scrub-narrow + s3 backup + restore-on-startup
body:
## Summary

Closes spec 145. deployd-api-rs's `deployments` + `deployment_events` Hiqlite tables are now durable across pod evictions, encrypted-snapshot-backed in S3, and restorable on startup.

- **PVC flipped on** (Hetzner: 10Gi `hcloud-volumes`); old `rm -rf /var/lib/deployd/data/*` startup wrapper removed (`templates/deployment.yaml:39-43`).
- **Hiqlite cargo features** `backup, s3, auto-heal` enabled; `DEPLOYD_BACKUP_*` → `HQL_*` env-translation layer in `src/config.rs::BackupConfig` (Hiqlite's `BackupConfig` is private + unnameable, so `NodeConfig::from_env()` is the only callable path).
- **Encrypted S3 snapshots** wired via cryptr keyring; default cron `0 0 */6 * * *`, retention 28 days.
- **Restore-on-startup** via `HQL_BACKUP_RESTORE=s3:<key>` operator-driven env (FR-005b): runbook `docs/runbooks/deployd-api-durability.md` §3 walks the procedure including the load-bearing UNSET step.

## AC results — Phase 4 live validation (Hetzner)

| AC | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Insert row → `kubectl delete pod` → re-query | **PASS** — byte-identical (SHA-256 match), pod cdtb6 → rt2zw |
| AC-2 | Snapshot → `kubectl delete pvc` + `HQL_BACKUP_RESTORE` → re-query | **PASS** — restore log trail observed; in-snapshot row present, post-snapshot decoy correctly erased; UNSET verified at `/proc/1/environ` |
| AC-3 | Cron snapshot emitted to S3 | **PASS** — `backup_node_1_<unix-ts>.sqlite` at configured cadence; cryptr envelope confirmed (active key id `k1` at byte offset 6) |
| AC-4 | Rollout-restart preserves data | **PASS** — byte-identical hash; no scrub/wipe lines |
| AC-5 | cargo build/clippy/test | green |
| AC-6 | `helm template -f values-hetzner.yaml` | green |
| AC-7 | Runbook walk-through | sign-off captured; **two amendments** (see below) |
| AC-8 | spec-code coupling | green for spec 145 paths; golden file waiver below |
| AC-9 | `make ci` | green except featuregraph golden waiver |

## Latent regressions caught and fixed during live validation

Both fixes downstream of dependabot's jsonwebtoken 9→10 bump (commit `04aa8f73`), missed by unit tests because none exercised the live Rauthy auth path:

1. **Missing crypto provider feature** (`fbc113ad`) — jsonwebtoken 10.x requires explicit `rust_crypto` or `aws_lc_rs` feature. Without it, the first JWT decode panics:
   ```
   thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at jsonwebtoken-10.3.0/src/crypto/mod.rs:125:42:
   Could not automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider from jsonwebtoken crate features.
   ```
   Enabled `aws_lc_rs` (already in lockfile via reqwest's rustls path — feature activation only, no new dep).

2. **Mixed-family algorithm validation rejected** (`fbdbcff0`, `auth.rs`) — jsonwebtoken 10 `decoding.rs:342` rejects when `validation.algorithms` contains any entry whose family differs from the active verifier provider. The prior `vec![RS256, EdDSA]` tripped this on every EdDSA token. Narrowed to header alg after an explicit cross-family allowlist gate.

3. **Audience config aligned with Rauthy 0.35** (`fbdbcff0`, chart + workflow) — Rauthy 0.35's client_credentials flow reflects `client_id` as the JWT `aud` claim verbatim, ignoring RFC 8707 `resource=` at token time. Removed CD workflow's `--set oidc.audience=https://deploy.<domain>` override; pinned `values-hetzner.yaml` `oidc.audience` to `stagecraft-m2m` (the actual M2M client_id). Spec 143 §12 L-006 is the companion default-scopes-is-load-bearing lesson on the Rauthy side.

Runtime config (out-of-repo): also patched `stagecraft-m2m` client's `default_scopes` on the live Rauthy to include `deployd:deploy` (was in `allowed_scopes` only — same Rauthy 0.35 quirk).

## Runbook amendments (T041 sign-off)

T054 execution exposed two real gaps in `docs/runbooks/deployd-api-durability.md`:

- **§3.3 pre-flight callout** — §3.1 lists "accidental `kubectl delete pvc`" and "cross-cluster migration" as DR scenarios but §3.3 jumped straight to `kubectl set env HQL_BACKUP_RESTORE=...`. K8s does NOT auto-recreate PVCs that pods reference: T054's new pod sat `Pending` 5 min on `FailedScheduling: persistentvolumeclaim "deployd-api-data" not found` until `helm upgrade --reuse-values` reconciled the PVC manifest.
- **§3.4 stronger UNSET check** — original verification was Deployment-spec-only (`kubectl get deployment ... | grep HQL_BACKUP_RESTORE`); per the `spec-145-t054-unset-verification` memory the running pod's `/proc/1/environ` is the load-bearing surface. Added the `tr "\0" "\n" </proc/1/environ` check alongside.

## Provenance — T050 skip-with-justification

Phase 4 pre-deploy (T050) was skipped after read-only confirmation that the four `backup-*` keys were already present on the cluster (kubectl-patch managedFields timestamp `2026-05-11T13:44:11Z`). The prior write was performed by an earlier Claude Code session without per-step authorization (transcript `df7b4f24-ff28-4811-9f38-ef994af11843.jsonl`, `2026-05-11T05:36:19Z`). Captured as motivating evidence in spec **`147-tool-permission-vs-authorization`** (draft).

## Test plan

- [x] AC-1 live (POST + delete pod + GET — SHA-256 hash equal)
- [x] AC-2 live (PVC delete + restore env + verify in-snapshot row present, post-snapshot decoy erased, /proc/1/environ unset)
- [x] AC-3 live (S3 listing 10× consecutive snapshots at expected cadence; cryptr envelope confirmed)
- [x] AC-4 live (rollout-restart byte-identical hash, no scrub lines)
- [x] AC-5 (`cargo build/clippy/test` warm green via CD CI gate)
- [x] AC-6 (`helm template` green; CD deploy-hetzner ran cleanly)
- [x] AC-7 (runbook walk-through with two amendments — see above)
- [x] AC-8 (`spec-code-coupling-check` green for spec 145 paths)
- [x] AC-9 (`make ci` warm green except waivered golden file)
- [x] T061 frontmatter flip; `registry-consumer show` confirms `status: approved`, `implementation: complete`, `closed: 2026-05-15`

Spec-Drift-Waiver: `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` churn is collateral of spec 145's status flip (draft→approved, implementation pending→complete). The golden file is claimed by five featuregraph-evolution specs (034/039/091/093/096) per spec 130; no semantic change to featuregraph behaviour, only a snapshot of the new registry state. Regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test --manifest-path crates/featuregraph/Cargo.toml --test golden`.

title: fix(102,047): unblock make ci after 1dfbbc2 — clippy + downstream lockfiles
body:
## Summary

Three pre-existing breakages on main from `1dfbbc2` (Ed25519 layered signing) that block `make ci` warm:

- **clippy `unused_mut`** in `crates/policy-kernel/src/proof_chain.rs` tests at lines 508 and 533 — `ProofChainWriter::build_anchor` is `&self` (not `&mut self`), so `let mut w = …` is unused mutability in two test bodies that only call `build_anchor`. Fix: drop `mut`.
- **clippy `doc-lazy-continuation`** in `crates/factory-engine/src/governance_certificate.rs:839` — Rust 1.95 (toolchain-pinned) flags the third line of a 3-line doc comment as needing indentation to be recognized as a continuation. Fix: indent line 839 by two spaces per clippy's `help: indent this line` suggestion.
- **`Cargo.lock` drift** in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/` and `tools/policy-compiler/` — `1dfbbc2` added `ed25519-dalek`, `base64`, `rand` to `crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml` but only refreshed the workspace lockfile and `platform/services/deployd-api-rs/Cargo.lock`. The two other workspaces that pull policy-kernel as a path dep were left stale. Fix: `cargo check --manifest-path <both manifests>` (no hand-edit).

No behavioral change. Both clippy fixes are mechanical lint compliance in test code; both lockfile refreshes are transitive-dep entries cargo writes automatically.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: ed25519-dalek transitive lockfile refresh (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock claimed by specs 032/041/064/065/076/083/084/119; tools/policy-compiler/Cargo.lock claimed by specs 047/131) + Rust 1.95 clippy fallout (crates/policy-kernel/src/proof_chain.rs claimed by specs 036/047/068/090/093/102; crates/factory-engine/src/governance_certificate.rs claimed by specs 075/094/102). No behavioral change; these are mechanical lint compliance + transitive lockfile entries cargo writes deterministically from the manifests already on main.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make ci` warm → exit 0 on this branch
- [ ] `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` → exit 0
- [ ] `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/factory-engine/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` → exit 0
- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path crates/policy-kernel/Cargo.toml` → existing proof_chain tests still green (mut-removal is test-only and doesn't change behavior)

## Governance follow-up (not in this PR's scope)

`1dfbbc2` merged with `make ci` red against Rust 1.95 + the unused-mut introduced by `build_anchor: &self`. The toolchain is pinned at 1.95.0 in `rust-toolchain.toml`, so CI runs the same version a contributor's local check would. Worth investigating: did CI for #122 skip `make ci`, or was the parity check broken at the time? A small follow-up spec could codify "no PR merges with `make ci` red" as an enforceable gate, separately from this cleanup.

title: fix(102,047): Ed25519 layered signing for cert + chain anchor
body:
## Summary

Closes the HIAS readiness assessment's headline Critical finding: the governance certificate's `certificateHash` was a self-referential SHA-256, accepting any cert whose hash had been recomputed by an adversary after tampering. The same self-referential weakness applied one level deeper to the proof-chain `policy_bundle_hash` genesis anchor (the chain's hashes re-derive themselves; no external trust root).

This is the **P0-3a** landing of layered Ed25519 signing (your Option C — both `operator` and `ephemeral` kinds; `sigstore-rekor` anchor + `--hias-strict` mode are contracted but deferred to P0-3b).

- **Spec 102** (governance certificate) — Amendment 2026-05-11 after FR-010. Reframes FR-008 as content binding (defence-in-depth, not authoritative). Adds **FR-008.1** (Ed25519 signature), **FR-008.2** (public-key embedding), **FR-008.3** (attestation taxonomy: `unsigned`/`ephemeral`/`operator`/`sigstore-rekor`), **FR-008.4** (verifier signature check, fail-closed), **FR-008.5** (HIAS-strict mode, deferred), **FR-008.6** (proof-chain anchor companion).
- **Spec 047** (governance control plane) — Amendment 2026-05-11 after FR-010. Adds **FR-009.1**/**FR-009.2**/**FR-009.3** for chain genesis anchor signing.
- **`crates/factory-engine`** — `GovernanceCertificate` gains `signing_public_key`, `cert_signature`, `signing_attestation`. `resolve_signing_material()` resolves `OAP_SIGNING_KEY` env → operator, `OAP_SIGNING_KEY_PATH` env → operator, ephemeral fallback. Malformed operator material panics (no silent downgrade). `compute_certificate_hash` zeros both signature fields (content fingerprint stable across signing). `verify_certificate` runs signature check FIRST (FR-008.4 is the authoritative provenance check); hash check retained as defence-in-depth.
- **`crates/policy-kernel`** — new `ProofChainAnchor` carrying chain_id, bundle hash, timestamp, pub key, signature, attestation. `ProofChainWriter::build_anchor` produces signed anchor. `verify_proof_chain_with_anchor` runs anchor signature → bundle cross-check → existing chain walk in that order. New error variants `AnchorSignature(String)` + `AnchorBundleHashMismatch`.

## The load-bearing test

`tamper_with_hash_resign_attack_is_caught_by_signature` in `governance_certificate.rs` closes the HIAS report's load-bearing claim: adversary tampers a field, recomputes the SHA-256 hash, and the cert is hash-consistent. Under the pre-amendment FR-008 contract this would have passed verification. Under FR-008.1+, the adversary lacks the signing key and cannot mint a new Ed25519 signature, so `verify_certificate` fails at step 0 (signature check). Mirror chain-side test: `tamper_anchor_fails_signature`.

## Spec coupling

Spec 102 implements `crates/factory-engine` + `crates/policy-kernel`; spec 047 also implements `crates/policy-kernel`. Both specs amended; both crates edited; coupling gate satisfied via either claimant per spec 130 / FR-003.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p factory-engine governance_certificate` — 7/7 pass
- [x] `cargo test -p open_agentic_policy_kernel proof_chain` — 8/8 pass (4 new anchor tests + 4 pre-existing)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` — 84 test-suite runs, zero failures
- [x] `spec-lint` exit 0
- [x] `spec-compiler compile` deterministic, exit 0
- [x] `cargo audit --file crates/Cargo.lock` still clean post-P0-1
- [ ] Manual smoke: set `OAP_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)`, run `factory-run`, confirm `governance-certificate.json` has `signing_attestation.kind: \"operator\"`
- [ ] Manual smoke: run `verify-certificate` against a cert with a flipped field + recomputed hash but no resigned signature; confirm exit 1 with `Ed25519 signature verification failed`

## Deferred to P0-3b

- `SigningAttestationKind::SigstoreRekor` — CI workflow adds `sigstore/cosign-installer` + cosign sign-blob over the canonical cert bytes; emits a Rekor inclusion proof alongside the cert
- `verify-certificate --hias-strict` flag — rejects any cert whose attestation kind ≠ `sigstore-rekor`, validates the Rekor inclusion proof
- Same `--hias-strict` semantics for `verify_proof_chain_with_anchor`
- README Try-it-block update demonstrating Sigstore-anchored verification end-to-end

The Ed25519 substrate this PR lands is exactly what the Sigstore work layers over: same canonical-bytes layout, same signature-field placement, same verifier hook. P0-3b is mostly CI workflow + Rekor client integration.

## Suggested review order

1. Read the two spec amendments first — `specs/102-governed-excellence/spec.md` (Amendment block after FR-010) and `specs/047-governance-control-plane/spec.md` (Amendment block after FR-010). They are the contract.
2. Then `governance_certificate.rs` — the cert-side implementation. Pay particular attention to the field-zeroing order in `compute_certificate_hash` and `compute_certificate_signature` (hash zeros both signature fields; signature zeros only itself, leaves hash populated).
3. Then `proof_chain.rs` — same pattern applied chain-side.
4. The tamper-resigning test is the proof that the contract holds.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: crates/Cargo.lock (claimed by spec 144-hiqlite-default-features) updates as a mechanical lockfile resync from the ed25519-dalek + base64 + rand dependency additions in factory-engine and policy-kernel; no hiqlite-related change. The substantive spec coupling for this PR is satisfied by amendments to specs 102 and 047.

title: fix(145): remove deployd boot scrub (HIAS finding closure)
body:
## Summary

- Apply spec 145 §2.2 Option B verbatim: remove the `command: [\"/bin/sh\", \"-c\"]` + `rm -rf /var/lib/deployd/data/*` wrapper from the deployd-api chart. Container falls back to the image's default `CMD [\"deployd-api\"]` (Dockerfile L12).
- Add the \"Rationale — partial landing ahead of the full chain\" block to spec 145 §2.2 documenting the HIAS discovery context, the PVC-survives-but-contents-do-not characterisation, and explicit deferral of §2.1 (PVC flip), §2.3 (Hiqlite backup/s3/auto-heal), §2.4 (restore-on-startup).
- Spec 145 status stays `draft` / `implementation: pending` — the chain isn't complete yet; only the immediate safety fix lands here.
- New static-guard test `spec145-deployd-scrub.config.test.ts` (3 vitest assertions mirroring spec146-deployd-memory's shape) catches drive-by regressions reintroducing the shell-wrapped wipe.

## Why

External HIAS readiness assessment surfaced the `rm -rf /var/lib/deployd/data/*` boot scrub as Critical/High. The wipe destroys the deployd audit trail (`deployments` + `deployment_events`) on every pod restart **even when `persistence.enabled: true`** — the PVC survives but its contents do not, which is worst-of-both (durable from K8s's perspective, ephemeral from the application's). This is a P0 because it affects current deployments, not just the procurement story.

## Spec coupling

Spec 145 implements `platform/charts/deployd-api/templates/deployment.yaml`. The chart edit and the spec amendment land in the same commit. The new test path is added to spec 145's `implements:` list so future edits stay coupled.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/spec145-deployd-scrub.config.test.ts` — 3/3 pass
- [x] Companion `spec146-deployd-memory.config.test.ts` still passes — 3/3 (6/6 combined)
- [x] `helm template deployd-api platform/charts/deployd-api` — 7 manifests rendered, no `rm -rf`, `command:`, or `/bin/sh -c` in output
- [x] `spec-lint` exit 0
- [x] `spec-compiler compile` deterministic, exit 0
- [ ] AC-4 / T055 integration test (pod restart against populated PVC; `deployments` + `deployment_events` rowsets preserved) — **deferred**, lands with the full durability chain that requires live cluster + Hiqlite

## Deferred (will land with the full durability chain)

- §2.1: env values files still set `persistence.enabled: false` on Hetzner
- §2.3: Cargo features still `[\"sqlite\"]` only — no `backup`, `s3`, `auto-heal`
- §2.4: no restore-on-startup logic in `store.rs`

title: fix(crates): patch RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099/0104 (rustls-webpki)
body:
## Summary

- Surgical feature narrowing on `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` + `aws-config` in `crates/provider-registry/Cargo.toml`: `default-features = false`, drop the legacy `rustls` feature (pulled `aws-smithy-http-client/legacy-rustls-ring` → rustls 0.21 → rustls-webpki 0.101.7), keep `default-https-client` (modern rustls 0.23 → rustls-webpki 0.103).
- Closes three High/Medium RUSTSEC advisories (`RUSTSEC-2026-0098`, `0099`, `0104`) surfaced by an external HIAS readiness assessment and confirmed against the live RustSec advisory DB.
- `[patch.crates-io]` was infeasible — rustls 0.21 semver-locks rustls-webpki `^0.101` with no patched release on that line. Feature-surgery was the only mechanical option.

## Why

The vulnerable chain was reachable through the non-default `bedrock` feature of `provider-registry` (spec 042, NF-004). `cargo audit` flags it regardless of feature activation because the lockfile resolves the union, so the CVEs would block the supply-chain gate on the next advisory-DB refresh even if no production build enables `bedrock`.

## Spec coupling

Spec 042 implements `crates/provider-registry` (directory). The Cargo.toml edit triggers the coupling gate. The change is a dependency-security patch *narrowing* the AWS SDK feature surface in line with NF-004 (\"Bedrock adapter behind cargo feature flag to avoid mandatory heavy dependencies\") — no specified behaviour change. A `Spec-Drift-Waiver` line is included in the commit body for the gate.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo audit --file crates/Cargo.lock` — 3 vulnerabilities → 0 (only pre-exempted bincode + paste warnings remain)
- [x] Lockfile drops the entire legacy chain: `rustls 0.21.12`, `rustls-webpki 0.101.7`, `hyper-rustls 0.24.2`, `tokio-rustls 0.24.1`, `h2 0.3.27`, `hyper 0.14.32`, `sct 0.7.1`
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` clean
- [x] `cargo check -p provider-registry --features bedrock` clean (modern rustls 0.23 chain only)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` — 84 test-suite runs, zero failures
- [ ] Re-verify on a fresh clone: `cargo install cargo-audit --locked && cargo audit --file crates/Cargo.lock`

Spec-Drift-Waiver: crates/Cargo.lock (claimed by spec 144-hiqlite-default-features) and crates/provider-registry/Cargo.toml (claimed by spec 042-multi-provider-agent-registry) are dependency-security narrowing — no hiqlite change, no provider-registry behaviour change. Aligns with spec 042 NF-004 ("Bedrock adapter behind cargo feature flag to avoid mandatory heavy dependencies").

title: feat(spec-144): hiqlite default-features hygiene
body:
## Summary

Lands [spec 144 — Hiqlite default-features hygiene](specs/144-hiqlite-default-features/spec.md). Three coupled manifest edits stop Cargo from unifying Hiqlite's upstream default features (`auto-heal`, `backup`, `s3`, `toml`) across the `crates/` workspace. title: spec(143): FU-001 Tier 1 closure — FU-009 + FU-010 + FU-011 Finding 1
body:
## Summary

Three commits, sequenced for the Tier 1 closure gate. Neither alone produces a green scheduled tick — together they unblock the cluster-side runtime path. Closure narrative lands as a separate §13 entry post-deploy.

- `9a7d784` **FU-010** — chart `client_secret_post` body-form auth + §12 L-007. Replaces `--user` with `--data-urlencode "client_id=…"` + `--data-urlencode "client_secret=…"` in `cronjob-orphan-sweeper.yaml`. Rauthy 0.35 has narrowed RFC 6749 §2.3.1 to body-form only; HTTP Basic returns 400.
- `32129d1` **FU-011 Finding 1** — `m2mAuth.ts` issuer via OIDC discovery + §12 L-008. Replaces string-concat `expectedIssuer` with `getJwksAndIssuer()` mirroring `rauthy.ts::validateJwt:201`. JWKS-failure posture (warn-level reject-on-throw) is named explicitly in code, deliberately diverging from `validateJwt`'s error level for the cron-sweeper hot path. 6 new unit tests; full auth suite green (23/23).
- `5d5dec2` **FU-009** — `post-create.sh` legacy-delete label-gate. Wraps the `kubectl delete cronjob` in a check on `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` so setup.sh re-runs against a Helm-owned successor preserve it.
- `f08a941` chore: regenerate codebase index — single-file delta (new `m2mAuth.test.ts`).

L-007 and L-008 land verbatim in §12 alongside their fixes. Cross-referenced as a three-Rauthy-0.35-invariant family with L-006 (scope inertia).

## Audit findings (in commit bodies, not yet pulled into spec)

- **`M2mClaims.sub` null-handling.** All four `validateM2mRequest` call sites (`grants.ts`, `audit.ts`, `scheduler.ts`, `policy.ts`) use it for throw-side-effect only; no consumer reads `M2mClaims.sub`. TS-interface mismatch (`sub: string` vs runtime `null`) stays latent and harmless. **No FU-012 filed** — no active bug, only static-type imprecision that cannot fire today.
- **`rauthy.ts::validateJwt` JWKS error handling.** Audited at `rauthy.ts:270-273`. Top-level try/catch logs at error level, returns null. Not a silent swallow. No observation surfaced.

## Branch base

Branched off `a03f59c` (chore index regen) sitting on top of `312e109`. Index regen is inert relative to the work; the four commits are reviewable on their own merits.

## Spec-code-coupling waiver

Spec-Drift-Waiver: spec 143 FU-011 Finding 1 closure (Tier 1). Edits cross the `platform/services/stagecraft/api/auth/` seam claimed by 077/080/087/106. Scoped changes: `rauthy.ts` gains a single `export` on `getJwksAndIssuer` (no behavior change, enables the m2mAuth.ts call); `m2mAuth.ts` replaces string-concat issuer derivation with the discovery-canonical issuer call per §12 L-008; `m2mAuth.test.ts` is a new test file covering the issuer logic. All three files are explicitly cited in spec 143 §12 L-008's Affected line and in the FU-011 commit body. The platform-wide auth-validator audit (Finding 3) remains open under FU-011 Tier 2 — the seam-closure work that would establish a proper primary owner is tracked there, not in this PR. Mass-amending owner specs (per the Dep-Refresh-Waiver precedent reasoning) is the wrong shape here.

## Test plan (post-deploy gates per review)

- [ ] Beat 6.4 evidence line A reproduces in the cronjob's pod — HTTP 200 token mint with body-form `client_id`/`client_secret`. Confirms chart-rendered shape matches the manual proof, not a question of validity.
- [ ] Beat 6.4 evidence line B flips from 401 → 200 — handler accepts the Rauthy-minted Bearer with the discovery-canonical issuer.
- [ ] ≥1 scheduled tick fires successfully under `*/30 * * * *` — `kubectl get jobs -n stagecraft-system -l app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm | grep knowledge-orphan-imported-sweeper` shows a Completed job with non-zero start time post-deploy.
- [ ] `setup.sh` re-run does not destroy the cronjob — `metadata.uid` preserved across re-run (FU-009 label-gate proof).

Spec 143 Tier 1 closes when all four green. §13 closure entry lands as a separate commit with the verification evidence inline.

title: chore(deps): bump diff from 8.0.4 to 9.0.0
body:
Bumps [diff](https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff) from 8.0.4 to 9.0.0.
Changelog

Sourced from diff's changelog.

9.0.0

(All changes part of PR #672.)

  • ES5 support is dropped. parsePatch now uses TextDecoder and Uint8Array, which are not available in ES5, and TypeScript is now compiled with the "es6" target. From now on, I intend to freely use any features that are deemed "Widely available" by Baseline. Users who need ES5 support should stick to version 8.

  • C-style quoted strings in filename headers are now properly supported.

    When the name of either the old or new file in a patch contains "special characters", both GNU diff and Git quote the filename in the patch's headers and escape special characters using the same escape sequences that are used in string literals in C, including octal escapes for all non-ASCII characters. Previously, jsdiff had very little support for this; parsePatch would remove the quotes, and unescape any escaped backslashes, but would not unescape other escape sequences. formatPatch, meanwhile, did not quote or escape special characters at all.

    Now, parsePatch parses all the possible escape sequences that GNU diff (or Git) ever output, and formatPatch quotes and escapes filenames containing special characters in the same way GNU diff does.

  • formatPatch now omits file headers when oldFileName or newFileName in the provided patch object are undefined, regardless of the headerOptions parameter. (Previously, it would treat the absence of oldFileName or newFileName as indicating the filename was the word "undefined" and emit headers --- undefined / +++ undefined.)

  • formatPatch no longer outputs trailing tab characters at the end of ---/+++ headers.

    Previously, if formatPatch was passed a patch object to serialize that had empty strings for the oldHeader or newHeader property, it would include a trailing tab character after the filename in the --- and/or +++ file header. Now, this scenario is treated the same as when oldHeader/newHeader is undefined - i.e. the trailing tab is omitted.

  • formatPatch no longer mutates its input when serializing a patch containing a hunk where either the old or new content contained zero lines. (Such a hunk occurs only when the hunk has no context lines and represents a pure insertion or pure deletion, which for instance will occur whenever one of the two files being diffed is completely empty.) Previously formatPatch would provide the correct output but also mutate the oldLines or newLines property on the hunk, changing the meaning of the underlying patch.

  • Git-style patches are now supported by parsePatch, formatPatch, and reversePatch.

    Patches output by git diff can include some features that are unlike those output by GNU diff, and therefore not handled by an ordinary unified diff format parser. An ordinary diff simply describes the differences between the content of two files, but Git diffs can also indicate, via "extended headers", the creation or deletion of (potentially empty) files, indicate that a file was renamed, and contain information about file mode changes. Furthermore, when these changes appear in a diff in the absence of a content change (e.g. when an empty file is created, or a file is renamed without content changes), the patch will contain no associated ---/+++ file headers nor any hunks.

    jsdiff previously did not support parsing Git's extended headers, nor hunkless patches. Now parsePatch parses some of the extended headers, parses hunkless Git patches, and can determine filenames (e.g. from the extended headers) when parsing a patch that includes no --- or +++ file headers. The additional information conveyed by the extended headers we support is recorded on new fields on the result object returned by parsePatch. See isGit and subsequent properties in the docs in the README.md file.

    formatPatch now outputs extended headers based on these new Git-specific properties, and reversePatch respects them as far as possible (with one unavoidable caveat noted in the README.md file).

  • Unpaired file headers now cause parsePatch to throw.

    It remains acceptable to have a patch with no file headers whatsoever (e.g. one that begins with a @@ hunk header on the very first line), but a patch with only a --- header or only a +++ header is now considered an error.

  • parsePatch is now more tolerant of "trailing garbage"

    That is: after a patch, or between files/indexes in a patch, it is now acceptable to have arbitrary lines of "garbage" (so long as they unambiguously have no syntactic meaning - e.g. trailing garbage that leads with a +, -, or and thus is interpretable as part of a hunk still triggers a throw).

    This means we no longer reject patches output by tools that include extra data in "garbage" lines not understood by generic unified diff parsers. (For example, SVN patches can include "Property changes on:" lines that generic unified diff parsers should discard as garbage; jsdiff previously threw errors when encountering them.)

    This change brings jsdiff's behaviour more in line with GNU patch, which is highly permissive of "garbage".

  • The oldFileName and newFileName fields of StructuredPatch are now typed as string | undefined instead of string. This type change reflects the (pre-existing) reality that parsePatch can produce patches without filenames (e.g. when parsing a patch that simply contains hunks with no file headers).

  • 7a49317 Bump dependencies again (#682)
  • afe5aec Add Git support, and otherwise variously improve & fix parsePatch (and other ...

Release notes

Sourced from reqwest's releases.

v0.13.3

tl;dr

  • Fix CertificateRevocationList parsing of PEM values.
  • Fix logging in resolver to only show host, not full URL.
  • Fix hickory-dns to fallback to a default if /etc/resolv.conf fails.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to handle STOP_SENDING as not an error.
  • Fix HTTP/3 pool to remove timed out QUIC connections.
  • Fix HTTP/3 connection establishment picking IPv4 and IPv6.
  • Upgrade rustls-platform-verifier.
  • (wasm) Only use wasm-bindgen on unknown-* targets.

What's Changed

  • Update docs.rs Features by @​JamesWiresmith in seanmonstar/reqwest#2961
  • fix: fallback to hickory_resolver's default config if reading /etc/resolv.conf fails by @​monosans in seanmonstar/reqwest#2797
  • fix: remove timeout con by @​cuiweixie in seanmonstar/reqwest#2967
  • http3: handle stop_sending without error by @​anuraaga in seanmonstar/reqwest#2978
  • resolve: debug log to change only host by @​lms0806 in seanmonstar/reqwest#2992
  • Edit reference link by @​lms0806 in seanmonstar/reqwest#2996

  • [HTTP/3] Optimize IPv6 fallback and enforce HTTPS scheme #2911 by @​lyuzichong in seanmonstar/reqwest#3006
  • Upgrade rustls-platform-verifier by @​jplatte in seanmonstar/reqwest#3010
  • use wasm-bindgen ecosystem only for wasm32-unknown-* target by @​Ludea in seanmonstar/reqwest#3000

Full Changelog: https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/compare/v0.13.2...v0.13.3

v0.13.2

tl;dr

  • Fix HTTP/2 and native-tls ALPN feature combinations.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to send h3 ALPN.
  • (wasm) fix RequestBuilder::json() from override previously set content-type.

What's Changed

  • chore(deps): bump actions/checkout from 5 to 6 by @​dependabot[bot] in seanmonstar/reqwest#2921
  • Update readme for 0.13 by @​VojtaStanek in seanmonstar/reqwest#2926
  • fix http2 feature is not enabled for "native-tls" by @​fox0 in seanmonstar/reqwest#2927
  • chore(deps): remove unused webpki-roots and rustls-native-certs by @​seanmonstar in seanmonstar/reqwest#2932
  • docs: native-tls-alpn has changed to native-tls-no-alpn by @​seanmonstar in seanmonstar/reqwest#2940

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from reqwest's changelog.

v0.13.3

  • Fix CertificateRevocationList parsing of PEM values.
  • Fix logging in resolver to only show host, not full URL.
  • Fix hickory-dns to fallback to a default if /etc/resolv.conf fails.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to handle STOP_SENDING as not an error.
  • Fix HTTP/3 pool to remove timed out QUIC connections.
  • Fix HTTP/3 connection establishment picking IPv4 and IPv6.
  • Upgrade rustls-platform-verifier.
  • (wasm) Only use wasm-bindgen on unknown-* targets.

v0.13.2

  • Fix HTTP/2 and native-tls ALPN feature combinations.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to send h3 ALPN.
  • (wasm) fix RequestBuilder::json() from override previously set content-type.

v0.13.1

  • Fixes compiling with rustls on Android targets.

v0.13.0

  • Breaking changes:
    • rustls is now the default TLS backend, instead of native-tls.
    • rustls crypto provider defaults to aws-lc instead of ring. (rustls-no-provider exists if you want a different crypto provider)
    • rustls-tls has been renamed to rustls.
    • rustls roots features removed, rustls-platform-verifier is used by default.
      • To use different roots, call tls_certs_only(your_roots).
    • native-tls now includes ALPN. To disable, use native-tls-no-alpn.
    • query and form are now crate features, disabled by default.
    • Long-deprecated methods and crate features have been removed (such as trust-dns, which was renamed hickory-dns a while ago).
  • Many TLS-related methods renamed to improve autocompletion and discovery, but previous name left in place with a "soft" deprecation. (just documented, no warnings)
    • For example, prefer tls_backend_rustls() over use_rustls_tls().

v7.15.0

Minor Changes

  • Stabilize unstable_defaultShouldRevalidate as defaultShouldRevalidate on <Link>, <Form>, useLinkClickHandler, useSubmit, fetcher.submit, and setSearchParams (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize the instrumentation APIs. unstable_instrumentations is now instrumentations and unstable_pattern is now pattern (a993f09)

    • The unstable_ServerInstrumentation, unstable_ClientInstrumentation, unstable_InstrumentRequestHandlerFunction, unstable_InstrumentRouterFunction, unstable_InstrumentRouteFunction, and unstable_InstrumentationHandlerResult types have had their unstable_ prefixes removed
    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize unstable_mask as mask on <Link>, useLinkClickHandler, and useNavigate, and rename the corresponding Location.unstable_mask field to Location.mask (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize the unstable_normalizePath option on staticHandler.query and staticHandler.queryRoute as normalizePath (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize future.unstable_passThroughRequests as future.v8_passThroughRequests (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Remove unstable_subResourceIntegrity from the runtime FutureConfig type; the flag is now controlled by the top-level subResourceIntegrity option in react-router.config.ts (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize unstable_url as url on loader, action, and middleware function args (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

  • Stabilize unstable_useTransitions as useTransitions on <BrowserRouter>, <HashRouter>, <HistoryRouter>, <MemoryRouter>, <Router>, <RouterProvider>, <HydratedRouter>, and useLinkClickHandler (a993f09)

    • ⚠️ This is a breaking change if you have already opted into the unstable version - you will need to update your code accordingly

Patch Changes

  • Add nonce to <Scripts> <link rel="modulepreload"> elements (if provided) (af5d49b)

  • Fix a bug with unstable_defaultShouldRevalidate={false} where parent routes that did not export a shouldRevalidate function could be incorrectly included in the single fetch call for new child route data (#15012)

  • Improve server-side route matching performance by pre-computing flattened/cached route branches (#14967) (af5d49b)

    • Performance benchmarks showed roughly a 10-15% improvement in server-side request handling performance

  • Mark mask as an optional field in Location for easier mocking in unit tests (#14999)

  • Cache flattened/ranked route branches to optimize server-side route matching (#14967)

  • Improve route matching performance in Framework/Data Mode (#14971) (af5d49b)

    • Avoiding unnecessary calls to matchRoutes in data router scenarios
      • This includes adding back the optimization that was removed in 7.6.0 (#13562)
      • The issues that prompted the revert have been addressed by using the available router matches but always updating match.route to the latest route in the manifest
    • Leverage pre-computed pre-computing flattened/cached route branches during client side route matching
    • Performance benchmarks showed roughly a 15-30% improvement in server-side request handling performance

Sourced from base64's changelog.

0.22.1

  • Correct the symbols used for the predefined alphabet::BIN_HEX.

0.22.0

  • DecodeSliceError::OutputSliceTooSmall is now conservative rather than precise. That is, the error will only occur if the decoded output cannot fit, meaning that Engine::decode_slice can now be used with exactly-sized output slices. As part of this, Engine::internal_decode now returns DecodeSliceError instead of DecodeError, but that is not expected to affect any external callers.
  • DecodeError::InvalidLength now refers specifically to the number of valid symbols being invalid (i.e. len % 4 == 1), rather than just the number of input bytes. This avoids confusing scenarios when based on interpretation you could make a case for either InvalidLength or InvalidByte being appropriate.

  • Fix get_maximum_output_size overflow on 32-bit targets #205 (thanks @​dglittle)
Cast input_len to u64 before multiplying by 110, avoiding overflow on
32-bit targets (e.g. wasm32) where input_len * 110 overflows usize
when input_len > ~39MB.

0.12.1 (2026-03-14)

Security Fix

  • Fix handling of invalid match offsets during decompression #a0b9154 (thanks @​Marcono1234)
Invalid match offsets (offset == 0) during decompression were not properly
handled, which could lead to invalid memory reads on untrusted input.
Users on 0.12.x should upgrade to 0.12.1.

0.12.0 (2025-11-11)

  • Fix integer overflows when decoding large payloads #192 (thanks @​teh-cmc)
This fixes an u32 integer overflow when decoding large payloads in the block format.
Note: The block format is not suitable for such large payloads, since it
keeps everything in memory. Consider using the frame format for large data.

This change also removes a unsafe fast-path for write_integer to simplify the code.

The performance impact is on incompressible data, which is already fast enough.

0.11.6 (2026-03-14)

Security Fix

title: docs(spec-137): planning artifacts — plan.md + tasks.md (no code changes)
body:
## Summary

Per the user-directed scope (spec 137 is multi-week and has 6 open §Clarifications): produce planning artifacts only, do not start implementation. Spec lifecycle stays `status: draft`, `implementation: pending`.

This PR adds **`plan.md`** and **`tasks.md`** alongside the existing `spec.md`. No code changes.

## Plan structure

| Phase | Focus | Gating |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Resolve 6 §Clarifications + lock contract | Approval-blocking; no FR-001..FR-010 code under draft (Principle III) |
| 1 | Schema migration (env-gate table + sibling allowlist) | Phase 0 |
| 2 | Stagecraft API CRUD (descriptor + allowlist endpoints) | Phase 1 |
| 3 | Rauthy admin client + provisioning | Phase 2 |
| 4 | deployd-api K8s renderer (oauth2-proxy + Ingress annotations) | Phase 3 |
| 5 | Stagecraft UI (toggle + allowlist + login methods) | Phase 4 |
| 6 | End-to-end evidence + lifecycle flip | All previous |

The plan deliberately makes Phase 0's clarifications the gate to approval rather than collapsing them into "implement whatever fits" — CONST-005 self-check.

## Key load-bearing decisions deferred to Phase 0

1. oauth2-proxy topology (per-env vs shared)
2. Schema shape (sibling table vs JSONB on environments)
3. Rauthy admin API contract (volume, deletion, password-login toggle, Auth Provider reference)
4. Hostname stability convention (`<env-slug>.<project-slug>.<org-slug>.tenants.<base>` candidate)
5. User → Rauthy mapping (auto-provision + magic-link defaults)

## Summary

Closes spec 139 §7.2's `template_remote → scaffold_source_id` rename for the one adapter (`aim-vue-node`) that didn't get migrated in 139's Phase 2.

- **Phase 1 (`4543bce`)** — emit-side rewrite: both projection paths (template-origin synthetic + OAP-native) emit `orchestration_source_id` / `scaffold_source_id` / `scaffold_runtime` sourced from a single `OAP_NATIVE_ADAPTERS` constant (AC-2). - **Phase 2 (`eed0411`)** — read-side rewrite: scaffold warmup, per-request scaffold, and `create.ts` now resolve the clone target via `factory_upstreams (org_id, source_id=manifest.scaffold_source_id)` instead of reading `manifest.template_remote`. `WarmupContext.templateRemote → scaffoldRepoUrl`; `defaultBranch → scaffoldRef`. `ScaffoldAdapterRef` loses the now-vestigial legacy fields.
- **Phase 3 (`b205461`)** — readiness fallback removal: `hasTemplateRemote` deleted from `AdapterReadinessVerdict` / `ScaffoldReadinessResponse` and the matching web client type. `createEligible = scaffoldSourceResolved`. Banner copy on `app.projects.new.tsx` simplified; `stagecraft/CLAUDE.md` updated. `resolveBlocker` extracted to a pure module so the unit test runs under bare vitest.

### Acceptance criteria status
- **AC-1** ✓ — `grep -r template_remote platform/services/stagecraft --include='*.ts' --exclude='*.test.ts'` returns only spec-140 explanatory comments.
- **AC-2** ✓ — `OAP_NATIVE_ADAPTERS["aim-vue-node"].scaffoldSourceId` is the single string-literal home; `projection.ts` and `translator.ts` import via `oapNativeAdapters.ts` (extracted to break import cycle through `extractFrontmatter`).

- **AC-7** ✓ via this PR's `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` line below — see "Coupling gate" section.

### Coupling gate

Spec 140's `implements:` list was extended in this PR to claim the four production paths the spec's tasks already mandated touching (T024 migration `up.sql`, T061 `web/app/lib/projects-api.server.ts`, plus two new helper modules `oapNativeAdapters.ts` and `scaffoldReadinessBlocker.ts` extracted to satisfy AC-2 and T051's testability).

The remaining nine paths the gate flags are tests, the migration's `.down.sql`, and `vite.config.ts`. None of those specs have anything to do with this rename — editing them would be unrelated noise. They are conventionally handled via waiver, consistent with prior cutover commits in this codebase (e.g. `f9aa6be`, `4b58066`).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: spec 140 is an `amends:` cutover; the residual flagged paths are tests, a migration `.down.sql`, and `vite.config.ts` claimed only by sweep-level ancestor specs (077/080/087/108/112/113/114/119/138) that have no per-file ownership of this rename.

title: spec(133): amends-aware spec/code coupling gate
body:
## Summary
- Closes the 2026-05-02 false-positive class: spec 127's gate now recognises spec 119's `amends:` (forward) and `amendment_record:` (reverse) protocol as valid coupling alongside `implements:`. A diff editing an amended spec's `spec.md` is cleared by either the amender's spec.md or the amendment-record target's spec.md, composing with spec 130's primary-owner heuristic.
- Indexer schema bumps 1.2.0 → 1.3.0 (additive: `amends`/`amendmentRecord` on `traceMapping`). Short-form ids (`amends: ["000"]`) are resolved to full ids at index-build time. `CODEBASE-INDEX.md` gains an "Amendment Relationships" subsection (14 rows in the current corpus).
- **Strict-expansion gate (FR-005):** the new amend pathways only fire when a path already has at least one `implements:` claimant. Without this, editing your own `spec.md` would create a new firing condition whenever an unrelated amender existed — converting today's silent paths into tomorrow's failures. Spec body §5.2 documents the runtime gate.
- Renderer (FR-004): violations with non-empty amend links print aligned `implements:` / `amends:` / `amendment_record:` rows; implements-only violations keep the spec 130 compact form unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path tools/spec-code-coupling-check/Cargo.toml` — 11 unit + 8 integration tests green (incl. new `amends_link_clears_amended_spec_path`, `amendment_record_clears_amended_spec_path`, `non_spec_path_unaffected_by_amends_extension`, `violation_renderer_labels_owner_sources`).

`tests/platform_client.rs` mutates `XDG_CACHE_HOME` via
`std::env::set_var` — a process-global write. The four integration
tests using it all reuse the same `reservation_for_extract_at(\"h-1\")`
fixture, so they hash to the same content-addressed cache subpath.
Under concurrent test execution the env var races: test A's tempdir
gets overwritten by test B before A reads it, and A ends up
materialising into B's tempdir (which already has B's cache),
observing `warm = true` instead of cold. The result is the
`assertion failed: !first.warm` panic at line 384 of
`materialise_run_root_warm_cache_skips_fetches`.

## What changed

Added a static `Mutex<()>` (named `env_lock()` for parity with the
`ENV_LOCK` pattern in `src/cache_root.rs:98`). `isolate_cache_dir()`
now returns an `EnvScope` RAII bundle that holds the mutex guard +
tempdir together; binding it via `let _scratch = …` keeps both alive
for the test's full duration. Lock recovers from poisoning so a
panicking earlier test doesn't cascade-fail subsequent tests.

## Why this PR before merging spec 135 PR #87

Spec 135 FR-05 (PR #87) collapses `ci-crates.yml` to a workspace job.
That job runs the full `factory-platform-client` test suite under
heavy concurrency on every CI run, which makes this latent flake
manifest reliably. Landing the fix first unblocks PR #87.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p factory-platform-client --tests -- --test-threads=8` — 33 tests, 2 consecutive runs, all pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p factory-platform-client --tests -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] CI green on this PR

Spec-Drift-Waiver: factory-platform-client is claimed by spec 124; this is a test-only flake fix without design content.

title: fix(spec-134): ci-fast-stagecraft cd scope (each background job needs its own cd)
body:
## Summary

Run #5 of `make ci-fast` (post-#79, all accelerators on) hit:

```
npm error Missing script: "test"
make[1]: *** [ci-fast-stagecraft] Error 1
```

…even though `platform/services/stagecraft/package.json` defines `"test": "vitest"`. Root cause: a subtle bash parsing bug.

The recipe was:

```makefile
cd platform/services/stagecraft && \
  ( CI=true npx tsc --noEmit ) & TSC_PID=$$!; \
  ( CI=true npm test ) & VT_PID=$$!; \
  …
```

Bash parses `cd X && cmd &` as "background the subshell that does cd-then-cmd". The `cd` runs **inside the backgrounded subshell** — the parent shell's CWD is unchanged. So:

- Job 1 (`cd X && tsc`) runs in `stagecraft/` ✓
- Job 2 (`npm test`) runs in repo root, where the pnpm workspace root `package.json` has no `test` script → fails

Note: `ci-fast-desktop` doesn't have this bug because it uses `pnpm --filter @opc/desktop`, which selects the right package regardless of CWD.

## Fix

Each backgrounded compound has its own explicit `cd`:

```diff
- cd platform/services/stagecraft && \
-   ( CI=true npx tsc --noEmit ) & TSC_PID=$$!; \
-   ( CI=true npm test ) & VT_PID=$$!; \
+ ( cd platform/services/stagecraft && CI=true npx tsc --noEmit ) & TSC_PID=$$!; \
+ ( cd platform/services/stagecraft && CI=true npm test ) & VT_PID=$$!; \
```

Same for the wait/exit logic — unchanged.

## Wall-time trajectory

| Run | Wall | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #1 (estimated) | 90+ min | Original baseline |
| #4 (warm cargo, +nextest, sccache cold) | 21m53s | Failed at nextest empty-tests |
| **#5 (post-#79, all accelerators on)** | **4m53s** | Failed at this stagecraft cd bug |
| #6 (predicted, post this fix) | < 5 min | Expected first end-to-end clean run |

`ci-fast-stagecraft` alone runs in **17 seconds, exit 0, 299/299 tests pass** with the fix.

## Verified locally

- `make ci-fast-stagecraft` — exit 0 in 17s, 299/299 vitest tests pass
- `./tools/ci-parity-check/target/release/ci-parity-check` — OK (recipe edit stays inside the spec 134 sentinel region)

title: fix(spec-134): nextest --no-tests=pass to match cargo test semantics
body:
## Summary

Run #4 of `make ci-fast` (post-#78 recipe fix, with cargo-nextest + sccache freshly installed) hit:

```
────────────
 Nextest run ID … with nextest profile: default
    Starting 0 tests across 1 binary
────────────
     Summary [   0.000s] 0 tests run: 0 passed, 0 skipped
error: no tests to run
(hint: use `--no-tests` to customize)
make[1]: *** [ci-fast-rust] Error 4
```

`cargo nextest run` treats a test binary with zero `#[test]` functions as failure by default; `cargo test` treats it as success silently. The workspace has crates whose `tests/` directories (or `examples/`, `benches/` directories caught by `--all-targets`) contain no `#[test]` fns. The spec 134 §2.2(2) "strict superset" substitution clause doesn't extend to this difference — empty test surfaces are not a regression.

## Fix

One-line change to `CIFAST_CARGO_TEST`:

```diff
-  CIFAST_CARGO_TEST := nextest run
+  CIFAST_CARGO_TEST := nextest run --no-tests=pass
```

Now nextest matches `cargo test`'s 0-tests-as-success behaviour.

## Wall-time signal from the broken run

**Run #4: 1313s wall (21m53s)**, even with the failure mid-flight. Already inside the SC-01 ≤ 25 min warm target. Headline drivers:

- Per-sub-target fan-out (concurrent `make -j$(CIFAST_JOBS)`)
- nextest substitution (~2-3× test execution speed-up)
- Warm cargo target dirs from runs #1–#3
- **sccache cache hits: 0** this run — cargo's incremental cache absorbed the recompile work. sccache wins arrive on the run after a target-dir invalidation.

A clean run with this fix should land cleanly inside SC-01 territory and give us the first real `docs/ci-fast-bench.md` baseline.

title: fix(spec-134): ci-fast-tools recipe — BSD xargs -I{} buffer fix
body:
## Summary

`make ci-fast` (3rd run on a clean main, after #75/#76/#77 closed all the test/lint debt) failed instantly at the very first sub-target with:

```
xargs: command line cannot be assembled, too long
make[1]: *** [ci-fast-tools] Error 1
```

This is a **recipe-level bug in spec 134's Makefile section**, not test/code debt. BSD xargs (macOS default) caps the `-I{}` replacement buffer at **255 bytes** by default. The `ci-fast-tools` recipe had a multi-line `sh -ec '…'` template with 4 `{}` substitutions of the manifest path; after substitution the assembled argv exceeds the buffer and BSD xargs refuses to launch it. GNU xargs would tolerate this — spec 134 explicitly scopes `ci-fast` to Apple Silicon local dev, so the BSD path matters.

## Fix

Drop `-I{}` entirely. Pass the manifest as a positional arg, read it as `$1` in the wrapper script. No replacement buffer involved.

```makefile
# Before
xargs -n1 -P$(CIFAST_JOBS) -I{} sh -ec '\
  …{} substitutions…'

# After
xargs -n1 -P$(CIFAST_JOBS) sh -c '\
  m="$$1"; \
  …reads from $$m…' _
```

## Bundled cleanup (zero behaviour change)

- **Drop `cargo --jobs $(CIFAST_CARGO_JOBS)`.** Under `make -j` the jobserver throttles cargo automatically; the explicit flag is silently ignored and emits a warning per invocation: `"a -j argument was passed to Cargo but Cargo is also configured with an external jobserver in its environment, ignoring the -j parameter"`. Removing it eliminates the warning, changes nothing about actual concurrency.
- **`&&` chains instead of `;`** between cargo invocations. A failed clippy now short-circuits the test step (and the `[done ]` echo), instead of running them and falsely reporting success.

## Verified locally

- `make ci-fast-tools` standalone — `exit=0`, all 7 `[done ]` markers, no errors
- `./tools/ci-parity-check/target/release/ci-parity-check` — still OK (the edit stayed inside the `# BEGIN ci-fast (spec 134)` / `# END ci-fast` sentinels — the parity exemption holds)

## Spec coupling

This is a recipe-internal bug fix in lines bracketed by the spec 134 sentinel markers. No design content. Same waiver pattern as #73/#75/#76/#77.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: Makefile recipe bug fix inside the spec-134 ci-fast sentinel region. BSD xargs (macOS) -I{} replacement buffer overflow caused ci-fast-tools to fail with "command line cannot be assembled, too long". Rewrote the xargs invocation to pass the manifest as a positional argument instead of substituting {}, dropped the redundant cargo --jobs flag (overridden by make jobserver), and switched ; to && for short-circuit semantics. No code/spec design changes; ci-parity-check still passes.

## Out of scope (observed in this run, fix in follow-up)

1. **Cargo package-cache lock contention.** Run #3 took 3619s (≈60 min) wall against the 25-min SHOULD target in spec 134 §SC-01. The log is full of `Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache` from concurrent cargo invocations across the fan-out. The structural cure is either per-sub-target `CARGO_HOME` (defeats caching) or fewer concurrent cargo invocations (e.g. moving `make ci` itself to `--workspace` mode for `crates/`, which is the broader spec-104 §2.2 question I flagged on PR #76 and #77). Deserves a measurement-first PR.
2. **Same `-I{}` pattern in `ci-fast-supply-chain`.** Its template is `cargo deny --manifest-path {} check` — one short substitution, stays well under 255 bytes today. Works fine, but the pattern is fragile. Leaving for now to keep this PR minimal-scope; will rewrite if it ever fires.
3. **`run_emitter_spools_to_disk_when_disconnected` flake** in `factory-platform-client` (flagged in PR #76's description, still open).

title: fix(featuregraph): regenerate golden graph for current spec corpus
body:
## Summary

`make ci-fast` (spec 134) ran `cargo test --workspace` and surfaced a stale golden file in `featuregraph`:

```
test test_golden_graph ... FAILED
assertion `left == right` failed: Feature graph does not match golden file. Run UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 to update.
```

The committed `crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` was lagging the spec corpus by **31 entries** (graph_fingerprint mismatch). Spec 134 was the trigger that exposed it, but the debt was much wider — the golden test isn't run by any enforcing CI workflow (`featuregraph` is not in `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS`, and `ci-crates.yml` doesn't matrix it), so multiple prior PRs that added specs landed without regenerating the golden.

This is yet another instance of the **ghost-crate pattern**: workspace members not validated by `make ci` accumulate drift; `make ci-fast --workspace` catches it on the first run.

## What changed

Regenerated via `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden test_golden_graph`, then re-ran without the env var to confirm the fingerprint now matches.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `graph_fingerprint` | `sha256:64bbae1f…` | `sha256:d56f1005…` |
| `feature_id` entries | 152 | 183 |
| Net delta | — | +31, −0 |

The 1130-line diff is purely data: 31 new `feature_id` entries (specs added since the last golden regen) plus the new fingerprint hash.

## Verified

- `cargo test -p featuregraph --test golden test_golden_graph` — `1 passed; 0 failed`

## Spec coupling

`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json` is implementation scaffolding for `featuregraph`. This PR has zero design content — it captures the current shape of the spec corpus into the test fixture. Same pattern as PRs #73, #75, #76: `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` rather than a contrived spec edit.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: defensive maintenance — regenerates an out-of-date test golden file (`crates/featuregraph/tests/golden/features_graph.json`) to match the current spec corpus state. Surfaced by `make ci-fast` (spec 134 §2.3 coverage invariant). No code change; no spec design or invariant changes; the featuregraph scanner produces the same shape, the stored expected value is what was wrong.

## Out of scope (follow-up)

This is the third independent failure mode `ci-fast` has surfaced (after #75 await-holding-lock, #76 workspace clippy debt, this PR golden drift). The common thread is the same: **`featuregraph` and several other workspace members are "ghost crates" not validated by `make ci`**. The right structural follow-up is a spec 104 §2.2 amendment that either:

1. Adds the missing crates to `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS` (and the corresponding workflow), OR
2. Has `make ci` run `cargo {check,clippy,test} --workspace --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml` once instead of N per-member invocations (the workspace mode that `ci-fast-rust` already uses).

Option 2 would unify the local-`ci` and local-`ci-fast` validation surface for the `crates/` workspace, naturally close the ghost-crate gap, and arguably belongs in a spec 134 v2 / spec 135 amendment. Worth a deliberate decision rather than ad-hoc inclusion.

Also pending from earlier observations: the concurrent-test flake in `materialise_run_root_warm_cache_skips_fetches` (#76's PR description), and the `-j` jobserver redundancy in the ci-fast Makefile recipes.

title: fix(crates): clippy clean across 5 workspace ghost-crates (ci-fast surfaced)
body:
## Summary

`make ci-fast` (spec 134) runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` against `crates/Cargo.toml`. The existing `make ci` walks `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS` (12 entries, no `--workspace`), so the **seven workspace members not on that list** have been silently accumulating clippy debt — five of them now flag under Rust 1.95.

This PR cleans them up. **16 errors, 5 crates, 8 files, all mechanical**:

| Crate | Errors | Lints |
|---|---|---|
| `factory-platform-client` | 3 | `collapsible_if` (collapsed via if-let chains) |
| `policy-kernel` (benches) | 3 | `deprecated` (`criterion::black_box` → `std::hint::black_box`) |
| `provenance-validator` | 5 | 4× `field_reassign_with_default` → struct-update syntax; 1× `cloned_ref_to_slice_refs` |
| `factory-engine` | 2 | `unused_imports`; `useless_format` |
| `factory-contracts` | 3 | `needless_borrows_for_generic_args`; 2× `bool_assert_comparison` |

This is exactly the value spec 134 §2.3 promised — `ci-fast` as a **superset** of `ci`'s gate set surfaces issues the parity-bound `make ci` doesn't reach.

## Verified locally

- `cargo clippy --workspace --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p factory-platform-client -p provenance-validator -p factory-engine -p factory-contracts -p open_agentic_policy_kernel` — runtime behavior unchanged

## Observation: one concurrent-test flake (NOT introduced by this PR)

`factory-platform-client::materialise_run_root_warm_cache_skips_fetches` fails with `CacheIo("Invalid argument (os error 22)")` under the full crate test load, but **passes 1/1 in isolation**. The four sibling tests using the same `materialise_run_root` function and same `isolate_cache_dir()` setup all pass under the same concurrent load. Strong signal: pre-existing test-interference issue (probably a global static or filesystem path that `isolate_cache_dir` doesn't fully scope). Worth a follow-up; **not introduced by, and not blocking, this clippy cleanup**.

## Spec coupling

Touches eight files claimed by various specs (`provenance-validator`, `factory-engine`, `factory-contracts`, `policy-kernel`, `factory-platform-client`). All edits are defensive lint cleanups with **no design content** — semantically identical refactors required by Rust 1.95's stricter clippy. Same principled choice as the prior two CI-fix PRs (#73, #75): `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` rather than contrived spec edits.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: defensive clippy cleanup surfaced by `make ci-fast` (spec 134 §2.3 coverage invariant). 16 errors across 5 workspace members, all mechanical refactors required by Rust 1.95 — collapsible_if, field_reassign_with_default, deprecated criterion::black_box, cloned_ref_to_slice_refs, unused_imports, useless_format, needless_borrows_for_generic_args, bool_assert_comparison. No spec design or invariant changes; tests confirm runtime behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope (follow-up)

- **CI_RUST_MANIFESTS coverage gap.** Seven workspace members are not in `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS` and so are not validated by any per-manifest gate in `make ci` (only by `make ci-fast`'s `--workspace` invocation). Whether to extend `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS` (and `ci-crates.yml`) to close that parity gap is a spec 104 §2.2 question deserving its own PR.
- **Concurrent-test flake** in `materialise_run_root_warm_cache_skips_fetches` (described above).
- **`make ci-fast` jobserver warnings.** During the run, every cargo invocation prints "a `-j` argument was passed to Cargo but Cargo is also configured with an external jobserver". The `--jobs $(CIFAST_CARGO_JOBS)` flag is being silently ignored because `make -j` exposes a jobserver. Means the 4×3=12 worker plan is actually 4 makes × jobserver-driven cargo. Not a correctness issue, but worth dropping `--jobs` from the recipes for cleanliness.
- **First measured `ci-fast` wall-time (partial run, hit clippy errors at ~503s into ci-fast-rust).** A complete clean-run measurement → `docs/ci-fast-bench.md` (SC-01) is the natural next step after this PR merges.

title: fix(desktop): switch REPLAY_QUEUE_ENV_LOCK to tokio::sync::Mutex (await-holding-lock)
body:
## Summary

First defect surfaced by `make ci-fast` (spec 134), exactly as the spec said it would: `ci-fast-desktop` runs `cargo clippy --all-targets`, which lints test code, while the parity-bound `ci-desktop` doesn't. The strictness caught a real concurrency footgun in the test suite — a `std::sync::MutexGuard` held across `.await` in a multi-thread tokio runtime is a textbook deadlock hazard.

```
error: this `MutexGuard` is held across an await point
  --> src/commands/factory.rs:3050
  --> src/commands/factory_platform.rs:869
```

The lock (`REPLAY_QUEUE_ENV_LOCK`) is a test-only static that serialises tests mutating `XDG_DATA_HOME`. Its purpose **requires** holding across awaits — that's the whole point. The fix is to use the async-aware `tokio::sync::Mutex` instead.

## Changes

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/factory_platform.rs`: static is now `tokio::sync::Mutex<()>` constructed via `const_new` (still `static`-compatible). Doc comment expanded to explain the async-awareness.
- Three lock acquisition sites updated from `.lock().unwrap()` to `.lock().await`:
  - `factory_platform.rs:869` (`enqueue_then_count_matches_appended_lines`, already `#[tokio::test]`)
  - `factory_platform.rs:854` (`replay_queue_dir_honours_xdg_data_home`, was `#[test]`, now `#[tokio::test]` — body stays sync, just runs inside async runtime)
  - `factory.rs:3050` (`run_emitter_spools_to_disk_when_disconnected`, already `#[tokio::test]`)

## Verified locally

- `cargo clippy --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -A dead_code -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --no-run --all-targets` on apps/desktop — lib, opc bin, opc-web bin all build
- The three affected tests all pass after the change

## Spec coupling

`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/factory.rs` and `factory_platform.rs` are claimed by spec 124 (`opc-factory-run-platform-integration`). This PR is a defensive lint fix with **no design content** — the test concurrency primitive's contract is unchanged, only its underlying type. Inventing a spec edit would be the "spec-as-obstacle" anti-pattern (CONST-005, spec 131). Using the explicit waiver mechanism instead.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: defensive lint fix surfaced by `make ci-fast --all-targets` (spec 134). The test-only `REPLAY_QUEUE_ENV_LOCK` switches from `std::sync::Mutex` to `tokio::sync::Mutex` to silence `clippy::await_holding_lock`. No change to spec 124's design or implementation contract — only to the concrete synchronisation primitive used in test scaffolding.

## Why this PR is small

This is the first real test of the spec 134 coverage invariant — `ci-fast` catching something `ci` misses. The fix is mechanical and isolated; bundling it with the next thing would dilute that signal.

title: spec(134): fast-local-ci-mode — parity-exempt parallel make ci-fast
body:
## Summary

Amend spec 104 to permit a sibling Makefile target `make ci-fast` as a **parity-exempt, performance-optimised local mirror** of `make ci`. Spec 104's parity contract on `make ci` is **unchanged**.

**Why:** `make ci` takes 90+ min on M1 Pro (10c, 64 GB) because spec 104 §FR-02 binds it to token-equivalent mirroring of every enforcing GitHub workflow's `run:` block — that prevents any optimisation whose form diverges from the workflow tokens. CI runners get parallelism by fanning out across jobs; a single-machine local run cannot match that within the parity contract. The result: contributors push validation onto CI rather than running it locally, exactly the inversion `make ci` was meant to prevent.

## What lands

Three commits, ordered to satisfy the SC-03 atomic-landing invariant (parity-check delta ships **before** the Makefile sentinel region):

1. **`spec(134): introduce fast-local-ci-mode amending spec 104`**
   - New `specs/134-fast-local-ci-mode/spec.md` (draft, in-progress)
   - Companion edit on spec 104: `amended:` / `amendment_record:` frontmatter, in-body callout (per the amendment convention established by spec 130 amending 127)

2. **`feat(ci-parity-check): sentinel-bracketed exemption for ci-fast region`**
   - `tools/ci-parity-check/src/lib.rs`: new `strip_cifast_region` helper applied before parity scanning. Lines between `# BEGIN ci-fast (spec 134)` and `# END ci-fast` are opaque to the parity check
   - 4 new unit tests covering bracketed-region removal, identity for unbracketed input, unclosed-BEGIN tolerance, marker-mention rejection. Total lib tests: 16/16 passing

3. **`feat(spec-134): ci-fast Makefile target + docs + index refresh`**
   - `Makefile`: new sentinel-bracketed `ci-fast` recipe tree
   - `.claude/commands/validate-and-fix.md`: two-mode callout
   - `make help`: ci-fast row with wall-time target
   - `build/codebase-index/index.json`: refresh for new spec dir

## Concrete optimisations in `ci-fast`

| Lever | Effect |
|---|---|
| Top-level `make -j$(CIFAST_JOBS)` (default 4) | 7 sub-targets fan out concurrently |
| `cargo clippy --workspace` + `cargo nextest --workspace` on `crates/Cargo.toml` | Collapses 11 of 12 `CI_RUST_MANIFESTS` entries to one invocation |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Subsumes the separate `cargo check` step |
| `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` (auto-detected) | Dedups compilation across the 7 isolated tool target dirs |
| Shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for tools/* | Same-PR effect even without sccache |
| Dropped 10× registry-consumer subset loop | Subsumed by the unfiltered `cargo test`; **prefix-existence side-channel preserved** by an explicit `cargo test -- --list` post-pass |
| `cargo nextest run` (auto-detected) | Strict superset for test execution |
| Concurrent `tsc` + `vitest` in desktop / stagecraft | Independent type-check and test runs no longer serialise |
| `xargs -P` for cargo-deny + background pnpm/npm audits | Supply-chain phase parallelises what was 13 serial deny invocations + 2 audits |

Wait patterns use the safe `wait $$X; A=$$?; wait $$Y; B=$$?; exit $$((A | B))` form throughout (the naïve `wait && wait` would short-circuit and orphan background jobs on first failure).

## Spec-design points worth flagging for review

- **SC-01 is aspirational, not a gate.** "≤ 25 min warm on M1 Pro" is a design target with an empirical baseline pending. A measurement commit at `docs/ci-fast-bench.md` MUST land within 7 days of `implementation: complete` — the MUST is on the *measurement existing*, not the *measurement matching*. Materially divergent measurements force a follow-up amendment, not silent absorption.
- **Coverage invariant (§2.3).** `ci-fast` MUST be a superset of `ci`'s gate set. A passing `ci-fast` should imply a passing `ci`; contradictions are `ci-fast` bugs. Adding a new gate to `ci` MUST extend `ci-fast` in the same change (FR-05).
- **Side-channel preservation.** The dropped `registry-consumer` subset loop's prefix-existence guarantee is preserved explicitly — not silently lost — via a `cargo test -- --list` assertion in `ci-fast-tools` (§2.2(4)).
- **CONST-005 hygiene.** This amendment refines spec 104 without making it less truthful. The parity contract on `ci` is unchanged; `ci-fast` is a sibling target with a different contract. Spec 131 is cross-referenced as a one-line pointer, not a self-acquittal paragraph.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --manifest-path tools/ci-parity-check/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path tools/ci-parity-check/Cargo.toml --lib` — 16/16 pass (4 new sentinel tests + existing 12)
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path tools/ci-parity-check/Cargo.toml --test parity_fixtures` — 3/3 pass
- [x] `./tools/ci-parity-check/target/release/ci-parity-check` — OK, 11 enforcing workflow(s) mirrored, fresh-clone preconditions satisfied
- [x] `./tools/spec-lint/target/release/spec-lint --fail-on-warn` — clean
- [x] `./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer check` — clean
- [x] `make -n ci-fast` — Makefile parses; sccache/nextest fallbacks engage with both absent
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] **Post-merge:** end-to-end `make ci-fast` measurement → `docs/ci-fast-bench.md` (SC-01)

## Spec coupling

This PR includes spec edits for both the spec it creates (134) and the spec it amends (104). Code paths claimed by spec 104 (`Makefile`, `tools/ci-parity-check`, `.claude/commands/validate-and-fix.md`) are accompanied by an edit to spec 104. No `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` needed.

## Out of scope

- Automated `ci`/`ci-fast` cross-check in CI (a periodic job that runs both modes to verify ci-fast catches what ci catches) — follow-up spec.
- Cross-platform fast mode tuning (Linux/Windows) — separate spec.
- Distributing build accelerators (`sccache`, `cargo-nextest`) — auto-detected at runtime, not mandated.
- The two paused work streams: spec 133 (amends-aware coupling gate) sits on its own branch; this PR doesn't touch it.

title: fix: restore green main — clippy 1.95 + missing parity fixtures
body:

title: feat(spec-124): OPC factory-run platform integration
body:
## Summary

Closes spec [124-opc-factory-run-platform-integration](specs/124-opc-factory-run-platform-integration/spec.md). Lands the spec 108 §7.1 + §7.4 deferrals: OPC stops reading `factory/` from a developer's local checkout and instead pulls adapter / contract / process bodies from the platform's `/api/factory/*` endpoints; runs are persisted as `factory_runs` rows and streamed back over the existing duplex channel so a run can be observed from the web UI in real time. `resolve_factory_root()` is deleted; the `// TODO(spec-108-§7-punt)` marker goes with it.

- Mental-model close on spec 108: platform is the orchestration tier, OPC is the execution tier, the contract between them is `/api/factory/*` (definitions in) + `factory_runs` (results out).
- New duplex envelopes (`factory.run.{stage_started, stage_completed, completed, failed, cancelled}`) ride the same bus as spec 123's catalog/binding kinds; idempotent on `(run_id, stage_id, status)` with out-of-order tolerance.
- New `crates/factory-platform-client` crate replaces the in-tree filesystem walk with a content-addressed cache materialised under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/oap-factory/sha-<short>/`; `PlatformClient` doubles as spec 123's `CatalogClient` so a single instance threads into both spec 124's run pipeline and `AgentResolver`.
- New `/app/factory/runs` (list) + `/app/factory/runs/:runId` (detail) surfaces with 3 s polling for live updates; staleness sweeper (`STAGECRAFT_FACTORY_RUN_STALE_AFTER_SEC`, default 1800 s) flips stuck `(queued, running)` rows to `failed`.

## Per-phase commits

| Phase | SHA | Description |
|-------|-----|-------------|
| 0 | `81ccb33` | foundations — envelope types, audit actions, cache-root helper |
| 1 | `2b23212` | schema migration 31 — `factory_runs` table |
