title: refactor(stagecraft-web): finish spec 119 workspace→project collapse on SSR layer
body:
## Summary

The API side of spec 119 (commits 86c99ff / 284e1fc / d621cc8) collapsed `workspaces` into `projects` and deleted `/api/workspaces/*`. The React Router v7 SSR layer was still calling those routes, breaking production with `Error: No route matches URL "/api/workspaces/by-org/default"` on every shell load. This PR migrates the web to the project-shaped API.

- **Lib layer**: rename `workspace-api.server.ts` → `project-api.server.ts`; strip `workspaceId` from factory helpers, KnowledgeObjectRow, SourceConnectorRow, SyncRunRow; drop `workspaceId` from ProjectListEntry / OpcBundle.project / checkCloneAvailability; drop `oap_workspace_id` from JWT claims; replace `workspace_id` with `project_id` on CatalogAgent / CatalogAuditEntry; route `listAgents`/`createAgent` through `/api/projects/:projectId/agents` (the API moved to project-scoped paths).
- **Agent UI moves under the project shell**: delete `app.workspace.agents.*.tsx` (6 files), add `app.project.$projectId.agents.*.tsx` (6 files). Add an Agents tab to the project subnav. Update `routes.ts`.
- **App shell**: drop the default-workspace bootstrap, the workspace pill, the top-level Agents nav, and the workspace outlet context.
- **Pipelines route**: drop the `getProject().workspaceId` pull and every workspaceId form field / parameter.
- **Other project routes** (knowledge, knowledge.\$id, deploys, settings.connectors\*): switch imports from workspace-api to project-api.
- **projects.{clone-availability,new,import}.tsx**: drop workspaceId param, remove the dead "No active workspace" error branch, refresh copy.
- **`_index.tsx` marketing copy**: workspace → project.

## Verification

- `grep -rn "/api/workspaces" platform/services/stagecraft/web` → **0**
- `grep -rn "workspace" web/app` outside generated `client.ts` → **0**
- `npm test`: **233/233 pass**
- `npm run build:frontend`: clean SSR build
- Typecheck: **79 → 43 errors** (-36 fixed, 0 new). Remaining 43 are pre-existing — `CatalogFrontmatter = Record<string, unknown>` (deliberate API-side weakening per spec 111 §2.1) plus unrelated issues in admin.sessions, projects.new, CloneProjectDialog.

The two surviving `workspace` mentions in `lib/client.ts` are in generated code (line 1: `// Code generated by the Encore v1.56.7 client generator. DO NOT EDIT.`) and originate in API-side doc-strings (`api/projects/projects.ts` createPromotion comment, sync envelope schema comment). They will be swept by the next `encore gen client` if those API comments are updated; per the constraint not to touch the API side, they're left alone.

## Test plan

- [ ] Sign in to stagecraft web; load `/app` — shell renders without the `Error: No route matches URL "/api/workspaces/by-org/default"` log line.
- [ ] Navigate to a project: `/app/project/:projectId` — Overview, Knowledge, Agents, Pipelines, Deploys, Settings tabs all load.
- [ ] Knowledge: list, upload (single + folder), detail view, retry failed extraction, download link.
- [ ] Agents: list (status tabs + search), New draft → save → publish → fork → retire → history. Confirm URL is `/app/project/:projectId/agents/...`.
- [ ] Pipelines: init form lists adapters + bound knowledge, pipeline status renders, gate approve/reject works without a workspaceId form field.
- [ ] Connectors: list, create, edit, sync, delete, test connection — all through `/app/project/:projectId/settings/connectors/...`.
- [ ] Deploys: environments list renders without `getDefaultWorkspace` failing.
- [ ] Clone Project dialog: availability check, clone submission, polling — no workspaceId in any request.
- [ ] Org switcher in the header still works.
- [ ] Verify the `/auth/user-orgs` shell call still returns 200 — only the workspace fetch was removed.

title: chore(deps): consolidate 16 dependabot PRs (React 19, TS 6, lucide v1)
body:
## Summary

Apply 14 of 16 open dependabot PRs (#52–#67) in one verified batch and resolve major-version breakage exposed by React 19, TypeScript 6, lucide-react v1. Closing those individual PRs after merge. PRs #53 and #56 stay open — see "Dropped from this batch" below.

## Bumps applied

**Cargo**
- dashmap 5 → 6 — closes #52
- similar 2.7 → 3.1 — closes #54
- deployd-api-rs cargo-minor-patch group (5 updates) — closes #55
- tokio-tungstenite 0.28 → 0.29 — closes #65
- toml 0.8 → 0.9 — closes #66
- window-vibrancy 0.5 → 0.6 — closes #67

**npm / pnpm**
- vite-tsconfig-paths 5 → 6 in stagecraft — closes #57
- vitest 2 → 4 in stagecraft — closes #58
- typescript 5 → 6 (root + stagecraft) — closes #59, closes #60
- react-dom + @types/react-dom (React 19) — closes #61
- recharts 2 → 3 — closes #62
- lucide-react 0.468 → 1.14 — closes #63
- react-markdown 9 → 10 — closes #64
- vite 6.0.3 → 6.4.2 (closes high-severity GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583, dev-server arbitrary file read; was pre-existing on main)

**Versions**
- opc desktop 0.2.4 → 0.2.5
- axiomregent 0.1.0 → 0.1.1

## Dropped from this batch

- **#53 octocrab 0.41 → 0.49** and **#56 reqwest 0.12 → 0.13** — octocrab 0.49 transitively pulls jsonwebtoken@10 → rsa@0.9.10, which carries RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin Attack timing sidechannel). The repo deny.toml explicitly forbids vulnerability ignores, and there is no upstream `rsa` fix yet. Both PRs stay open and can be re-attempted when either jsonwebtoken upgrades off rsa or rsa ships a constant-time implementation.

## Migration fallout (resolved in this PR)

- **React 19** — callback refs can no longer return arbitrary values; rewrote 3 sites (`AgentExecution.tsx`, `ClaudeCodeSession.tsx`) to wrap in a block. `useRef<NodeJS.Timeout>()` now requires an explicit initial value (`TabContext.saveTimeoutRef`).
- **lucide-react v1** dropped the `Github` brand icon. New `apps/desktop/src/components/icons/GithubIcon.tsx` (small inline SVG mark). Routed `LoginScreen` and `ProjectContextOverview` through it; removed the entry from `IconPicker` — existing agents with `icon: "github"` fall back to the bot icon via `ICON_MAP[selectedIcon] || ICON_MAP.bot`.
- **TypeScript 6** — dropped deprecated `baseUrl` from `apps/desktop/tsconfig.json` and `platform/services/stagecraft/web/tsconfig.json` (paths resolve relative to tsconfig location since TS 5.0). Relaxed `AgentIconName` to `string` since `keyof Record<string, X>` surfaces as `string | number` under stricter TS 6 inference.
- **Zustand v5** — wrapped projects-list selector in `useShallow` to prevent re-render churn (`WorkspaceProjectsPanel`).
- **Windows runner** — pinned `shell: bash` on the SBOM upload step in `release-desktop.yml`.

## Test plan

- [x] `gmake ci` green locally — Rust crates, tools, desktop tsc + clippy + lib tests, stagecraft tsc + vitest, supply-chain (cargo-deny, pnpm/npm audit at `--audit-level=high` with `BLOCKING=true`).
- [x] Stagecraft `encore.gen/` and `web/app/lib/client.ts` regenerated locally with encore CLI 1.56.7 to match the bumped `encore.dev` package; `package-lock.json` regenerated from scratch.
- [ ] CI green on this branch (await Actions).
- [ ] Smoke-test desktop app launch and login screen (GithubIcon renders, agent IconPicker still works).

19.2.1 (December 3rd, 2025)

React Server Components

  • Bring React Server Component fixes to Server Actions (@​sebmarkbage #35277)

19.2.0 (Oct 1, 2025)

Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

Read the React 19.2 release post for more information.

New React Features

  • <Activity>: A new API to hide and restore the UI and internal state of its children.
  • useEffectEvent is a React Hook that lets you extract non-reactive logic into an Effect Event.
  • cacheSignal (for RSCs) lets your know when the cache() lifetime is over.
  • React Performance tracks appear on the Performance panel’s timeline in your browser developer tools

New React DOM Features

  • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Web Streams:
    • resume: to resume a prerender to a stream.
    • resumeAndPrerender: to resume a prerender to HTML.
  • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Node Streams:
    • resumeToPipeableStream: to resume a prerender to a stream.
    • resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream: to resume a prerender to HTML.
  • Updated prerender APIs to return a postponed state that can be passed to the resume APIs.

Notable changes

  • React DOM now batches suspense boundary reveals, matching the behavior of client side rendering. This change is especially noticeable when animating the reveal of Suspense boundaries e.g. with the upcoming <ViewTransition> Component. React will batch as much reveals as possible before the first paint while trying to hit popular first-contentful paint metrics.

body:
Bumps [vite-tsconfig-paths](https://github.com/aleclarson/vite-tsconfig-paths) from 5.1.4 to 6.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from vite-tsconfig-paths's releases.

v6.1.0

Features

  • New importerFilter option: Provides fine-grained control over which files should have their imports resolved by this plugin. (Closes #175, #193)
  • Ignore .d.ts overrides: The plugin now ignores resolutions that point to .d.ts files, avoiding issues when tsconfig is used for opt-in type overrides. (Closes #179, #180)

Performance

  • Hoisted regular expressions out of the hot path in the resolver for better performance.

Internal

  • Added resolvedToDeclarationFile event to the debug log file.

v6.0.0

Note: No intentional breaking changes. Major version bump due to extensive internal refactoring; downgrade to v5 if needed.

Highlights

  • On-demand tsconfig discovery via projectDiscovery: "lazy", while eager discovery remains the default.
  • tsconfig/jsconfig files are watched and reloaded automatically in both modes, including during vite build --watch.
  • New logFile option for per-import resolution traces (pass true for vite-tsconfig-paths.log or provide a path).
  • Support for root /* aliases and other absolute-style imports.
  • Support for .astro files when allowJs/loose is enabled.

Fixes

  • More reliable tsconfig watching and resolver refreshes: handles lazy discovery edge cases, recreates resolvers after file changes, tolerates missing directories, and copes better with virtual importers.
  • Windows path handling now normalizes drive-letter casing to avoid missed matches (#183).

Upgrade notes

  • Install the stable release: pnpm add -D vite-tsconfig-paths.
  • Opt into lazy discovery or logging when needed:
import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths'

export default {
plugins: [
tsconfigPaths({
projectDiscovery: 'lazy',
logFile: true,
}),
],
}

  • Rooted path patterns such as "/*": ["src/*"] now resolve the same way tsserver does.

title: chore(deps): update similar requirement from 2.7.0 to 3.1.0 in /crates/axiomregent
body:
Updates the requirements on [similar](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/similar) to permit the latest version.
Changelog

Sourced from similar's changelog.

3.1.0

  • Added capture_diff_slices_by_key and capture_diff_slices_by_key_deadline as convenience helpers for diffing slices by derived keys.
  • Fixed Compact emitting inconsistent DiffOp cursor positions after compaction, which could leave Delete/Insert operations with stale new_index/old_index values.
  • Added explicit lifetime capture (+ use<...>) on iterator-returning APIs to improve compatibility with Rust 2024 lifetime capture behavior. #93

3.0.0

  • Added a Git-style Histogram diff implementation exposed as Algorithm::Histogram, including deadline-aware Myers fallback and comprehensive regression/behavior tests.
  • Raised MSRV to Rust 1.85 and moved the crate to Rust 2024 edition.
  • Added a Hunt-style diff implementation exposed as Algorithm::Hunt.
  • Added configurable inline refinement via InlineChangeOptions and InlineChangeMode, including semantic cleanup and new TextDiff::iter_inline_changes_with_options* methods. #92
  • Added a global disjoint-input fast path in algorithms::diff_deadline to avoid pathological runtimes on large, fully distinct inputs.
  • Improved Algorithm::Myers performance on heavily unbalanced diffs to avoid pathological slowdowns.
  • Added diff_deadline_raw entrypoints in the algorithm modules to bypass shared heuristics and keep minimal intrinsic trait bounds where needed.
  • Added test files in examples/diffs that can be used with the some of the examples as input pairs.
  • Added CachedLookup, a helper for adapting virtual or computed sequences by materializing items on first access and then serving borrowed values through normal indexing. The owned-lookup example demonstrates this approach for issue #33.
  • Fixed ranged indexing in the classic LCS table algorithm.
  • Improved diff compaction to merge adjacent delete hunks across equal runs.
  • Excluded development scripts from published crate contents. #87
  • TextDiff::from_* and TextDiffConfig::diff_* now accept owned inputs (String, Vec<u8>, Cow) in addition to borrowed inputs. This allows returning text diffs from functions without external owner lifetimes. #65
  • TextDiff no longer exposes old_slices / new_slices. Use old_len, new_len, old_slice, new_slice, iter_old_slices, iter_new_slices, old_lookup, and new_lookup instead.
  • TextDiff::iter_changes now panics on invalid out-of-bounds DiffOp ranges instead of silently truncating iteration.
  • utils::diff_lines_inline now takes &TextDiff and options rather than (Algorithm, old, new, options).
  • utils::diff_lines now avoids a second line-tokenization pass.
  • Renamed get_diff_ratio to diff_ratio.
  • Added first-class no_std + alloc support with an explicit default std feature.
  • Added optional hashbrown backend for no_std map storage

title: spec 116: rustls-webpki transitive CVE bump (RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099/0104) — needs lockfile policy decision
body:
## Backlog

Three rustls-webpki CVEs surface on the workspace cargo-deny check:

| ID | Severity | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0098 | high | Name constraints for URI names incorrectly accepted |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0099 | high | Name constraints accepted for certs asserting wildcard names |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0104 | high | Reachable panic in CRL parsing |

All fixed in `rustls-webpki >= 0.103.11` (latest patched: `0.103.13`). Our transitive resolution lands on `0.103.10` via `rustls 0.23.37`.

## Why it's not a one-line fix

- **No direct dep:** rustls-webpki is purely transitive (rustls → rustls-webpki). Can't bump it from any of our `[dependencies]` blocks.
- **`[patch.crates-io]` doesn't apply:** cargo rejects same-source patches (`patches must point to different sources`). The patch mechanism is for swapping crates.io packages with git/path forks, not for pinning a different version of the same crate.
- **Lockfile is gitignored:** `crates/Cargo.lock` is excluded by .gitignore (Rust convention for library workspaces). CI regenerates fresh and resolves to the highest-compatible — which still lands on 0.103.10 because of constraint chains.

## Three viable paths

1. **Commit `crates/Cargo.lock`.** Reverses the gitignore convention. With `publish = false` on every workspace member (landed in PR #47), the workspace is effectively all-binaries; committing the lockfile gives reproducible builds AND lets us pin transitive CVEs directly. Affects spec 117's lockfile-generation step (could simplify it).
2. **Add a direct rustls dep as a version anchor.** Add `rustls = "0.23.40"` to a workspace member that doesn't currently use it (e.g., axiomregent — already pulls it transitively). The version constraint propagates through the resolver, yielding `rustls-webpki 0.103.11+`. Slightly hacky but minimal blast radius.
3. **Bump the actual parent.** Find what pins `rustls 0.23.37` and bump it. May cascade into multiple manifest edits.

## Recommendation

Option 1 (commit `crates/Cargo.lock`) — but only after broader discussion. The gitignore convention encodes a deliberate choice about library-vs-binary workspace governance, and reversing it should be intentional, not a side-effect of a CVE fix.

Option 2 is the targeted fix if option 1 is rejected.

## Blocking

Spec 116 promotion (`vars.SUPPLY_CHAIN_BLOCKING=true`) requires advisories to be empty. These 3 CVEs + 5 unmaintained-crate advisories are the remaining backlog after PR #47 lands.

title: fix(ci): drop broken rust-cross matrix (was failing 100% since merge)
body:
## Summary

The M7 cross-target \`cargo check\` matrix added in PR #6 has failed on **every PR run since merge**. Removing.

## Root cause

\`apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml\` declares the \`macos-private-api\` Tauri feature cross-target, but only \`tauri.macos.conf.json\` declares \`macOSPrivateApi: true\`. Direct \`cargo check --target <linux|windows>\` invokes tauri-build's build.rs against the base \`tauri.conf.json\` (which lacks the field), producing:

\`\`\`
The `tauri` dependency features on the `Cargo.toml` file does not match
the allowlist defined under `tauri.conf.json`.
Please run `tauri dev` or `tauri build` or remove the `macos-private-api` feature.
\`\`\`

## Why removing is safe

\`release-desktop.yml\`'s \`tauri-action\` already validates real cross-target builds at tag time, passing the correct per-target \`--configPath\` (\`tauri.linux.conf.json\` etc.). The PR-time gate has been redundant noise that's blocked nothing real (because no PR could have ever passed it).

## Reintroduction path (future)

A proper PR-time cross-target check needs either \`TAURI_CONFIG=$(cat tauri.<os>.conf.json) cargo check\` env-var injection per matrix shard, or splitting \`macos-private-api\` behind a target-conditional Cargo feature. Either is invasive enough to warrant a focused follow-up rather than carrying broken CI in the meantime. The replacement comment block in \`ci-desktop.yml\` records this for anyone reintroducing the gate.

## Unblocks

- PR #47 (cargo-deny semantic config) — currently red on this matrix only.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`ci-desktop\` workflow runs to green on this PR (no rust-cross legs).
- [ ] \`ci-parity\` confirms the Makefile change.

title: fix(codebase-indexer): retain dump-inputs diagnostic + rebuild-on-invoke (closes #46)
body:
## Summary

Closes #46 — the cross-platform hash divergence was **operator error**, not a real bug.

## Investigation

Added a \`dump-inputs\` diagnostic subcommand (\`<rel-path>\\t<sha256-of-normalized-content>\`, sorted) and ran it on macOS dev + Linux CI at the same SHA:

\`\`\`
$ md5 /tmp/inputs-mac.tsv /tmp/inputs-linux/inputs.tsv
f39b0ddae5506ccd756f17ce2c1c37b6  inputs-mac.tsv
f39b0ddae5506ccd756f17ce2c1c37b6  inputs-linux/inputs.tsv
$ ./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer compile  # local
\"contentHash\": \"39b185f4a2a950c045ba67b8c982bdf2c4cb3400139ed635bdcef099cd8e4441\"
$ git show main:build/codebase-index/index.json | grep contentHash
\"contentHash\": \"39b185f4a2a950c045ba67b8c982bdf2c4cb3400139ed635bdcef099cd8e4441\"
\`\`\`

Identical. The hash function is deterministic across platforms.

## Real cause

A \`codebase-indexer\` binary built from a previous session's source was being invoked against newer source on main. Phase 5 (spec 118) added a workflow scanner to the indexer's input set; any binary built before that change ignores the new inputs and produces a different hash. Same for the SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the same change. The symptom looked cross-platform because each fresh pull from main carried the source change, while the dev's \`target/release/codebase-indexer\` lagged.

## Changes

- **Keep** \`dump-inputs\` subcommand — small, self-contained diagnostic worth having for any future investigation. Output format is stable; usage in subcommand help.
- **Drop** \`.github/workflows/debug-indexer-inputs.yml\` — one-shot, no longer needed.
- **Makefile**: \`index\`, \`index-check\`, \`index-render\` now depend on a rebuild rule. Cargo's incremental cache makes this free on warm builds. This is the **preventive fix** — a stale binary can no longer silently produce a stale hash.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`make index-check\` triggers a cargo build of the indexer if any \`tools/codebase-indexer/src/*.rs\` is newer than the binary.
- [ ] \`make index-check\` is a no-op if the binary is already current.
- [ ] \`./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer dump-inputs | head\` shows sorted path+hash output.

## Closes

#46

title: fix(cargo-deny): proper config — private/wildcards/license (towards spec 116 promotion)
body:
## Summary

\`cargo deny check\` on main produced 30+ noise errors on internal workspace crates (\`unlicensed\`, \`wildcard\`), hiding the real backlog. Three correctness fixes:

1. **\`[licenses.private] ignore = true\`** + \`publish = false\` on 24 internal Cargo.toml files. First-party AGPL crates are intentionally absent from the third-party \`[licenses].allow\` list; cargo-deny's \`private.ignore\` exempts unpublished workspace members.
2. **\`[bans] allow-wildcard-paths = true\`** — path deps carry no version by convention. Registry-level \`version = "*"\` still errors.
3. **License allowlist additions** for genuine permissive licenses encountered (\`MIT-0\`, \`CDLA-Permissive-2.0\`, \`NCSA\`). Removed two unmatched entries.

## Before / after

\`\`\`
Before: 30+ false errors on internal crates, real backlog hidden
After:  advisories FAILED (5 unmaintained + 3 rustls-webpki CVEs)
        bans       ok
        licenses   ok
        sources    ok
\`\`\`

## Real backlog (deferred to follow-up PRs)

| Severity | Source | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 3 vulns | rustls-webpki (RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099/0104) | \`cargo update\` or \`[patch]\` |
| 5 unmaintained | atty, bincode, instant, number_prefix, paste | \`[advisories].ignore\` with rationale per crate |
| pnpm | protobufjs/lodash/vite | overrides + vite bump |
| npm/stagecraft | drizzle-orm + esbuild chain | \`npm audit fix\` + breaking-change review |

Each will be a focused PR. Spec 116 promotion (\`vars.SUPPLY_CHAIN_BLOCKING=true\`) is gated on those landings — the 2026-05-28 date in the spec was a target, not a hard deadline.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`make ci-supply-chain\` locally: cargo-deny licenses + bans + sources pass; advisories surface real backlog only.
- [ ] CI: \`ci-supply-chain\` workflow produces clean license/bans output (warn-only window means even advisory failures don't block — but the license/bans output should now show "ok").

title: tools/codebase-indexer: cross-platform hash divergence (macOS dev vs Linux CI)
body:
## Problem

`codebase-indexer check` reports stale on macOS dev machines after every merge to `main`, even on a clean working tree at the same SHA that CI just validated as fresh. Reproduced after PR #6, PR #33, and again after PR #45 merges.

| State | macOS local hash | Linux CI hash (committed) |
|---|---|---|
| post-PR #6 merge (a4bd57a) | `318d2c…` | `524ec4…` |
| post-PR #33 merge | `318d2c…` | `5f05d8…` |
| post-PR #45 merge | (TBD on next pull) | (TBD) |

Each side reproduces deterministically — same input, same hash, every run.

## Reproduction

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer check
# → exits 2 with "expected <CI hash>, got <local hash>"
./tools/codebase-indexer/target/release/codebase-indexer compile
git diff build/codebase-index/index.json
# → only contentHash differs; all other content is byte-identical
```

CI's staleness gate (`ci-codebase-index.yml`) reports `success` on the same SHA — confirming Linux side computes `<CI hash>` from the same input set.

## Practical impact

- Mac devs hit false-positive staleness errors on every `make ci-tools` after pulling main.
- Hides real staleness drift behind a known-noise baseline.
- Forces local recompile commits that don't actually change anything except the hash field.

## Hypothesis space

The hash function (`tools/codebase-indexer/src/hash.rs`) normalizes line endings + strips BOM. So the issue is one of:

1. **File set divergence.** `collect_input_files` enumerates directories on local that don't exist or are differently populated on CI (e.g., AppleDouble files, `.DS_Store` slipping past extension filters).
2. **Path-string encoding.** macOS HFS+/APFS may surface filenames in NFD; Linux ext4 in NFC. `PathBuf::to_string_lossy()` would produce different bytes for any non-ASCII filename.
3. **Directory traversal nondeterminism.** `fs::read_dir` returns OS-dependent order; the code sorts after collection but if any sort uses unstable ordering on equal keys, divergence could leak.
4. **Stale local cargo target poisoning collect_input_files** — checked locally; the input-file set is currently scoped to authoring artefacts only (Cargo.toml, package.json, specs, workflows, etc.) so this is unlikely but worth ruling out.

## Diagnostic plan

Add a `--dump-inputs` flag to `codebase-indexer` that prints every input path + its normalized-content sha256. Run on macOS local and Linux CI; diff. The first divergent line tells us which file (or which path encoding) breaks determinism.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Spec 101 (`codebase-index-mvp`) and spec 103 (`init-protocol-governed-reads`) both treat the codebase index as a governed structural inventory. If it can't be independently recomputed across platforms, the gate is one-sided — Mac devs can't verify their own changes against the gate. That's a soft form of "CI is the only source of truth," which spec 104 was explicitly trying to avoid for the Makefile.

## Fix likely small

The diagnostic's first diverging line will probably point at a single fix (e.g., normalize NFD→NFC at path read time, or strip a hidden directory entry that should never have been in the input set).

title: fix(release): generate-lockfile before SBOM scan (AC-6, take 3)
body:
## Summary

Smoke #3 (\`axiomregent-v0.0.2-attestation-smoke\`) on PR #43's syft-version bump still returned \`components: 0\`. Real cause: \`crates/Cargo.lock\` is **gitignored**.

\`\`\`
$ grep Cargo.lock .gitignore
Cargo.lock                              # everything ignored except…
!tools/spec-compiler/Cargo.lock         # …these explicit allowlist entries
!tools/registry-consumer/Cargo.lock
!tools/spec-lint/Cargo.lock
!tools/policy-compiler/Cargo.lock
!tools/codebase-indexer/Cargo.lock
!apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock
\`\`\`

Fresh CI checkouts have **no \`Cargo.lock\` anywhere under \`crates/\`**. syft's \`rust-cargo-lock-cataloger\` walks \`Cargo.toml\` files but finds zero lockfiles → 0 components. Local repros showed components > 0 only because the developer's working tree had stale per-member \`Cargo.lock\` files from past builds.

## Fix

\`release-axiomregent.yml\` only — desktop and tools workflows already have committed lockfiles:

1. Pin Rust toolchain (1.95.0, matching the rest of CI).
2. \`cargo generate-lockfile --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml\` before SBOM.
3. Scope SBOM to \`path: crates\` (workspace root, where the new lockfile lands) — not \`path: crates/axiomregent\` (member crate, one level below the lockfile). syft only walks down from the scan root.

The new SBOM enumerates every workspace member's transitive dependencies — what a built axiomregent binary actually links against (orchestrator, policy-kernel, agent, …).

## Spec 117 update

§6 AC-6 amended with the **third lesson learned**:

| Take | Smoke run | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | v0.0.0 | 0 components | scope = stripped binaries | path → source tree (PR #42) |
| 2 | v0.0.1 | 0 components | syft 1.11 cataloger no-op | bump action v0.17.8 → v0.24.0 (PR #43) |
| 3 | v0.0.2 | 0 components | gitignored lockfile | generate-lockfile + scan workspace root (this PR) |

## Test plan

- [ ] Smoke #4 (\`axiomregent-v0.0.3-attestation-smoke\`) returns \`components > 0\`.
- [ ] Cleanup all four smoke releases once #4 verifies AC-6.

title: fix(release): bump anchore/sbom-action v0.17.8 → v0.24.0 (AC-6, take 2)
body:
## Summary

Smoke #2 (\`axiomregent-v0.0.1-attestation-smoke\`) on PR #42's source-scope fix still returned \`components: 0\`. Local repro identified the real cause:

| Tool | Components |
|---|---|
| Local \`syft 1.43.0\` against \`dir:crates/axiomregent\` | **661** |
| CI \`syft 1.11.1\` (shipped with \`anchore/sbom-action@v0.17.8\`) | **0** |

The pinned action dates to early 2025 and carries a syft whose Rust cataloger silently no-ops on \`Cargo.lock\` in this directory shape. Bumping to \`v0.24.0\` (2026-03-20, ships syft 1.30+) across all three release workflows.

## Changes

- \`.github/workflows/release-{axiomregent,desktop,tools}.yml\`: \`anchore/sbom-action@61119d4 # v0.17.8\` → \`@e22c3899 # v0.24.0\`
- \`specs/117-release-artifact-attestations/spec.md\` §6 AC-6: amended with both lessons learned (path scope from PR #42 + action version from this PR).

Provenance flow unaffected (\`actions/attest-build-provenance\` already verified end-to-end on smoke #1).

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge, dispatch smoke #3 (\`axiomregent-v0.0.2-attestation-smoke\`) and verify \`jq '.components | length' sbom-axiomregent.cdx.json > 0\`.
- [ ] Cleanup \`axiomregent-v0.0.0-...\` and \`axiomregent-v0.0.1-...\` smoke releases once smoke #3 confirms the fix.

title: fix(release): scope SBOM scan to source tree (spec 117 AC-6)
body:
## Summary

Smoke run \`axiomregent-v0.0.0-attestation-smoke\` (#25118354551) verified spec 117 AC-1 (assets attached) and AC-4 (\`gh attestation verify\` succeeds with correct workflow + repo + SHA + SLSA v1 predicate). **AC-6 failed**: SBOM has 0 components.

Root cause: \`anchore/sbom-action\` with \`path: dist/\` (or the Tauri \`target/\` equivalent) scopes syft to stripped release binaries. Syft can't recover crate metadata from stripped Rust binaries — output is a CycloneDX doc with zero \`components[]\`.

## Fix

Scope SBOM to source trees where \`Cargo.toml\` + \`Cargo.lock\` exist:

| Workflow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| \`release-axiomregent.yml\` | \`path: dist/\` | \`path: crates/axiomregent\` |
| \`release-desktop.yml\` | \`path: apps/desktop/src-tauri/target\` | \`path: apps/desktop\` |
| \`release-tools.yml\` | \`path: dist/\` | \`path: src/tools\` (with new \`checkout\` into \`src/\` — publish job previously had no checkout) |

Provenance attestations are unaffected (sha256 digest-based, independent of SBOM scan).

Spec 117 §6 AC-6 amended with the lesson learned.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`ci-parity\` and \`ci-codebase-index\` pass on this PR (no enforcing-workflow changes).
- [ ] After merge, dispatch a follow-up smoke run (e.g. \`axiomregent-v0.0.1-attestation-smoke\`) and confirm \`jq '.components | length' sbom-axiomregent.cdx.json\` returns >0.

## Cleanup

The current smoke release \`axiomregent-v0.0.0-attestation-smoke\` is best left in place until this PR merges and the follow-up smoke validates AC-6. After that, both can be deleted with \`gh release delete --cleanup-tag\`.

Release notes

Sourced from uuid's releases.

v1.23.1

What's Changed

  • Remove deprecated msrv feature from wasm-bindgen dependency by @​guybedford in uuid-rs/uuid#877
  • fix: Timestamp::from_gregorian deprecation note by @​aznashwan in uuid-rs/uuid#878
  • Prepare for 1.23.1 release by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#879

New Contributors

  • @​guybedford made their first contribution in uuid-rs/uuid#877
  • @​aznashwan made their first contribution in uuid-rs/uuid#878

Full Changelog: https://github.com/uuid-rs/uuid/compare/v1.23.0...v1.23.1

v1.23.0

What's Changed

  • feat: add support for 'hyphenated' format in the serde module by @​FrenchDilettante in uuid-rs/uuid#865
  • Fix a number of bugs in time-related code by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#872
  • Reword invalid char error message by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#873
  • Impl cleanups by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#874
  • Use LazyLock to synchronize v1/v6 context initialization by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#875
  • Prepare for 1.23.0 release by @​KodrAus in uuid-rs/uuid#876

New Contributors

  • @​FrenchDilettante made their first contribution in uuid-rs/uuid#865

Special thanks

@​meng-xu-cs raised a series of bugs against the timestamp logic in uuid using automated tooling. The issues themselves were reasonably and responsibly presented and the end result is a better uuid library for everyone. Thanks!

Deprecations

This release includes the following deprecations:

  • Context: Renamed to ContextV1
  • Timestamp::from_gregorian: Renamed to Timestamp::from_gregorian_time

Change to Version::Max

Version::Max's u8 representation has changed from 0xff to 0x0f to match the value returned by Uuid::get_version_num.

Change to Uuid::get_version for the max UUID

Uuid::get_version will only return Some(Version::Max) if the UUID is actually the max UUID (all bytes are 0xff). Previously it would return Some if only the version field was 0x0f. This change matches the behaviour of the nil UUID, which only returns Some(Version::Nil) if the UUID is the nil UUID (all bytes are 0x00).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/uuid-rs/uuid/compare/v1.22.0...v1.23.0

title: fix(ci): resync codebase index + Claude CLI version pin
body:
## Summary

Two follow-up fixes from PR #6 ship together because they're both single-line corrections to artifacts that landed broken on main:

1. **`build/codebase-index/index.json` resync** — fix-up commit `a0353da` modified files in the indexer hash inputs (`specs/116-.../spec.md`, `.github/workflows/ci-supply-chain.yml`) without re-running `codebase-indexer compile`. Recomputed hash: `524ec4 → 318d2c`.
2. **`CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION` pin** — Phase 1 pinned `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.88`, which was never published. Every AI PR review since merge has failed with `npm ETARGET`. Re-pinned to `2.1.116` (current `stable` dist-tag).

## Test plan

- [ ] `ci-codebase-index` workflow passes (also acts as the discriminator for whether there's a real cross-platform indexer hash bug).
- [ ] `ai-review / diff scan` passes — first end-to-end run of the new stdin-fed prompt against a real PR diff.

## Open question

The `ci-codebase-index` gate on the merge of PR #6 (commit `a4bd57a`) reported success despite the local-vs-committed hash mismatch. If this PR's gate run computes a third hash, we have a real cross-platform determinism bug in the indexer and a follow-up is needed in `tools/codebase-indexer/src/hash.rs`.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/compare/v0.13.2...v0.13.3

Changelog

Sourced from reqwest's changelog.

v0.13.3

  • Fix CertificateRevocationList parsing of PEM values.
  • Fix logging in resolver to only show host, not full URL.
  • Fix hickory-dns to fallback to a default if /etc/resolv.conf fails.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to handle STOP_SENDING as not an error.
  • Fix HTTP/3 pool to remove timed out QUIC connections.
  • Fix HTTP/3 connection establishment picking IPv4 and IPv6.
  • Upgrade rustls-platform-verifier.
  • (wasm) Only use wasm-bindgen on unknown-* targets.

v0.13.2

  • Fix HTTP/2 and native-tls ALPN feature combinations.
  • Fix HTTP/3 to send h3 ALPN.
  • (wasm) fix RequestBuilder::json() from override previously set content-type.

v0.13.1

  • Fixes compiling with rustls on Android targets.

v0.13.0

  • Breaking changes:
    • rustls is now the default TLS backend, instead of native-tls.
    • rustls crypto provider defaults to aws-lc instead of ring. (rustls-no-provider exists if you want a different crypto provider)
    • rustls-tls has been renamed to rustls.
    • rustls roots features removed, rustls-platform-verifier is used by default.
      • To use different roots, call tls_certs_only(your_roots).
    • native-tls now includes ALPN. To disable, use native-tls-no-alpn.
    • query and form are now crate features, disabled by default.
    • Long-deprecated methods and crate features have been removed (such as trust-dns, which was renamed hickory-dns a while ago).
  • Many TLS-related methods renamed to improve autocompletion and discovery, but previous name left in place with a "soft" deprecation. (just documented, no warnings)
    • For example, prefer tls_backend_rustls() over use_rustls_tls().

v0.12.28

  • Fix compiling on Windows if TLS and SOCKS features are not enabled.

v0.12.27

  • Add ClientBuilder::windows_named_pipe(name) option that will force all requests over that Windows Named Piper.

v0.12.26

  • Fix sending Accept-Encoding header only with values configured with reqwest, regardless of underlying tower-http config.

body:
Updates the requirements on [jsonschema](https://github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from jsonschema's releases.

[Python] Release 0.46.3

Fixed

  • Memory not reclaimed when a validator for a schema with recursive $ref or $dynamicRef is dropped. #1125
Changelog

Sourced from jsonschema's changelog.

[0.46.3] - 2026-04-28

Fixed

  • Memory not reclaimed when a Validator for a schema with recursive $ref or $dynamicRef is dropped. #1125
  • Compilation failure on wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-emscripten targets.

[0.46.2] - 2026-04-20

Fixed

  • required not enforced when additionalProperties is a schema object and required lists exactly 2 keys.

[0.46.1] - 2026-04-18

Fixed

  • required not enforced when properties has 15 or more entries and required lists exactly 2 keys.

[0.46.0] - 2026-04-10

Added

  • ValidatorMap for validating instances against subschemas identified by URI-fragment JSON pointer. #1075
  • CLI: Accept multiple values after -i/--instance (e.g. jsonschema validate schema.json -i *.json). #1085
  • dereference function to recursively inline $ref references. #422
  • CLI: jsonschema dereference subcommand to dereference a schema from the command line.

Breaking Changes

  • Registry construction now uses an explicit prepare step, and with_registry now borrows the prepared registry. ValidationOptions::with_resource and ValidationOptions::with_resources were removed in favor of building a Registry first. See the Migration Guide for the details.

Performance

  • Avoid registry clones and document clones during validator construction. This improves real-world schema compilation by roughly 10-20% in internal benchmarks.

[0.45.1] - 2026-04-06

Fixed

  • Incorrect handling of multipleOf validation for negative numeric instances.
  • Incorrect handling of duration format when hours and seconds appear without minutes, or years and days without months.

[0.45.0] - 2026-03-08

Added

  • bundle(schema) / async_bundle(schema) / ValidationOptions::bundle: produce a Compound Schema Document with external $ref targets embedded in a draft-appropriate container (definitions for Draft 4/6/7, $defs for Draft 2019-09/2020-12) while preserving $ref values. #791.
  • CLI: jsonschema validate and jsonschema bundle subcommands. Flat invocation (jsonschema schema.json -i …) is deprecated — use jsonschema validate instead. #791.
  • ValidationError::absolute_keyword_location() to get the absolute keyword location URI of the schema node that produced the error. #737.

Changelog

Sourced from jsonwebtoken's changelog.

10.3.0 (2026-01-27)

  • Export everything needed to define your own CryptoProvider
  • Fix type confusion with exp/nbf when not required

10.2.0 (2025-11-06)

  • Remove Clone bound from decode functions

10.1.0 (2025-10-18)

  • add dangerous::insecure_decode
  • Implement TryFrom &Jwk for DecodingKey

10.0.0 (2025-09-29)

  • BREAKING: now using traits for crypto backends, you have to choose between aws_lc_rs and rust_crypto
  • Add Clone bound to decode
  • Support decoding byte slices
  • Support JWS

9.3.1 (2024-02-06)

  • Update base64

9.3.0 (2024-03-12)

  • Add Validation.reject_tokens_expiring_in_less_than, the opposite of leeway

9.2.0 (2023-12-01)

  • Add an option to not validate aud in the Validation struct
  • Get the current timestamp in wasm without using std
  • Update ring to 0.17

9.1.0 (2023-10-21)

  • Supports deserialization of unsupported algorithms for JWKs

9.0.0 (2023-10-16)

title: feat(ci): governed CI/CD hardening — 25 findings, 3 specs, 6 phases
body:
## Summary

Closes all 25 findings from the `.github/` + `Makefile` audit (3 High, 8 Medium, 10 Low, 4 cross-cutting) plus three new specs covering supply-chain, release attestations, and workflow traceability. One branch, phase-grouped commits.

## Specs added

- **`116-supply-chain-policy-gates`** — cargo-deny + npm/pnpm audit, 30-day warn window, `deny.toml` policy bundle.
- **`117-release-artifact-attestations`** — CycloneDX SBOM + SLSA provenance per shipped binary; pre-public-release ordering constraint.
- **`118-workflow-spec-traceability`** — `# Spec: NNN-slug` header convention, codebase-indexer Layer 5, `I-105` diagnostic, schema bump 1.0.0 → 1.1.0.

## Phases

| Phase | Commit | Findings | What changed |
|-------|--------|----------|---|
| Specs | `d0139af` | — | 116, 117, 118 spec.md files |
| 0 | `c5b62a7` | H1, L10 | rust-toolchain pin lockstep, dependabot.yml |
| 1 | `afc656d` | H2, H3, H4, M6 | dedicated codebase-index gate, AI-review shell injection fix, Claude CLI bump, draft-PR skip |
| 3 | `4fb015b` | M2, M8 | release attestations + tools workflow_run sequencing |
| 2 | `feb2964` | M1, M3, M4, M5, M7 | supply-chain workflow + Makefile mirror, real Encore codegen, cache key unification, timeouts everywhere, cross-target desktop matrix |
| 4 | `bd085e0` | L1-L9 | de-hardcode org/repo, regex tightening, helm secret masking, CODEOWNERS |
| 5 | `e2610d3` | spec 118 + 5.2 | workflow header backfill (19/19), indexer Layer 5, parity-check fixture tests |

## Findings closed (by ID)

**High:** H1 (Rust toolchain pinning) · H2 (codebase-index staleness path filter) · H3 (AI workflow shell injection) · H4 (Claude CLI version)
**Medium:** M1 (supply-chain) · M2 (release attestations) · M3 (Encore codegen) · M4 (rust-cache keys) · M5 (job timeouts) · M6 (draft-PR skip) · M7 (desktop cross-target) · M8 (release-tools race)
**Low:** L1 (org/repo coupling) · L2 (`make stop` regex) · L3 (`make clean` scope) · L5 (encore cache arch key) · L6 (agent-frontmatter help) · L7 (helm kubeconfig masking) · L8 (CODEOWNERS) · L9 (ai-changelog shell) · L10 (dependabot)
**Cross-cutting:** workflow-to-spec traceability convention · ci-parity-check fixture-based tests

## Validation done locally

- `ci-parity-check`: clean — Makefile mirrors all 9 enforcing workflows
- `codebase-indexer check`: clean — index hash matches inputs
- `codebase-indexer compile + render`: 19/19 workflows header-tagged via spec 118 convention; zero `I-105`
- `cargo test --manifest-path tools/ci-parity-check/Cargo.toml`: 12 unit + 3 fixture tests pass
- `cargo test --manifest-path tools/codebase-indexer/Cargo.toml`: full suite passes including new workflow scanner tests + schema conformance against bumped 1.1.0 schema
- `cargo test --manifest-path tools/spec-compiler/Cargo.toml`: passes (registry compiles 116/117/118 cleanly as draft)

## Test plan (CI will exercise)

title: fix(stagecraft-chart): surface required PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY
body:
## Summary

- Adds `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to the chart's ESO `secrets.keys` list so ESO-provisioned clusters pull the key from the remote secret store.
- Adds a `NOTES.txt` that enumerates every env var the pod requires when running with `secrets.create=false` (self-managed secret), so operators don't miss a key on a clean deploy.

## Why

`api/factory/upstreamPat.ts` calls `encryptPat()`, which requires the `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` Encore secret. The chart never surfaced this key, so the Hetzner production deploy shipped without it — every `POST /api/factory/upstreams/pat` returned 500 (`failed to resolve secret`), the `factory_upstream_pats` row never got written, and the sync worker fell back to an installation token that couldn't see the configured upstream (`GovAlta-Pronghorn/*`), returning `Repository not found` from `git clone`.

Prod was unblocked by directly patching `stagecraft-api-secrets` with a freshly generated key. This PR closes the chart gap so the next clean deploy doesn't regress.

## Operator action required

The current Hetzner prod is running with a `PAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` that exists in the K8s secret but is **not** backed by the external source / password manager unless operators also save it there. The new `NOTES.txt` makes this explicit; operators should copy the generated key into a password manager (or operator vault, when we have one). Rotating the key invalidates every stored PAT.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm lint platform/charts/stagecraft` — passes
- [x] `helm template` against `values.yaml + values-hetzner.yaml` — renders (6 resources)
- [ ] On next CD run, confirm `NOTES.txt` is printed at the end of the Helm upgrade log

title: feat(032): T006 gitctx MCP enrichment (Rust stdio bridge)
body:
mplements Feature 032 T006: gitctx MCP enrichment via a Rust-owned per-request stdio bridge; native git stays source-of-truth; governance/axiomregent out of scope.

### Runtime model

- gitctx MCP is Rust-owned and executes through a per-request stdio bridge in `commands/mcp.rs`.
- `get_sidecar_ports` is not used for gitctx; port discovery remains only for sidecars that actually announce ports, such as axiomregent.
- Desktop enrichment readiness is defined by the result of the MCP bridge call itself.
- Native git remains source-of-truth for branch, dirty state, and ahead/behind; gitctx is additive enrichment only.

**Reviewer one-liner:** This PR unifies gitctx on a single Rust-owned per-request stdio MCP path and keeps native git authoritative, with gitctx acting only as additive enrichment.
